The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque, whose surroundings We have blessed, that We might show him some of Our signs. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.﴾ (17:1)

Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: By His saying, exalted is His remembrance, ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾, He means: the declaration of the One who took His servant by night as transcendent, and His exoneration from what the polytheists say about Him, namely that He has partners among His creation, that He has a consort and a son. It also means His exaltation and magnification above what they ascribe to Him and attribute to Him out of their ignorance and the errors of their statements.

I have already explained earlier that His saying, *subhan* (glory), is a noun placed in the position of a verbal noun (*masdar*), and so it is in the accusative case because it occupies that position, which makes it unnecessary to repeat the verb here. Some have said that it is in the accusative because it is not qualified. The Arabs use *tasbih* (glorification) in several contexts. Among them is prayer. Many of the people of interpretation (*ahl al-ta'wil*) interpreted God's saying, ﴿Had he not been of those who glorify [God]﴾ (37:143), as meaning: had he not been of those who pray. Among them is exception (*istithna'*). Some interpreted God's saying, ﴿Did I not tell you? Why do you not glorify [God]?﴾ (68:28), as meaning: why do you not make an exception? He claimed that this is a dialect of some people of Yemen, and he cited as evidence for the soundness of his interpretation His saying, ﴿When they swore that they would surely harvest it in the morning, and did not make an exception﴾ (68:17–18), and ﴿The most moderate of them said: Did I not tell you? Why do you not glorify [God]?﴾ (68:28). Thus He mentioned their failure to make an exception. Among them is light. Some interpreted the report related from the Prophet ﷺ: "Were it not for that, the glories (*subuhat*) of His face would have burned away whatever His sight reached," as meaning by "the glories of His face" the light of His face.

Those who interpret the Qur'an (*ahl al-ta'wil*) have said the same thing as what we have said regarding the interpretation of His saying, ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

* Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from 'Uthman ibn Mawhab, from Musa ibn Talha, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he was asked about *tasbih*, that a person says: "Subhan Allah." He said: "The declaration that God is far removed from evil."

* Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: 'Abdah ibn Sulayman told us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, "Subhan Allah," that he said: "The declaration of God's sovereignty and the affirmation of His transcendence (*innakaf li-llah*)." We have already mentioned in what has preceded in this book of ours the reports on this matter, which are sufficient.

*Al-Isra'* and *al-Sura* mean travel by night. Whoever says *asra* (with the alif) says *yusri, isra'*; whoever says *sara* says *yasri, sara*, as the poet said:

*Many a night of darkness have I traveled, and it did not turn me away from it, a night like this (*layt*).*

* [Footnote: The two verses are cited in *Lisan al-Arab* (under *layt*) as evidence that *lataho* 'an wajhihi, *yalitahu* and *yaluthuhu*, *layt*, means: he held him back from his direction and turned him away. The rajaz verse is: "And a night of travel (*sura*) I traveled." ... etc. It was said the meaning is: nothing turned me away from its travel so that I would regret and say: "Would that I had not traveled it." It was also said the meaning is: no one turned me from its travel, i.e., no one blamed me, so the verbal noun was placed in the position of the proper noun. In *al-Tahdhib*: nothing turned me from it—no deficiency and no incapacity. Likewise *alatahu 'an wajhihi*: *fa'ala* and *af'ala* have the same meaning. End. And in *Lisan al-'Arab* (under *sara*): *al-Sura*: travel by night, in general; it was said *al-sura* is travel of the whole night. The Arabs treat it as masculine and feminine. *Sarayt sara wa masra*, and *asrayt*, both meaning: when one travels at night. With the alif is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz. The Mighty Qur'an came with both. End. On this basis the author cited the verse. Al-Suhayli said in *al-Rawd al-Unuf* (1:243): The narrators agreed on calling it *isra'*, and none of them named it *sura*, even though the lexicographers said *sara* and *asra* have the same meaning. This indicates that the lexicographers did not verify the expression... until he said: It is not permissible to say "sara bi-'abdihi" in any way; therefore the recitation came only in one form in this story. End.]

It is also transmitted: "a night of dew (*nada*) I traveled."

By His saying, ﴿a night﴾ (*layl*), He means: during the night. Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman used to recite it this way.

* Abu Kurayb told us, saying: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, and a man was narrating a hadith in his presence about the night the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the night journey (*uisriya*). He said to him: "Do not bring the likes of 'Asim or Zirr." [He said:] Hudhayfah recited: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque﴾ with *min al-layl* (during the night), and so did 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) recite.

As for His saying, ﴿from the Sacred Mosque﴾, there is disagreement regarding it and its meaning. Some said: it means from the Sacred Precinct (*al-Haram*), and said: the entire Haram is a mosque. We have explained this in more than one place in this book of ours. He also said: It has been related to us that when the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the night journey to the Farthest Mosque, he was sleeping in the house of Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salamah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib told me, from Abu Salih Ibn Badhdham, from Umm Hani' bint Abi Talib, regarding the night journey of the Prophet ﷺ, that she used to say: The Messenger of God ﷺ was not taken on the night journey except while he was in my house, sleeping with me that night. He prayed the late evening prayer (*al-'isha' al-akhira*), then slept, and we slept. When it was close to dawn, the Messenger of God ﷺ woke us. When he had prayed the dawn prayer and we had prayed with him, he said: "O Umm Hani', I prayed with you the late evening prayer in this valley as you saw. Then I came to Bayt al-Maqdis and prayed there. Then I prayed the morning prayer with you now, as you see."

Others said: Rather, he was taken on the night journey from the mosque, and in it he was at the time he was taken.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Abi 'Adi told us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, a man of his people, who said: The Prophet of God ﷺ said: "While I was by the House (*al-bayt*), between sleep and wakefulness, I heard someone say, one of three, and a basin of gold was brought to me containing Zamzam water. My chest was opened up to here and there." Qatadah said: I asked: What does he mean by it? He said: To the bottom of his belly. He said: "My heart was taken out and washed with Zamzam water, then returned to its place, then it was filled with faith and wisdom. Then I was brought a white animal," and in another report: "a white animal called al-Buraq, above the donkey and below the mule, whose step reaches as far as its gaze, and I was carried upon it. Then we set off until we came to Bayt al-Maqdis, and I prayed in it leading the prophets and messengers. Then I was taken up to the lowest heaven..." and he mentioned the hadith.

* Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik, meaning Ibn Sa'sa'ah, a man of his people, from the Prophet ﷺ, similar to it.

* Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi told us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, from Malik ibn Sa'sa'ah, a man of his people, who said: The Prophet of God ﷺ said, then he mentioned something similar.

* Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salamah told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman told me, from al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "While I was sleeping in al-Hijr, Gabriel came to me and nudged me with his foot. I sat up but saw nothing, so I returned to my bed. He came to me a second time and nudged me with his foot, and I sat up but saw nothing, so I returned to my bed. He came to me a third time and nudged me with his foot, and I sat up, and he took hold of my arm, and I stood up with him. He brought me out to the door of the mosque, and there was a white animal between the donkey and the mule, with two wings on its thighs with which it propelled its legs, placing its hoof at the limit of its gaze. He carried me upon it, then he set out with me, neither outpacing me nor being outpaced by me."

* al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman told us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Shurayk ibn Abi Namir [Footnote: al-Nawawi said in his commentary on Sahih Muslim (Egyptian edition 2:210) that al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, cited this narration of Shurayk from Anas in his Sahih and presented the hadith in full. The Hafiz 'Abd al-Haqq, may God have mercy on him, said in his book *al-Jam' bayn al-Sahihayn*, after mentioning this narration: This hadith with this wording is from the narration of Shurayk ibn Abi Namir from Anas, and he added an unknown addition and used expressions that are not known. Many reliable memorizers and famous imams narrated the hadith of the night journey, such as Ibn Shihab, Thabit al-Bunani, and Qatadah (meaning from Anas), yet none of them brought what Shurayk brought, and Shurayk is not a memorizer according to the people of hadith. See also what al-Shihab al-Khafaji said in *Nasim al-Riyad fi Sharh Shifa' al-Qadi 'Iyad* (2:243–244), in his critique of Shurayk ibn Abi Namir's narration, both its chain and its text.] He said: I heard Anas narrate to us about the night of the journey of the Messenger of God ﷺ from the mosque of the Ka'bah, that three men came to him before he was revealed to, while he was sleeping in the Sacred Mosque. The first of them said: "Which of them is he?" The middle one said: "He is the best of them." One of them said: "Take the best of them." So that was that night, and he did not see them until they came another night, as his heart perceived, while the Prophet's eyes sleep but his heart does not sleep. Likewise the prophets' eyes sleep but their hearts do not sleep. They did not speak to him until they carried him and placed him by the well of Zamzam. Gabriel, peace be upon him, took charge of him, split him open from the throat to the lower chest, until he had emptied his chest and abdomen, washed him with Zamzam water until his abdomen was cleansed. Then a basin of gold was brought to him containing a bowl filled with faith and wisdom, and he filled with it his abdomen, his chest, and his *ladhadhayn* [Footnote: In al-Bukhari (Chapter of Monotheism): "he filled with it his chest (*sudur*) and his *ladhadhayn*," meaning the veins of his throat.] Then he closed it, and mounted al-Buraq, and went until he was taken to Bayt al-Maqdis, where he prayed leading the prophets and messengers. Then he was taken up to the lowest heaven, and he struck one of its gates. The people of the heaven called out: "Who is this?" He said: "This is Gabriel." It was said: "Who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad." It was said: "Has he indeed been sent to him?" [Footnote: In al-Bukhari (Halabi edition 9:183): "and he has been sent." We have left the narration of the author as it is, due to differences in the copies of al-Bukhari in the wording of some words.] He said: "Yes." They said: "Welcome to him, and well come." The people of the heaven rejoiced at him. The people of the heaven do not know what God intends for the people of the earth until He informs them. He found Adam in the lowest heaven, and Gabriel said to him: "This is your father, so greet him." He greeted him and he returned the greeting, and said: "Welcome to you and well come, O my son. How excellent a son you are." Then he went with him to the second heaven, and Gabriel asked for opening at one of its gates. It was said: "Who is this?" He said: "Gabriel." It was said: "And who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad." It was said: "Has he indeed been sent to him?" He said: "Yes, he has indeed been sent to him." It was said: "Welcome to him and well come," and it was opened for them. When he ascended into it, he saw two rivers flowing, and he said: "What are these two rivers, O Gabriel?" He said: "This is the Nile and the Euphrates, their source." [Footnote: So it is also in al-Bukhari.] Then he was taken up to the third heaven, and Gabriel asked for opening at one of its gates. It was said: "Who is this?" He said: "Gabriel." It was said: "And who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad." It was said: "Has he indeed been sent to him?" He said: "Yes, he has indeed been sent to him." It was said: "Welcome to him and well come," and it was opened for him. Then he saw a river upon which were domes and palaces of pearl, emerald, and ruby, and other things that no one knows but God. He went to smell its soil, and it was musk, pungent. He said: "O Gabriel, what is this river?" He said: "This is al-Kawthar, which your Lord has kept for you in the Hereafter." Then he was taken up to the fourth, and they said to him the like of that. Then he was taken up to the fifth, and they said to him the like of that. Then he was taken up to the sixth, and they said to him the like of that. Then he was taken up to the seventh, and they said to him the like of that. In every heaven there were prophets, whom Anas named. I remember from them Idris in the second, Harun in the fourth, another in the fifth whose name I did not memorize, Ibrahim in the sixth, and Musa in the seventh, by the excellence of his being spoken to by God. Musa said: "My Lord, I did not think that anyone would be raised above me." Then he ascended with him beyond that, to a place that no one knows but God, until he came to the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary (*sidrat al-muntaha*), and he drew near the gate of the Mighty Compeller, Lord of Majesty. He drew near and came close, ﴿at a distance of two bow-lengths or nearer﴾ (53:9), and He revealed to His servant what He willed. God revealed among what He revealed fifty prayers upon his community each day and night. Then he descended until he reached Musa, who detained him, and said: "O Muhammad, what did your Lord charge you with?" He said: "He charged me with fifty prayers upon my community each day and night." He said: "Your community cannot bear that. Return, and let Him lighten it for you and for them." So he turned to Gabriel, as if seeking his counsel in that, and he gestured to him, "Yes." So Gabriel brought him back until he came to the Mighty and Majestic One, while he was in his place, and he said: "My Lord, lighten it for us, for my community cannot bear this." So He removed ten prayers from him. Then he returned to Musa, peace be upon him, who detained him, and Musa kept sending him back to his Lord until it became five prayers. Then he detained him at the five, and said: "O Muhammad, by God, I tried the Children of Israel with less than these five, and they grew weak and abandoned it. Your community is weaker in bodies, hearts, sight, and hearing. Return, and let your Lord lighten it for you." Each time he turned to Gabriel to seek his counsel, and Gabriel did not dislike that. He raised him at the five, and said: "My Lord, my community is weak in their bodies, hearts, hearing, and sight, so lighten it for us." The Mighty One, majestic in His majesty, said: "O Muhammad." He said: "At Your service and Your pleasure." He said: "Indeed, the word is not changed before Me, as I have decreed for you in the Mother of the Book, and for you there is a reward of ten times for every good deed, and they are fifty in the Mother of the Book, and they are five upon you." So he returned to Musa, who said: "What did you do?" He said: "He lightened it for me, giving us ten times the reward for every good deed." He said: "By God, I tried the Children of Israel with less than this, and they abandoned it. Return, and let Him lighten it for you further." He said: "O Musa, by God, I have become too shy before my Lord about what I keep returning to." He said: "Descend in the name of God." Then he awoke, and he was in the Sacred Mosque.

The most correct of these opinions, in my view, is that it should be said: God, Mighty and Majestic, informed that He took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque, and the Sacred Mosque is that which people recognize among themselves when they mention it. His saying, ﴿to the Farthest Mosque﴾, means: the Mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis. It was called "the Farthest" because it is the most distant of the mosques visited, and in visiting it one seeks virtue after the Sacred Mosque. Thus the meaning of the speech is the declaration of God's transcendence and His exoneration from what the polytheists attribute to Him of association, rivals, and a consort, and from whatever is beneath His majesty, exalted is He, who journeyed with His servant by night from His Sacred House to His Farthest House.

Then the people of knowledge differed regarding the manner of God's taking His Prophet ﷺ, blessed and exalted is He, from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque. Some said: God took him by night with his body, on al-Buraq, from His Sacred House to His Farthest House until he reached it, and showed him what He willed of the wonders of His command, His signs, and the greatness of His dominion. The prophets were gathered for him there, and he led them in prayer there. He was then raised to the heaven, until he was taken above the seven heavens, and God revealed to him there what He willed to reveal. Then he returned to the Sacred Mosque that same night and prayed the dawn prayer with them.

Mention of those who said that, and mention of some of the reports transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ confirming it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 1 (part 2 of 5):

⁕ Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was taken on the Night Journey (isra') upon al-Buraq, which was the mount of Ibrahim (Abraham) with which he used to visit the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram), placing its hoof at the limit of its gaze. He said: Then he passed by a caravan of the caravans of Quraysh in one of those valleys, and the caravan shied, and in it was a camel carrying two saddlebags, one black and one blue, until he reached Iliya'. He was brought two vessels: a vessel of wine and a vessel of milk. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the vessel of milk, and Jibril said to him: "You have been guided to the natural disposition (fitrah). Had you taken the vessel of wine, your nation would have gone astray." Ibn Shihab said: Ibn al-Musayyab informed me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) met there Ibrahim, Musa and Isa, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) described them, saying: "As for Musa, he is a man of hair, curly-haired, as if he were one of the men of Shanu'a. As for Isa, he is a red-complexioned man, as if he had just come out of a bathhouse (dimas). The one he most resembles among those I have seen is Urwa ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi. As for Ibrahim, I am the one most like his offspring in appearance." When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned, he told the Quraysh that he had been taken on the Night Journey. Abd Allah said: Many people then apostatized after they had embraced Islam. Abu Salama said: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was approached and it was said to him: "Do you have any word about your companion? He claims that he was taken to Bayt al-Maqdis and returned in a single night." Abu Bakr said: "Did he say that?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then I bear witness that if he said that, he has spoken the truth." They said: "Do you testify that he went to al-Sham in a single night?" He said: "Indeed, I believe him in what is even more distant than that; I believe him concerning the news of the heaven." Abu Salama said: I heard Jabir ibn Abd Allah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When Quraysh denied me, I stood up, and Allah displayed Bayt al-Maqdis before me, and I began to inform them about its signs while I was looking at it."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ya'qub ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri narrated to me, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hashim ibn Utba ibn Abi Waqqas, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: When Jibril (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with al-Buraq, it seemed to strike its tail, and Jibril said to it: "Calm down, O Buraq, for by Allah, no one greater than him has ever mounted you." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set off, and suddenly he came upon an old woman bent aside from the road, i.e., on the side of the road.

Abu Ja'far said: It should be said "na'iyah," but the feminine marker has been dropped from it.

He said: "What is this, O Jibril?" He said: "Proceed, O Muhammad." So he proceeded for as long as Allah willed him to proceed. Then there was something calling him, inclining away from the road, saying: "Come here, O Muhammad." Jibril said: "Proceed, O Muhammad," so he proceeded for as long as Allah willed. He said: Then he met a group of creatures, and one of them said: "Peace be upon you, O First; peace be upon you, O Last; peace be upon you, O Gatherer." Jibril said to him: "Return the greeting, O Muhammad." So he returned the greeting. Then he met the second, who said to him the like of what the first had said, then the third likewise [[The text of this phrase is in al-Durr al-Manthur of al-Suyuti (4: 139), then the rest of the second, who said to him the like of that, then the third likewise; there may be a lacuna in the text.]] until he reached Bayt al-Maqdis, and water, milk and wine were presented to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the milk, and Jibril said to him: "You have chosen the natural disposition, O Muhammad. Had you drunk the water, you and your nation would have drowned; had you drunk the wine, you would have gone astray and your nation would have gone astray." Then Adam and those prophets below him were sent for, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) led them in prayer that night. Then Jibril said to him: "As for the old woman you saw on the side of the road, only as much of the world remains as remains of that old woman's lifespan. As for the one who wanted you to incline toward him, that was the enemy of Allah, Iblis, who wanted you to incline to him. As for those who greeted you with peace, they were Ibrahim, Musa and Isa."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 1 (part 3 of 5):

⁕ Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah al-Riyahi, from Abu Hurayrah or another, [Abu Ja'far] doubted, concerning the words of Allah, mighty and majestic, ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, that We might show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾. He said: Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and with him was Mika'il. Jibril said to Mika'il: "Bring me a basin of Zamzam water, so that I may purify his heart and expand his breast for him." He said: So he split open his belly, and washed it three times, and Mika'il brought him three basins of Zamzam water. Thus his breast was expanded, and whatever rancor was in it was removed, and it was filled with forbearance, knowledge, faith, certainty and submission. And he sealed between his shoulders with the Seal of Prophethood. Then he brought him a steed, and he was carried upon it, each step of it reaching as far as his gaze could see. He said: So he traveled, and Jibril, peace be upon him, traveled with him. He passed by a people who were sowing in one day and reaping on another day; whenever they reaped, it returned as it was. The Prophet ﷺ said: "O Jibril, what is this?" He said: "These are the strugglers in the way of Allah; a good deed is multiplied for them seven hundredfold, and whatever they spend, He replaces it, and He is the best of providers." Then he passed by a people whose heads were being crushed with stones; whenever they were crushed, they returned as they were, and nothing of this relented for them. He said: "What are these, O Jibril?" He said: "These are those whose heads are heavy against the obligatory prayer." Then he passed by a people, on their front parts were rags and on their back parts were rags, and they roamed as cattle and sheep roam, and they ate of the thorny plant (al-dari') and the zaqqum and the hot stones of Hell and its rocks. He said: "What are these, O Jibril?" He said: "These are those who do not pay the charity of their wealth. And Allah did not wrong them at all, and Allah is not unjust to the servants." Then he passed by a people before whom was meat cooked in pots, and other meat raw, foul and filthy; they began to eat from the raw and leave the cooked, good meat. He said: "What are these, O Jibril?" He said: "This is a man from your Ummah who has a lawful, good wife, yet goes to a wicked woman and spends the night with her until morning; and a woman rises from her husband, lawful and good, and goes to a wicked man and spends the night with him until morning." He said: Then he passed by a piece of wood on the road; no garment passed by it without being torn, and nothing without being ripped. He said: "What is this, O Jibril?" He said: "This is the likeness of people from your Ummah who sit on the road and cut it off." Then he recited ﴿Do not sit on every path, threatening and turning away﴾, the verse. Then he passed by a man who had gathered a great bundle of firewood which he could not carry, yet he kept adding to it. He said: "What is this, O Jibril?" He said: "This is a man from your Ummah who has the trusts of people and cannot discharge them, yet he keeps adding to them and wants to carry them, but he cannot." Then he passed by people whose tongues and lips were being cut with iron scissors; whenever they were cut, they returned as they were, and nothing of this relented for them. He said: "What are these, O Jibril?" He said: "These are the preachers of your Ummah, the preachers of sedition, who say what they do not do." Then he passed by a small hole from which a great bull was emerging; the bull wanted to return to where it had come out, but could not. He said: "What is this, O Jibril?" He said: "This is a man who speaks a great word, then regrets it, and cannot take it back." Then he passed by a valley, and found a good, cool fragrance in it, and in it the scent of musk, and he heard a sound. He said: "O Jibril, what is this good, cool wind and this fragrance like musk, and what is this sound?" He said: "This is the sound of Paradise, saying: 'O Lord, give me what You promised me, for my chambers, my brocade, my silk, my sundus, my 'abqari, my pearls and coral, my silver and gold, my cups, my dishes and my ewers, my fruits, my date palms and my pomegranates, my milk and my wine have multiplied. So give me what You promised me.'" He said: "For you is every Muslim man and woman, every believing man and woman, and whoever believes in Me and My messengers, does righteous deeds, does not associate anything with Me, and does not take rivals besides Me; and whoever fears Me is secure, whoever asks Me I will give him, whoever lends to Me I will repay him, whoever relies upon Me I will suffice him. Indeed I am Allah; there is no god but I; I do not break My promise. The believers have succeeded, and blessed is Allah, the best of creators." She said: "I am content." Then he passed by a valley and heard a terrible sound and found a foul smell. He said: "What is this wind, O Jibril, and what is this sound?" He said: "This is the sound of Hell, saying: 'O Lord, give me what You promised me, for my chains and my shackles, my blaze and my inferno, my dari' and my ghassaq, my torment and my punishment have multiplied, my depth has grown far and my heat has become intense. So give me what You promised me.'" He said: "For you is every polytheist man and woman, every disbeliever man and woman, every wicked person, and every tyrant who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning." She said: "I am content." He said: Then he traveled until he came to Bayt al-Maqdis, and he dismounted, tied his steed to a rock, then entered and prayed with the angels. When the prayer was finished, they said: "O Jibril, who is this with you?" He said: "Muhammad." They said: "Has he been sent to him?" He said: "Yes." They said: "May Allah welcome him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother and how excellent a successor, and how excellent the coming that has come!" He said: Then he met the spirits of the prophets, and they praised their Lord. Ibrahim said: "Praise be to Allah who took me as a close friend, gave me a great kingdom, made me a nation, devout to Allah, who is followed, rescued me from the Fire and made it cool and safe for me." Then Musa praised his Lord and said: "Praise be to Allah who spoke to me directly, made the destruction of the family of Pharaoh and the deliverance of the Children of Israel at my hands, and made among my people a community that guides by truth and by it does justice." Then Dawud, peace be upon him, praised his Lord and said: "Praise be to Allah who gave me a great kingdom, taught me the Zabur, softened iron for me, subjected the mountains to glorify with me and the birds, gave me wisdom and decisive speech." Then Sulayman praised his Lord and said: "Praise be to Allah who subjected the winds to me, subjected the devils to me, who work for me whatever I wish: sanctuaries, statues, basins like reservoirs, and mighty cauldrons; taught me the speech of birds, gave me of everything abundance, subjected to me the armies of the devils, humans and birds, favored me over many of His believing servants, and gave me a kingdom such as none after me should have, and made my kingdom a good kingdom with no reckoning against me." Then Isa, peace be upon him, praised his Lord and said: "Praise be to Allah who made me His word and made my likeness like that of Adam, whom He created from dust, then said to him: 'Be,' and he was. He taught me the Book, wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel, and made me shape from clay the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by Allah's permission; and made me heal the blind and the leper and raise the dead by Allah's permission, and raised me up and purified me, and protected me and my mother from the accursed Satan, so Satan had no way over us." He said: Then Muhammad ﷺ praised his Lord and said: "Every one of you has praised his Lord, and I praise my Lord." He said: "Praise be to Allah who sent me as a mercy to the worlds, and as a comprehensive message to mankind, a bringer of good tidings and a warner; and sent down upon me the Furqan, in which is the clarification of everything; and made my Ummah the best Ummah brought forth for mankind; and made my Ummah a middle nation; and made my Ummah the first and the last; and expanded my breast, removed my burden, raised my remembrance, and made me the opener and the sealer." Ibrahim said: "With this, Muhammad has excelled you." — Abu Ja'far said, and he is al-Razi: "The Seal of Prophethood, and the opener through intercession on the Day of Resurrection." Then three vessels with covered mouths were brought to him. He took one of them, which contained water, and it was said: "Drink," and he drank a little from it. Then another vessel containing milk was given to him, and it was said to him: "Drink," and he drank until he was satisfied. Then another vessel containing wine was given to him, and it was said to him: "Drink." He said: "I do not want it, I am satisfied." Jibril, peace be upon him, said to him: "As for it, it will be forbidden to your Ummah; had you drunk from it, only a few of your Ummah would have followed you." Then he ascended with him to the lowest heaven. Jibril asked for entry, and it was said: "Who is this?" He said: "Jibril." It was said: "Who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad." They said: "Has he been sent to him?" He said: "Yes." They said: "May Allah welcome him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother and how excellent a successor, and how excellent the coming that has come!" He entered, and there he found a man of perfect creation, whose creation lacked nothing as the creation of people lacks. On his right was a gate from which a good wind was coming out, and on his left was a gate from which a foul wind was coming out. When he looked at the gate on his right, he laughed and rejoiced, and when he looked at the gate on his left, he wept and grieved. I said: "O Jibril, who is this old man of perfect creation, lacking nothing in his creation, and what are these two gates?" He said: "This is your father Adam. The gate on his right is the gate of Paradise; when he looks at those of his descendants who enter it, he laughs and rejoices. The gate on his left is the gate of Hell; when he looks at those of his descendants who enter it, he weeps and grieves." Then Jibril ascended with him to the second heaven and asked for entry. It was said: "Who is this?" He said: "Jibril." It was said: "Who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah." They said: "Has he been sent to him?" He said: "Yes." They said: "May Allah welcome him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother and how excellent a successor, and how excellent the coming that has come!" He said: Then he found two youths, and he said: "O Jibril, who are these two youths?" He said: "This is Isa son of Maryam, and Yahya son of Zakariyya, the two cousins." He said: Then he ascended with him to the third heaven, asked for entry, and they said: "Who is this?" He said: "Jibril." They said: "Who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad." They said: "Has he been sent to him?" He said: "Yes." They said: "May Allah welcome him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother and how excellent a successor, and how excellent the coming that has come!" He said: He entered and found a man who surpassed all people in beauty, as the moon on the night of the full moon surpasses the other stars. He said: "Who is this, O Jibril, who surpasses people in beauty?" He said: "This is your brother Yusuf." Then he ascended with him to the fourth heaven, asked for entry, and it was said: "Who is this?" He said: Jibril. They said: "Who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad." They said: "Has he been sent to him?" He said: "Yes." They said: "May Allah welcome him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother and how excellent a successor, and how excellent the coming that has come!" He said: He entered and found a man. He said: "Who is this, O Jibril?" He said: "This is Idris, whom Allah raised to a lofty place." Then he ascended with him to the fifth heaven, Jibril asked for entry, and they said: "Who is this?" He said: "Jibril." They said: "Who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad." They said: "Has he been sent to him?" He said: "Yes." They said: "May Allah welcome him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother and how excellent a successor, and how excellent the coming that has come!" Then he entered and found a man sitting, and around him a people to whom he was narrating. He said: "Who is this, O Jibril, and who are those around him?" He said: "This is Harun, beloved among his people, and these are the Children of Israel." Then he ascended with him to the sixth heaven, Jibril asked for entry, and it was said to him: "Who is this?" He said: "Jibril." They said: "Who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad." They said: "Has he been sent to him?" He said: "Yes." They said: "May Allah welcome him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother and how excellent a successor, and how excellent the coming that has come!" Then he found a man sitting; he passed him by, and the man wept. He said: "O Jibril, who is this?" He said: "Musa." He said: "Why is he weeping?" He said: "The Children of Israel claim that I am the most honored of the sons of Adam before Allah, but this is a man of the sons of Adam who has been raised above me in the world, while I am in the Hereafter. Had he been alone, I would not mind, but every prophet has his own Ummah." Then he ascended with him to the seventh heaven, Jibril asked for entry, and it was said: "Who is this?" He said: "Jibril." They said: "Who is with you?" He said: "Muhammad." They said: "Has he been sent to him?" He said: "Yes." They said: "May Allah welcome him as a brother and a successor. How excellent a brother and how excellent a successor, and how excellent the coming that has come!" He said: He entered and found a grey-haired man sitting at the gate of Paradise on a throne, and with him were people sitting, with white faces like parchment, and people with some discoloration in their complexions. Those with discoloration in their complexions stood up, entered a river and bathed in it, and came out with the discoloration removed from them. Then they entered another river... [this is the Sidrat al-Muntaha: at it ends every one who has gone along your path from your Ummah]; and he also said concerning its leaf that it shades all creation, and the angels cover it like crows when they settle on a tree, out of love for Allah, mighty and majestic. The rest of the narration is like the narration of Ali.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-Ala narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Harun al-Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri; and al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar narrated to us, saying: Abu Harun al-Abdi informed us, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, and the wording is that of the narration of al-Hasan ibn Yahya, concerning the words of Allah, ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa﴾. He said: The Prophet ﷺ narrated to us about the night he was taken on the journey, and the Prophet of Allah said: "I was brought a beast resembling most the mule, having two quivering ears, and it was the Buraq, the one that the prophets rode before me. I mounted it, and it set off with me, placing its hoof at the limit of its sight. I heard a call from my right: 'O Muhammad, wait, I want to ask you,' but I went on and did not turn to it. Then I heard a call from my left: 'O Muhammad, wait, I want to ask you,' but I went on and did not turn to it. Then a woman met me on the road, adorned with every adornment of the world, raising her hand, saying: 'O Muhammad, wait, I want to ask you,' but I went on and did not turn to her. Then I came to Bayt al-Maqdis, or he said the al-Masjid al-Aqsa, and I dismounted from the beast and tied it to the ring that the prophets used to tie to. Then I entered the mosque and prayed in it. Jibril said to me: 'What did you see in your face?' I said: 'I heard a call from my right: O Muhammad, wait, I want to ask you, but I went on and did not turn to it.' He said: 'That was the caller of the Jews; had you stopped to it, your Ummah would have become Jews.'" He said: "Then I heard a call from my left: O Muhammad, wait, I want to ask you, but I went on and did not turn to it." He said: "That was the caller of the Christians; had you stopped to it, your Ummah would have become Christians." I said: "Then a woman met me, adorned with every adornment of the world, raising her hand, saying: 'Wait, I want to ask you,' but I went on and did not turn to her." He said: "That was the world, which adorned itself for you; had you stopped to her, your Ummah would have chosen the world over the Hereafter." Then two vessels were brought to me, one containing milk and the other containing wine, and it was said to me: "Drink whichever you wish." I took the milk and drank it. He said: "You have chosen the natural disposition (al-fitrah)," or he said: "You have taken the natural disposition."

Ma'mar said: Al-Zuhri also informed me, from Ibn al-Musayyab, that it was said to him: "Had you taken the wine, your Ummah would have gone astray."

Abu Harun said, in the report of Abu Sa'id: "Then the mi'raj (ascension ladder) was brought, in which the souls of the children of Adam ascend. It was the most beautiful thing I had ever seen. Have you not seen how the dying person fixes his gaze upon it? So I was ascended in it until we reached the gate of the lowest heaven. Jibril asked for it to be opened, and it was said: 'Who is this?' He said: 'Jibril.' It was said: 'And who is with you?' He said: 'Muhammad.' It was said: 'Has he been sent for?' He said: 'Yes.' So they opened and greeted me. There was an angel appointed to guard the heaven, called Isma'il, with seventy thousand angels, each of whom had a hundred thousand with him." Then he recited: ﴿And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾. "And there I saw a man in his form on the day Allah created him, nothing about him had changed. The souls of his offspring were presented to him. When the soul of a believer came, he said: 'A good soul and a good scent. Place his book in 'Illiyyin.' When the soul of an unbeliever came, he said: 'An evil soul and an evil scent. Place his book in Sijjin.'" I said: "O Jibril, who is this?" He said: "Your father Adam." He greeted me, welcomed me, prayed good for me, and said: "Welcome, the righteous Prophet and the righteous son." Then I looked and saw people with lips like the lips of camels, and someone was assigned to take hold of their lips, and then a rock of fire was placed in their mouths, coming out from their lower parts. I said: "O Jibril, who are these?" He said: "These are those who devour the wealth of orphans unjustly." Then I looked and saw people whose flesh was being cut from their bodies and put into their mouths, and it was said to them: "Eat as you used to eat." And they hated that which Allah had created for them. I said: "Who are these, O Jibril?" He said: "These are the backbiters and slanderers, who eat the flesh of people and violate their honour with abuse." Then I looked and saw people at a table on which was roasted meat, as good as the best meat I had ever seen, and around them were carcasses. They began to lean toward the carcasses and eat from them, leaving that meat. I said: "Who are these, O Jibril?" He said: "These are the adulterers, who went to what Allah had forbidden them and left what Allah had made lawful for them." Then I looked and saw people with bellies like houses, and they were on a path of the family of Pharaoh. When the family of Pharaoh passed by them, they were roused, and one of them would be thrown down by his belly, and the family of Pharaoh would trample them with their feet, and they are presented to the Fire morning and evening. I said: "Who are these, O Jibril?" He said: "These are the consumers of usury (riba). Its growth was in their bellies, so their likeness is that of one whom Satan has confused by touch." Then I looked and saw women hanging by their breasts, and women hanging upside down by their feet. I said: "Who are these, O Jibril?" He said: "These are the women who committed adultery and killed their children." He said: "Then we ascended to the second heaven, and there I found Yusuf, with a following of his community around him, and his face was like the moon on the night of the full moon. He greeted me and welcomed me. Then we went on to the third heaven, and there I found the two cousins, Yahya and 'Isa, resembling one another, their garments and hair alike. They greeted me and welcomed me. Then we went on to the fourth heaven, and there I found Idris, who greeted me and welcomed me, and Allah had said: ﴿And We raised him to a high station﴾. Then we went on to the fifth heaven, and there I found Harun, beloved among his people, with a large following of his community around him. The Prophet ﷺ described him: 'Long-bearded, his beard almost touching his navel.' He greeted me and welcomed me. Then we went on to the sixth heaven, and there I found Musa ibn 'Imran. The Prophet ﷺ described him, saying: 'Abundant of hair; if he had two garments on, his hair would come out of them.' Musa said: 'People think that I am the most honoured of creation before Allah, but this one is more honoured before Allah than me. Had he been alone, I would not have minded, but every prophet has with him those of his community who follow him.' Then we went on to the seventh heaven, and there I found Ibrahim, sitting with his back leaning against the Bayt al-Ma'mur (the frequented House). He greeted me and said: 'Welcome, the righteous Prophet and the righteous son.' It was said: 'This is your place and the place of your community.' Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, the people most worthy of Ibrahim are those who followed him, and this Prophet, and those who believe. And Allah is the Protector of the believers﴾. Then I entered the Bayt al-Ma'mur and prayed in it, and it is entered every day by seventy thousand angels who do not return until the Day of Resurrection. Then I looked and saw a tree, whose leaves, if one of them were to be placed upon, would cover this community. At its root was a flowing spring that divided into two branches. I said: 'What is this, O Jibril?' He said: 'As for this, it is the River of Mercy, and as for this, it is al-Kawthar, which Allah has given you.' I bathed in the River of Mercy, and my past and future sins were forgiven. Then I proceeded on al-Kawthar until I entered Paradise, and there was in it what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not occurred to the heart of any human. In it there were pomegranates like the skins of camels laden with saddles, and there were birds like the Bukht camels. Abu Bakr said: 'Those birds are surely pleasant.' He said: 'Those who eat them are more pleasant than them, O Abu Bakr, and I hope that you will eat of them.' I also saw a maiden there, and I asked her: 'To whom do you belong?' She said: 'To Zayd ibn Harithah.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave Zayd the good news of her. He said: 'Then Allah commanded me with His command, and enjoined upon me fifty prayers. I passed by Musa, and he said: "With what has your Lord commanded you?" I said: "He has enjoined upon me fifty prayers." He said: "Return to your Lord and ask Him for lightening, for your community will not be able to bear this." So I returned to my Lord and asked Him, and He removed ten from me. Then I returned to Musa, and I did not cease returning to my Lord whenever I passed by Musa, until He enjoined upon me five prayers. Musa said: "Return to your Lord and ask Him for lightening." I said: "I have returned to my Lord until I became shy," or he said: "I said: I will not return." It was said to me: "For these five prayers you have fifty prayers. A good deed is rewarded tenfold. Whoever intends a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is written for him; and whoever does it, ten are written for him. Whoever intends an evil deed but does not do it, nothing is written for him; and if he does it, one is written."'"

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said: Rawh ibn al-Qasim related to me, from Abu Harun 'Imarah ibn Juwayn al-'Abdi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. And Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, he said: And Abu Ja'far related to me, from Abu Harun, from Abu Sa'id, who said: I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "When I finished with what was in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), the mi'raj was brought, and I had never seen anything more beautiful than it. It is the thing toward which your dying person directs his eyes when he is present. My companion ascended me in it until he reached a gate among the gates called the Gate of the Guardians. Upon it was an angel called Isma'il, under whose hands were twelve thousand angels, and under the hand of each of them were twelve thousand angels." When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ related this hadith, he recited: ﴿None knows the hosts of your Lord except Him﴾. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ma'mar from Abu Harun, except that in his report he said: "Then he took me into Paradise, and I saw in it a maiden, and I asked her: 'To whom do you belong?' She had impressed me when I saw her. She said: 'To Zayd ibn Harithah.' So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave Zayd ibn Harithah the good news of her." Here ends the report of Ibn Humayd from Salamah.

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn al-Musayyib, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ described for his companions, on the night he was taken on the journey, Ibrahim, Musa and 'Isa. He said: "As for Ibrahim, I did not see a man more like your companion than him. As for Musa, he was a dark-skinned man, tall, with curly hair and an aquiline nose, as if he were one of the men of Shanu'ah. As for 'Isa, he was a reddish man, between short and tall, with straight hair, abundant freckles on his face, as if he had come out of a bathhouse, and as if his head were dripping water though there was no water on it. The one he most resembled among those I have seen was 'Urwah ibn Mas'ud."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, a similar report, but he did not say "from Abu Hurayrah."

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Prophet ﷺ was brought the Buraq (a steed of light) on the night he was taken on the journey, saddled and bridled, so that he might ride it, but it was difficult for him. Jibril said to it: "What has moved you to this? By Allah, no one has ever ridden you who was more honoured by Allah than him." He said: then it broke into a sweat.

⁕ Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed﴾. The Prophet of Allah was taken by night from Makkah to Bayt al-Maqdis, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ prayed in it, and Allah showed him some of His signs and gave him His command in whatever He willed on the night he was taken. Then he woke in Makkah in the morning. It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "I was mounted upon a beast called the Buraq, above the donkey and below the mule, placing its hoof at the limit of its sight." He informed the people of Makkah of this, and the polytheists denied it and rejected it and said: "O Muhammad, you tell us that you went to Bayt al-Maqdis and came back during your night, then you were with us in Makkah in the morning. What you bring us is something you have been bringing before this day, along with this." Abu Bakr confirmed him, and for that reason Abu Bakr was named al-Siddiq (the Truthful).

⁕ Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad related to us, he said: Sulayman al-Shaybani related to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Shaddad, who said: When the night came that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was taken on the journey, he was brought a beast called the Buraq, below the mule and above the donkey, placing its hoof at the limit of its nail. When he came to Bayt al-Maqdis, he was brought two vessels: one of milk and one of wine, and he drank the milk. Jibril said to him: "You have been guided, and your community has been guided."

And others said: The Prophet ﷺ was taken to al-Masjid al-Aqsa with his soul and his body, peace be upon him, except that he did not enter Bayt al-Maqdis, did not pray in it, and did not dismount from the Buraq until he returned to Makkah.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan related to us, he said: Sufyan related to me, from 'Asim ibn Bahdalah, from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, from Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa﴾: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not pray in it, for had he prayed in it, prayer in it would have been prescribed for you, just as prayer at the Ka'bah has been prescribed for you."

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, he said: I heard Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash, and a man was narrating in his presence a hadith about the night the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the journey. He said to him: "Do not bring the likes of 'Asim or Zirr." He said: Hudhayfah said to Zirr ibn Hubaysh; and Zirr was a noble man among the nobles of the Arabs. He said: Hudhayfah recited: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, that We might show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾. And 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) also recited it thus. He said: "This is like what they say: that he entered the mosque, prayed in it, then entered and tied up his mount." He said: I said: "By Allah, he did enter it." He said: "Who are you? For I recognise your face but do not know your name." I said: "Zirr ibn Hubaysh." He said: "What has this made you do?" I said: "From the Qur'an." He said: "Whoever holds to the Qur'an prospers." Then I said: ﴿Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed﴾. He looked at me and said: "O bald one, do you see that he entered it?" I said: "No, by Allah." Hudhayfah said: "Indeed, by Allah, besides whom there is no god, he did not enter it. Had he entered it, prayer in it would have been obligatory upon you. No, by Allah, he did not dismount from the Buraq until he saw Paradise and Hell, and what Allah has prepared in the Hereafter, all of it." And he said: "Do you know what the Buraq is?" I said: "A beast below the mule and above the donkey, whose stride is as far as the eye can see."

And others said: Rather, he was taken by his spirit and not by his body.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said: Ya'qub ibn 'Utbah ibn al-Mughirah ibn al-Akhnas related to me, that Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, whenever he was asked about the night journey of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, would say: "It was a true vision from Allah."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, from Muhammad, he said: some of the family of Abu Bakr related to me, that 'A'ishah used to say: "The body of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was not missing, but Allah took him on the journey by his spirit."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Salamah related to us, he said: Ibn Ishaq said: Al-Hasan did not deny this statement of hers, and that this verse was revealed: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾. And from Allah's report about Ibrahim, when he said to his son: ﴿O my son, indeed I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you, so see what you think﴾. Then he proceeded on that. So I understood that revelation comes to the prophets from Allah both while awake and while asleep. And the Messenger ﷺ used to say: "My eyes sleep, but my heart is awake." Allah knows best which of these it was that came to him and in which he witnessed what he witnessed of the command of Allah, in whatever state he was, asleep or awake. All of it is truth and sincerity.

The correct position on this matter, in our view, is to say: God carried His servant Muhammad (ﷺ) by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, as God informed His servants, and as the reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) have widely attested, that God mounted him on the Buraq when it came to him, and that he prayed there with those of the prophets and messengers who prayed, and that He showed him what He showed him of the signs. There is no sense in the saying of one who says that he was carried by night in spirit without body, for if that were so, there would be nothing in it requiring that it be a proof of his prophethood, nor an argument for his messengership, nor would those who denied the reality of it have been from among the polytheists, who used to repel his truthfulness with it, since it would not have been considered strange by them, nor by anyone of sound nature among the children of Adam, that one of them should see in a dream what is a year's journey away, so how much more so what is a month's journey or less? Moreover, God only informed in His Book that He carried His servant by night, and He did not tell us that He carried the spirit of His servant, and it is not permissible for anyone to go beyond what God said to something else. If someone thinks that this is permissible, since the Arabs do this in their speech, as their poet said:

I thought the bleating of my she-camel was the cry of a young goat, and it was not, by the Lord, other than you, a young goat.[[The verse was previously cited in (4: 92) of this tafsir, and al-Farra' cited it (in Ma'ani al-Quran, p. 179) but did not clarify its point of evidence as the author clarifies it here, which is that the Arabs may omit the mudaf (the governed noun) and place the mudaf ilayh (the genitive noun) in its position, as in the verse, since he means: I thought the bleating of my she-camel was the sound of a young goat.]]

That is, "I thought the bleating of my she-camel was the sound of a young goat," so he omitted "the sound" and sufficed with "young goat." The Arabs do this in matters whose meaning is understood from the speech and intended by the speaker. But in matters for which there is no indication except by their manifest sense, and the intention of the speaker can only be known through their clarification, they do not omit that. There is no indication that God's intent by His saying ﴿He carried His servant by night﴾ is that He carried the spirit of His servant; rather, the clear proofs and the consecutive reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) indicate that God carried him by night on a beast called the Buraq. Had the night journey been in spirit, the spirit would not have been carried on the Buraq, since beasts carry only bodies. Unless someone says: the meaning of our saying "he was carried by night in spirit" is: he saw in a dream that he was carried by night in body on the Buraq. Then this would contradict the meaning of the reports transmitted from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that Jibril carried him on the Buraq, because if it was a dream according to the one who says this, and the spirit is not among what rides beasts, and the body of the Prophet (ﷺ) was not carried on the Buraq, then according to his saying the Prophet (ﷺ) was not carried on the Buraq, neither his body nor any part of him, and the matter becomes for him like some dreams of sleepers. That is a rejection of the apparent sense of the revelation and of what the reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) consecutively affirm, and what was reported from the leading Companions and Successors.

* *

His saying ﴿the one whose surroundings We blessed﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: He who made blessing around it for its inhabitants in their livelihoods, their sustenance, their crops and their plantings.

* *

His saying ﴿that We might show him of Our signs﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: that We might show Our servant Muhammad of Our signs, that is, of Our lessons, proofs and arguments, and that is what I have mentioned in the reports I related earlier, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was shown on his way to Bayt al-Maqdis and after arriving there, of wondrous lessons and admonitions.

As follows:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿that We might show him of Our signs﴾: what God showed him of signs and lessons on the way to Bayt al-Maqdis.

* *

His saying ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed, the One who carried His servant by night is the All-Hearing of what these polytheists of Mecca say about the journey of Muhammad (ﷺ) from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis, and of other than that from their saying and the saying of others, the All-Seeing of the deeds they do; nothing of that is hidden from Him, and not the knowledge of any part of it escapes Him; rather, He encompasses all of it in knowledge and counts it in number, and He is in wait for them, so that He may recompense all of them for what they deserve.

Some of the Basran grammarians used to say: the "inna" in His saying ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ is kasra-vowelled because the meaning of the speech is: "Say, O Muhammad: Glory be to the One who carried His servant by night," and "Say: Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing."

The interpretation of His words, exalted be He: ﴿And We gave Moses the Book and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel: "Do not take anyone other than Me as a guardian."﴾

He, exalted be His remembrance, says: Glory be to the One who took His servant by night and gave Moses the Book. He returned the speech to ﴿And We gave﴾, though He had begun with "took by night," as we have mentioned before, following the practice of the Arabs in similar cases, where the report begins with a report about an absent party, then returns to direct address and the like. By "the Book that was given to Moses" He means the Torah. ﴿And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾: that is, We made the Book, which is the Torah, a clarification of the truth and a proof for them of the path of rightness regarding what He made obligatory upon them, what He commanded them to do, and what He forbade them from.

* *

As for His words ﴿that you not take anyone other than Me as a wakil (guardian/trustee)﴾:

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read ﴿a lā tattakhidhū﴾ with the letter ta', meaning: "We gave Moses the Book, that you, O Children of Israel, not take anyone other than Me as a wakil." Some reciters of Basra read ﴿a lā yattakhidhū﴾ with the letter ya', as a report about the Children of Israel, meaning: "We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, that the Children of Israel not take anyone other than Me as a wakil." Both readings are sound in meaning, agreeing rather than conflicting. Whichever of them a reciter reads is correct. However, I prefer the reading with ta', because it is better known in recitation and more widely transmitted among them than the reading with ya'. The meaning of the speech is: "We gave Moses the Book and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, that you not take for yourselves any protector besides Me." We have already explained the meaning of wakil above. Mujahid used to say that its meaning in this place is: a partner.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿that you not take anyone other than Me as a wakil﴾, he said: "a partner."

It seems that Mujahid regarded whoever sets up something other than God in His place as having made it a partner to Him and a wakil for the one he has set in God's place.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said regarding the interpretation of this verse.

Those who said so:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And We gave Moses the Book and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾: God made it a guidance for them, bringing them out of darkness into light, and made it a mercy for them.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿The offspring of those whom We carried with Noah. Indeed, he was a grateful servant.﴾

His saying, exalted be His mention: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, and We gave Moses the Book and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel: ﴿the offspring of those whom We carried with Noah﴾. By "the offspring" He means all of the peoples of the various nations whom He, mighty is His praise, has argued against with this Qur'an, Arabs and non-Arabs, the Children of Israel and others. This is because everyone on the earth from the children of Adam is of the offspring of those whom God carried with Noah in the Ark.

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿the offspring of those whom We carried with Noah﴾: All people are the offspring of those whom God saved in that Ark. It has been related to us that none were saved in it on that day except Noah, his three sons, his wife, and three women; they were Sam, Ham, and Japheth. As for Sam, he is the father of the Arabs; as for Ham, he is the father of the Habash [[al-Habash: they are not Hamites; rather, they are a branch and a language of the Semites. The descendants of Ham are the Zanj.]]; and as for Japheth, he is the father of the Romans.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿the offspring of those whom We carried with Noah﴾, he said: His sons were three, and their wives, and Noah and his wife.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying, both: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Mujahid said: His sons and their wives and Noah, and his wife was not included.

We have explained this in another place earlier, in a manner sufficient to avoid repeating it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾:

By His saying, exalted be His mention, "Indeed he" – i.e., Noah – and the pronoun referring to the mention of Noah – "was a grateful servant" to God for His blessings.

The interpreters have differed regarding the reason for which God named him "grateful." Some of them said: God named him thus because he would praise God over his food when he ate it.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Taymi, from Abu 'Uthman, from Salman, who said: When Noah wore a garment or ate food, he would praise God, and so he was named "a grateful servant."

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Sa'id ibn Mas'ud, with the like of it.

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from 'Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Sa'id ibn Mas'ud, who said: Noah never wore anything new, nor ever ate food, without praising God; therefore God said ﴿a grateful servant﴾.

* Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri told me, saying: Ayyub told me, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman, who said: Noah was named "a grateful servant" only because when he wore a garment he praised God, and when he ate food he praised God.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿the offspring of those whom We carried with Noah﴾ – from the Children of Israel and others – ﴿Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾, he said: He never renewed a garment without praising God, and never wore out a garment without praising God, and whenever he drank a sip he praised God, saying: "Praise be to God who gave it to me with desire, pleasure and health." There is nothing in its interpretation that when he drank a sip he said this, but it has reached me thus.

* al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Fudalah narrated to us, from al-Nadr ibn Shafi, from 'Imran ibn Sulaym, who said: Noah was named "a grateful servant" only because when he ate food he said: "Praise be to God who fed me; had He willed, He could have made me hungry." And when he drank he said: "Praise be to God who gave me to drink; had He willed, He could have made me thirsty." And when he wore a garment he said: "Praise be to God who clothed me; had He willed, He could have left me naked." And when he put on a sandal he said: "Praise be to God who shod me; had He willed, He could have left me barefoot." And when he relieved a need he said: "Praise be to God who expelled its harm from me; had He willed, He could have held it back."

And others said regarding this what follows:

* Yunus narrated to me with it, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Jabbar ibn 'Umar told me that Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to him, saying: God named Noah "a grateful servant" only because when he came out of the privy he said: "Praise be to God who made this pure for you and expelled its harm from me, and kept its benefit."

And others said regarding this what follows:

* Bishr narrated to us with it, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: God said to Noah ﴿Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾. It has been related to us that he never wore a new garment without praising God, and he used to order that when a man wore a new garment he should say: "Praise be to God who clothed me with what I beautify myself with and cover my nakedness with."

* Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah ﴿Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾, he said: When he wore a garment he said: "Praise be to God," and when it wore out he said: "Praise be to God."

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture that you would surely cause corruption in the land twice, and you would surely become haughty with great haughtiness. (4) So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they went through the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled.﴾ (5)

We have already explained earlier that the meaning of *qada'* (decree) is the completion of a matter, and it is then used for anything that has been completed. So the interpretation of the speech in this place is: "Your Lord completed [His command] concerning the Children of Israel in what He sent down in His Book to Moses, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him, by informing them and telling them ﴿that you would surely cause corruption in the land twice﴾," meaning: "You, O assembly of the Children of Israel, will surely disobey God and oppose His command in His lands twice." ﴿And you will surely become haughty with great haughtiness﴾ means: "And you will surely be arrogant towards God by your audacity against Him, with severe arrogance."

Concerning this, the people of *ta'wil* (interpretation) said in agreement with what we have said:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel﴾: "He said: We informed them."

⁕ 'Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel﴾: "He said: We informed them."

Others said: The meaning of that is: "We decreed against the Children of Israel in the Mother of the Book and in His foreknowledge."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel﴾: "He said: It is a decree that has passed over them."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel﴾: "A decree which He decreed upon the people, as you hear."

Others said: The meaning of that is: "He informed us."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture﴾: "He said: He informed the Children of Israel."

All these sayings return in their meanings to what I have said concerning the meaning of His words ﴿And We decreed﴾. Although the interpretation we have chosen concerning it is closer to the truth, because the readers (qurra') agree on the recitation of His words ﴿لَتُفْسِدُنَّ﴾ (*latufsidunna*, with the *ta'*) rather than the *ya'* (*layufsidunna*). Had the meaning of the speech been "We decreed against them in the Book," the recitation with the *ya'* would have been more preferable than with the *ta'*. But its meaning, since it was "We informed them and told them, and said to them," the *ta'* was closer and more appropriate for direct address.

The corruption of the Children of Israel in the land the first time was as follows:

⁕ Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned from Abu Salih, and from Abu Malik, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murra, from 'Abd Allah, that God covenanted with the Children of Israel in the Torah: ﴿You will surely cause corruption in the land twice﴾. The first of the two corruptions was the killing of Zakariyya, so God sent against them the king of the Nabataeans, who was called Sahabin [[In the History of al-Tabari (vol. 2, part 1, p. 657, Europe edition): "Sayhanin," and in some copies in its margin, "Sahaʾin," "Sahabin," and "Sanhariba." And at 656 of it: "Sayhun." And in a narration in its margin, several forms for completion.]]. He sent the armies, and his cavalry were from the people of Persia, and they were people of severe might. The Children of Israel fortified themselves, and Bukhtnassar came out among them as an orphan, a poor man; he only came out seeking food, and he behaved gently until he entered the city and came to their gatherings, and he heard them saying: "If our enemy knew what terror has been cast into our hearts because of our sins, they would not have intended to fight us." So Bukhtnassar went out when he heard that from them, and the rising against the army intensified, so they returned. That is the saying of God: ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they went through the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled.﴾ Then the Children of Israel prepared themselves, and they fought the Nabataeans, and they took from them spoils and recovered what was in their hands. That is the saying of God: ﴿Then We gave you the return against them, and We aided you with wealth and sons, and made you more in number.﴾ He said: "Numbers."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Their corruption, which they committed in the land twice, was the killing of Zakariyya and Yahya ibn Zakariyya. God gave power over them to Sabur Dhu al-Aktaf, a king from the kings of Persia, who killed Zakariyya, and He gave power over them to Bukhtnassar, who killed Yahya.

⁕ 'Isam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri related to us, saying: Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir related to us, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when the Children of Israel transgressed and became haughty, and killed the prophets, God sent against them the king of Persia, Bukhtnassar, and God had granted him dominion for seven hundred years. He marched against them until he entered Bayt al-Maqdis, and besieged it and conquered it, and killed seventy thousand over the blood of Zakariyya, then he took captive its people and the sons of the prophets, and he plundered the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and he extracted from it seventy thousand and one hundred thousand carts of ornaments, until he brought them to Babylon." Hudhayfa said: I said: "O Messenger of God, was Bayt al-Maqdis great in the sight of God?" He said: "Yes. Sulayman ibn Dawud built it of gold, pearls, rubies and chrysolite, and its floor was one slab of gold and one slab of silver, and its pillars were gold. God gave him that, and subjected the devils to him, bringing him these things in the twinkling of an eye. Then Bukhtnassar set off with these things until he alighted with them in Babylon. The Children of Israel remained in his hands for a hundred years, being tortured by the Magians and the sons of the Magians, among them were prophets and the sons of prophets. Then God had mercy on them, and He revealed to a king from the kings of Persia called Kurush, who was a believer, that he should go to the remnants of the Children of Israel until he delivers them. So Kurush set out with the Children of Israel and the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis until he returned them to it. The Children of Israel remained obedient to God for a hundred years. Then they returned to disobedience, so God gave power over them to Abtinahus [[In al-Durr al-Manthur by al-Suyuti (4: 165): "Abtanahus."]], who raided with the sons of those who had raided with Bukhtnassar. He raided the Children of Israel until he came to them at Bayt al-Maqdis, and took captive its people, and burned Bayt al-Maqdis, and said to them: 'O Children of Israel, if you return to disobedience, we will return against you with captivity.' They returned to disobedience, so God sent against them the third captivity, the king of Rome, called Qaqas ibn Isbayus. He raided them by land and sea, took them captive, plundered the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and burned Bayt al-Maqdis with fire." Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "This is from the work of the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and al-Mahdi will return them to Bayt al-Maqdis, and they are a thousand ships and seven hundred ships, which will be moored with them at Jaffa until they are transported to Bayt al-Maqdis, and with them God will gather the first and the last."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Among what God sent down to Moses in His account concerning the Children of Israel, and in their events, was what they would do after him. So He said: ﴿And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture that you would surely cause corruption in the land twice, and you would surely become haughty with great haughtiness﴾ ... up to His words ﴿And We made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾.
