The Children of Israel were thus, and among them were youthful follies and sins, and God was in that forgiving of them, showing kindness to them and benevolent towards them. So among what was sent down upon them for their sins was what He had previously announced to them through the tongue of Moses concerning what would be sent down upon them for their sins. The first of those events that befell them was that a king from among them, called Siddiqa, ruled over them. Whenever God made a king reign over them, He sent a prophet to guide and direct him, to be between him and God, and to communicate to him concerning their affairs. The scriptures were not sent down to them; rather, they were commanded to follow the Torah and the rulings in it, and were forbidden from disobedience, and called to what they had abandoned of obedience. So when that king ruled, God sent with him Sha'ya ibn Amusa [[His name in the Bible is Isaiah ibn Amoz. See the account of the prophet Sha'ya in the History of al-Tabari (2, part 1, p. 639), Europe edition.]], and that was before the mission of Zakariyya, Yahya, 'Isa, and Sha'ya, who gave glad tidings of 'Isa and Muhammad. So that king ruled over the Children of Israel and Bayt al-Maqdis for a time. When his rule ended, the youthful follies among them increased, and Sha'ya was with him. God sent against them Sanhariba, king of Babylon, with six hundred thousand banners. He advanced until he alighted near Bayt al-Maqdis, while the king was ill with an ulcer on his leg. The prophet Sha'ya came and said to him: "O king of the Children of Israel, Sanhariba, king of Babylon, has alighted against you with his soldiers, six hundred thousand banners, and the people have feared them and dispersed from them." This weighed heavily upon the king, and he said: "O prophet of God, has any revelation from God come to you concerning what has happened, so you may inform us how God will deal with us and with Sanhariba and his soldiers?" The prophet said to him: "No revelation has come to me concerning your affair." While they were in that state, God revealed to the prophet Sha'ya: "Go to the king of the Children of Israel, and command him to make his bequest and to appoint as successor over his kingdom whomever he wishes from among his family." So Sha'ya the prophet came to the king of the Children of Israel, Siddiqa, and said to him: "Your Lord has revealed to me that I should command you to make your bequest and appoint as successor over your kingdom whomever you wish from your family, for you are dying." When Sha'ya said that to Siddiqa, he turned towards the qibla, prayed, glorified God, supplicated, and wept, and said, while weeping and humbling himself before God with a sincere heart, trust, patience, truthfulness, and true assurance: "O God, Lord of lords, God of gods, Holy One of the holy, O Merciful, O Compassionate, the Forgiving, the Kind, whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes, remember me for my deed, my action, and my good judgment concerning the Children of Israel, and all that was from You; You know it better than myself. My secret and my open are for You." And the Merciful responded to him, and he was a righteous servant. So God revealed to Sha'ya that he should inform the king Siddiqa that his Lord had responded to him, accepted from him, and had mercy upon him, and had seen his weeping, and had postponed his term by fifteen years, and had saved him from his enemy Sanhariba, king of Babylon, and his soldiers. Sha'ya the prophet came to that king and informed him of this. When he told him that, the pain left him, and evil and sorrow ceased from him, and he fell down in prostration and said: "O my God and God of my fathers, to You I prostrate, glorify, honour, and exalt. You are the One who gives kingship to whom You will, and removes it from whom You will, honours whom You will, and humbles whom You will. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You are the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and You are merciful and answer the supplication of the distressed. You are the One who loved my supplication and had mercy upon my humility." When he raised his head, God revealed to Sha'ya that he should tell the king Siddiqa to command one of his servants to bring figs, and he would bring fig water and place it on his ulcer, and he would be healed, and in the morning he would be cured. He did that, and was healed. The king said to the prophet Sha'ya: "Ask your Lord to give us a sign of what He will do with this enemy of ours." He said: So God said to the prophet Sha'ya: "Tell him: I have sufficed you against your enemy and saved you from him, and they will all be dead in the morning except Sanhariba and five of his scribes." When they awoke in the morning, a crier came to them and announced it, crying at the gate of the city: "O king of the Children of Israel, God has sufficed you against your enemy, so come out, for Sanhariba and those with him have perished." When the king went out, he sought Sanhariba but did not find him among the dead, so the king sent to seek him, and the pursuers caught him in a cave with five of his scribes, one of whom was Bukhtnassar. They put them in chains and brought them to the king of the Children of Israel. When he saw them, he fell down in prostration from sunrise until the afternoon. Then he said to Sanhariba: "How do you see the deed of our Lord against you? Did He not kill you by His might and power, while we and you were heedless?" Sanhariba said to him: "The news of your Lord and His victory over you has reached me, and the mercy with which He showed mercy to you before I left my land. I did not obey a guide, and nothing brought me to wretchedness except the weakness of my mind. Had I listened or understood, I would not have fought you. But wretchedness overcame me and those with me." The king of the Children of Israel said: "Praise be to God, Lord of might, who has sufficed us against you by what He willed. Our Lord did not spare you and those with you out of honour for you before Him, but He spared you and those with you only for what is worse for you, that you may increase in wretchedness in this world and in punishment in the Hereafter, and that you may inform those behind you of what you encountered from the deed of our Lord, and that you may warn those after you. Had it not been for that, He would not have spared you. Your blood and the blood of those with you is less in the sight of God than the blood of a tick, were you to kill it." Then the king of the Children of Israel commanded the commander of his guard, and he put the chains on their necks, and he paraded them for seventy days around Bayt al-Maqdis, Iliya, and he provided them each day with two loaves of barley for every man. Sanhariba said to the king of the Children of Israel: "Death is better than what is being done to us, so do what you have been commanded." So the king took them to the prison of death. God revealed to the prophet Sha'ya: "Tell the king of the Children of Israel to send Sanhariba and those with him so that they may warn those behind them, and to honour them and carry them until they reach their lands." The prophet Sha'ya conveyed that to the king, and he did it. So Sanhariba and those with him set out until they arrived in Babylon. When they arrived, he gathered the people and informed them how God had dealt with his soldiers. His priests and sorcerers said to him: "O king of Babylon, we used to relate to you the news of their Lord and the news of their prophet, and God's revelation to their prophet, but you did not obey us. They are a nation that no one can withstand with their Lord." The matter of Sanhariba was as they had warned. Then God sufficed them as a reminder and a lesson. Then Sanhariba remained after that for seven years, and then he died.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 4–5 (part 2 of 3):

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Sennacherib (Sanharib) died, Nebuchadnezzar (Bakhtnasr), the son of his son, succeeded him in what his grandfather had held, acting by his conduct and judging by his judgments, and he remained for seventeen years. Then God took the kingship of the Children of Israel, and they were in a state of chaos. They competed for rule until some of them killed others over it, while their prophet Sha'ya (Isaiah) was among them, and they would not submit to him or accept from him. When they did that, God said, as it has reached us, to Sha'ya: "Stand among your people, and I will inspire you through your tongue." When the prophet stood up, God made his tongue speak the revelation, and he said: "O heaven, listen! O earth, be attentive! For God wishes to recount the affair of the Children of Israel, whom He raised with His blessing, chose for Himself, singled out for His honor, and preferred over His servants, and He gave them preference in honor. They are like sheep that are lost with no shepherd. So He sheltered their strays, gathered their lost ones, set their broken ones, treated their sick, fattened their emaciated, and guarded their fat ones. But when He did that, they grew insolent, so their rams butted one another and killed one another, until no sound bone remained to which a broken one could be set. Woe to this sinful nation, and woe to these sinful people, who do not know where their appointed doom has come upon them. Indeed, a camel may remember its homeland and return to it, and a donkey may remember the barley-store on which it was fed and go back to it, and a bull may remember the pasture in which it grew fat and return to it. And these people do not know from where their doom has come upon them, though they are people of understanding and intellect, not cattle or donkeys. I will strike them a parable, so let them hear it. Say to them: How do you see a land that was desolate for a time, a ruined, lifeless place with no habitation in it, and which had a wise, mighty lord who turned to it with cultivation? He disliked that his land should be ruined while he was mighty, or that it be said he neglected it while he was wise. So he walled it around, built a palace in it, dug a river in it, planted in it saplings of olive, pomegranate, date-palm, and grape, and all kinds of fruit. He entrusted that to a keeper who was of sound judgment and resolve, vigilant, strong, and trustworthy, and he awaited its fruit patiently. But when it bore fruit, its fruit came out as carob. They said: 'Wretched is this land! We think its walls and palace should be demolished, its river filled in, its keepers seized, and its saplings burned, until it becomes as it was the first time, a ruined, lifeless place with no habitation in it.' God said to them: 'As for the wall, it is My protection; the palace is My law; the river is My Book; the keepers are My prophets; the saplings are themselves; and the carob that the saplings bore are their wicked deeds. I have decreed upon them their own decree against themselves. This is a parable God has struck for them: they draw near to Me by slaughtering cattle and sheep, yet no flesh reaches Me, nor do I eat it. They claim they draw near by piety and by refraining from killing the souls that I have forbidden, yet their hands are stained with them and their garments are soaked in their blood. They build houses for Me as mosques and purify their insides, while they defile their hearts and bodies and soil them. They adorn the houses and mosques for Me and decorate them, while they corrupt and spoil their minds and reason. What need have I for building houses when I do not dwell in them? And what need have I for embellishing mosques when I do not enter them? I only commanded that they be raised so that My name may be mentioned in them and I may be glorified in them, and that they may be a guide for whoever wishes to pray in them.' They say: 'If God were able to unite our hearts, He would have united them; and if God were able to give our hearts understanding, He would have given them understanding.' So go to two dry reeds, bring them, call to them in the midst of the most gathered of people, and say to the two reeds: 'God commands you to become one reed.' When he said that to them, they joined together and became one. Then God said: 'Say to them: I have power over the union of dry reeds and I can bring them together. So how can I not be able to unite their hearts, if I wish, or how can I not be able to give their hearts understanding, when I am the One who fashioned them? They say: We fasted but our fast was not raised up; we prayed but our prayer was not illuminated; we gave charity but our charity was not purified; we called upon Him with the sound of doves' cooing and we wept with the howling of wolves, yet in all of that we are not heard and are not answered.' God said: 'Ask them, what prevents Me from answering them? Am I not the Hearer of those who hear, the Seer of those who see, the Nearest of those who respond, and the Most Merciful of the merciful? Is it because My hand is empty? How can it be, when My hands are outstretched with goodness; I spend as I will, and the keys of the treasuries are with Me, and none opens or closes them but Me. Indeed, My mercy encompasses all things, and the merciful show mercy only through its bounty. Or is it because I am stingy? Am I not the most generous of the generous, the Opener of good things, more bountiful than any giver, and more gracious than any who is asked? If these people had regarded their own selves with the wisdom that shone in their hearts, but they cast it aside and sold it for this world, then they would have seen from where they had come, and they would have known with certainty that their own selves are their worst enemies. How then should I raise up their fasting when they wear it with false speech and strengthen it with food of the unlawful? How should I illuminate their prayer, when their hearts incline toward those who wage war against Me and oppose Me and violate what I have forbidden? Or how should their charity grow before Me, when they give in charity from the wealth of others, or from property seized from its rightful owners who were wronged? Or how should I answer their supplication, when it is only words on their tongues while their deeds are far from it? I answer only the one who calls out humbly, and I hear only the speech of the weak and the needy. Indeed, a sign of My pleasure is the pleasure of the poor. So if they had shown mercy to the needy, drawn near to the weak, granted justice to the wronged, supported the one who was seized, dealt justly for the absent, and given to the widow, the orphan, and the needy, and to every person of right his right, then—if it were fitting for Me to speak to humankind—I would have spoken to them, and I would have been the light of their sight, the hearing of their ears, and the understanding of their hearts; I would have strengthened their hands and feet, and I would have been the strength of their hands and feet, and I would have made firm their tongues and minds.' They say, when they heard My speech and My messages reached them: 'These are fabricated sayings, transmitted tales, and compositions of the sort that sorcerers and soothsayers compose.' They claim that if they wished, they could bring a discourse like it, and that they could obtain knowledge of the unseen with what the devils reveal to them. Yet each of them hides what he says and conceals it, while they know that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what they reveal and what they conceal. Indeed, on the day I created the heavens and the earth, I decreed a decree which I recorded upon Myself, and I set before it a term appointed which will surely come. So if they are truthful in what they claim of the knowledge of the unseen, let them inform you when I will carry it out, or at what time it will occur. And if they are able to bring about whatever they wish, let them bring the like of the power by which I carried it out, for I will make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists dislike it. And if they are able to say whatever they wish, let them compose the like of the wisdom by which I have managed the affair of that decree, if they are truthful. For I decreed, on the day I created the heavens and the earth, that I would place prophethood among the hired laborers, transfer kingship to the shepherds, give might to the humbled, strength to the weak, wealth to the poor, abundance to the few, cities to the wastelands, thickets to the deserts, reeds to the fields, knowledge to the ignorant, and judgment to the unlettered. So ask them: when will this be, who will be the one to establish it, at whose hand will it be founded, and who will be its helpers and supporters, if they know? Indeed, I will raise up for this a prophet who is unlettered, neither blind among the blind nor astray among the astray, neither harsh nor coarse, neither loud in the markets, nor adorned with obscenity, nor a speaker of foul words. I will guide him to all that is beautiful, and I will bestow upon him every noble character. I will make tranquility his garment, righteousness his emblem, piety his inner nature, wisdom his understanding, truthfulness and faithfulness his disposition, pardon and kindness his character, justice and goodness his way, truth his law, guidance his leader, and Islam his creed. His name is Ahmad. Through him I will guide after misguidance, give knowledge after ignorance, raise up after lowliness, make famous after obscurity, multiply after scarcity, enrich after poverty, unite after division, and bring together hearts that are different, desires that are scattered, and nations that are dispersed. I will make his community the best community brought forth for humankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, affirming My oneness, faith, and sincerity toward Me. They will pray to Me standing and sitting, bowing and prostrating; they will fight in My cause in rows and in advancing waves; they will leave their homes and their wealth seeking My pleasure. I will inspire them with magnification, unity, glorification, praise, and exaltation of Me in their mosques, their gatherings, their beds, their comings and goings, and their dwellings. They will magnify and proclaim My oneness, and they will sanctify Me at the heads of the markets; they will purify their faces and extremities for Me, and they will gather their garments up to the middle. Their offering is their blood, and their Gospels are their breasts. They are monks by night and lions by day. That is My bounty, which I grant to whom I will, and I am the Possessor of tremendous bounty.'" When their prophet Sha'ya finished his discourse to them, they attacked him, as it has reached me, to kill him. He fled from them, and a tree met him and split open, and he entered it. Satan reached him and seized a fringe of his garment and showed it to them. They placed the saw at its middle and sawed it until they cut it through, and they cut him in its middle.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: According to the view we have mentioned from Ibn Abbas through the narration of al-Suddi, and the statement of Ibn Zayd, the corruption of the Children of Israel in the land the first time was their killing of Zakariyya, the prophet of God (ﷺ), together with what had preceded from them before that and after it, until God sent against them the one through whose hand He brought down His punishment upon them for their disobedience to God and their arrogance toward their Lord. As for the view of Ibn Ishaq that we have related from him, their first corruption was what was described: their killing of Sha'ya ibn Amsiya, the prophet of God. Ibn Ishaq mentioned that some of the people of knowledge informed him that Zakariyya died a natural death and was not killed, and that the one killed was Sha'ya, and that Bakhtnasr was the one empowered over the Children of Israel the first time after their killing of Sha'ya. Ibn Humayd narrated this to us from Salamah, from him.

As for their corruption in the land the second time, there is no disagreement among the people of knowledge that it was their killing of Yahya ibn Zakariyya. They have differed about the one whom God empowered over them to take vengeance on them at that time, and I will mention their differences on that, God willing.

As for His saying ﴿and you will surely become exceedingly arrogant﴾, we have mentioned the view of the one who said that it means their arrogance toward God through their audacity against Him and their opposition to His command.

Mujahid used to say concerning that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and you will surely become exceedingly arrogant﴾, he said: "and you will surely make the people exceedingly arrogant."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

As for His saying ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came﴾, it means: when the promise of the first of the two times in which they would corrupt in the land came.

As:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came﴾, he said: "When the promise of the first of those two times came, of which We decreed to the Children of Israel: ﴿You will surely cause corruption in the land twice﴾."

* *

His saying ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours, possessing great might, and they roamed through the inner parts of the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled﴾.

The Most High means by His saying ﴿We sent against you﴾: We directed toward you and dispatched against you ﴿servants of Ours possessing great might﴾, meaning: possessors of severe force in war.

* *

His saying ﴿so they roamed through the inner parts of the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled﴾:

It means: they moved back and forth among the houses and dwellings, went and came. It is said: "The people roamed (jasa) among the dwellings and searched (hasa) among them," with the same meaning, and I roamed (jastu) and I roam (ajus) a roaming (jawsan) and a roaming (jawsanan).

The report has also been narrated from Ibn Abbas in a manner similar to what we have said.

⁕ Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and they roamed through the inner parts of the homes﴾, he said: "They walked."

Some people of knowledge of the language of the Arabs from the people of Basra used to say: the meaning of jasu is: they killed. He cites as evidence for this claim the verse of Hassan:

"And among us is one who met with the sword of Muhammad, so he trampled the enemies across the breadth of the armies." [[This verse is evidence that jasa means "to kill." In Lisan al-Arab (root j-w-s): al-jawsu is the verbal noun of jasa, jawsan and jawsanan, meaning to roam about. In the Revealed Book: "they roamed through the inner parts of the homes," i.e., they roamed among them for raiding. Al-Farra' said: they killed you among your houses; he said: jasa and hasa have the same meaning, namely they go and come. Al-Zajjaj said: "they roamed through the inner parts of the homes" means: they went round through the inner parts of the homes, looking to see whether anyone remained whom they had not killed. In al-Sihah: "they roamed through the inner parts of the homes," i.e., they penetrated them and sought what was in them, as a man searches for news, that is, seeks it.]]

It is possible that its meaning is: they roamed through the inner parts of the homes and killed them as they went and came, so both interpretations are valid. And His saying ﴿and it was a promise fulfilled﴾ means: the roaming of the people whom We sent against them through the inner parts of their homes was a promise from God to them, fulfilled, without doubt, because He does not break His promise.

Then the people of interpretation differed about those whom God meant by His saying ﴿possessing great might﴾, concerning what they did in the first time with the Children of Israel when they were sent against them, and who was sent against them in the second time, and what they did to them. Some said: the one whom God sent against them the first time was Jalut (Goliath), who was from the people of al-Jazira.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours possessing great might, and they roamed through the inner parts of the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled﴾, he said: "God sent Jalut against them, and he roamed through the inner parts of their homes and imposed upon them tribute and humiliation. So they asked God to send them a king who would fight in the way of God, and God sent Talut (Saul), and they fought Jalut, and God gave the Children of Israel victory, and Jalut was killed at the hands of Dawud (David), and God restored to the Children of Israel their kingship."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying (﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours possessing great might, and they roamed through the inner parts of the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled﴾), he said: "It was a decree which God decreed upon the people, as you hear. He sent against them in the first instance Jalut al-Jazari, who took captives and killed, and they roamed through the inner parts of the homes, as God said. Then the people returned, with some remnant of corruption among them."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "As for the first time, God empowered Jalut over them, until Talut was sent, with Dawud alongside him, and Dawud killed him."

Others said: rather, the one sent against them the first time was Sanharib (Sennacherib). We have already mentioned some of those who said this in what has passed, and we will mention those we have not mentioned before whose statements have reached us.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu al-Mu'alla, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say, regarding His saying ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours possessing great might﴾: "God, blessed and exalted, sent against them the first time Sanharib from the people of Athur and Nineveh." I asked Sa'id about them, and he claimed they were Mosul.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 4–5 (part 3 of 3):

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ya'la ibn Muslim ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to me, that he heard him say: A man from the Children of Israel used to recite, and when he reached ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours possessed of great might﴾, he would weep and his eyes would overflow, and he would close the Qur'an. He continued like this for as long as God willed. Then he said: "My Lord, show me this man whom You have made the destruction of the Children of Israel to be at his hands." So he was shown in a dream a poor man in Babel called Bakhtnasar. The Israelite set out with his wealth and his servants, and he was a wealthy man. He was asked, "Where are you going?" He said, "I am going for trade," until he descended upon a house in Babel, which he rented, and in which there was no one but himself. He began calling the poor and treating them kindly, until no poor person was left. He said, "Is there any poor person left besides you?" They said, "Yes, a poor man in the quarter of such-and-such a family, sick, called Bakhtnasar." He said to his servants, "Go, bring him to me." So they went to him, and he said, "What is your name?" He said, "Bakhtnasar." So he said to his servants, "Carry him," and they carried him to him. He nursed him until he recovered, clothed him, and gave him provision. Then the Israelite announced his departure, and Bakhtnasar wept. The Israelite said, "What makes you weep?" He said, "I weep because you have done to me what you have done, and I find nothing with which to repay you." He said, "Yes, a small thing: if you become king, obey me." The other kept following him and saying, "You are mocking me." What prevented him from giving him what he asked was only that he thought he was mocking him. The Israelite wept and said, "I know what prevents you from giving me what I asked of you, except that God wills to carry out what He has decreed and written in His Book, and the ages have struck their blows." One day Sayhun, who was the king of Persia at Babel, said: "What if we send a vanguard to Sham?" They said, "What harm would it do you if you did?" He said, "Whom do you see [fit for it]?" They said, "So-and-so." He sent a man and gave him a hundred thousand, and Bakhtnasar went out in his kitchen; he had gone out only to eat in his kitchen. When he arrived in Sham and the commander of the vanguard saw that the land of God had more horsemen and sturdy foot soldiers, this weighed on his mind, so he did not ask them about anything. [Note in al-Tha'labi's ʿArāʾis al-majālis: "So he did not ask them about anything."] He said: Bakhtnasar began to sit in the gatherings of the people of Sham and say: "What prevents you from raiding Babel? If you raided it, nothing beneath its treasury would be left." They said, "We do not fight well." He said, "But if you raided it—" They said, "We do not fight well, and we will not fight until I have passed through the gatherings of the people of Sham." Then they returned, and the vanguard informed their king of what he had seen. Bakhtnasar began saying to the cavalry of the king: "If the king had summoned me, I would have told him something other than what so-and-so told him." This was reported to [the king], so he summoned him and told him the news, saying: "When so-and-so saw that the land of God had more horsemen and sturdy foot soldiers, this magnified itself in his heart, and he did not ask them about anything. I, however, did not leave a gathering in Sham without sitting with its people, and I said to them such-and-such, and they said to me such-and-such," which is what Sa'id ibn Jubayr mentioned he had said to them. The vanguard said to Bakhtnasar: "You have disgraced me [for] a hundred thousand for you, and you turn away from what you said." [Note: thus in the History of al-Tabari, Leiden edition. In the original: "in your company" (sahibtani), a distortion.] He said: "If you gave me the treasury of Babel's wealth, I would not turn away; the ages have struck their blows." The king said: "What if we send a flying cavalry squadron to Sham? If they find an opening, they will advance, and if not, they will turn back from what they cannot achieve." They said, "What harm would it do you if you did?" He said, "Whom do you see [fit for it]?" They said, "So-and-so." He said, "Rather, the man who told me what he told me." So he summoned Bakhtnasar and sent him, and he selected four thousand of their horsemen with him. They set out and roamed through the midst of the dwellings. They took captives as God willed, but they did not destroy and did not kill. King Sayhun died [Note: thus in al-Tha'labi's ʿArāʾis al-majālis, p. 336, Halabi edition. In the original: "and he threw in a funeral sahuran."] They said: "Appoint a man [as ruler]." They said: "Take it slowly until you reach your companions, for they are your horsemen; they will not overturn anything against you. Wait." So they waited until Bakhtnasar came with the captives and what he had with him. He distributed them among the people. They said: "We have seen no one more worthy of the kingship than this man," and so they made him king.

⁕ Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal informed me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib say: Bakhtnasar prevailed over Sham, destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis, and killed them. Then he came to Damascus, and there he found blood boiling on a dunghill (kaba), that is, a refuse heap. He asked them, "What is this blood?" They said, "We found our fathers upon this, and whenever the dunghill is struck, it [the blood] rises." He said: He then killed seventy thousand of the Muslims and others over that blood, and it subsided.

And others said: By this is meant a people from Persia. They said: In the first instance there was no fighting.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours possessed of great might, and they roamed between the dwellings﴾: "It is those who came to them from Persia to spy on their affairs and to listen to their talk, with whom was Bakhtnasar, who memorized their sayings from among his companions. Then the Persians returned, and there was no fighting. The Children of Israel were victorious over them. This is the promise of the first."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours possessed of great might﴾: "An army that came to them from Persia to spy on their affairs," and then he mentioned something similar.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours possessed of great might﴾: "That is, those who came to them from Persia," and then he mentioned something similar.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture that you would surely cause corruption in the land twice, and you would surely become haughty with great haughtiness. (4) So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they went through the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled.﴾ (5)

We have already explained earlier that the meaning of *qada'* (decree) is the completion of a matter, and it is then used for anything that has been completed. So the interpretation of the speech in this place is: "Your Lord completed [His command] concerning the Children of Israel in what He sent down in His Book to Moses, may the blessings and peace of God be upon him, by informing them and telling them ﴿that you would surely cause corruption in the land twice﴾," meaning: "You, O assembly of the Children of Israel, will surely disobey God and oppose His command in His lands twice." ﴿And you will surely become haughty with great haughtiness﴾ means: "And you will surely be arrogant towards God by your audacity against Him, with severe arrogance."

Concerning this, the people of *ta'wil* (interpretation) said in agreement with what we have said:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the words of God ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel﴾: "He said: We informed them."

⁕ 'Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel﴾: "He said: We informed them."

Others said: The meaning of that is: "We decreed against the Children of Israel in the Mother of the Book and in His foreknowledge."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel﴾: "He said: It is a decree that has passed over them."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel﴾: "A decree which He decreed upon the people, as you hear."

Others said: The meaning of that is: "He informed us."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture﴾: "He said: He informed the Children of Israel."

All these sayings return in their meanings to what I have said concerning the meaning of His words ﴿And We decreed﴾. Although the interpretation we have chosen concerning it is closer to the truth, because the readers (qurra') agree on the recitation of His words ﴿لَتُفْسِدُنَّ﴾ (*latufsidunna*, with the *ta'*) rather than the *ya'* (*layufsidunna*). Had the meaning of the speech been "We decreed against them in the Book," the recitation with the *ya'* would have been more preferable than with the *ta'*. But its meaning, since it was "We informed them and told them, and said to them," the *ta'* was closer and more appropriate for direct address.

The corruption of the Children of Israel in the land the first time was as follows:

⁕ Harun narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hammad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, in a report he mentioned from Abu Salih, and from Abu Malik, from Ibn 'Abbas, and from Murra, from 'Abd Allah, that God covenanted with the Children of Israel in the Torah: ﴿You will surely cause corruption in the land twice﴾. The first of the two corruptions was the killing of Zakariyya, so God sent against them the king of the Nabataeans, who was called Sahabin [[In the History of al-Tabari (vol. 2, part 1, p. 657, Europe edition): "Sayhanin," and in some copies in its margin, "Sahaʾin," "Sahabin," and "Sanhariba." And at 656 of it: "Sayhun." And in a narration in its margin, several forms for completion.]]. He sent the armies, and his cavalry were from the people of Persia, and they were people of severe might. The Children of Israel fortified themselves, and Bukhtnassar came out among them as an orphan, a poor man; he only came out seeking food, and he behaved gently until he entered the city and came to their gatherings, and he heard them saying: "If our enemy knew what terror has been cast into our hearts because of our sins, they would not have intended to fight us." So Bukhtnassar went out when he heard that from them, and the rising against the army intensified, so they returned. That is the saying of God: ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they went through the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled.﴾ Then the Children of Israel prepared themselves, and they fought the Nabataeans, and they took from them spoils and recovered what was in their hands. That is the saying of God: ﴿Then We gave you the return against them, and We aided you with wealth and sons, and made you more in number.﴾ He said: "Numbers."

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Their corruption, which they committed in the land twice, was the killing of Zakariyya and Yahya ibn Zakariyya. God gave power over them to Sabur Dhu al-Aktaf, a king from the kings of Persia, who killed Zakariyya, and He gave power over them to Bukhtnassar, who killed Yahya.

⁕ 'Isam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, saying: My father related to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Sa'id al-Thawri related to us, saying: Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir related to us, from Rib'i ibn Hirash, who said: I heard Hudhayfa ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when the Children of Israel transgressed and became haughty, and killed the prophets, God sent against them the king of Persia, Bukhtnassar, and God had granted him dominion for seven hundred years. He marched against them until he entered Bayt al-Maqdis, and besieged it and conquered it, and killed seventy thousand over the blood of Zakariyya, then he took captive its people and the sons of the prophets, and he plundered the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and he extracted from it seventy thousand and one hundred thousand carts of ornaments, until he brought them to Babylon." Hudhayfa said: I said: "O Messenger of God, was Bayt al-Maqdis great in the sight of God?" He said: "Yes. Sulayman ibn Dawud built it of gold, pearls, rubies and chrysolite, and its floor was one slab of gold and one slab of silver, and its pillars were gold. God gave him that, and subjected the devils to him, bringing him these things in the twinkling of an eye. Then Bukhtnassar set off with these things until he alighted with them in Babylon. The Children of Israel remained in his hands for a hundred years, being tortured by the Magians and the sons of the Magians, among them were prophets and the sons of prophets. Then God had mercy on them, and He revealed to a king from the kings of Persia called Kurush, who was a believer, that he should go to the remnants of the Children of Israel until he delivers them. So Kurush set out with the Children of Israel and the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis until he returned them to it. The Children of Israel remained obedient to God for a hundred years. Then they returned to disobedience, so God gave power over them to Abtinahus [[In al-Durr al-Manthur by al-Suyuti (4: 165): "Abtanahus."]], who raided with the sons of those who had raided with Bukhtnassar. He raided the Children of Israel until he came to them at Bayt al-Maqdis, and took captive its people, and burned Bayt al-Maqdis, and said to them: 'O Children of Israel, if you return to disobedience, we will return against you with captivity.' They returned to disobedience, so God sent against them the third captivity, the king of Rome, called Qaqas ibn Isbayus. He raided them by land and sea, took them captive, plundered the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and burned Bayt al-Maqdis with fire." Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "This is from the work of the ornaments of Bayt al-Maqdis, and al-Mahdi will return them to Bayt al-Maqdis, and they are a thousand ships and seven hundred ships, which will be moored with them at Jaffa until they are transported to Bayt al-Maqdis, and with them God will gather the first and the last."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to me, saying: Among what God sent down to Moses in His account concerning the Children of Israel, and in their events, was what they would do after him. So He said: ﴿And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture that you would surely cause corruption in the land twice, and you would surely become haughty with great haughtiness﴾ ... up to His words ﴿And We made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾. The Children of Israel were thus, and among them were youthful follies and sins, and God was in that forgiving of them, showing kindness to them and benevolent towards them. So among what was sent down upon them for their sins was what He had previously announced to them through the tongue of Moses concerning what would be sent down upon them for their sins. The first of those events that befell them was that a king from among them, called Siddiqa, ruled over them. Whenever God made a king reign over them, He sent a prophet to guide and direct him, to be between him and God, and to communicate to him concerning their affairs. The scriptures were not sent down to them; rather, they were commanded to follow the Torah and the rulings in it, and were forbidden from disobedience, and called to what they had abandoned of obedience. So when that king ruled, God sent with him Sha'ya ibn Amusa [[His name in the Bible is Isaiah ibn Amoz. See the account of the prophet Sha'ya in the History of al-Tabari (2, part 1, p. 639), Europe edition.]], and that was before the mission of Zakariyya, Yahya, 'Isa, and Sha'ya, who gave glad tidings of 'Isa and Muhammad. So that king ruled over the Children of Israel and Bayt al-Maqdis for a time. When his rule ended, the youthful follies among them increased, and Sha'ya was with him. God sent against them Sanhariba, king of Babylon, with six hundred thousand banners. He advanced until he alighted near Bayt al-Maqdis, while the king was ill with an ulcer on his leg. The prophet Sha'ya came and said to him: "O king of the Children of Israel, Sanhariba, king of Babylon, has alighted against you with his soldiers, six hundred thousand banners, and the people have feared them and dispersed from them." This weighed heavily upon the king, and he said: "O prophet of God, has any revelation from God come to you concerning what has happened, so you may inform us how God will deal with us and with Sanhariba and his soldiers?" The prophet said to him: "No revelation has come to me concerning your affair." While they were in that state, God revealed to the prophet Sha'ya: "Go to the king of the Children of Israel, and command him to make his bequest and to appoint as successor over his kingdom whomever he wishes from among his family." So Sha'ya the prophet came to the king of the Children of Israel, Siddiqa, and said to him: "Your Lord has revealed to me that I should command you to make your bequest and appoint as successor over your kingdom whomever you wish from your family, for you are dying." When Sha'ya said that to Siddiqa, he turned towards the qibla, prayed, glorified God, supplicated, and wept, and said, while weeping and humbling himself before God with a sincere heart, trust, patience, truthfulness, and true assurance: "O God, Lord of lords, God of gods, Holy One of the holy, O Merciful, O Compassionate, the Forgiving, the Kind, whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes, remember me for my deed, my action, and my good judgment concerning the Children of Israel, and all that was from You; You know it better than myself. My secret and my open are for You." And the Merciful responded to him, and he was a righteous servant. So God revealed to Sha'ya that he should inform the king Siddiqa that his Lord had responded to him, accepted from him, and had mercy upon him, and had seen his weeping, and had postponed his term by fifteen years, and had saved him from his enemy Sanhariba, king of Babylon, and his soldiers. Sha'ya the prophet came to that king and informed him of this. When he told him that, the pain left him, and evil and sorrow ceased from him, and he fell down in prostration and said: "O my God and God of my fathers, to You I prostrate, glorify, honour, and exalt. You are the One who gives kingship to whom You will, and removes it from whom You will, honours whom You will, and humbles whom You will. Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You are the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and You are merciful and answer the supplication of the distressed. You are the One who loved my supplication and had mercy upon my humility." When he raised his head, God revealed to Sha'ya that he should tell the king Siddiqa to command one of his servants to bring figs, and he would bring fig water and place it on his ulcer, and he would be healed, and in the morning he would be cured. He did that, and was healed. The king said to the prophet Sha'ya: "Ask your Lord to give us a sign of what He will do with this enemy of ours." He said: So God said to the prophet Sha'ya: "Tell him: I have sufficed you against your enemy and saved you from him, and they will all be dead in the morning except Sanhariba and five of his scribes." When they awoke in the morning, a crier came to them and announced it, crying at the gate of the city: "O king of the Children of Israel, God has sufficed you against your enemy, so come out, for Sanhariba and those with him have perished." When the king went out, he sought Sanhariba but did not find him among the dead, so the king sent to seek him, and the pursuers caught him in a cave with five of his scribes, one of whom was Bukhtnassar. They put them in chains and brought them to the king of the Children of Israel. When he saw them, he fell down in prostration from sunrise until the afternoon. Then he said to Sanhariba: "How do you see the deed of our Lord against you? Did He not kill you by His might and power, while we and you were heedless?" Sanhariba said to him: "The news of your Lord and His victory over you has reached me, and the mercy with which He showed mercy to you before I left my land. I did not obey a guide, and nothing brought me to wretchedness except the weakness of my mind. Had I listened or understood, I would not have fought you. But wretchedness overcame me and those with me." The king of the Children of Israel said: "Praise be to God, Lord of might, who has sufficed us against you by what He willed. Our Lord did not spare you and those with you out of honour for you before Him, but He spared you and those with you only for what is worse for you, that you may increase in wretchedness in this world and in punishment in the Hereafter, and that you may inform those behind you of what you encountered from the deed of our Lord, and that you may warn those after you. Had it not been for that, He would not have spared you. Your blood and the blood of those with you is less in the sight of God than the blood of a tick, were you to kill it." Then the king of the Children of Israel commanded the commander of his guard, and he put the chains on their necks, and he paraded them for seventy days around Bayt al-Maqdis, Iliya, and he provided them each day with two loaves of barley for every man. Sanhariba said to the king of the Children of Israel: "Death is better than what is being done to us, so do what you have been commanded." So the king took them to the prison of death. God revealed to the prophet Sha'ya: "Tell the king of the Children of Israel to send Sanhariba and those with him so that they may warn those behind them, and to honour them and carry them until they reach their lands." The prophet Sha'ya conveyed that to the king, and he did it. So Sanhariba and those with him set out until they arrived in Babylon. When they arrived, he gathered the people and informed them how God had dealt with his soldiers. His priests and sorcerers said to him: "O king of Babylon, we used to relate to you the news of their Lord and the news of their prophet, and God's revelation to their prophet, but you did not obey us. They are a nation that no one can withstand with their Lord." The matter of Sanhariba was as they had warned. Then God sufficed them as a reminder and a lesson. Then Sanhariba remained after that for seven years, and then he died.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 4–5 (part 2 of 3):

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Sennacherib (Sanharib) died, Nebuchadnezzar (Bakhtnasr), the son of his son, succeeded him in what his grandfather had held, acting by his conduct and judging by his judgments, and he remained for seventeen years. Then God took the kingship of the Children of Israel, and they were in a state of chaos. They competed for rule until some of them killed others over it, while their prophet Sha'ya (Isaiah) was among them, and they would not submit to him or accept from him. When they did that, God said, as it has reached us, to Sha'ya: "Stand among your people, and I will inspire you through your tongue." When the prophet stood up, God made his tongue speak the revelation, and he said: "O heaven, listen! O earth, be attentive! For God wishes to recount the affair of the Children of Israel, whom He raised with His blessing, chose for Himself, singled out for His honor, and preferred over His servants, and He gave them preference in honor. They are like sheep that are lost with no shepherd. So He sheltered their strays, gathered their lost ones, set their broken ones, treated their sick, fattened their emaciated, and guarded their fat ones. But when He did that, they grew insolent, so their rams butted one another and killed one another, until no sound bone remained to which a broken one could be set. Woe to this sinful nation, and woe to these sinful people, who do not know where their appointed doom has come upon them. Indeed, a camel may remember its homeland and return to it, and a donkey may remember the barley-store on which it was fed and go back to it, and a bull may remember the pasture in which it grew fat and return to it. And these people do not know from where their doom has come upon them, though they are people of understanding and intellect, not cattle or donkeys. I will strike them a parable, so let them hear it. Say to them: How do you see a land that was desolate for a time, a ruined, lifeless place with no habitation in it, and which had a wise, mighty lord who turned to it with cultivation? He disliked that his land should be ruined while he was mighty, or that it be said he neglected it while he was wise. So he walled it around, built a palace in it, dug a river in it, planted in it saplings of olive, pomegranate, date-palm, and grape, and all kinds of fruit. He entrusted that to a keeper who was of sound judgment and resolve, vigilant, strong, and trustworthy, and he awaited its fruit patiently. But when it bore fruit, its fruit came out as carob. They said: 'Wretched is this land! We think its walls and palace should be demolished, its river filled in, its keepers seized, and its saplings burned, until it becomes as it was the first time, a ruined, lifeless place with no habitation in it.' God said to them: 'As for the wall, it is My protection; the palace is My law; the river is My Book; the keepers are My prophets; the saplings are themselves; and the carob that the saplings bore are their wicked deeds. I have decreed upon them their own decree against themselves. This is a parable God has struck for them: they draw near to Me by slaughtering cattle and sheep, yet no flesh reaches Me, nor do I eat it. They claim they draw near by piety and by refraining from killing the souls that I have forbidden, yet their hands are stained with them and their garments are soaked in their blood. They build houses for Me as mosques and purify their insides, while they defile their hearts and bodies and soil them. They adorn the houses and mosques for Me and decorate them, while they corrupt and spoil their minds and reason. What need have I for building houses when I do not dwell in them? And what need have I for embellishing mosques when I do not enter them? I only commanded that they be raised so that My name may be mentioned in them and I may be glorified in them, and that they may be a guide for whoever wishes to pray in them.' They say: 'If God were able to unite our hearts, He would have united them; and if God were able to give our hearts understanding, He would have given them understanding.' So go to two dry reeds, bring them, call to them in the midst of the most gathered of people, and say to the two reeds: 'God commands you to become one reed.' When he said that to them, they joined together and became one. Then God said: 'Say to them: I have power over the union of dry reeds and I can bring them together. So how can I not be able to unite their hearts, if I wish, or how can I not be able to give their hearts understanding, when I am the One who fashioned them? They say: We fasted but our fast was not raised up; we prayed but our prayer was not illuminated; we gave charity but our charity was not purified; we called upon Him with the sound of doves' cooing and we wept with the howling of wolves, yet in all of that we are not heard and are not answered.' God said: 'Ask them, what prevents Me from answering them? Am I not the Hearer of those who hear, the Seer of those who see, the Nearest of those who respond, and the Most Merciful of the merciful? Is it because My hand is empty? How can it be, when My hands are outstretched with goodness; I spend as I will, and the keys of the treasuries are with Me, and none opens or closes them but Me. Indeed, My mercy encompasses all things, and the merciful show mercy only through its bounty. Or is it because I am stingy? Am I not the most generous of the generous, the Opener of good things, more bountiful than any giver, and more gracious than any who is asked? If these people had regarded their own selves with the wisdom that shone in their hearts, but they cast it aside and sold it for this world, then they would have seen from where they had come, and they would have known with certainty that their own selves are their worst enemies. How then should I raise up their fasting when they wear it with false speech and strengthen it with food of the unlawful? How should I illuminate their prayer, when their hearts incline toward those who wage war against Me and oppose Me and violate what I have forbidden? Or how should their charity grow before Me, when they give in charity from the wealth of others, or from property seized from its rightful owners who were wronged? Or how should I answer their supplication, when it is only words on their tongues while their deeds are far from it? I answer only the one who calls out humbly, and I hear only the speech of the weak and the needy. Indeed, a sign of My pleasure is the pleasure of the poor. So if they had shown mercy to the needy, drawn near to the weak, granted justice to the wronged, supported the one who was seized, dealt justly for the absent, and given to the widow, the orphan, and the needy, and to every person of right his right, then—if it were fitting for Me to speak to humankind—I would have spoken to them, and I would have been the light of their sight, the hearing of their ears, and the understanding of their hearts; I would have strengthened their hands and feet, and I would have been the strength of their hands and feet, and I would have made firm their tongues and minds.' They say, when they heard My speech and My messages reached them: 'These are fabricated sayings, transmitted tales, and compositions of the sort that sorcerers and soothsayers compose.' They claim that if they wished, they could bring a discourse like it, and that they could obtain knowledge of the unseen with what the devils reveal to them. Yet each of them hides what he says and conceals it, while they know that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what they reveal and what they conceal. Indeed, on the day I created the heavens and the earth, I decreed a decree which I recorded upon Myself, and I set before it a term appointed which will surely come. So if they are truthful in what they claim of the knowledge of the unseen, let them inform you when I will carry it out, or at what time it will occur. And if they are able to bring about whatever they wish, let them bring the like of the power by which I carried it out, for I will make it prevail over all religion, even if the polytheists dislike it. And if they are able to say whatever they wish, let them compose the like of the wisdom by which I have managed the affair of that decree, if they are truthful. For I decreed, on the day I created the heavens and the earth, that I would place prophethood among the hired laborers, transfer kingship to the shepherds, give might to the humbled, strength to the weak, wealth to the poor, abundance to the few, cities to the wastelands, thickets to the deserts, reeds to the fields, knowledge to the ignorant, and judgment to the unlettered. So ask them: when will this be, who will be the one to establish it, at whose hand will it be founded, and who will be its helpers and supporters, if they know? Indeed, I will raise up for this a prophet who is unlettered, neither blind among the blind nor astray among the astray, neither harsh nor coarse, neither loud in the markets, nor adorned with obscenity, nor a speaker of foul words. I will guide him to all that is beautiful, and I will bestow upon him every noble character. I will make tranquility his garment, righteousness his emblem, piety his inner nature, wisdom his understanding, truthfulness and faithfulness his disposition, pardon and kindness his character, justice and goodness his way, truth his law, guidance his leader, and Islam his creed. His name is Ahmad. Through him I will guide after misguidance, give knowledge after ignorance, raise up after lowliness, make famous after obscurity, multiply after scarcity, enrich after poverty, unite after division, and bring together hearts that are different, desires that are scattered, and nations that are dispersed. I will make his community the best community brought forth for humankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, affirming My oneness, faith, and sincerity toward Me. They will pray to Me standing and sitting, bowing and prostrating; they will fight in My cause in rows and in advancing waves; they will leave their homes and their wealth seeking My pleasure. I will inspire them with magnification, unity, glorification, praise, and exaltation of Me in their mosques, their gatherings, their beds, their comings and goings, and their dwellings. They will magnify and proclaim My oneness, and they will sanctify Me at the heads of the markets; they will purify their faces and extremities for Me, and they will gather their garments up to the middle. Their offering is their blood, and their Gospels are their breasts. They are monks by night and lions by day. That is My bounty, which I grant to whom I will, and I am the Possessor of tremendous bounty.'" When their prophet Sha'ya finished his discourse to them, they attacked him, as it has reached me, to kill him. He fled from them, and a tree met him and split open, and he entered it. Satan reached him and seized a fringe of his garment and showed it to them. They placed the saw at its middle and sawed it until they cut it through, and they cut him in its middle.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: According to the view we have mentioned from Ibn Abbas through the narration of al-Suddi, and the statement of Ibn Zayd, the corruption of the Children of Israel in the land the first time was their killing of Zakariyya, the prophet of God (ﷺ), together with what had preceded from them before that and after it, until God sent against them the one through whose hand He brought down His punishment upon them for their disobedience to God and their arrogance toward their Lord. As for the view of Ibn Ishaq that we have related from him, their first corruption was what was described: their killing of Sha'ya ibn Amsiya, the prophet of God. Ibn Ishaq mentioned that some of the people of knowledge informed him that Zakariyya died a natural death and was not killed, and that the one killed was Sha'ya, and that Bakhtnasr was the one empowered over the Children of Israel the first time after their killing of Sha'ya. Ibn Humayd narrated this to us from Salamah, from him.

As for their corruption in the land the second time, there is no disagreement among the people of knowledge that it was their killing of Yahya ibn Zakariyya. They have differed about the one whom God empowered over them to take vengeance on them at that time, and I will mention their differences on that, God willing.

As for His saying ﴿and you will surely become exceedingly arrogant﴾, we have mentioned the view of the one who said that it means their arrogance toward God through their audacity against Him and their opposition to His command.

Mujahid used to say concerning that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and you will surely become exceedingly arrogant﴾, he said: "and you will surely make the people exceedingly arrogant."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

As for His saying ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came﴾, it means: when the promise of the first of the two times in which they would corrupt in the land came.

As:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came﴾, he said: "When the promise of the first of those two times came, of which We decreed to the Children of Israel: ﴿You will surely cause corruption in the land twice﴾."

* *

His saying ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours, possessing great might, and they roamed through the inner parts of the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled﴾.

The Most High means by His saying ﴿We sent against you﴾: We directed toward you and dispatched against you ﴿servants of Ours possessing great might﴾, meaning: possessors of severe force in war.

* *

His saying ﴿so they roamed through the inner parts of the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled﴾:

It means: they moved back and forth among the houses and dwellings, went and came. It is said: "The people roamed (jasa) among the dwellings and searched (hasa) among them," with the same meaning, and I roamed (jastu) and I roam (ajus) a roaming (jawsan) and a roaming (jawsanan).

The report has also been narrated from Ibn Abbas in a manner similar to what we have said.

⁕ Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and they roamed through the inner parts of the homes﴾, he said: "They walked."

Some people of knowledge of the language of the Arabs from the people of Basra used to say: the meaning of jasu is: they killed. He cites as evidence for this claim the verse of Hassan:

"And among us is one who met with the sword of Muhammad, so he trampled the enemies across the breadth of the armies." [[This verse is evidence that jasa means "to kill." In Lisan al-Arab (root j-w-s): al-jawsu is the verbal noun of jasa, jawsan and jawsanan, meaning to roam about. In the Revealed Book: "they roamed through the inner parts of the homes," i.e., they roamed among them for raiding. Al-Farra' said: they killed you among your houses; he said: jasa and hasa have the same meaning, namely they go and come. Al-Zajjaj said: "they roamed through the inner parts of the homes" means: they went round through the inner parts of the homes, looking to see whether anyone remained whom they had not killed. In al-Sihah: "they roamed through the inner parts of the homes," i.e., they penetrated them and sought what was in them, as a man searches for news, that is, seeks it.]]

It is possible that its meaning is: they roamed through the inner parts of the homes and killed them as they went and came, so both interpretations are valid. And His saying ﴿and it was a promise fulfilled﴾ means: the roaming of the people whom We sent against them through the inner parts of their homes was a promise from God to them, fulfilled, without doubt, because He does not break His promise.

Then the people of interpretation differed about those whom God meant by His saying ﴿possessing great might﴾, concerning what they did in the first time with the Children of Israel when they were sent against them, and who was sent against them in the second time, and what they did to them. Some said: the one whom God sent against them the first time was Jalut (Goliath), who was from the people of al-Jazira.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours possessing great might, and they roamed through the inner parts of the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled﴾, he said: "God sent Jalut against them, and he roamed through the inner parts of their homes and imposed upon them tribute and humiliation. So they asked God to send them a king who would fight in the way of God, and God sent Talut (Saul), and they fought Jalut, and God gave the Children of Israel victory, and Jalut was killed at the hands of Dawud (David), and God restored to the Children of Israel their kingship."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying (﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours possessing great might, and they roamed through the inner parts of the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled﴾), he said: "It was a decree which God decreed upon the people, as you hear. He sent against them in the first instance Jalut al-Jazari, who took captives and killed, and they roamed through the inner parts of the homes, as God said. Then the people returned, with some remnant of corruption among them."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: "As for the first time, God empowered Jalut over them, until Talut was sent, with Dawud alongside him, and Dawud killed him."

Others said: rather, the one sent against them the first time was Sanharib (Sennacherib). We have already mentioned some of those who said this in what has passed, and we will mention those we have not mentioned before whose statements have reached us.

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu al-Mu'alla, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say, regarding His saying ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours possessing great might﴾: "God, blessed and exalted, sent against them the first time Sanharib from the people of Athur and Nineveh." I asked Sa'id about them, and he claimed they were Mosul.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 4–5 (part 3 of 3):

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ya'la ibn Muslim ibn Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to me, that he heard him say: A man from the Children of Israel used to recite, and when he reached ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours possessed of great might﴾, he would weep and his eyes would overflow, and he would close the Qur'an. He continued like this for as long as God willed. Then he said: "My Lord, show me this man whom You have made the destruction of the Children of Israel to be at his hands." So he was shown in a dream a poor man in Babel called Bakhtnasar. The Israelite set out with his wealth and his servants, and he was a wealthy man. He was asked, "Where are you going?" He said, "I am going for trade," until he descended upon a house in Babel, which he rented, and in which there was no one but himself. He began calling the poor and treating them kindly, until no poor person was left. He said, "Is there any poor person left besides you?" They said, "Yes, a poor man in the quarter of such-and-such a family, sick, called Bakhtnasar." He said to his servants, "Go, bring him to me." So they went to him, and he said, "What is your name?" He said, "Bakhtnasar." So he said to his servants, "Carry him," and they carried him to him. He nursed him until he recovered, clothed him, and gave him provision. Then the Israelite announced his departure, and Bakhtnasar wept. The Israelite said, "What makes you weep?" He said, "I weep because you have done to me what you have done, and I find nothing with which to repay you." He said, "Yes, a small thing: if you become king, obey me." The other kept following him and saying, "You are mocking me." What prevented him from giving him what he asked was only that he thought he was mocking him. The Israelite wept and said, "I know what prevents you from giving me what I asked of you, except that God wills to carry out what He has decreed and written in His Book, and the ages have struck their blows." One day Sayhun, who was the king of Persia at Babel, said: "What if we send a vanguard to Sham?" They said, "What harm would it do you if you did?" He said, "Whom do you see [fit for it]?" They said, "So-and-so." He sent a man and gave him a hundred thousand, and Bakhtnasar went out in his kitchen; he had gone out only to eat in his kitchen. When he arrived in Sham and the commander of the vanguard saw that the land of God had more horsemen and sturdy foot soldiers, this weighed on his mind, so he did not ask them about anything. [Note in al-Tha'labi's ʿArāʾis al-majālis: "So he did not ask them about anything."] He said: Bakhtnasar began to sit in the gatherings of the people of Sham and say: "What prevents you from raiding Babel? If you raided it, nothing beneath its treasury would be left." They said, "We do not fight well." He said, "But if you raided it—" They said, "We do not fight well, and we will not fight until I have passed through the gatherings of the people of Sham." Then they returned, and the vanguard informed their king of what he had seen. Bakhtnasar began saying to the cavalry of the king: "If the king had summoned me, I would have told him something other than what so-and-so told him." This was reported to [the king], so he summoned him and told him the news, saying: "When so-and-so saw that the land of God had more horsemen and sturdy foot soldiers, this magnified itself in his heart, and he did not ask them about anything. I, however, did not leave a gathering in Sham without sitting with its people, and I said to them such-and-such, and they said to me such-and-such," which is what Sa'id ibn Jubayr mentioned he had said to them. The vanguard said to Bakhtnasar: "You have disgraced me [for] a hundred thousand for you, and you turn away from what you said." [Note: thus in the History of al-Tabari, Leiden edition. In the original: "in your company" (sahibtani), a distortion.] He said: "If you gave me the treasury of Babel's wealth, I would not turn away; the ages have struck their blows." The king said: "What if we send a flying cavalry squadron to Sham? If they find an opening, they will advance, and if not, they will turn back from what they cannot achieve." They said, "What harm would it do you if you did?" He said, "Whom do you see [fit for it]?" They said, "So-and-so." He said, "Rather, the man who told me what he told me." So he summoned Bakhtnasar and sent him, and he selected four thousand of their horsemen with him. They set out and roamed through the midst of the dwellings. They took captives as God willed, but they did not destroy and did not kill. King Sayhun died [Note: thus in al-Tha'labi's ʿArāʾis al-majālis, p. 336, Halabi edition. In the original: "and he threw in a funeral sahuran."] They said: "Appoint a man [as ruler]." They said: "Take it slowly until you reach your companions, for they are your horsemen; they will not overturn anything against you. Wait." So they waited until Bakhtnasar came with the captives and what he had with him. He distributed them among the people. They said: "We have seen no one more worthy of the kingship than this man," and so they made him king.

⁕ Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal informed me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib say: Bakhtnasar prevailed over Sham, destroyed Bayt al-Maqdis, and killed them. Then he came to Damascus, and there he found blood boiling on a dunghill (kaba), that is, a refuse heap. He asked them, "What is this blood?" They said, "We found our fathers upon this, and whenever the dunghill is struck, it [the blood] rises." He said: He then killed seventy thousand of the Muslims and others over that blood, and it subsided.

And others said: By this is meant a people from Persia. They said: In the first instance there was no fighting.

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours possessed of great might, and they roamed between the dwellings﴾: "It is those who came to them from Persia to spy on their affairs and to listen to their talk, with whom was Bakhtnasar, who memorized their sayings from among his companions. Then the Persians returned, and there was no fighting. The Children of Israel were victorious over them. This is the promise of the first."

⁕ al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿We sent against you servants of Ours possessed of great might﴾: "An army that came to them from Persia to spy on their affairs," and then he mentioned something similar.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours possessed of great might﴾: "That is, those who came to them from Persia," and then he mentioned something similar.

The commentary on His words, "Then We gave you back your turn of victory over them and aided you with wealth and sons and made you more numerous in manpower" (﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَا لَكُمُ الْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَأَمْدَدْنَاكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا﴾).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Then We gave you, O Children of Israel, the upper hand over those people whom He, may His praise be exalted, described as having been sent against you. That turn of victory and return was in your favour against them. As al-Suddi mentioned in his report, the Children of Israel attacked them, inflicted losses on them, and recovered what was in their hands. According to others, it was the release by the king who had attacked them of their captives, and the return to them of what he had taken of their wealth, without fighting. According to the saying of Ibn Abbas, transmitted by Ata' from him, it was God giving them power over their enemy Jalut (Goliath) until they killed him. We have mentioned all of these with their chains of transmission earlier.

﴿وَأَمْدَدْنَاكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾ means: We increased for you, in addition to what We had given you, wealth and sons.

And His words, ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا﴾:

He means: We made you more numerous in the number of those who go forth to fight than they were. The people of interpretation (ta'wil, the science of explaining the meaning of the Qur'an) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words, ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا﴾: that is, in number, and that was in the time of Dawud (David).

Musa narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا﴾, he says: in number.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, and they both said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words, ﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَا لَكُمُ الْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾, to the Children of Israel, after the defeat had been theirs and the others had withdrawn from them, ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ أَكْثَرَ نَفِيرًا﴾, he said: We made you, after this, more numerous.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَا لَكُمُ الْكَرَّةَ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: then the turn was returned to the Children of Israel.
