Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Sufyan, concerning His words, ﴿وَأَمْدَدْنَاكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ﴾, he said: four thousand.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 7 (part 1 of 4):

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿If you do good, you do good for your own souls; and if you do evil, it is for them.  So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, [We will send others] to disfigure your faces and to enter the Masjid as they entered it the first time, and to destroy with destruction whatever they overcame.﴾ (7)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the Children of Israel, concerning what He decreed for them in the Torah: ﴿If you do good﴾, O Children of Israel, by obeying God, setting your affairs right, and adhering to His commands and prohibitions, ﴿you do good for your own souls﴾, because by doing such deeds you benefit your own souls, both in this world and in the Hereafter. As for this world, God repels from you those who wish you harm, increases your wealth for you, and adds strength to your strength. As for the Hereafter, God rewards you with His Gardens. ﴿And if you do evil﴾, meaning: if you disobey God and commit what He has forbidden you at that time, then it is against your own souls that you do evil, for by this you incur the displeasure of your Lord upon yourselves. So He gives your enemy power over you in this world, enables those who wish you harm to overcome you, and makes you abide in the humiliating punishment in the Hereafter. He, may His praise be exalted, also said ﴿And if you do evil, it is for them﴾, and the meaning is: "it is for them" (lahā), as in His words ﴿because your Lord has inspired her (lahā)﴾, meaning: inspired to her.
* *
As for His words ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes﴾:
That is, when the promise of the second of your two corruptions in the land comes, O Children of Israel, ﴿to disfigure your faces﴾, meaning: so that the arrival of that promise for the second time disfigures your faces and makes them ugly.

The reciters differed over the reading of His words ﴿to disfigure your faces (liyasū'ū wujūhakum)﴾. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read ﴿liyasū'ū wujūhakum﴾, meaning: so that the powerful servants whom God sends against you disfigure your faces. Those who read this way cited in support of their reading His words ﴿and to enter the Masjid﴾, and said: this is a report about the whole group, so the words ﴿liyasū'ū﴾ should likewise be read in the plural. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read ﴿liyasū'a wujūhakum﴾ in the singular and with the letter yā’ (ya), and this may bear two interpretations. One of them is what I have mentioned: that the arrival of the promise disfigures your faces. The other is: God disfigures your faces. Whoever directs the interpretation toward "the arrival of the promise disfigures your faces" makes the answer to "when" (idhā) a deleted element, which is dispensed with by what appears, and that deleted element is "came" (jā'), so the sense is: "When the promise of the Hereafter came, to disfigure your faces, it came." Whoever directs the interpretation toward "God disfigures your faces" also has a deleted element in the sentence, dispensed with here by what appears, but the deleted element in this case is other than "came"; so the meaning becomes: "When the promise of the Hereafter came, We sent them, so that God disfigures your faces," and the omitted element is "We sent them," which is the answer to "when" in that case.

Some of the Kufan Arabic grammarians read ﴿linasū'a wujūhakum﴾ (in the first person plural), as a report from God, may His name be blessed and exalted, about Himself.

The arrival of the promise of the second time was at the time of their killing of Yahya.
Mention of the narration to that effect, and report of what came to them from God at that time:
As follows:
⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, in the report whose chain of transmission we mentioned earlier, that a man from the Children of Israel saw in a dream that the ruin of Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis) and the destruction of the Children of Israel would be at the hands of an orphan boy, the son of a widow from the people of Babylon, called Bukhtnassar. They used to believe in dreams, and their dreams would come true. So he set out to seek him, until he reached his mother's house while he was gathering firewood. When he came with a bundle of wood on his head, he threw it down, sat in a corner of the house, and embraced him. Then he gave him three dirhams and said: "Buy us food and drink with these." He bought meat with one dirham, bread with another, and wine with the third, and they ate and drank. On the second day he did the same, and on the third day he did the same. Then he said to him: "I wish that you would write me a guarantee of safety if you should ever become king for a day." He said: "Are you mocking me?" He said: "I am not mocking you, but what harm is it to you to put me under an obligation to you?" His mother spoke to him, saying: "What harm is it to you if that happens? If it does not, it will not diminish anything of yours." So he wrote him a guarantee of safety. He said: "What if I come while the people are around you, and they have stood between me and you? Give me a sign by which I may recognize you." He said: "We will raise your document on a reed, and I will recognize you by it." Then he clothed him and gave him gifts.

Then the king of the Children of Israel used to honour Yahya ibn Zakariya, bring him near his council, and consult him on his affairs, and he would not decide a matter without him. He wished to marry the daughter of one of his wives, so he asked Yahya about it, and Yahya forbade him to marry her, saying: "I am not content for her for you." When this reached her mother, she resented Yahya for forbidding the king to marry her daughter. So the girl's mother, when the king sat down over his wine, dressed her in thin red garments, perfumed her, and adorned her with jewelry. It was also said that she put a black cloak over that, and sent her to the king, instructing her to pour him drink and to offer herself to him; if he wanted her, she should refuse him until he gave her what she asked. When he gave it to her, she was to ask him to bring the head of Yahya ibn Zakariya on a platter. She did so: she kept pouring for him and offering herself. When drink took hold of him, he sought to have her, but she said: "I will not, until you give me what I ask of you." He said: "What is it you ask of me?" She said: "I ask you to send to Yahya ibn Zakariya and have his head brought to me on this platter." He said: "Woe to you, ask me for something other than this." She said: "I do not want to ask you for anything but this." He said: when she insisted on him, he sent for him, and his head was brought, and the head was speaking until it was placed before him, saying: "It is not lawful for you to do that." When morning came, behold, his blood was boiling. He ordered earth to be brought and thrown upon it, but the blood rose above the earth, boiling; he threw earth on it again, and the blood rose above it. He kept throwing earth on it until it reached the wall of the city, and it was still boiling, and it reached Sahabin. It stirred up the people, and he wanted to send against them an army and to appoint a man over them. Then Bukhtnassar came to him, spoke with him, and said: "The man whom you had sent that time was weak, and I have entered the city and heard the speech of its people; so send me." He sent him. Bukhtnassar marched until, when they reached that place, they found the people fortified in their cities against him, and he could not overcome them. When the stay grew hard on them and his companions became hungry, they wanted to return. Then an old woman from the old women of the Children of Israel came out to them and said: "Where is the commander of the army?" He was brought to her, and she said to him: "It has reached me that you intend to return with your troops before conquering this city." He said: "Yes, my stay has been long, and my companions are hungry, and I cannot remain beyond what has already happened to me." She said: "What if I open the city for you; will you give me what I ask of you, and kill whom you are ordered to kill, and refrain when you are ordered to refrain?" He said: "Yes." She said: "When morning comes, divide your army into four quarters, station a quarter at each corner, then raise your hands to heaven and call out: 'We seek victory from You, O God, by the blood of Yahya ibn Zakariya,' for it will then flow down." They did so, and the city collapsed, and they entered from its sides. She said to him: "Kill upon this blood until it is quiet," and she took him to the blood of Yahya, which was upon much dust, and he killed upon it until it became quiet, seventy thousand [men] and women. When the blood was still, she said to him: "Withhold your hand, for God, blessed and exalted, when a prophet is killed, is not pleased until He kills those who killed him, and those who were pleased with his killing." The man of the document came to him with his document, and he refrained from them and from his household. He ruined Jerusalem and ordered that carrion be cast into it, and said: "Whoever casts carrion into it, he has his tribute for that year." The Romans helped him in its destruction, because the Children of Israel had killed Yahya. When Bukhtnassar had destroyed it, he took away with him the notables and chiefs of the Children of Israel, and took Daniel, Aliya, Azariya and Mishael, all of them sons of prophets, and he took with him the head of Jalut. When he came to the land of Babylon, he found that Sahabin had died, so he ruled in his place. The people most honoured by him were Daniel and his companions, and the Magians envied them for this, so they informed on them to him, saying: "Daniel and his companions do not worship your god, and do not eat of your slaughtered animals." He summoned them and questioned them, and they said: "Yes, we have a Lord whom we worship, and we do not eat of your slaughter." He ordered a pit to be dug for them, and they were thrown into it, six of them, and a ravenous lion was thrown in with them to devour them. He said: "Go on, let us eat and drink." They went and ate and drank, then in the morning they found them sitting, with the lion stretched out its forelegs among them, and it had not scratched any of them or harmed them in any way. They also found a man with them; they counted them and found seven. They said: "What about this seventh? There were only six." The seventh came out to them, and he was one of the angels; he slapped the lion with a slap so that it fled into the wild. He stayed among them for seven years, and every wild beast that saw him came to him to mate with him, as he used to do with men. Then he returned, and God restored his kingdom to him, and they were the most honoured of God's creation to him.

Then the Magians informed on him a second time, and they threw a lion into a well that had become ferocious; they used to throw a rock to it and it would seize it. They threw Daniel to it, and the lion stood on one side while Daniel stood on the other, not touching him, and they took him out. Before that, they had dug a trench for them and lit a fire in it, and when it was blazing they threw them into it, but God extinguished it upon them, and nothing of it reached them.

Then Bukhtnassar saw afterwards in his dream an idol whose head was of gold, its neck of silver, its chest of iron, its belly of mixed gold, silver and glass, and its legs of clay. While he was standing looking at it, a rock came down from heaven from the direction of the qibla and struck the idol and reduced it to dust. He awoke in terror and forgot it. He summoned the sorcerers and soothsayers and asked them, saying: "Tell me what I saw." They said: "No, you tell us what you saw, and we will interpret it for you." He said: "I do not know." They said: "Then those youths whom you honour, summon them and ask them. If they do not tell you what you saw, what will you do with them?" He said: "I will kill them." He sent for Daniel and his companions, summoned them, and said: "Tell me what I saw." Daniel said: "No, you tell us what you saw, and we will interpret it for you." He said: "I do not know; I have forgotten it." Daniel said to him: "How can we know a dream you have not told us?" Then he ordered the doorkeeper to kill them. Daniel said to the doorkeeper: "The king has only ordered our killing because of his dream. Delay us three days; if we tell the king his dream, well and good, otherwise strike off our necks." He gave them a respite, and they prayed to God. When the third day came, each of them saw Bukhtnassar's dream separately. They came to the doorkeeper and told him, and he entered upon the king and informed him. He said: "Bring them in to me." Bukhtnassar did not know any of his dream except something they reminded him of. They said to him: "You saw such and such," and they recounted it to him. He said: "You have spoken truly." They said: "We will interpret it for you. As for the idol whose head you saw of gold, it is a good kingdom, like gold, and it had ruled all the earth. As for the neck of silver, it is the kingdom of your son after you, which will rule, and its rule will be good, though not like gold. As for its chest of iron, it is the kingdom of the people of Persia, who will rule after your son, and their rule will be harsh like iron. As for its belly of mixed materials, the kingdom of the Persians will pass away, and people will contend for kingship in every town, so that a king will rule for a day or two, or a month or two, and then be killed, and people will have no stability in that, just as the idol had no stability on two legs of clay. While they were in that state, God, exalted is He, will send a prophet from the land of the Arabs, and He will make him victorious over the remnant of the kingdom of the Persians, the remnant of your son's kingdom and your kingdom, and he will destroy it and annihilate it until nothing of it remains, just as the rock came and demolished the idol." Bukhtnassar then felt kindly towards them and loved them. Then the Magians informed on Daniel a second time, saying: "When Daniel drinks wine, he cannot restrain himself from urinating," and this was a disgrace among them. So Bukhtnassar prepared food for them, and they ate and drank, and he said to the doorkeeper: "Watch the first one who comes out to you needing to urinate, and strike him with the mace; and if he says, 'I am Bukhtnassar,' say, 'You are lying; Bukhtnassar ordered me.'" God withheld urine from Daniel, and the first of the company to rise wanting to urinate was Bukhtnassar, who rose at night hurriedly, dragging his garments. When the doorkeeper saw him, he attacked him, and he said: "I am Bukhtnassar." He said: "You are lying; Bukhtnassar ordered me to kill the first one who came out," and he struck him and killed him.

⁕ Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from Abu al-Mu'alla, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say: God sent against them in the first time Sanharib. He said: Then God gave them back the turn over them, as He had said. He said: Then they disobeyed their Lord and returned to what they had been forbidden, so He sent against them in the second time Bukhtnassar, who killed the fighting men, took captive the offspring, and seized whatever wealth they found, and they entered Bayt al-Maqdis, as God, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿and to enter the Masjid as they entered it the first time, and to destroy with destruction whatever they overcame﴾. They entered it, destroyed it and ruined it, and cast into it whatever they could of filth, menstrual cloths, carrion and refuse. Then God said: ﴿It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you; but if you return, We will return﴾. He had mercy on them, returned their kingdom to them, and released those of the offspring of the Children of Israel who were in their hands, and He said to them: "If you return, We will return." Abu al-Mu'alla said: I know nothing of this except from this report, and it did not promise them a return to their kingdom.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, to disfigure your faces﴾: He said: God sent the king of Persia with an army to Babylon, and appointed Bukhtnassar over them. They came to the Children of Israel and destroyed them, and this was the Hereafter and its promise.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Mujahid, similarly.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ya'la ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When the king Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) laid his neck (in submission), he said: "Three (days). Whoever among you remains behind after them, let him go to his cross." So he invaded Syria, and that was when (Jerusalem) was plundered, and he drove (the people) out of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). He stripped its ornaments and made them into vessels from which to drink wine, and into a table on which to eat pork. He took the Torah with him and then threw it into the fire. Among those he brought back were a hundred youths, among them Daniel, Azariah, Hananiah and Mishael. He said to a man: "Prepare the bodies of these (youths) for me, so that I may choose four of them to serve me." Daniel said to his companions: "They have only been victorious over you because you changed the religion of your fathers. Do not eat the flesh of swine, and do not drink wine." They said to the man who was preparing their bodies: "Would you be willing to feed us a food that is less costly for you to provide than what you feed our companions? If we do not grow fatter than them, then you may do as you see fit." He said: "What (food)?" They said: "Barley bread and leeks." He did so, and they grew fatter than their companions. So Bukhtnassar took them to serve him. While they were in this state, Bukhtnassar saw a dream. He sat up and forgot it. He went back to sleep and saw it again; he got up and forgot it. He then went back to sleep and saw it again, so he went out to the chamber, and forgot it. When morning came, he summoned the scholars and the soothsayers and said: "Tell me what I saw last night, and interpret my dream for me; otherwise, let every one of you go to his cross. Your appointment is the third (day)." They said: "If he had told us his dream, we could have spoken of it," and he said some words I did not memorize. Daniel, whenever one of his relatives passed by him, would say: "If the king had summoned me, I would have told him his dream and interpreted it for him." They began saying: "How foolish this Israelite youth is!" Until an elderly man passed by him, and he said this to him. He returned to the king and informed him. (The king) said: "Go on." (Daniel) said: "His neck was of silver." (The king) said: "Go on." (Daniel) said: "His chest was of iron." (The king) said: "Go on." (Daniel) said: "His belly was of brass." (The king) said: "Go on." (Daniel) said: "His legs were of tin." (The king) said: "Go on." (Daniel) said: "His feet were of clay." (The king) said: "Is this what you saw?" (Daniel) said: "Go on." Then a pebble came and struck his head, then his neck, then his chest, then his belly, then his legs, then his feet. (Daniel) said: "I destroyed him." (The king) said: "What is this?" (Daniel) said: "As for the gold, it is your kingdom. As for the silver, it is the kingdom of your son after you, then the kingdom of your son's son. As for the clay, it is the kingdom of women." He clothed him in a robe, [[Thus in the original text; the word is distorted. In the Book of Daniel, chapter 5: "Then Belshazzar commanded that they clothe Daniel with purple and put a chain of gold around his neck."]] and made him ride (a horse) and paraded him around the town, and he gave him his ring. When Persia saw this, they said: "This is nothing but the affair of this Israelite." They said: "Approach him in the guise of the three youths, and do not mention Daniel to him, for he will not confirm your claim about him." They came to him and said: "These three youths are not upon your religion, and the sign of that is that if you bring them pork and wine, they will neither eat nor drink." So he ordered a great quantity of firewood to be placed, then had them ascend it, then lit a fire under it. Then he went out at the end of the night to urinate, and suddenly they were talking together, and with them was a fourth, who was moving about praying. He said: "Who is this, O Daniel?" (Daniel) said: "This is Gabriel. You have wronged them." He said: "I have wronged them. Let them come down." So he ordered them to be brought down, and they came down. He said: God Most High transformed Bukhtnassar into all kinds of beasts, making his head that of a beast of prey from each kind: the head of a lion among the beasts, and the head of an eagle among the birds. His son became king, and he saw a palm emerge between two tablets, then two lines were written (on them). He summoned the soothsayers and scholars, but they found no knowledge of it. His mother said to him: "If you were to restore Daniel to the position he held with your father, he would inform you." He had (previously) rejected him, so he summoned him and said: "I will restore you to the position you held with my father. So inform me: what are these two lines?" (Daniel) said: "As for restoring my position with your father, I have no need of it. As for these two lines, you will be killed tonight." So he expelled everyone in the palace, all of them, and ordered its gate locked. The doors were locked upon him, and with him he admitted the most trustworthy people of the town, and he had a sword in his hand. He said: "Whoever comes to you from among God's creatures, kill him, even if he says, 'I am so-and-so.'" God sent upon him the sickness of the belly, so he began walking until it was midnight. He slept, and his companion slept. Then the sickness of the belly awakened him, and he went off walking while the other was asleep. He returned and woke him, and (the man) said to him: "I am so-and-so," and he struck him with the sword and killed him.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words (﴿If you do good, you do good for yourselves, and if you do evil, it is against yourselves. Then when the promise of the Hereafter comes﴾): "the last of the two punishments; ﴿to disfigure your faces, and to enter the Sanctuary as they entered it the first time﴾, as their enemy had entered it before that; ﴿and to destroy with destruction whatever they had conquered﴾." So God sent against them in the last (time) Bukhtnassar the Magian, the Babylonian, the most hateful of God's creatures to Him. He took captives, killed, and ruined Bayt al-Maqdis, and afflicted them with a terrible punishment.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said concerning (﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes﴾), of the two times, (﴿to disfigure your faces﴾), he said: "to make your faces ugly." (﴿And to destroy with destruction whatever they had conquered﴾), he said: "to lay waste to what they had conquered with destruction." He said: "That was Bukhtnassar, whom God sent against them in the last time."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "When they corrupted (the land), God sent against them in the last time Bukhtnassar, who ruined the mosques and destroyed whatever they had conquered with destruction."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: "As has reached me": God appointed over the Children of Israel after that, meaning after they killed Sha'ya', a man from among them called Nasha ibn Amus. God sent al-Khadir as a prophet. As has reached me, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to say: "Al-Khadir was only called Khadir (the green one) because he sat on a white barren patch of land, and when he rose from it, it had turned green." He said: The name of al-Khadir, as Wahb ibn Munabbih claimed on the authority of the Children of Israel, was Armiya ibn Halfiya, and he was from the tribe of Harun ibn 'Imran.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 17, verse 7 (part 3 of 4)**

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Zanjawayh told me, both saying: Isma'il ibn Abd al-Karim told us, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Ma'qil told us, from Wahb ibn Munabbih. And Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq, from someone whom he did not suspect, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani. The wording is that of the hadith of Ibn Humayd, that he used to say:

God, blessed and exalted, said to Irmiya (Jeremiah) when He sent him as a prophet to the Children of Israel: "O Irmiya, before I created you I chose you; before I formed you in your mother's womb I sanctified you; before I brought you out from your mother's womb I purified you; before you reached the age of striving I gave you prophethood; before you reached maturity I chose you; and for a great matter I have singled you out."

God then sent Irmiya to that king of the Children of Israel, to strengthen and guide him, and to bring him news from God concerning what lay between him and God.

He said: Then the calamities among the Children of Israel grew great. They committed sins, made lawful what was forbidden, and forgot what God had done for them, and how He had saved them from their enemy Sanharib (Sennacherib) and his armies. God revealed to Irmiya: "Go to your people, the Children of Israel, relate to them what I command you, remind them of My blessing upon them, and make known to them their misdeeds."

Irmiya said: "I am weak unless You strengthen me; I am incapable unless You convey (Your message through) me; I am bound to err unless You guide me; I am forsaken unless You help me; I am humiliated unless You honour me."

God, blessed and exalted, said: "Do you not know that all affairs proceed from My will, and that all hearts and tongues are in My hand? I turn them as I wish, so they obey Me. I am God, and there is nothing like Me. The heavens and the earth and what is in them stand by My word. I spoke to the seas and they understood My speech; I commanded them and they comprehended My command. I set for them a boundary of sand, and they do not transgress My limit. They come with waves like mountains, until when they reach My limit I clothe them in the humbleness of obedience to Me, in fear and in acknowledgement of My command.

"I am with you, and nothing will reach you while I am with you. I have sent you to a great people of My creation, so that you may convey My messages to them, and so that you may deserve the like of the reward of those among them who follow you, which will not diminish their rewards in the least. But if you fall short in it, then you will bear the like of the burden of those who abandon it blindly, which will not diminish their burdens in the least.

"Go to your people and say: God has mentioned to you the righteousness of your fathers, and this moved Him to ask you to repent, O assembly of sons. Ask them how their fathers found the outcome of obedience to Me, and how they found the outcome of disobedience to Me, and whether they knew that anyone before them who obeyed Me was made wretched by his obedience, or who disobeyed Me was made happy by his disobedience. For beasts remember their good homelands, and so they return to them. But these people have pastured in meadows of destruction.

"As for their rabbis and monks, they have taken My servants as slaves, so that they worship them instead of Me, and they have ruled over them without My Book, until they made them ignorant of My command, made them forget My remembrance, and deceived them concerning Me.

"As for their leaders and commanders, they have been insolent toward My blessing, felt secure from My plan, cast aside My Book, forgot My covenant, and altered My way. So My servants submitted to them with the obedience that is fitting only for Me. They obey them in their disobedience toward Me, and follow them in the innovations they introduce into My religion, out of audacity toward Me, deception, and slander against Me and My messengers. Glory be to My majesty, the exaltedness of My station and the greatness of My affair. Is it fitting for a human to be obeyed in disobedience to Me? Is it fitting for Me to create servants and make them lords other than Me?

"As for their reciters and jurists, they worship in the mosques and adorn their construction for other than Me, seeking the world through religion. They gain understanding in them for other than knowledge, and they learn in them for other than action.

"As for the sons of the prophets, they are numerous, subdued, and plundered. They plunge in with those who plunge, and they wish from Me the like of the victory of their fathers and the honour with which I honoured them, claiming that none is more worthy of that than they are, without truthfulness, without reflection, and without contemplation. They do not remember how their fathers were patient for My sake, how earnest they were in My affair when the plunderers plundered, and how they gave up their souls and their blood, and were patient and truthful, until My affair became mighty and My religion became manifest.

"So I was patient with these people, perhaps they would respond. I prolonged (My forbearance) toward them and overlooked them, perhaps they would return. I multiplied and extended their lifespans, perhaps they would remember. I gave them every excuse in all of this. I sent rain down upon them from the sky, made the earth grow for them, clothed them with well-being, and made them victorious over their enemy, yet they increase only in transgression and distance from Me. How long will this go on? Do they wrestle with Me, or do they deceive Me?

"I swear by My might that I will surely bring upon them a trial in which the forbearing will be bewildered, and in which the opinion of the one of opinion and the wisdom of the wise will go astray. Then I will surely set over them a tyrant, harsh and insolent, whom I will clothe with awe, and from whose breast I will remove compassion, mercy and eloquence. He will be followed by a multitude and a mass like the darkness of the dark night. He will have armies like pieces of clouds, and mounts like dust-storms. The rustling of his banners will be like the flight of vultures, and the charge of his horsemen like the swoop of eagles."

Then God revealed to Irmiya: "I will destroy the Children of Israel through Yafith (Japheth), and Yafith is the people of Babylon, who are descendants of Yafith ibn Nuh (Noah)."

When Irmiya heard the revelation of his Lord, he cried out, wept, tore his garments, threw dust upon his head, and said: "Cursed is the day on which I was born, and the day on which I received the Torah, and it is one of the worst of my days that I was born in it. You have left me, the last of the prophets, only for what is worse for me. Had He intended good for me, He would not have made me the last of the prophets among the Children of Israel. Because of me misfortune and destruction will befall them."

When God heard the humble supplication and weeping of Irmiya, and how he spoke, He called out to him: "O Irmiya, is this hard upon you, what I have revealed to you?"

He said: "Yes, O my Lord. Let me die before I see among the Children of Israel what does not gladden me."

God said: "By My glorious might, I will not destroy Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) and the Children of Israel until the command concerning that comes from you."

At that, Irmiya rejoiced at what his Lord had said to him, his soul was comforted, and he said: "No, by the One who sent Moses and his prophets with the truth, I will never command my Lord to destroy the Children of Israel."

Then he went to the king of the Children of Israel and informed him of what God had revealed to him. The king rejoiced and was glad, and said: "If our Lord punishes us, it will be for many sins we have sent ahead for ourselves. And if He pardons us, it will be by His power."

Then they remained for three years after this revelation, increasing only in disobedience and persistence in evil. This was when their destruction drew near. Revelation became scarce because they did not remember the Hereafter, and it ceased for them because the world and its affairs had diverted them.

Their king said to them: "O Children of Israel, desist from what you are upon before the punishment of God seizes you, and before a people who have no mercy for you are sent against you. Your Lord is near in accepting repentance, His hands are outstretched with good, and He is merciful to whoever repents to Him."

But they refused to turn away from anything they were doing.

God had cast into the heart of Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) ibn Nujur Zadhan ibn Sanharib ibn Daryas ibn Nimrud ibn Falikh ibn Abir ibn Nimrud, the one who argued with Ibrahim (Abraham) concerning his Lord, the desire to march toward Bayt al-Maqdis, and to do there what his forefather Sanharib had intended to do. So he set out with six hundred thousand banners, intending the people of Bayt al-Maqdis.

When he set out on his march, news reached the king of the Children of Israel that Bukhtnassar had approached with his armies, intending you. So the king sent for Irmiya, and he came. The king said: "O Irmiya, where is what you told us, that your Lord revealed to you that He would not destroy the people of Bayt al-Maqdis until the command concerning that came from you?"

Irmiya said to the king: "My Lord does not break His promise, and I trust in Him."

When the appointed term drew near, the end of their kingdom approached, and God resolved to destroy them, God sent an angel from Him and said to him: "Go to Irmiya and ask him for a legal ruling (istaftihi)," and He commanded him concerning what he should ask about.

The angel came to Irmiya, having appeared to him in the form of a man from the Children of Israel. Irmiya said to him: "Who are you?"

He said: "A man from the Children of Israel who wishes to ask you a ruling concerning some matter of mine."

Irmiya gave him permission, and the angel said: "O prophet of God, I have come to ask you about my kinsfolk. I have maintained ties with their kin as God commanded me, I have done nothing to them but good, and I have withheld no honour from them. Yet my kindness toward them only increases them in provoking Me. So give me a ruling concerning them, O prophet of God."

He said to him: "Be good in what lies between you and God, maintain the ties God commanded you to maintain, and rejoice in good," and he turned away from him.

He stayed for some days, then came back to him in the form of that same man, and sat before him.

Irmiya said: "Who are you?"

He said: "I am the man who came to you to ask about my family."

The prophet of God said: "Have their characters not yet become clear to you, and have you not seen from them what you love?"

He said: "O prophet of God, by the One who sent you with the truth, I know of no kindness that any person has shown to his kin that I have not shown to them, and more than that."

The prophet said: "Return to your family and be good to them. I ask God, who sets right His righteous servants, to set right your relations among yourselves, to gather you upon His pleasure, and to keep you away from His wrath."

The angel went away from him.

Then he stayed for some days, while Bukhtnassar and his armies had camped around Bayt al-Maqdis, with a host of his people like swarms of locusts. The Children of Israel were struck with severe terror at them, and this weighed heavily upon the king of the Children of Israel. He summoned Irmiya and said: "O prophet of God, where is what God promised you?"

He said: "I trust in my Lord."

Then the king came to Irmiya, who was sitting on the wall of Bayt al-Maqdis, laughing and rejoicing in the victory of his Lord that had been promised to him. He sat before him, and Irmiya said to him: "Who are you?"

He said: "I am the one who came to you twice concerning my family."

The prophet said: "Has the time not come for them to refrain from what they persist in?"

The king said to him: "O prophet of God, every harm that I suffered from them before today I endured patiently, knowing that their aim in that was my anger. But when I came to them today, I saw them engaged in a deed that does not please God, and that God, mighty and majestic, does not love."

The prophet of God said: "What deed did you see them doing?"

He said: "O prophet of God, I saw them engaged in a great deed that incurs God's wrath. Had they been upon what they were upon before today, my anger would not have grown severe against them. I would have been patient with them and hoped for them. But today I became angry for the sake of God and for your sake. So I came to you to inform you of their condition, and I ask you by God who sent you with the truth, to pray to your Lord against them, that He destroy them."

Irmiya said: "O Possessor of the heavens and the earth, if they are upon truth and right, then spare them. But if they are upon Your wrath and a deed You do not approve, then destroy them."

The word had not left Irmiya's mouth before God sent a thunderbolt from the sky upon Bayt al-Maqdis. The place of the sacrifice (al-qurban) caught fire, and the earth swallowed up seven of its gates.

When Irmiya saw that, he cried out, tore his garments, threw dust upon his head, and said: "O King of the heavens and the earth, in Your hand is the dominion of everything, and You are the most merciful of the merciful. Where is Your promise which You made to me?"

Irmiya was called out to: "They were not struck by what struck them except because of your ruling which you gave to Our messenger."

The Prophet (ﷺ) was certain that it was his ruling, which he had given three times, and that he was the messenger of his Lord.

Then Irmiya flew away until he mingled with the wild beasts. Bukhtnassar and his armies entered Bayt al-Maqdis, trod upon Syria, killed the Children of Israel until he annihilated them, and laid Bayt al-Maqdis waste. He ordered each of his soldiers to fill his shield with dirt and then hurl it into Bayt al-Maqdis. They threw the dirt into it until they filled it.

Then he turned back toward the land of Babylon, taking with him the captives of the Children of Israel. He ordered them to gather everyone who was in Bayt al-Maqdis, all of them, and every young and old of the Children of Israel was gathered before him. He selected from them seventy thousand boys.

When the spoils of his army were brought out, and he wished to divide them among them, the kings who were with him said to him: "O king, all our spoils are yours, but divide among us these boys whom you have chosen from the Children of Israel." He did so, and each man received four boys.

Among those boys were Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah, Mishael, seven thousand from the household of Dawud (David), eleven thousand from the tribe of Yusuf ibn Ya'qub (Joseph son of Jacob) and his brother Binyamin (Benjamin), eight thousand from the tribe of Ashir ibn Ya'qub, fourteen thousand from the tribe of Zabulun ibn Ya'qub and Naftali ibn Ya'qub, four thousand from the tribe of Yahudha ibn Ya'qub, four thousand from the tribes of Ruben and Levi, the two sons of Ya'qub, and whoever remained of the Children of Israel.

Bukhtnassar divided them into three groups: one third he left in Syria, one third he took captive, and one third he killed. He carried off the vessels of Bayt al-Maqdis until he brought them to Babylon, and he took the seventy thousand boys until he brought them to Babylon.

This was the first calamity that God sent upon the Children of Israel, because of their innovations and their wrongdoing.

When Bukhtnassar turned back from them toward Babylon with the captives of the Children of Israel that were with him, Irmiya approached on a donkey of his, with a container of grape juice (?) with him. Then he recounted his story, when God caused him to die for one hundred years, then raised him up again, then the account of Bukhtnassar's dream and the matter of Daniel, the destruction of Bukhtnassar, the return to Syria of the remnant of the Children of Israel who were in the hands of Bukhtnassar's companions after his destruction, the rebuilding of Bayt al-Maqdis, and the affair of Uzayr (Ezra) and how God restored the Torah to him.

⁕ Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Salamah told us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: Then the Children of Israel after that committed acts of wrongdoing, meaning after the death of Uzayr; and God returned to them, and sent among them Umar ibn Abd Allah ibn Urwa, from Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, that he said, while relating the killing of Yahya ibn Zakariyya:

"Yahya ibn Zakariyya was not killed except because of a prostitute from among the prostitutes of the Children of Israel. There was a king among them, and Yahya ibn Zakariyya was under the authority of that king. The daughter of that king desired her father and said: 'If only I could marry my father, so that his sovereignty would belong to me alone, without women.' She said to him: 'O father, marry me,' and she invited him to herself. He said to her: 'O daughter, Yahya ibn Zakariyya does not permit us this.' She said: 'Who will deal with Yahya ibn Zakariyya for me? He has restricted me and prevented me from marrying my father, so that I may take over his kingdom and his worldly affairs, to the exclusion of women.'"

He said: "So she commanded the jesters, and she plotted that through them to kill Yahya ibn Zakariyya. She said: 'Go in to him and amuse him, and when you have finished, he will give you a ruling. Say: "The blood of Yahya ibn Zakariyya, and accept nothing else."'"

The king's name was Rawad, and his daughter, the prostitute, was named. Whenever the king among them spoke and lied, or promised and broke his word, he was deposed and someone else was put in his place. So when they amused him and his amazement at them increased, he said: "Ask me, and I will give you (anything)."

They said: "We ask you for the blood of Yahya ibn Zakariyya; give it to us."

He said: "Woe to you! Ask me for something other than this."

They said: "We will ask you for nothing other than it."

He feared for his kingship, that if he broke his word to them, his deposition would be justified by that. So he sent for Yahya ibn Zakariyya, who was sitting in his prayer niche (mihrab) praying. They slaughtered him over a basin, then cut off his head. A man carried it in his hand while the blood was carried in the basin with him.

He said: "He came out carrying the head until he stood with it before the king, and the head was speaking in the hand of the one who carried it: 'This is not lawful for you.'"

A man from the Children of Israel said: "O king, if you were to grant me this blood?"

He said: "And what will you do with it?"

He said: "I will purify the earth with it, for he had made it narrow for us."

He said: "Give him this blood." So he took it, put it in a jar, then went with it to a room in the sanctuary, placed the jar there, and locked it in. It boiled in the jar until it came out from under the door of the room in which it was.

When the man saw that, he was alarmed by it. He took it out and placed it in a wasteland, and it kept boiling. Calamities among them grew great. Some of them said: "Let it remain in its place in the sacrifice (al-qurban), and let it not be moved."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 7 (part 4 of 4):

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq said: When God raised Jesus from among them, and they killed Yahya ibn Zakariyya [some people say: they killed Zakariyya], God sent against them a king of the kings of Babylon called Khardus. He marched toward them with the people of Babylon until he entered upon them in al-Sham. When he prevailed over them, he commanded a chief of his army called Nabur Zadan, the master of the killing, and said to him: "I had sworn by my god that if we prevailed over the people of Bayt al-Maqdis, I would kill them until their blood flowed in the midst of my camp, unless I found no one to kill." He ordered him to kill them until Nabur Zadan had carried this out upon them. He entered Bayt al-Maqdis and stood in the place where they used to offer their sacrifices, and he found there blood boiling. He asked them, saying: "O Children of Israel, what is the matter with this blood that boils? Tell me its story and do not conceal from me any part of its affair." They said: "This is the blood of a sacrifice that we had offered, but it was not accepted from us; that is why it boils as you see. We have offered sacrifices for eight hundred years, and they were accepted from us except this one sacrifice." He said: "You have not told me the truth." They said to him: "If it were as in the first of our time, it would have been accepted from us, but kingship, prophethood and revelation have ceased from us, and therefore it was not accepted from us." Then Nabur Zadan slaughtered on that blood seven hundred and seventy souls from their leaders, but it did not calm. He then ordered seven hundred boys from among them to be slaughtered upon the blood, but it did not calm. He ordered seven thousand of their adherents and their wives to be slaughtered upon the blood, and it did not cool nor calm. When Nabur Zadan saw that the blood would not calm, he said to them: "Woe to you, O Children of Israel, be truthful with me and be patient over the command of your Lord, for you have ruled long on earth, doing there whatever you wished, before I leave none of you who kindles a fire, neither female nor male, without killing him." When they saw the hardship and severity of the killing, they told him the story truthfully. They said to him: "This is the blood of a prophet from among us, who used to forbid us many things that anger God. Had we obeyed him in them, it would have been more rightly guided for us. He used to inform us of your affair, but we did not believe him, so we killed him, and this is his blood." Nabur Zadan said to them: "What was his name?" They said: "Yahya ibn Zakariyya." He said: "Now you have told me the truth; with the like of this your Lord takes vengeance upon you." When Nabur Zadan saw that they had spoken truthfully to him, he fell down prostrating and said to those around him: "Close the gates, the gates of the city, and expel whoever is here of Khardus's army." He was alone among the Children of Israel and then said: "O Yahya ibn Zakariyya, my Lord and your Lord knows what has befallen your people on your account, and what has been killed of them on your account. So be calm by God's leave before I leave none of your people alive." The blood of Yahya ibn Zakariyya became calm by God's leave. Nabur Zadan lifted the killing from them and said: "I have believed in what the Children of Israel believed in, and I have confirmed and become certain that there is no lord but Him. Had there been another with Him, it would not be right; had He had a partner, the heavens and the earth would not have held firm; had He had a son, it would not be right. Blessed and sanctified is He, glorified, magnified and exalted, the King of kings, to whom belongs the dominion of the seven heavens and the earth and what is in them and between them, and He is Able over all things. To Him belong forbearance, knowledge, might and majesty. He is the One who spread out the earth and cast into it firm mountains lest it shake, and so it is fitting that my Lord be and that His dominion be." God then revealed to a chief among the remnant of the prophets that Nabur Zadan is a ḥabbūr, a truthful one, and that ḥabbūr in Hebrew means "the word of faith." Nabur Zadan said to the Children of Israel: "O Children of Israel, the enemy of God, Khardus, has commanded me to kill you until your blood flows in the midst of his army, and I am not able to disobey him." They said to him: "Do what you have been commanded." So he ordered them, and they dug a trench, and he ordered their property—horses, mules, donkeys, cattle, sheep, and camels—to be brought, and he slaughtered them until the blood flowed through the camp. He ordered the previously slain to be thrown onto the slaughtered livestock until they were on top of them, and Khardus thought only that what was in the trench were Children of Israel. When the blood reached his camp, he sent to Nabur Zadan: "Lift from them, for their blood has reached me, and I have avenged myself upon them for what they did." Then he withdrew from them to the land of Babylon, having annihilated the Children of Israel or nearly so. This was the final calamity which God brought upon the Children of Israel. God, mighty is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture that you would cause corruption in the earth twice, and you would become exceedingly arrogant. So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they went through the homes; and it was a promise fulfilled. Then We gave you the return against them, and We aided you with wealth and sons and made you more numerous in manpower. If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, it is for them. So when the promise of the last came, to make your faces grievous and to enter the Masjid as they entered it the first time and to destroy what they had conquered with total destruction. It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you; but if you return, We will return, and We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers.﴾ The promise of God is true. The first calamity was Bakhtnassar and his armies; then God gave you the return against them. The final calamity was Khardus and his armies, and it was the greater of the two calamities: in it their lands were ruined, their men were killed, and their children and women were taken captive. God, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿and to destroy what they had conquered with total destruction﴾. Then God restored them and increased their numbers and scattered them through their lands. Then they altered and introduced innovations, replaced their Book with another, committed sins, made lawful what was forbidden, and neglected the limits.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Abu ʿAttab, a man of the Taghlib tribe who had been a Christian for a long part of his life, and then later embraced Islam, recited the Qur'an, and gained understanding of the religion. It was reported that he had been a Christian for forty years, and then he lived forty years in Islam. He said: The last of the prophets of the Children of Israel was a prophet whom God sent to them. He said to them: "O Children of Israel, God says to you: I have taken away your voices, and I have hated you because of your abundant innovations." They intended to kill him, and God, blessed and exalted, said to him: "Go to them and strike a parable for Me and for them. Say to them: God, blessed and exalted, says to you: Judge between Me and My vineyard. Did I not choose for it the land, and make the soil good for it, and enclose it with a hedge, and plant it with sorghum, thorns, hedges and thistles, and surround it with My mantle, and protect it from the world, and favour it? Yet it met Me with thorns and trunks, and every tree that is not edible. I did not choose the land for this, nor make the soil good for this, nor enclose it with a hedge, nor plant it with sorghum, nor surround it with My mantle, nor protect it from the world. I favoured you and completed My blessing upon you, and then you encountered Me with everything I dislike of disobedience and opposition to My command. Indeed the donkey knows its manger; indeed the cow knows its master. I have sworn by My mighty might and My strong arm that I will surely take My mantle, and I will surely raze the wall, and I will make you beneath the feet of the world." He said: They leapt upon their prophet and killed him, so God imposed humiliation upon them and removed kingship from them. They are not among any nation except that they have humiliation, abasement and a poll-tax they pay, and kingship is among others of mankind; and so they will remain as they are forever, as long as they are upon what they are upon.

He said: This is what has reached us of the compilation of the reports of the Children of Israel.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿So when the promise of the last came, to make your faces grievous and to enter the Masjid as they entered it the first time and to destroy what they had conquered with total destruction﴾: "The last was far more severe than the first. The first was only defeat, while the last was total destruction; Bakhtnassar burned the Torah until not a single letter of it remained, and he ruined the Masjid."

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Jesus, son of Mary, sent Yahya ibn Zakariyya, along with twelve of the disciples, to teach the people. Among what he forbade them was marrying a brother's daughter. The king of theirs had a niece who pleased him, and he wished to marry her, and she had a request to be granted each day. When her mother heard of this, she said to her: 'When you enter upon the king and he asks you for your request, say: My request is that you slaughter Yahya ibn Zakariyya for me.' When she entered upon him, he asked her for her request, and she said: 'My request is that you slaughter Yahya ibn Zakariyya.' He said: 'Ask for something other than this!' She said: 'I ask you for nothing but this.' When she refused him, he called Yahya, called for a basin, and slaughtered him. A drop of his blood fell upon the ground and continued to boil until God sent Bakhtnassar against them. An old woman from the Children of Israel came to him and guided him to that blood. God cast into his soul that he should kill upon that blood from among them until it became calm, so he killed seventy thousand of them of one age, and it calmed."

* *

As for His words ﴿and to enter the Masjid as they entered it the first time﴾:
He means: and let your enemy whom I send against you enter the Masjid of Bayt al-Maqdis, overpowering you and prevailing over you, as they entered it the first time when you committed the first corruption in the earth.

As for His words ﴿and to destroy what they had conquered with total destruction﴾, He means: and let them destroy, with total destruction, what they overcame of your lands. It is said from this: "dammartu al-balad" (I destroyed the land) when I ruined it and destroyed its people; and "tabara, tabran wa tabaran," and "tabbartuhu atabbaruhu tatbiran," and from it is God's saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿and do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction﴾, meaning: perdition.

Similar to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said regarding ﴿and to destroy what they had conquered with total destruction﴾: "Destruction."

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah regarding ﴿and to destroy what they had conquered with total destruction﴾, he said: "They will destroy what they overcame with total destruction."

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you; but if you return [to sin], We will return [to punishment]. And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Perhaps your Lord, O Children of Israel, will have mercy on you after His vengeance upon you through the people whom God will send against you, so that they may bring evil to your faces and enter the Sanctuary as they entered it the first time, and so that He will rescue you from their hands, lift you out of the humiliation He will bring upon you, and raise you from the abjection to which you will be reduced, and then give you honor after that. "Perhaps" (ʿasā) from God is a binding certainty, and God did this for them: their numbers grew afterward, He raised their lowliness, and He made kings and prophets from among them. Then He, majestic is His praise, said to them: "But if you return," O assembly of Children of Israel, to disobedience of Me, opposition to My command, and killing of My messengers, "We will return," against you with killing and captivity, and the imposition of humiliation and abasement upon you. They returned, and God returned against them with His punishment and the imposition of His wrath upon them.

Those of the exegetes said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said this:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿAtiyyah narrated to us, from ʿUmar ibn Thabit, from his father, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you; but if you return, We will return﴾: He said: They returned, and He returned. Then they returned, and He returned. Then they returned, and He returned. He said: So God set over them three kings of the kings of Persia: Sindabadan, Shahrbadan, and another.

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: God, blessed and exalted, said after the first and the last [transgression]: ﴿It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you; but if you return, We will return﴾. He said: They returned, so God set the believers over them.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: ﴿It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you﴾, so God returned to them with His kindness and mercy. ﴿But if you return, We will return.﴾ He said: The people returned to the worst of what they were present for, so God sent against them whatever of His vengeance and punishment He willed. Then the conclusion of that was that God sent against them this tribe of the Arabs, and they are in torment at their hands until the Day of Resurrection. God, mighty and majestic, said in another verse: ﴿And when your Lord declared that He would surely send against them until the Day of Resurrection...﴾ — the verse — so God sent against them this tribe of the Arabs.

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, who said: ﴿It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you; but if you return, We will return﴾. They returned, so God sent against them Muhammad (ﷺ), and they now give the jizyah from their hand while they are humbled.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning the words of God Most High ﴿It may be that your Lord will have mercy upon you﴾, said after this: ﴿But if you return﴾ — for what you did in the like of this, killing Yahya and other prophets — ﴿We will return﴾ against you with the like of this.

* *

As for His words ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾:

The exegetes differed concerning its interpretation. Some of them said: And We have made Hell a prison for them, where they are imprisoned.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Masʿadah narrated to us, saying: Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu ʿImran concerning ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾: He said: A prison.

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me... from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾, he says: God made their abode in it.

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾: He said: A confining place, a restraining one.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾, he says: A prison.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning God's words ﴿hasiran﴾: He said: They will be confined therein.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾: He said: They will be confined therein.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾: A prison in which they are imprisoned, confined therein.

ʿAli ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾: He says: A prison.

Others said: Its meaning is: And We have made Hell for the disbelievers a bed and a cradle.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, who said: al-Hasan said: "Hasir" means a bedding and a couch. Al-Hasan, by this statement, took the meaning of hasir in this place to be the mat that is spread out and laid down, since the Arabs call a small carpet a ḥaṣīr. Thus al-Hasan directed the meaning of the speech to mean that God Most High made Hell for those who disbelieve in Him a carpet and a cradle, as He said: ﴿For them from Hell is a bed, and above them are coverings﴾. This is a good direction and a sound interpretation. As for the others, they directed it to being a form of ḥaṣr, which is confinement. I have clarified this with its evidence in Surat al-Baqarah. The Arabs also call a king ḥaṣīr, in the sense that he is confined (maḥṣūr), i.e., veiled from the people, as Labid said:

"And a gathering of strong-necked men, as if they were jinn at the gate of the ḥaṣīr standing..."

[Footnote: The verse is in the Diwan of Labid (Leiden 1891, p. 39), where the reading is "beside the edge of the ḥaṣīr." Its reading in Majaz al-Quran of Abu ʿUbaydah (p. 371) and in Lisan al-ʿArab (qawm) is as the author cites here. They said: a king is called ḥaṣīr because he is veiled. Al-maqamah and al-maqam mean a sitting-place; maqamat al-nas are their assemblies, and al-maqamah means the nobles; al-ghulb is the plural of aghlab, an adjective from ghalaba ghalaban (like faraha farahan), when the neck is thick. In Lisan (hasar), this verse is cited as the author's reading, with "wa-qamaqim" in place of "wa-maqamah," and the other reading is noted. Then it says: al-hasir is the confined place, and in the revelation: "And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers," al-Qutaybi said: it is from haṣartuhu, I confined him, so he is mahṣur, and this is his ḥaṣīr, i.e., his place of confinement.]

By ḥaṣīr is meant the king. It is also said of the miser that he is ḥaṣūr and ḥaṣir, because he withholds what he has of wealth from those in need, and confines it from spending, as al-Akhtal said:

"A drinker, delighted with the cup, who kept me company, not stingy and not a hoarder of it..."

[Footnote: The explanation of this verse was given earlier in the third volume of this commentary (p. 255).]

It is also reported as sa'ar. From it comes ḥaṣr in logic, since it is impossible for him, and his being held back when he wants it. From it also comes ḥaṣūr regarding women, since that is impossible for him and he refrains from intercourse. Likewise ḥaṣr regarding excretion means being held back from leaving. The root of all this is one, though its wording differs. As for ḥaṣīrān, they are the two sides, as al-Tirimmah said:

"Little by little, his need was fulfilled, then he was carried up to the height, over every spread-out one of the two ḥaṣīrs, a fat one..."

[Footnote: The verse is in the Diwan of al-Tirimmah ibn Hakim (Leiden 1927, p. 164). Talla al-shay': he followed it; and tatalla also means: a remnant of his religion remained. ʿUwwiliyat: it was taken toward the height, which is Najd. The ḥaṣīr is a woven mat made of papyrus and reed, then spread out.]

By ḥaṣīrayn is meant the two sides.

The correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is to say: the meaning of ﴿And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers﴾ is a bed and a cradle, not separated from the ḥaṣīr in the sense of a carpet. For if that is so, it combines the meaning of confinement and spreading out. Moreover, ḥaṣīr in the sense of carpet is better known in Arabic speech than in the sense of confinement. When they wish to describe something in the sense of confining something, they say: "he is its ḥāṣir or muḥṣir." As for ḥaṣīr, it is not found in their speech except when you describe it as a passive object, so it takes the form faʿīl with the meaning of maf'ūl. Do you not see Labid's verse: "beside the gate of the ḥaṣīr"? He said "beside the gate of the ḥaṣīr" because he meant "beside the gate of the maḥṣūr," so he shifted maf'ūl to faʿīl. As for faʿīl in the sense of ḥaṣr, meaning describing him as the one who confines, we do not find that in the speech of the Arabs. Therefore I say that al-Hasan's view is more correct in this. Some grammarians of Basra have claimed that this is permissible, but I know of no valid basis for what he said except a remote one: that it may be said "ḥaṣīr" meaning "ḥāṣir," as "ʿalīm" means "ʿālim" and "shahīd" means "shāhid." But this has not been heard used for ḥāṣir as we have heard it for ʿālim and shāhid.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 9–10:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright and gives good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward﴾ (9) ﴿And that those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have prepared for them a painful punishment﴾ (10).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, this Qur'an, which We have sent down upon our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), guides and directs whoever is guided by it ﴿to that which is most upright﴾, meaning: to the path that is more upright than other paths, and that is the religion of God with which He sent His prophets, which is Islam. His, may His praise be exalted, meaning: this Qur'an guides the servants of God who are guided by it to the straightest path, from which all other people of the religions who deny it have strayed.

As related:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright﴾: "That which is most correct (aswab): it is the correct and it is the truth; and the opposing is falsehood." He recited the words of God, exalted is He, (In it are books of great value [kutubun qayyimah]), and said: "In it is truth, with no crookedness in it." And he recited ﴿And He did not make for it any crookedness; [but] upright (qayyiman)﴾, meaning: upright and straight.

* *

And His words ﴿and gives good tidings to the believers﴾:

Meaning: and it gives good tidings, in addition to guiding whoever is guided by it to the most rightly-directed path, to those who believe in God and His Messenger, and who act in their worldly life by what God has commanded them, and refrain from what He has forbidden them, that ﴿for them is a great reward﴾ from God for their faith and their righteous deeds, ﴿great﴾, meaning: a mighty reward and an abundant recompense, and that is Paradise, which God, exalted is He, has prepared for whoever is pleased with his deeds.

As related:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿that they will have a great reward﴾: "It is Paradise. Everything in the Qur'an described as a great reward, a generous reward, or a generous provision, is Paradise."

The "anna" in His words ﴿that for them is a great reward﴾ is in the accusative due to the good tidings falling upon it, and the second "anna" is conjoined to it.

* *

And His words ﴿And that those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And that those who do not affirm the return to God, and do not acknowledge reward and punishment in this world, are therefore not restrained from committing the disobediences of God, ﴿We have prepared for them﴾, meaning: We have prepared for them, for their coming before their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿a painful punishment﴾, meaning: a painful one, and that is the punishment of Hell.
