The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: "And man prays for evil as he prays for good; and man is ever hasty" (17:11)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, reminding His servants of His favours upon them: "Man prays against himself, his offspring and his wealth for evil," saying, "O Allah, destroy him and curse him," in his impatience and anger, just as he prays for good. That is: as he prays to his Lord that He grant him well-being and give him safety in his person, his wealth and his offspring. The meaning is: if his prayers against himself, his wealth and his offspring for evil were answered as his prayers for good are answered, he would perish; but Allah, in His bounty, does not answer him in that.

Scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: "And man prays for evil as he prays for good; and man is ever hasty." He means the man's saying: "O Allah, curse him and be angry with him." If that were hastened for him as good is hastened for him, he would perish. He said: It is said that it is: "And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing" [10:12], [asking] that the harm afflicting him be removed. Blessed and Exalted is He, says: If only he had remembered Me, obeyed Me, and followed My command in times of ease as he calls upon Me in times of trial, it would have been better for him.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "And man prays for evil as he prays for good; and man is ever hasty." He prays against his wealth, so he curses his wealth and his offspring; and if Allah had answered him, He would have destroyed him.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "And man prays for evil as he prays for good." He said: He prays against himself with what, if it were answered for him, would destroy him, and against his servant or his wealth.

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "And man prays for evil as he prays for good; and man is ever hasty." He said: That is the man's praying for evil against his offspring and his wife, and it is hastened: he prays against them, though he does not wish it to befall them.

Interpreters differed regarding His words "and man is ever hasty." Mujahid and those whose statements I have mentioned said: its meaning is that man is hasty in praying for what he dislikes, that it be answered for him in it.

Others said: it refers to Adam, that he was hasty when the spirit was breathed into him before it had run through his whole body; he tried to rise, so his offspring were described as hasty, because of the haste of their father Adam in rising before his creation was complete.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from al-Hakam, from Ibrahim, that Salman al-Farisi said: The first thing Allah created of Adam was his head; he began to look while he was being created. He said: His legs remained; then, after the 'Asr prayer, he said: "O Lord, hasten [the night] before dark." That is His words: "and man is ever hasty."

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Sa'id related to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Imarah related to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When Allah breathed into Adam of His spirit, the breath came to his head first, and nothing of it flowed into his body without becoming flesh and blood. When the breath reached his navel, he looked at his body and was pleased with what he saw of it, so he tried to stand but could not. This is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: "and man is ever hasty." He said: impatient, having no patience in ease or in hardship.

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day give sight, that you may seek bounty from your Lord and that you may know the number of years and the reckoning. And We have explained every matter in detail.﴾ (17:12)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Among His favours upon you, O people, is His differentiating between the sign of the night and the sign of the day: by darkening the sign of the night and brightening the sign of the day. [He did this] so that you may rest in the one and move about, seeking the provision of Allah which He has decreed for you by His bounty, in the other. And so that you may know, through their alternation, the number of years, their passing, and the beginning of their arrival, and the reckoning of the hours and times of the day and night. ﴿And every matter We have explained in detail﴾: that is, He says, We have clarified everything for you, O people, with a sufficient clarity, so that you may thank Allah for the blessings He has bestowed upon you, and devote worship to Him alone, to the exclusion of the gods and idols.

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

**Those who said so:**

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Rufayʿ, from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa' [[Ibn al-Kawwa': he is ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Kawwa' al-Khariji, one of those who were with ʿAli at Siffin, then parted from him after the arbitration. He was one of the leaders of the Kharijites.]] said to ʿAli: "O Commander of the Faithful, what is this blemish that is in the moon?" He said: "Woe to you! Do you not read the Qur'an: ﴿So We effaced the sign of the night﴾? This is its effacement."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Talq narrated to us, from Za'idah, from ʿAsim, from ʿAli ibn Rabiʿah, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa' asked ʿAli, saying: "What is this blackness in the moon?" ʿAli said: ﴿So We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day give sight﴾ — this is the effacement.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Israʾil narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, who said: I was with ʿAli when Ibn al-Kawwa' asked him about the blackness that is in the moon. He said: "That is the sign of the night that was effaced."

- Ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: ʿImran ibn Hudayr narrated to us, from Rafiʿ ibn Abi Kathir, who said: ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Ask me about whatever you wish." Ibn al-Kawwa' stood up and said: "What is the blackness that is in the moon?" He said: "May Allah fight you! Why did you not ask about the matter of your religion and your Hereafter?" [Then] he said: "That is the effacement of the night."

- Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Aban al-Misri narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUfayr narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahiʿah narrated to us, from Hayyi ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs, that a man said to ʿAli: "What is the blackness that is in the moon?" He said: "Indeed Allah says: ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day give sight﴾."

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night﴾, he said: "It is the blackness of the night."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: "The moon used to shine as the sun shines, and the moon is the sign of the night and the sun is the sign of the day. ﴿So We effaced the sign of the night﴾: the blackness that is in the moon."

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj mentioned, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾, he said: "The sun is the sign of the day and the moon is the sign of the night. ﴿So We effaced the sign of the night﴾: the blackness that is in the moon. And thus Allah created it."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾, he said: "The night and the day, thus did Allah create them." Ibn Jurayj said: "ʿAbd Allah ibn Kathir informed us, saying: ﴿So We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day give sight﴾," [and] he said: "The darkness of the night and the dimness [sadfah] of the day."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs, then We effaced the sign of the night and made the sign of the day give sight﴾, that is: "luminous." And the creation of the sun is brighter and greater than that of the moon.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqaʾ narrated to us; all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And We made the night and the day two signs﴾, he said: "The night and the day; thus Allah made them."

The grammarians (ahl al-ʿarabiyyah) differed regarding the meaning of His words ﴿And We made the sign of the day give sight [mubsirah]﴾. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: its meaning is "luminous" (mudi'ah). Likewise His words ﴿and the day giving sight [mubsiran]﴾ mean "luminous," as if he took it that it was said "mubsir" because its light gives sight to people.

Others said: rather, it is derived from abṣara al-nahar (the day gave sight): when people are able to see in it, it is "mubsir," as in their saying: "rajul mujabbin" (a man whose people and companions are cowards) and "rajul mudʿaf" (a man whose narrators are weak). Thus "al-nahar mubsiran" means that its people are those who see.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿that you may seek bounty from your Lord﴾, he said: "He made for you a long period of [daytime] movement [sabh]."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And every matter We have explained in detail﴾, that is: "We have explained it with explanation."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 13:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird (ta'ir) to his neck, and We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find wide open.﴾

The Exalted says: And every person We have bound to what He decreed for him, that he will do, and what he will arrive at of wretchedness or happiness by his deeds, is fastened to his neck and does not leave him. The phrase ﴿fastened his bird﴾ is a figure of speech, because the Arabs used to take omens (tafa'ul) or bad omens (tasha'um) from the flights and movements of birds. So He informed them, may His praise be exalted, that every one of them has had his Lord fasten his bird to his neck, whether that bird was ill-omened and wretchedness leading him to the Blaze, or was good fortune leading him to the Gardens of Eden.

Those of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no contagion (adwa) and no bad omen (tiyarah), and every person We have fastened his bird to his neck."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird to his neck﴾: He said: The bird is his deed. He said: "The bird" refers to many things, including the bad omen by which people take omens from one another.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata al-Khurasani informed me, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird to his neck﴾: He said: His deed and what he has power over; it is attached to him wherever he is, and it departs with him wherever he departs. Ibn Jurayj said: And he said: "His bird" is his deed. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid, who said: His deed and what Allah has written for him.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "His bird": his deed.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us; and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, all of them from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird to his neck﴾: He said: His deed.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, the same.

Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Amr al-Fuqaymi, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird to his neck﴾: He said: No child is born except that in his neck is a paper on which is written wretched or happy. He said: And I heard him say: "Those will receive their portion of the Book" — he said: that is what has preceded.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird to his neck﴾: Yes, by Allah, with his happiness and his wretchedness by his deed.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "His bird": his deed.

If someone says: How did He say "We have fastened his bird to his neck," if the matter is as you have described, and did not say "We have fastened it to his hands and feet" or some other part of the body? It is said: Because the neck is the place of marks, the place of necklaces and collars, and other things that adorn or disfigure. So the speech of the Arabs attributed things that bind the sons of Adam and others to their necks, and this usage became so common that they attributed what binds all the body to the necks, just as they attributed the offenses of the body's members to the hand, saying: "That is for what his hands have earned," even if what dragged him into it was his tongue or his private parts. Likewise His words ﴿We have fastened his bird to his neck﴾.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find wide open﴾. Some of the people of Madinah and Makkah, namely Nafi' and Ibn Kathir, and most of the readers of Iraq, read ﴿wa-nukhriju﴾ with a nun, ﴿la-hu yawm al-qiyamah kitaban yalqahu manshuran﴾ with a fatha on the ya' of yalqahu and a light qaf, meaning: "And We will bring out for him, We Ourselves, on the Day of Resurrection," in response to His words ﴿We have fastened﴾: "And We bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection the record of his deed, wide open." Some of the readers of Syria agreed with these on reading ﴿wa-nukhriju﴾ but differed with them on ﴿yalqahu﴾, reading ﴿wa-yulaqqahu﴾ with a damma on the ya' and a doubled qaf, meaning: "And We bring out for him, We Ourselves, on the Day of Resurrection a record that he meets," then referring it to the unnamed agent, so the sense is: "A person will meet that record wide open."

It is related from Mujahid that:

Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from Humayd, from Mujahid, that he read it ﴿wa-yakhruju la-hu yawm al-qiyamah kitaba﴾. He said: Yazid said: He means the bird brings out a record. I think he read it with a fatha on the ya', and this is the reading of al-Hasan al-Basri and Ibn Muhaysin. The one who read this reading directed the meaning to: "And the bird that We fastened to the neck of the person brings out for him on the Day of Resurrection, so it becomes a record he reads wide open." Some of the people of Madinah read ﴿wa-yukhraju la-hu﴾ with a damma on the ya' according to the unnamed-agent form, and it seems he directed the meaning to: "And the bird brings out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record," meaning: "And Allah brings out that bird, having made it a record," except that he moved it in the manner of the unnamed-agent form.

The most correct of these readings, in our view, is the reading of the one who read ﴿wa-nukhriju﴾ with a nun and a damma, ﴿la-hu yawm al-qiyamah kitaban yalqahu manshuran﴾ with a fatha on the ya' and a light qaf, because the report before it was from Allah, the Exalted, that He is the One who fastened on His creatures what He fastened. So it is correct that what follows it is also a report about Him, that He is the One who brings it out for them on the Day of Resurrection, and that it be with a nun as the preceding report was with a nun. As for His words ﴿yalqahu﴾, the consensus of the authoritative readers on the correctness of what we have chosen in this reading, and the rarity of what contradicts it, is a sufficient proof for us, given the closeness of the meaning of the two readings, namely the damma and fatha of the ya', and the doubling and lightening of the qaf in it. So if the correct reading is what we have chosen, by the evidence we have given, then the interpretation of the speech is: Every person among you, O assembly of the sons of Adam, We have fastened to him his good fortune and his ill fortune, his wretchedness and his happiness, according to what has preceded in Our knowledge that he will arrive at it, and the good and evil he does is on his neck. He will not exceed in any of his deeds what We decreed upon him that he would do, and what We wrote for him that he would arrive at. And We will bring out for him, when he comes to Us, a record he will find wide open, with the deeds he did in the world, and with his bird which We wrote for him and fastened on his neck, and his Lord has counted against him in it everything that passed in the world.

Those of the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find wide open﴾: He said: It is his deed, which was counted against him; so there is brought out for him on the Day of Resurrection what was written against him of deed, which he will find wide open.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record he will find wide open﴾: That is, his deed.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿We have fastened his bird to his neck﴾: He said: His deed. ﴿And We will bring out for him﴾: He said: We will bring out that deed. ﴿A record he will find wide open﴾. Ma'mar said: al-Hasan recited ﴿On the right and on the left sits a watcher﴾, "O son of Adam, your record has been spread out for you, and two noble angels have been appointed over you, one on your right and the other on your left. As for the one on your right, he guards your good deeds, and as for the one on your left, he guards your bad deeds. So act as you wish, little or much, until when you die your record is folded and placed on your neck with you in your grave, until you bring it out on the Day of Resurrection, a record you will find wide open. ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾." By Allah, He has been just to you in making you the reckoner of your own self.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "His bird": his deed, and We bring out for him, by that deed, a record he will find wide open.

Some of the grammarians interpreted His words ﴿And every person We have fastened his bird to his neck﴾ as: that is, his portion, from their saying: "The arrow of so-and-so flew with such-and-such," when his arrow came out on one of the shares. Although this is a view that has some basis, the interpretation of the people of interpretation is as I have explained, and it is not permissible to go beyond what they said in interpreting the Qur'an to something else. Moreover, if this speaker meant by his words "his portion of the deed, the wretchedness and the happiness," then the meaning of his words is not far from the meaning of theirs.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 14–15:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is your soul this day as a reckoner against you﴾

Allah, may He be remembered, says: ﴿And We bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find laid wide open﴾, and it will be said to him: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is your soul this day as a reckoner against you.﴾ The words "We say to him" are omitted here, being understood from the context. By His words ﴿Read your record﴾ He means: read the record of your deeds that you did in the world, which our two recording angels wrote down and which We have counted against you. ﴿Sufficient is your soul this day as a reckoner against you﴾ means: your own soul suffices you today as one who reckons against you, counting your deeds and recording them against you. We seek no other witness against you than it, and we demand no other accounter than it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Read your record; sufficient is your soul this day as a reckoner against you﴾: On that day, one who was not a reader in the world will read.

* *

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his own soul, and whoever goes astray only goes astray to its detriment. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And We would never punish until We sent a messenger﴾

Allah, may He be remembered, says: Whoever keeps to the path of truth and follows it, and that is the religion of Allah with which He sent His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿Whoever is guided is only guided for his own soul﴾ means: his adherence to uprightness and his faith in Allah and His Messenger benefit no one but himself. ﴿And whoever goes astray﴾ means: whoever deviates from the straight way, takes a path other than guidance, and disbelieves in Allah, in Muhammad ﷺ, and in what came to him from Allah of the truth; then his straying and his deviation from guidance harm no one but himself, for it makes necessary for his soul the anger of Allah and His painful punishment. By His words ﴿he only goes astray to its detriment﴾ He means: he earns the sin of his straying upon his own soul, not upon another. His words ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ mean: no one bearing a load will bear the load of another's sins. He said ﴿bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾ because its meaning is: no soul bearing a burden bears the burden of another soul. It is said from this: "I bear (wazara) such-and-such, I bear it (azuru) and burden (wizr)." The wizr is sin, and its plural is awzar, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿But we were made to carry loads of the ornaments of the people﴾. The meaning of the statement seems to be: no sinner bears the sin of another, but each soul has its own sin, not the sin of other souls.

As follows:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾: By Allah, Allah does not place upon a servant the sin of another, and He does not hold anyone accountable except for his own deed.

* *

As for His words ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a messenger﴾

Allah, may He be remembered, says: We would not destroy any people except after giving them warning through messengers and establishing the proof against them through signs that cut off their excuse.

As follows:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a messenger﴾: Indeed, Allah, blessed and exalted, does not punish anyone until a report from Allah reaches him beforehand, or a clear proof comes to him from Allah, and He punishes no one except for his sin.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah, blessed and exalted, will gather the souls of those who died in the interval (fatrah), the insane, the deaf, the mute, and the senile elders to whom Islam came when they had grown senile. Then He will send a messenger to them, [saying]: "Enter the Fire." They will say: "How, when no messenger came to us? By Allah, if they entered it, it would be coolness and safety for them." Then He will send to them, and whoever would have obeyed Him before will obey Him. Abu Hurayrah said: Recite if you wish: ﴿And We would never punish until We sent a messenger﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Hammam, from Abu Hurayrah, similarly.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 14–15:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is your soul this day as a reckoner against you﴾

Allah, may He be remembered, says: ﴿And We bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find laid wide open﴾, and it will be said to him: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is your soul this day as a reckoner against you.﴾ The words "We say to him" are omitted here, being understood from the context. By His words ﴿Read your record﴾ He means: read the record of your deeds that you did in the world, which our two recording angels wrote down and which We have counted against you. ﴿Sufficient is your soul this day as a reckoner against you﴾ means: your own soul suffices you today as one who reckons against you, counting your deeds and recording them against you. We seek no other witness against you than it, and we demand no other accounter than it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Read your record; sufficient is your soul this day as a reckoner against you﴾: On that day, one who was not a reader in the world will read.
