On this meaning the author cited the verse.]], the blind one, that he asked Abdullah ibn Mas'ud about this verse ﴿and do not squander wastefully﴾, and he said: "Spending wealth in what is not its right."

● Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Hakam, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from Abu al-Ubaydin, from Abdullah, the like of it.

● Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah informed us, from al-Hakam ibn Utaybah, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, that Abu al-Ubaydin was blind, and he asked Ibn Mas'ud, saying: "What is tabdhir?" He said: "Spending wealth in what is not its right."

● Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us, saying: al-Mas'udi informed us, saying: Salamah ibn Kuhayl informed us, from Abu al-Ubaydin, and he had an affliction, and Abdullah knew of that about him, and he said: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman, what is tabdhir?" and he mentioned the like of it.

● Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Haw'ab narrated to us, from Ammar ibn Zuraiq, from Abu Ishaq, from Harithah ibn Mudrib, from Abu al-Ubaydin, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "We, the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, used to say that tabdhir is spending in what is not its right."

● Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Kathir al-Anbari narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I was walking with Abu Ishaq on the road to Kufa, when he came upon a house being built with plaster and bricks, and he said: "This is tabdhir according to the saying of Abdullah: spending wealth in what is not its right."

● Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and do not squander wastefully﴾, he said: "The squanderer is one who spends in what is not its right."

● Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abbad narrated to us, from Husayn, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The squanderer is one who spends in what is not its right."

● Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Do not spend in falsehood, for the squanderer is one who is extravagant in what is not right."

Ibn Juraij said: Mujahid said: "If a person spent all his wealth in what is right, it would not be tabdhir; and if he spent a mudd in falsehood, it would be tabdhir."

● Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and do not squander wastefully﴾, he said: "Tabdhir is spending in disobedience to Allah, in what is not right, and in corruption."

● Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And give the near of kin his right, and the needy, and the wayfarer﴾: "He began with the parents before this; when he finished with the parents and their right, he mentioned these, and said ﴿do not squander wastefully﴾: do not give in the disobedience of Allah."

As for His words ﴿Indeed, the squanderers are brothers of the devils﴾, it means: indeed, those who scatter their wealth in disobedience to Allah, spending it in what is not His obedience, are the allies of the devils. Likewise the Arabs say of everyone who keeps to the way of a people and follows their trail: "He is their brother." ﴿And the Satan has ever been ungrateful to his Lord﴾: he says, the Satan was ungrateful for the blessing of his Lord which He bestowed upon him, denying it and not thanking Him for it; rather he rejects it by abandoning obedience to Allah and committing His disobedience. Likewise his brothers among the children of Adam who squander their wealth in the disobedience of Allah do not thank Allah for His blessings upon them, but oppose His command and disobey Him, and follow the example of the Satan in what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has bestowed upon them of wealth which He entrusted to them, by abandoning gratitude for it and meeting it with ingratitude.

Like the one who:

● Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, the squanderers﴾: those who spend in the disobedience of Allah ﴿are brothers of the devils, and the Satan has ever been ungrateful to his Lord﴾.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you await, then speak to them a gentle word﴾ (17:28).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And if you turn away, O Muhammad, from those whom I commanded you to give their rights when you find the means to do so, by your face, when they ask you, what you cannot find a way to give, out of shame before them and mercy toward them, ﴿seeking mercy from your Lord﴾, meaning: awaiting provision that you expect from your Lord, and hoping for God's facilitation of it for you, so do not make them despair. But ﴿speak to them a gentle word﴾, meaning: but promise them a good promise, by saying: God will provide, and then I will give you, and what is similar to that of soft speech, not harsh, just as He, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿And as for the petitioner, do not repel him﴾ (93:10).

And the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿And if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you await﴾, he said: awaiting provision. ﴿Then speak to them a gentle word﴾, he said: gentle, you promise them.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿAta al-Khurasani, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿seeking mercy from your Lord﴾, he said: provision. ﴿Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have distributed among them their livelihood﴾ (43:32).

ʿImran ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: ʿAmara narrated to us, from ʿIkrima, concerning His saying ﴿And if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you await﴾, he said: awaiting provision from God that comes to you.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿIkrima, His saying ﴿And if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you await﴾, he said: If they ask you and they do not find with you what you can give them, seeking mercy, he said: provision that you await and hope for. ﴿Then speak to them a gentle word﴾, he said: promise them a good promise: when that happens, when it comes to us, we will do it, we will give you. That is the gentle word.

Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: If they ask you and you do not have what you can give them, and you turn away from them seeking mercy, he said: provision you await. ﴿Then speak to them a gentle word﴾.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿seeking mercy from your Lord﴾, he said: awaiting the provision of God.

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Abu al-Duha, from ʿUbayda, concerning His saying ﴿seeking mercy from your Lord which you await﴾, he said: seeking provision.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAta, from Saʿid, ﴿And if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you await﴾, he said: whatever provision you await. ﴿Then speak to them a gentle word﴾, i.e., a kind word.

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, ﴿Then speak to them a gentle word﴾, he said: promise them good. And al-Hasan said: speak to them a soft and easy word.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying ﴿And if you turn away from them﴾, he said: we find nothing you can give them, ﴿seeking mercy from your Lord﴾, he said: awaiting provision from your Lord. It was revealed concerning those among the poor who used to ask the Prophet ﷺ.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Harami ibn ʿUmara related to me, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, saying: ʿUmara related to me, from ʿIkrima, concerning God's saying ﴿Then speak to them a gentle word﴾, he said: gentleness.

Ibn Zayd used to say about this:

Yunus related it to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And if you turn away from them﴾, i.e., from those whom We instructed you about, ﴿seeking mercy from your Lord which you await﴾, if you fear that if you give them, they will strengthen themselves thereby in disobedience to God, mighty and majestic, and seek help with it therein, so you see fit to withhold good from them; then, if they ask you, ﴿speak to them a gentle word﴾, a good word: may God provide for you, may God bless you.

This saying which we have mentioned from Ibn Zayd, together with its opposition to the sayings of the people of interpretation regarding the interpretation of this verse, is distant in meaning from what its apparent wording indicates. This is because God, exalted, said to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you await﴾, and so He commanded him, if his turning away from those people he mentioned was seeking a mercy from God that he hopes for from his Lord, to say ﴿a gentle word﴾. That turning away, seeking mercy, cannot be free of one of two matters: either it is a turning away from him seeking a mercy from God that he hopes for for himself, in which case the meaning of the speech is as we have said, and as the people of interpretation whose sayings we mentioned have said, and contrary to his view; or it is a turning away from him seeking a mercy from God that he hopes for for the petitioners, whom the Prophet of God ﷺ was, according to his claim, commanded to withhold what they asked for, out of concern lest they spend it in disobedience to God. It is known that the anger of God against one who is not trusted to avoid spending what is given to strengthen himself in obedience to God, in disobedience to Him, is more to be feared than the hope of His mercy toward him, because God's mercy is only hoped for by the people of His obedience, not by the people of disobedience. Unless he meant to direct it toward the idea that the Prophet of God ﷺ was commanded to withhold what they asked of him, so that they would turn back from disobedience to God and repent by his withholding from them what they asked, in which case that would be a meaning that the wording of the verse can bear, though it would be contrary to the view of the people of interpretation.

The exposition of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it fully outstretched, lest you sit down reproached and destitute﴾ (17:29).

This is a parable that God, blessed and exalted, struck for the one who withholds spending in the rights that He has made obligatory upon the property of those who possess wealth. So He made him like one whose hand is shackled to his neck, unable to take with it or give with it.

The meaning of the speech is: Do not hold back, O Muhammad, your hand out of stinginess from spending in God's rights, so that you spend nothing in them, like the holding back of one whose hand is chained to his neck, who cannot extend it. ﴿Nor extend it fully outstretched﴾ means: do not extend it with giving to the utmost extent, so that nothing remains with you, and when you are asked you find nothing to give your petitioner. ﴿Lest you sit down reproached and destitute﴾ means: lest you sit, your petitioners reproaching you when you do not give them what they ask, and your own self reproaching you for your haste in squandering your wealth and its loss. "Destitute" (mahsur) means: blamed, cut off from you, with nothing left in your possession to spend. Its root is from the saying about a beast that has been driven until its journey is cut short, it has become weary and exhausted from travel, so it is called ḥasīr (exhausted). It is said of it: "I exhausted the beast (ḥasartu al-dābba), so I exhaust it (uḥsiruhā), exhausting it (ḥasran)," that is, when you wear it out by travel. And "I exhausted him by asking (ḥasartuhu bi'l-mas'alah)," when you ask him persistently and press him. And "the sight was exhausted (ḥasara al-baṣar), so it exhausts," which is when it reaches the farthest point of vision and grows weary. From it is His saying, mighty and majestic: ﴿The sight will return to you humbled while it is exhausted﴾ (67:4). Likewise, it applies to everything that becomes weary and wears down until it is worn out.

Scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said things similar to what we have said. Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Hawdhah related to us, saying: ʿAwf related to us, from al-Ḥasan, regarding His words ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾, he said: do not make it chained from spending. ﴿Nor extend it﴾: squandering with extravagance.

Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Yusuf ibn Bahz related to us, saying: Ḥawshab related to us, saying: Al-Ḥasan, whenever he recited this verse, ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it fully outstretched, lest you sit down reproached and destitute﴾, would say: Do not diminish My provision without My pleasure, nor place it in My displeasure, lest I strip you of what is in your hands, and you become destitute, with nothing from it in your hands.

Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: this is said about spending. He says: ﴿Do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾ means: do not extend it with good. ﴿Nor extend it fully outstretched﴾ means extravagance. ﴿Lest you sit down reproached﴾: he reproaches himself over what has passed of his wealth. ﴿Destitute﴾ means: his wealth has all gone, so he is destitute.

ʿAli related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Muʿawiyah related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿Do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾: this means stinginess.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿Do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾: that is, do not hold it back from obedience to God, nor from His right. ﴿Nor extend it fully outstretched﴾: he says, do not spend it in disobedience to God, nor on what does not benefit you nor is fitting for you, and that is extravagance. As for His words ﴿lest you sit down reproached and destitute﴾, he said: reproached among God's servants, destitute over what has passed of your life and what you neglected.

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, ﴿Do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾: he said, regarding spending, meaning do not hold back from spending. ﴿Nor extend it fully outstretched﴾: meaning do not squander with squandering. ﴿Lest you sit down reproached﴾ among God's servants, ﴿destitute﴾: meaning regretful over what has been neglected by you.

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Do not hold back from spending in what I have commanded you of the right, ﴿nor extend it fully outstretched﴾ in what I have forbidden you, ﴿lest you sit down reproached﴾: he said, sinful, ﴿destitute﴾: he said, cut off from you.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Do not make your hand chained to your neck﴾: chained, you do not extend it with good nor with a gift. ﴿Nor extend it fully outstretched﴾ in right and wrong, so that what you have is exhausted and what is in your hands runs out, and someone comes to you who wants you to give him, and you are destitute, so he reproaches you when you have given to these and not to them.

The Interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, your Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed, He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.﴾ (17:30)

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, extends His provision to whomever He wills of His servants, so He widens it for him, and He restricts [it] for whomever He wills, meaning: He withholds it from whomever He wills among them, so He constricts it for him. ﴿Indeed, He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted﴾: meaning: indeed your Lord is Knowing of His servants, and of who is made right by abundance of provision and who is corrupted by it, and of who is made right by scarcity and constriction and who is destroyed by it. ﴿and Seeing﴾: meaning: He is Seeing of their management and their governance. He means: so refrain, O Muhammad, and submit to Our command in what We have commanded you and forbidden you, regarding extending your hand, in what you extend it to and to whom you extend it, and withholding it from whom you withhold it and in what you withhold it. For We are more knowing of the interests of the servants than you, and than all creation, and more seeing of their management.

As related by:

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Then He informed us how He acts, and He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts﴾. He said: "yaqdiru" means "yuqallu" (He diminishes). Everything in the Qur'an with "yaqdiru" is like this. Then He informed His servants that it does not diminish Him or burden Him if He were to extend [provision] to them, but [He does so] out of consideration for them. So He said: ﴿And if Allah extended provision to His servants, they would surely rebel throughout the earth, but He sends down in measure what He wills. Indeed, He is, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾. He said: When the Arabs have abundance and provision is extended to them, they become insolent, some of them kill others, and corruption comes. But when there is drought, they are occupied away from that.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 31:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin.﴾

Exalted is He, says: ﴿And your Lord has decreed﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment﴾ (Qur'an 17:23). ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty﴾ — the place of "taqtulu" (kill) is in the accusative, in conjunction with "alla ta'budu" (that you not worship).

He means by His saying ﴿for fear of poverty (imlaq)﴾ fear of want and destitution. We have already explained this, with its evidence, in what has passed, and mentioned the transmission regarding it. Exalted is His praise, said this to the Arabs, because they used to kill their female children out of fear of hardship for themselves in providing for them.

As:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'd narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty﴾: i.e., for fear of destitution. The people of the Jahiliyyah used to kill their children out of fear of destitution, so God admonished them concerning that, and informed them that their provision and the provision of their children is upon God. So He said ﴿We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin.﴾

* Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿for fear of poverty﴾ he said: They used to kill the daughters.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Mujahid said, ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty﴾: "al-faqah" (destitution) and "al-faqr" (poverty).

* 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying ﴿for fear of poverty﴾: he said: "poverty."

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin (khita'an kabiran)﴾, the reciters differed in its recitation. The majority of the reciters of Madinah and Iraq recited ﴿khit'an kabiran﴾ with a kasrah on the kha' of "khit'" (khi't') and a sukun on the ta', and when it is recited thus, it has two interpretations. The first is that it is a noun from the saying of the speaker: "khati'tu, fa-ana akhta'" (I committed a sin, so I sin), meaning: I sinned and committed a transgression. It is related from the Arabs: "khati'tu" when you sin intentionally, and "akhta'tu" when the sin occurs from you by mistake, without intent on your part. The second is that it means "khata'" with a fatha on the kha' and the ta', then the kha' was given a kasrah and the ta' a sukun, as it is said: "qitb" and "qatb," "hidhar," and "najis" and "najas." The "khit'" with a kasrah is a noun, and "khata'" with a fatha on the kha' and ta' is a verbal noun from their saying "khati'a al-rajul" (the man sinned); and it may be a noun from their saying "akhta'a." As for its verbal noun, it is "ikhta'." It has been said that "khati'a" means "akhta'a," as the poet said:

"Ya lahfa Hindin idh khati'na kahilan"

(Footnote: This is a line in mashtur rajaz attributed to Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr al-Kindi, from a poem of nine lines (Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa, Halabi edition, p. 105). He said it when news reached him that Bani Asad had killed his father. "Ya lahf" means "O regret" or "O grief." Hind was his sister. "Khati'na" refers to the horses, i.e., they erred. He had pursued Bani Kahil of Bani Asad by night, and struck among Kinanah in error, and Bani Kahil fled from him. This line is the first of the verses in al-Aghani and in al-'Iqd al-Thamin of William Alwardt. The point of evidence in the line is that "khati'a khata'" and "akhta'a ikhta'" are two dialects with one meaning, when one does something and errs in it without intent, as in the line. "Al-khat'" with a kasrah on the kha' and sukun on the ta' is a noun in the sense of a verbal noun. Some lexicographers say that "khati'a khata'" means one fell into sin intentionally, unlike "akhta'a," which is without intent.)

meaning: "akhta'na" (they erred). Some of the reciters of Madinah recited ﴿inna qatlahum kana khata'an kabiran﴾ with a fatha on the kha' and ta', limited to the understanding that it is a noun from their saying: "akhta'a fulan khata'an" (so-and-so erred, an error). Some reciters of Makkah recited ﴿inna qatlahum kana khata'an kabiran﴾ with a fatha on the kha' and ta', and with a prolonged "khata'" (khata'a), in a sense close to the meaning of those who recited "khata'" with a fatha on the kha' and ta', except that it differs in lengthening the vowel.

The general scholars of the Arabic language among the people of Kufa and some of the Basrans held that "al-khat'" and "al-khata'" have one meaning, except that some of them claimed that "al-khat'" with a kasrah on the kha' and sukun on the ta' is more common in recitation, and that "al-khit'" with a fatha on the kha' and ta' is more widespread in people's speech, and that "al-khat'" with a kasrah on the kha' and sukun on the ta' has not been heard in any of their speech or poetry, except in a line recited by one of the poets:

"Al-khit'u fahishatun wal-birru nafilatun ... ka'ajwatin ghurisat fi al-ardi tu'tabar"

(Footnote: The author cited this line to show that some claimed that "al-khat'" (with kasrah and sukun) is more common in recitation, and that "al-khata'" (with fatha on kha' and sukun on ta') is more widespread in speech, and that "khit'" with kasrah and sukun has not been heard in their speech and poetry except in a line recited by one of the poets: "Al-khit'u fahishatun..." etc. I have not found the line or its composer in Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra', nor in Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah, except that al-Farra' said: al-Hasan recited "khata'an kabiran" with the mad (lengthening), and Abu Ja'far al-Madani recited "khata'an kabiran," shortened and with hamzah, and both are correct. It seems that "al-khata'" means sin, and it may mean the same as "khata'" with shortening, as they say "qatb" and "qatb," "hadhar" and "hadhar," "najs" and "najas." Similar is the recitation of one who recited "hum ula'i 'ala athari" and "athari." "Al-nafilah" is what is in addition to the obligation. "Al-'ajwah" is the finest date of Madinah, as in Lisan al-'Arab. "Tu'tabar" means it is improved by grafting so its fruit becomes better.)

I have already mentioned the difference between "khit'" with a kasrah on the kha' and sukun on the ta', and with fatha on both.

The most correct of these recitations in our view is the recitation upon which the reciters of Iraq and the majority of the people of the Hijaz agree, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it, and the irregularity of what differs from it. The meaning of that is: a sin and a transgression, not an error in action, because they used to kill them deliberately, not by mistake, and for their deliberate act their Lord rebuked them, and forbade them from it in advance.

Concerning what we have said, the people of interpretation spoke similarly.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿khit'an kabiran﴾, he said: i.e., a transgression.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, ﴿Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin﴾, he said: a transgression. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "khit'": i.e., a transgression.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: "And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse (al-zina). Indeed, it is ever an abomination and an evil way" (17:32)

He, the Exalted and Mighty, says: And He also decreed that you, O people, "do not approach" "unlawful sexual intercourse (al-zina). Indeed, it is ever an abomination" — that is, indeed unlawful sexual intercourse has been an abomination, "and an evil way" — that is, the way of unlawful sexual intercourse is an evil way, because it is the way of the people of disobedience to God and of those who oppose His command, so it is an evil way that leads its follower into the Fire of Hell.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 33:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have certainly given his heir authority, but let him not commit excess in killing. Indeed, he is ever supported.﴾ (17:33)

He, glory be to His praise, says: And He also decreed that ﴿do not kill﴾, O people, ﴿the soul which Allah has forbidden﴾ to be killed ﴿except by right﴾. Its right is that it not be killed except for apostasy after Islam, or adultery after being married, or retaliation for a soul; and if it is a disbeliever whose disbelief was not preceded by Islam, then that it not be killed when there has been a prior covenant or safe-conduct for it.

As follows:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right﴾: By Allah, we know of no permission to shed the blood of a Muslim man except by one of three: a man who kills deliberately, for whom there is retaliation (qawad); or one who commits adultery after being married, for whom there is stoning; or one who disbelieves after his Islam, for whom there is killing.

* Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah told us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah or other than him, who said: It was said to Abu Bakr: Will you fight those who think that they should not pay the zakah? He said: If they withhold from me even a camel's cord which they used to give to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), I would fight them over it. It was said to Abu Bakr: Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) not say: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, 'There is no god but Allah.' When they say it, they have protected their blood and their property from me, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah"? Abu Bakr said: This is part of its right.

* Musa ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Hashim told us, saying: Sulayman ibn Hayyan told us, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, 'There is no god but Allah.' When they say it, they have protected their blood and their property from me, except by its right, and their reckoning is with Allah." It was said: And what is its right? He said: Adultery after marriage, disbelief after belief, and killing a soul, so that he is killed for it.

* * *

And His words ﴿And whoever is killed wrongfully﴾

He says: And whoever is killed by other than the meanings we mentioned, which if he is killed for them it would be a killing by right, ﴿We have certainly given his heir authority﴾, meaning: We have given the heir of the wrongfully slain person authority over the slayer of his heir; if he wishes, he may take retribution from him and kill him in return for his heir; and if he wishes, he may pardon him; and if he wishes, he may take the blood-money (diyah).

The people of interpretation have differed regarding the meaning of the authority (sultan) given to the heir of the slain person. Some of them said regarding this what we have said.

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right. And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have certainly given his heir authority﴾: He said: It is a clear proof from Allah, mighty and majestic, which He sent down, that the heir of the slain seeks: either the blood-money ('aql) or retaliation (qawad); and that is the authority.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, regarding His words ﴿We have certainly given his heir authority﴾: He said: If he wishes, he pardons; and if he wishes, he takes the blood-money.

Others said: Rather, that authority is killing.

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have certainly given his heir authority﴾: It is the retaliation (qawad) which Allah, exalted is He, has made.

The more correct of the two interpretations, in our view, is the interpretation of those who explained it as: the authority mentioned by Allah in this place is what Ibn 'Abbas said, that the heir of the slain has the right to kill if he wishes, or to take the blood-money if he wishes, or to pardon. This is because of the soundness of the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said on the day of the conquest of Makkah: "Whoever has a slain relative, he has the choice of two things: either to kill or to take the blood-money." I have explained the ruling on this in our book: the Book of Injuries (Kitab al-Jirah).

* * *

And His words ﴿but let him not commit excess in killing﴾

The reciters differed in reciting this. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited ﴿fa-la tusrif﴾ ("so do not commit excess"), addressed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and intending by it him and the leaders after him, meaning: do not kill for the wrongly slain person anyone other than his slayer. This is because the people of the Jahiliyyah used to do that: if a man killed a man, the heir of the slain would go to a noble from the slayer's tribe and kill him in return for his heir, and leave the slayer. So Allah, mighty and majestic, forbade His servants from that, and said to His Messenger, peace be upon him: killing other than the slayer for the slain is disobedience and excess, so do not kill anyone other than his slayer; and if you kill the slayer for the slain, do not mutilate him. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited ﴿fa-la yusrif﴾ with the letter ya', meaning: let not the heir of the slain commit excess by killing someone other than his heir's slayer. It has also been said: what is meant is: let not the first slayer commit excess, not the heir of the slain.

The correct statement on this matter, in my view, is to say: they are two readings close in meaning. That is because the address of Allah, blessed and exalted is He, to His Prophet (ﷺ) with a command or prohibition in matters of religious law is a decree from Him concerning all His servants; and likewise His command and prohibition to some of them is a command and prohibition to all of them, except where it is indicated that it is specific to some and not others. If that is so, as we have explained in our book [the Book of Clarification, on the foundations of rulings], then it is known that His address, exalted is He, with His words ﴿so do not commit excess in killing﴾ to His Prophet (ﷺ), even though it is directed to him, is meant for all His servants; likewise His prohibition to the heir of the slain or to the slayer against excess in killing and transgression in it is a prohibition for all of them. So whichever of the two readings the reciter reads, he is correct, and the reading is sound.

The people of interpretation have differed in their interpretation of this in a manner similar to their differing in recitation.

Those who interpreted it as an address to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ):

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman told us, the two of them saying: Sufyan told us, from Mansur, from Talq ibn Habib, regarding His words ﴿so do not commit excess in killing﴾: He said: Do not kill other than his slayer, and do not mutilate him.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from Talq ibn Habib, with similar.

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Khusayf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿so do not commit excess in killing﴾: He said: Do not kill two for one.

* It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿So let him not commit excess in killing; indeed, he is ever supported﴾: This was in Makkah, and the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) was there, and it was the first thing revealed of the Qur'an concerning killing. The polytheists used to assassinate the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), so Allah, blessed and exalted, said: whoever among the polytheists kills you, let his killing of you not drive you to kill for him a father or a brother or anyone of his kin, even if they are polytheists; do not kill except your slayer. This was before Bara'ah (Surah al-Tawbah) was revealed and before they were commanded to fight the polytheists. That is His words ﴿so do not commit excess in killing﴾, meaning: do not kill other than your slayer. And it is today upon that position among the Muslims: it is not lawful for them to kill except their slayer.

Those who said: it refers to the heir of the slain. Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, saying: Abu Raja' told us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have certainly given his heir authority﴾: He said: A man would be killed, and his heir would say: I will not be satisfied until I kill for him so-and-so and so-and-so from the nobles of his tribe.

* Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿so do not commit excess in killing﴾: He said: Do not kill other than your slayer, and do not mutilate him.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿so let him not commit excess in killing﴾: He said: He does not kill other than his slayer; whoever kills with an iron implement is killed with an iron implement; whoever kills with a piece of wood is killed with a piece of wood; and whoever kills with a stone is killed with a stone. It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "Among the most rebellious of people against Allah, mighty is His praise, are three: a man who kills other than his slayer, or who kills with a dakhan in the Jahiliyyah, or who kills within the sanctuary of Allah."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard him, meaning Ibn Zayd, say regarding the saying of Allah, mighty is His praise, ﴿And whoever is killed wrongfully, We have certainly given his heir authority﴾: He said: The Arabs, when a slain person was killed among them, would not be satisfied to kill the slayer of their companion until they had killed someone more noble than the one who killed him. So Allah, mighty is His praise, said ﴿We have certainly given his heir authority﴾, to support him and give him his right, ﴿but let him not commit excess in killing﴾, by killing an innocent person.

Those who said it refers to the slayer: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿fa-la yusrif fi al-qatl﴾: He said: the slayer should not commit excess in killing.

We have mentioned the correct reading according to us. And since both aspects of the reading are correct in our view, likewise all the aspects of its interpretation that we have mentioned are not outside the truth, since the speech allows that; and because in Allah's prohibition, exalted is He, to some of His creatures against excess in killing, it is a prohibition from Him to all of them.

As for His words ﴿Indeed, he is ever supported﴾ (innahu kana mansuran), the people of interpretation differed about whom the pronoun in ﴿innahu﴾ refers to. Some said: it refers to the heir of the slain, and he is the one meant, and he is the one supported against the slayer.

Those who said that:

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿innahu kana mansuran﴾: He said: it is the Imam's handing over to him, that is, to the heir, so that if he wishes he kills, and if he wishes he pardons.

Others said: rather, the slain person is meant by it, and according to this view it refers back to "man" in His words ﴿And whoever is killed wrongfully﴾.

Those who said that: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿innahu kana mansuran﴾: that the slain person was supported.

Others said: it refers to the blood of the slain person, and they said: the meaning of the speech is that the blood of the slain was supported against the slayer.

The most likely of these to be correct in my view is the statement of those who said: it refers to the heir, and the pronoun returns to him, because he is the one wronged, and his heir is the slain; and it is closer to his mention than the mention of the slain. He is also the one supported, because Allah, mighty is His praise, decreed in His revealed Book that He gave him authority over the slayer of his heir, and made him the judge in it, by making it his to kill if he wishes, or to take the blood-money if he prefers, or to pardon if he sees fit; and that is sufficient as support for him from Allah, mighty is His praise. Therefore we say: he is the one meant by the pronoun in His words ﴿innahu kana mansuran﴾.

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner, until he reaches his maturity. And fulfill every commitment; indeed, the commitment is ever questioned﴾ [17:34].

His statement, exalted is His remembrance: And He has also decreed that you should not approach the property of the orphan by consuming it wastefully and hastily, fearing that he will grow up; rather, approach it in the best manner and the most excellent way, which is to manage it for him by investing, improving and safeguarding it.

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner﴾: When this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily on the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so they would not mix with them in food, eating, or anything else. Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed ﴿And if you mix with them, they are your brothers, and Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer﴾, and this gave them a concession.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner﴾, he said: They would not mix with them in property, food, or mounts, until ﴿And if you mix with them, they are your brothers﴾ was revealed.

Ibn Zayd said concerning this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the best manner﴾: It is eating in a reasonable way, that you eat with him when you are in need of it. Ubayy used to say this.

* *

As for His words ﴿until he reaches his maturity﴾:

That is, until he reaches the time of his strength in intellect, the management of his wealth, and the soundness of his condition in his religion.

﴿And fulfill the commitment﴾: that is, fulfill the contract you make with people, whether in a peace treaty between the people of war and Islam, or among yourselves, and in sales, leases, rentals, and other contracts.

﴿Indeed, the commitment is ever questioned﴾: that is, indeed Allah, may His praise be exalted, will question the one who breaks a commitment about breaking it. That is to say: do not break the lawful covenants between you and those with whom you have made a covenant, O people, so that you betray them and deal treacherously with those to whom you have given it. What is meant is that the covenant is one that will be demanded, as it is said in speech: "So-and-so will surely be asked about so-and-so's covenant."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 35:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with a true balance. That is better and more favourable in outcome.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: ﴿And give full measure﴾ to people ﴿when you measure﴾ for them, giving them their rights due from you, and do not diminish them, ﴿and weigh with a true balance﴾. He means: He has decreed that you also weigh correctly when you weigh for them, with the upright balance, which is justice without crookedness, without deceit, and without trickery.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed over the meaning of al-qistas (a balance, scale). Some of them said: it is the qabban (steelyard).

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Safwan ibn Isa narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Dhakwan narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿and weigh with a true balance﴾, he said: "al-qabban" (the steelyard).

Others said: it is "justice" in Byzantine (Roman) language.

Those who said this:

* Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: al-qistas: "justice" in Byzantine (Roman) language.

Others said: it is the balance, whether small or large. There are two dialectal forms: al-qistas with a kasra on the qaf, and al-qustas with a damma on it, like al-qirtas and al-qurtas. Most of the reciters of Kufa read it with the kasra, and the reciters of Madina and Basra read it with the damma, and some of the Kufan reciters also read it with the damma. Whichever of the two a reciter reads is correct, because they are two well-known dialects and two widely transmitted readings among the reciters of the cities.

* *

As for His words ﴿That is better﴾:

He means: your giving full measure, O people, to those for whom you measure, and your weighing justly for those for whom you weigh, is ﴿better for you﴾ than your diminishing it for them and wronging them in it.

* *

As for His words ﴿and more favourable in outcome﴾:

He means: and better in return and more fitting in its outcome for you, your doing that, because Allah, blessed and exalted, is pleased with it from you, and so He will give you a good reward for it.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with a true balance. That is better and more favourable in outcome﴾, meaning: better in reward and consequence.

And he informed us that Ibn Abbas used to say: "O company of clients (mawali), you have taken charge of two matters by which the people before you were destroyed: this measure, and this balance." He said: It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "No man is able to commit a forbidden act and then leave it, with nothing prompting him but the fear of Allah, except that Allah will replace it for him in the immediate life of this world, before the Hereafter, with something better for him than that."

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and more favourable in outcome﴾, he said: "consequence and reward."

The discussion of the words of the Exalted, ﴿And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — about all of these one will be questioned.﴾ (17:36)

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of His words ﴿and do not pursue (taqfu) that of which you have no knowledge﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: "and do not say that of which you have no knowledge."

Those who said this:

- Ali ibn Dawud related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge﴾: he means, "Do not say."

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — about all of these one will be questioned﴾: "Do not say 'I saw' when you have not seen, nor 'I heard' when you have not heard, for indeed Allah, blessed and exalted, will question you about all of that."

- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge﴾, he said: "Do not say 'I saw' when you have not seen, 'I heard' when you have not heard, and 'I know' when you do not know."

- It was related to me from Muhammad ibn Rabi'a, from Isma'il al-Azraq, from Abu Umar al-Bazzar, from Ibn al-Hanafiyya, who said: "It is false testimony (shahadat al-zur)."

Others said: rather, its meaning is: "and do not accuse (la tarmi)."

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge﴾: he means, "Do not accuse anyone of that of which you have no knowledge."

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and do not pursue﴾: "and do not accuse."

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

These two interpretations are close in meaning, for saying what the speaker has no knowledge of includes false testimony, casting accusations at people falsely, claiming to have heard what one did not hear, and claiming to have seen what one did not see. The root of qafw is slander and false accusation (al-'ada and al-bahat), and from it is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "We are the sons of al-Nadr ibn Kinana; we do not slander our mother, nor do we disown our father." Some of the Basrians used to recite a line of verse on this:

"And like statues, of noble-bridged faces, dwelling among them is modesty, they do not spread slander (al-taqafi)."

[The line is by al-Nabigha al-Ja'di, cited by Abu Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an as evidence that al-taqafi means mutual hurling (of accusations). Lisan al-Arab (q-f-w) says: Abu Ubayd said the original sense of qafw and iqtifa' is the slander a man hurls at his companion. Abu Bakr said: the expression "qafa fulan fulanan" — Abu Ubayd said it means he followed him with an ugly word. Al-Layth said: qafw is the verbal noun of qafa yaqfu, namely to follow something. The Exalted said ﴿wa la taqfu ma laysa laka bihi 'ilm﴾. Al-Farra' said: most readers make it from qafawtu. Some read it as "wa la taqif," like "wa la taqul." Al-Akhfash said: "la taqfu" means "la tattabi'" — do not follow what you do not know. It was said: "Do not say, 'I heard' when you have not heard, nor 'I saw' when you have not seen, nor 'I knew' when you have not known; indeed the hearing, the sight, and the heart — about all of these one will be questioned." "Dumā" is the plural of duma, a statue of marble, ivory, or the like. "Shumm al-'aranin" is the plural of shamma' al-'arnin, meaning those with raised nasal bridges, which is among the signs of their beauty.]

By al-taqafi is meant mutual hurling. He claims that the meaning of His words ﴿la taqfu﴾ is "do not follow what you do not know, and what does not concern you." And some of the scholars of Arabic from Kufa claimed that its origin is qiyafa, which is tracking footprints. If it is as they mention, the reading should be ﴿wa la taqfu﴾ with a damma on the qaf and a sukun on the fa', like "wa la taqul." He said: the Arabs say "qafawtu athrahu" and "quftu athrahu," sometimes placing the waw before the fa' and sometimes after it, as they say "qa'a al-jamalu al-naqata" (when he mounted her, "wa'a" and "'atha" etc.). And he recited from the Arabs by hearing:

"Had I struck you from nearby, it would have kept you from the wolf's call, the one who prevents."

[The line is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, to show that the Arabs say qafa al-shay' when they follow it, as they say qafah. As the poet said: "'aqi," meaning "'a'iq" (one who hinders). Al-Farra' said: most readers make it from qafawtu... and some said "wa la taqif." The Arabs say "qafat athrahu" and "qafawtuhu"; similarly "ya'tam" and "ya'tamy," and "'atha" and "'athā" meaning corruption, which is common, including "shaki al-silah" and "shakī al-silah." I heard some of the Qada'a say "ijtahā mālahu," while the common dialect is "ijtāḥa mālahu." A poet also said: "Had I seen you..." to the end of the line. We have quoted in the previous evidence al-Farra's statement as it appears in Lisan, and there is some divergence from his wording in Ma'ani al-Qur'an here, perhaps due to differing manuscripts. After this line al-Farra cited another line of the same metre and rhyme, belonging to Dhu al-Khirq al-Tuhawi, as in Lisan (b-gh-m): "I thought the bugham of my she-camel was an 'anaq; and it is not, by your life, a she-goat (al-'anaq)." This evidence has already been cited in more than one place in this tafsir.]

That is, "one who hinders," and similar instances are numerous in the speech of the Arabs.

The most correct of these opinions is the statement of the one who said: the meaning is: "Do not speak to people about what you have no knowledge of, for you would then cast falsehood upon them and bear witness against them without truth; that is qafw."

We said this is the most correct view because it is the predominant usage of the Arabs of qafw in this sense.

As for His words ﴿Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart — about all of these one will be questioned﴾, its meaning is: indeed Allah will question these organs about what their owner said — that he heard, or saw, or knew — and on that occasion his limbs will bear witness against him with the truth. He said "ulā'ika" and did not say "tilka," as the poet said:

"He blamed the dwellings after the abode of al-Lawa, and life after those days (ulā'ika al-ayyam)."

[The line is by Jarir ibn al-Khatafi (his Diwan, Sawi edition, p. 551), the second line of a poem in reply to al-Farazdaq, beginning: "Worries traveled, so they spent the night without sleep, and the one of worries seeks every goal." The evidence in this line is that he referred to the days as "ulā'ika," not "tilka," because "ulā'ika" is used for a large plurality, while "hā'ulā'" is used for a small plurality, whether masculine, feminine, rational, or otherwise.]

It was said "ulā'ika" because "ulā'ika" and "hā'ulā'" are used for the small plurality which is used for both masculine and feminine, while "hādhihi" and "tilka" are for the large plurality. The masculine form is used for the small plurality because, in nouns, the masculine came before the feminine, so the masculine applies to the first plurality, and the feminine to the second, the large plurality, since the Arabs model plurals on the pattern of nouns.

The interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly; indeed, you will not tear the earth [apart], nor will you reach the mountains in height.﴾ [37] ﴿All that is evil thereof is hateful in the sight of your Lord.﴾ [38]

Says the Exalted: And do not walk upon the earth arrogant and proud. ﴿Indeed, you will not tear the earth﴾ means: indeed, you will not cut through the earth by your strutting, as Ru'bah said:

"And the dim-depthed, desolate, cut-through [valley]" [[The line opens a lengthy rajaz poem (171 lines in the Leiden 1903 edition of Ru'bah's Diwan, p. 104). Mention of those who said that:

"What pleases him is the sakhun and the 'asid ... and dates, love (ḥubban), with no addition to it" [[These two lines are in the appendix to the poetry of Ru'bah ibn al-'Ajjaj at the end of his Diwan (Leipzig 1903, p. 172). * *

As for His saying: ﴿All that is evil thereof is hateful in the sight of your Lord﴾

The readers differ regarding it. Some of the readers of Medina and most of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿All that is evil thereof is hateful in the sight of your Lord﴾ with the idafah (genitive construction), meaning: all of this which we have mentioned, of these matters we have enumerated from the beginning of our saying ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him﴾ ... up to our saying ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly﴾ — ﴿its evil﴾ means: the evil of what we enumerated to you is hateful in the sight of your Lord.

Those who recited this reading said: ﴿kullu dhalika kana sayyi'uhu﴾ was said with the idafah because among what we enumerated, from His saying ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him﴾, there are matters which are commands to good, such as His saying ﴿And to parents, good treatment﴾ and His saying ﴿And give the relative his right﴾ and what is similar to that. They said: not everything in it is a prohibition from evil; rather, it contains a prohibition from evil and a command to good deeds. Therefore we read ﴿sayyi'uhu﴾. And most of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿kullu dhalika kana sayyi'atan﴾ and said: He only meant by that: all that we enumerated from our saying ﴿And do not kill your children for fear of poverty﴾ and what precedes it is not included. They said: all that we enumerated from that place to this place is evil with no good in it, so the correct recitation is with tanwin. Whoever recites this reading should intend that the hateful is placed before the evil, and that the meaning of the speech in his view is: all that was hateful, evil. For if he makes His saying "hateful" an attribute of "evil," it would necessitate that the reading be "all that was an evil thing hateful in the sight of your Lord," and that contradicts what is in the codices of the Muslims.

The more correct of the two readings in my view is the recitation of the one who reads ﴿kullu dhalika kana sayyi'uhu﴾ with the idafah of "evil" to the pronoun, meaning: all that which we enumerated from ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him﴾ ... ﴿its evil﴾ was, because among these matters are things prohibited and things commanded, and the beginning of the charge and covenant from that place, not from His saying ﴿And do not kill your children﴾, is only a conjunction with what preceded His saying ﴿And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him﴾. When this is so, the reading with the idafah of "evil" to the pronoun is more preferable and more deserving than the reading "sayyi'atan" with tanwin, meaning a single evil.

So the meaning of the speech, then, is: all of this which we have mentioned to you from the matters we enumerated upon you was an evil, hateful in the sight of your Lord, O Muhammad; He dislikes it and forbids it and does not approve of it, so beware of committing it and acting upon it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 39–40:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That is of what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom. And do not make with Allah another deity, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and banished.﴾ (39)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: This which We have explained to you, O Muhammad, of the good morals, whose good We have commanded you and whose evil We have forbidden you, ﴿of what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom﴾, meaning: of the wisdom which We have revealed to you in this Book of Ours.

As for what has been narrated:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿That is of what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom﴾: "It is the Qur'an."

We have already explained the meaning of wisdom (hikmah) earlier in this Book of ours, in a manner that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary.

﴿And do not make with Allah another deity, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and banished﴾: meaning, do not make a partner with Allah in your worship, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed, your own soul and those among the people who know you blaming you, ﴿banished﴾, meaning:

removed and driven away into the Fire. Rather, make your worship sincerely for Allah, the One, the Subduer, and you will be saved from His punishment.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said concerning His saying ﴿blamed and banished﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿blamed and banished﴾: he said: "Expelled."

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿blamed and banished﴾, he said: "Blamed in the worship of Allah, banished into the Fire."

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Has your Lord then chosen for you sons and taken from the angels females? Indeed, you say a terrible saying.﴾ (40)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to those among the polytheists of the Arabs who said: the angels are the daughters of Allah: ﴿Has your Lord then chosen (afasfakum)﴾, O people, ﴿for you sons (bil-banin)﴾, meaning: has your Lord singled you out with male offspring ﴿and taken from the angels females﴾, while you do not accept females for yourselves, but rather bury them alive and kill them, thus you have attributed to Allah what you do not accept for yourselves. ﴿Indeed, you say a terrible saying﴾: His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, to these polytheists who said, of the slander against Allah, what we have mentioned: indeed you, O people, say by your saying: the angels are the daughters of Allah, a terrible saying, and fabricate against Allah a lie of your own.

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿and taken from the angels females﴾, he said: "The Jews said: the angels are the daughters of Allah."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 41–42:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And We have certainly diversified [the lessons] in this Qur'an that they may be reminded, but it does not increase them except in aversion﴾ [17:41].

His saying, exalted be He, means: And We have certainly diversified, for these polytheists who invent lies against Allah, the lessons, signs and proofs in this Qur'an, and We have set forth for them therein examples, and warned them and admonished them therein, ﴿that they may be reminded﴾. He says: that they may remember those proofs against them, and understand the error of what they persist in, and take heed from the lessons, and be admonished by them, and turn back from their ignorance. But they do not take heed from them, nor are they reminded by the signs and warnings that come to them, and Our reminding them does not increase them ﴿except in aversion﴾. He says: except in departure from the truth, distance from it, and flight. The word "aversion" (nufur) in this place is a verbal noun from the expression: "So-and-so fled from this matter, flees from it, nafran and nufuran."

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Say: If there were with Him other gods, as they say, then they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne﴾ [17:42].

His saying, exalted be He, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who have set up another god alongside Allah: If the matter were as you claim, that there are other gods with Him, and it is not as you claim, then those gods would have sought nearness to Allah, the Owner of the Mighty Throne, and sought closeness to Him and a rank from Him.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Say: If there were with Him other gods, as they say, then they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne﴾, he said: If there were with Him other gods, then they would have known His virtue, His rank and His station over them, so they would have sought what brings them near to Him.

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿then they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne﴾, he said: They would have sought nearness to Him, though it is not as they claim.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 43–44:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they say, a great elevation.﴾ (43) ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing but that it glorifies [Him] by His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.﴾ (44)

This is a declaration of transcendence by Allah, the Exalted, of Himself above what the polytheists attribute to Him, those who associate other gods with Him and ascribe daughters to Him. So He said: "Glorification of Allah and exaltation of Him above what you say, O people, of fabrication and lies, for what you ascribe to Him of these matters is not among His attributes, and it is not fitting that He should have such an attribute."

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they say, a great elevation.﴾ "He glorifies Himself when slander is spoken against Him." And He said ﴿above what they say, a great elevation﴾ and did not say "ta'aliyan" (an elevation), just as He said ﴿and devote yourself to Him with devotion﴾ [al-Muzzammil 73:8]. As the poet said:

"You are the ransom for a Ka'bah you demolished,
and you pecked it with your two hands, every peck.
You prevented the dove from its resting place on its roof,
and from the Hatim, so every bird of flight took off."
[[The two verses are evidence that the two verbal nouns "naqr" and "tayyir," which are added to "kull" and are in the accusative as an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq), are not from the same root as the verb preceding them: "al-naqr" is from "naqqara" (with the doubled qaf), and "al-tayyir" is from "tayyara" (with the doubled ya'), though the two preceding verbs are trilateral. But the Arabs permit placing verbal nouns that differ from the verbs preceding them. From this in the Qur'an: "wa tabattal ilayhi tabtila" — the verbal noun of "tabattala" is "al-tabattul," not "al-tabtil," but that is permissible because the root letters are shared between the verbs and the verbal nouns that follow them.]]

* * *

As for His saying ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him﴾

He says: Allah is exalted, O polytheists, above what you attribute to Him, out of magnification and reverence for Him: the seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them, from the believers in Him among the angels, humankind and jinn — while you, despite His bounty upon you and His beautiful favours toward you, fabricate against Him what you fabricate.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿And there is not a thing but that it glorifies [Him] by His praise﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: There is nothing of His creation but that it glorifies Him with His praise.

As related:

* Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'la narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubaydah, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Shall I not inform you of something Noah commanded his son? Indeed Noah said to his son: 'O my son, I command you to say: Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him (Subhan Allah wa bihamdih), for it is the prayer of creation, the glorification of creation, and by it creation is provided for.' Allah said: ﴿And there is not a thing but that it glorifies [Him] by His praise﴾."

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Isa ibn Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard Ikrimah say: "Let none of you blame his beast or his garment, for indeed everything glorifies Him with His praise."

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from Ikrimah regarding ﴿And there is not a thing but that it glorifies [Him] by His praise﴾: "The tree glorifies, and the pillar glorifies."

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih and Zayd ibn Habbab narrated to us, both saying: Jarir Abu al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: We were with Yazid al-Raqashi, and al-Hasan was with him at a meal. They brought in the tablecloth, and Yazid al-Raqashi said: "O Abu Sa'id, does this tablecloth glorify?" He said: "It glorified once."

* Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, and Yunus, from al-Hasan, that they both said regarding His saying ﴿And there is not a thing but that it glorifies [Him] by His praise﴾: "Everything that has a soul."

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Kabir ibn Abd al-Majid narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: "Food glorifies."

* Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah regarding ﴿And there is not a thing but that it glorifies [Him] by His praise﴾: "Everything that has a soul glorifies, whether a tree or a thing that has a soul."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abd Allah ibn Abi, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, that when a man says: "There is no god but Allah," it is the word of sincerity (kalimat al-ikhlas) without which Allah accepts no deed from anyone until he says it; and when he says: "Praise be to Allah," it is the word of gratitude (kalimat al-shukr), by which no servant has ever been thanked by Allah until he says it; and when he says: "Allah is greatest," it fills what is between the heavens and the earth; and when he says: "Glory be to Allah," it is the prayer of all creatures, and no one among His creation calls upon Allah except that He illuminates him with prayer and glorification; and when he says: "There is no power nor strength except by Allah," He says: "My servant has submitted and surrendered."

* * *

As for His saying ﴿but you do not understand their glorification﴾

The Exalted says: But you do not understand the glorification of anything other than the glorification of those who glorify with the likes of your tongues. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing﴾ means: Indeed Allah is Forbearing, not hastening to punish His creatures who oppose His command and disbelieve in Him; and were it not for that, He would have hastened punishment upon these polytheists who call upon other gods and rivals along with Him. ﴿Forgiving﴾ means: concealing their sins for them when they repent of them, by His pardon toward them.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing﴾: "toward His creation, so He does not hasten as some of them hasten against others" ﴿Forgiving﴾: "toward them when they repent."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 43–44:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they say, a great elevation.﴾ (43) ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing but that it glorifies [Him] by His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.﴾ (44)

This is a declaration of transcendence by Allah, the Exalted, of Himself above what the polytheists attribute to Him, those who associate other gods with Him and ascribe daughters to Him. So He said: "Glorification of Allah and exaltation of Him above what you say, O people, of fabrication and lies, for what you ascribe to Him of these matters is not among His attributes, and it is not fitting that He should have such an attribute."

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they say, a great elevation.﴾ "He glorifies Himself when slander is spoken against Him." And He said ﴿above what they say, a great elevation﴾ and did not say "ta'aliyan" (an elevation), just as He said ﴿and devote yourself to Him with devotion﴾ [al-Muzzammil 73:8]. As the poet said:

"You are the ransom for a Ka'bah you demolished,
and you pecked it with your two hands, every peck.
You prevented the dove from its resting place on its roof,
and from the Hatim, so every bird of flight took off."
[[The two verses are evidence that the two verbal nouns "naqr" and "tayyir," which are added to "kull" and are in the accusative as an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq), are not from the same root as the verb preceding them: "al-naqr" is from "naqqara" (with the doubled qaf), and "al-tayyir" is from "tayyara" (with the doubled ya'), though the two preceding verbs are trilateral. But the Arabs permit placing verbal nouns that differ from the verbs preceding them. From this in the Qur'an: "wa tabattal ilayhi tabtila" — the verbal noun of "tabattala" is "al-tabattul," not "al-tabtil," but that is permissible because the root letters are shared between the verbs and the verbal nouns that follow them.]]

* * *

As for His saying ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him﴾

He says: Allah is exalted, O polytheists, above what you attribute to Him, out of magnification and reverence for Him: the seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them, from the believers in Him among the angels, humankind and jinn — while you, despite His bounty upon you and His beautiful favours toward you, fabricate against Him what you fabricate.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿And there is not a thing but that it glorifies [Him] by His praise﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: There is nothing of His creation but that it glorifies Him with His praise.

As related:
