* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing﴾: "toward His creation, so He does not hasten as some of them hasten against others" ﴿Forgiving﴾: "toward them when they repent."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 45:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾ [17:45]

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When you recite the Qur'an, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who do not affirm the resurrection and do not acknowledge reward and punishment, We place between you and them a barrier, which veils their hearts from understanding what you recite to them, so that they might benefit from it, as a punishment from Us for their disbelief. The barrier here is the concealing veil.

As follows:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾: "The hidden barrier is coverings upon their hearts, so that they do not comprehend it and do not benefit from it; they obeyed Satan, and so he overpowered them."

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿a hidden barrier﴾, he said: "It is the coverings (al-akinnah)."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾: He said: Ubayy said: "They do not understand it," and he recited ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you call us, and in our ears is deafness﴾ [41:5]; that does not reach them.

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: The meaning of His saying ﴿hijaban mastura (a hidden barrier)﴾ is "a concealing barrier" (hijaban satiran), but it was expressed in the passive form (mafʻul) while its meaning is active (fa'il), as one says: "You are inauspicious (mash'um) for us and auspicious (maymun)," when the actual meaning is "shā'im" and "yāmin," since it derives from their inauspiciousness and their fortune. He said: The barrier here is the concealing veil, and he said: "hidden" (mastur). Other scholars of the Arabic language used to say: The meaning of that is: a barrier hidden from the servants, so that they do not see it.

And this second view is more apparent in the sense of the speech, that the hidden thing be the barrier, so its meaning is that God has a veil from the sight of people, so their eyes do not perceive it; although the first view also has an understandable basis.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 46:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn away in aversion on their backs.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We have placed over the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter, when you recite the Qur'an to them, coverings (akinnah), which is the plural of kinan (covering), and that is what envelops them of Allah's forsaking them, so that they fail to understand what is recited to them. ﴿And in their ears deafness﴾ means: And We have placed in their ears a heaviness (waqr) preventing them from hearing it, and deafness. The waqr with a fath (a) in the ear means heaviness, and the wiqr with a kasrah (i) means a load.

* *

And His words ﴿And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an﴾

He says: And when you say, "There is no god but Allah," while reciting it, ﴿they turn away on their backs in aversion﴾ means: they scatter and leave you, in aversion to your saying it, out of arrogance toward it and considering it too great that Allah the Exalted be made One.

Some of the people of interpretation have said likewise regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn away﴾: When the Muslims said, "There is no god but Allah," the polytheists denied it and it was grievous to them, so Iblis and his soldiers lined up against it (saffaha) [[It is said: saffahu, with the fa' doubled, and he is musaffin, when he arranges his ranks opposite the enemy's ranks, and they lined up against him: they gathered in ranks.]]. But Allah refused except to let it proceed, support it, make it prevail, and make it manifest over those who oppose it. It is a word: whoever disputes by it prevails, and whoever fights by it is victorious. Only the people of this peninsula among the Muslims know it, the peninsula which a rider crosses in a few nights, and a long time passes among groups of people who do not know it nor acknowledge it.

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn away on their backs in aversion﴾: out of hatred for what is spoken, so that they would not hear it, just as the people of Noah used to put their fingers in their ears so that they would not hear what he commanded them of seeking forgiveness and repentance, and "they cover themselves with their garments" (yastaghshuna thiyabahum). He said: they wrap themselves in their garments, and put their fingers in their ears so that they would not hear, and so that they would not be looked at.

Others said: What is meant by His words ﴿they turn away on their backs in aversion﴾ is the devils, and that they flee from the recitation of the Qur'an and the remembrance of Allah.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dhari' narrated to me, saying: Rawh ibn al-Musayyab Abu Raja' al-Kalbi narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Malik narrated to us, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn away on their backs in aversion﴾: they are the devils.

The view we have stated is more consistent with what the apparent meaning of the revelation indicates, because Allah, the Exalted, followed that with His words ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a hidden barrier﴾. So it is more fitting that this be a report about them, since it is connected to their report, than that it be a report about those for whom mention is not permitted. As for nufur (aversion), it is the plural of nafir, just as qu'ud is the plural of qa'id and julus the plural of jalis. It is also permissible that it be a verbal noun (masdar) brought from a non-identical root, since His words ﴿they turned away﴾ carry the meaning of "they fled," so the meaning of the speech becomes "they fled in flight," as Imru' al-Qays said:

*"And I tamed her, so the unruly one was humbled with an humbling"* [[This is the second half of a verse by Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr al-Kindi, whose first half is: "And we came to the good, and our speech was stilted"... It is from a qasida of 54 verses, and this is the twenty-fifth in it (see Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa, Halabi edition, p. 38). The author cites it to show that the Qur'anic phrase "turned away on their backs in aversion" may have nufur as the plural of nafir, like julus as plural of jalis and qu'ud as plural of qa'id, and may also be a verbal noun of nafara, an absolute object of the verb "turned away," since it returns to the sense of "in aversion," just as Imru' al-Qays's "idhlal" returns to the sense of "dhull," with some difference in meaning between them. But the Arabs are lenient in putting some verbal nouns in place of others by interpretation.]]

When *rudt* means "I humbled," then the humbling is derived from its meaning, not from its wording.

The Word of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿We know best what they listen to when they listen to you, and when they confer privately, when the wrongdoers say, "You follow none but a man bewitched."﴾ (17:47)

Allah, the Exalted, says: We know best, O Muhammad, what those among your people who do not believe in the Hereafter, the polytheists, listen to when they listen to you while you recite the Book of Allah. ﴿And when they confer privately﴾. Some of the people of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'Arabiyya) from Basra used to say: the najwa (private conferring) is their act, so He made them the najwa itself, just as one says, "They are a people of riḍā (contentment)," when riḍā is in fact their act.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿when the wrongdoers say, "You follow none but a man bewitched"﴾:

He means: when the polytheists who associate others with Allah say, "You follow none but a man bewitched." It is reported that by the najwa He meant those who consulted together about the matter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the Dar al-Nadwa (the assembly house of the Quraysh).

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil, the people of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿when they listen to you﴾: he said, it is like the speech of al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and those with him in the Dar al-Nadwa.

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similarly.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿when they listen to you and when they confer privately, when the wrongdoers say...﴾ ... the verse. Their private conferring was that they claimed he was a madman and a sorcerer, and they said ﴿the fables of the ancients﴾.

Some of the people of Arabic grammar from Basra took His saying ﴿You follow none but a man bewitched﴾ to mean: you follow none but a man who has saḥr, that is, a lung (ri'a). The Arabs call the lung saḥr, and the musaḥḥar (one who has been fed, nourished) comes from their saying of a man when he is cowardly: "his saḥr has swelled." Likewise, anything of a human or other that has eaten or drunk is called maskhūr and musaḥḥar, as Labid said:

"So if you ask us what we are, we are—
sparrows among these musaḥḥar (fed) creatures."

[The line is in the Diwan of Labid (Tusi recension, Vienna edition 1880, p. 81). In its commentary: "'Asafir: small and weak. That is, we are the sons of a people who have passed away. Musaḥḥar: sustained by food and drink." And His saying, "You are only among the musaḥḥarin" (26:153) is from this. The author cited it for this, saying: "al-musaḥḥar: from their saying of a man when he is cowardly, 'his saḥr has swelled.' Likewise, anything that has eaten and drunk, of a human or other, is called maskhūr and musaḥḥar, as Labid said: 'So if you ask us...' the line." In Lisan al-'Arab (s-ḥ-r): Labid's words "So if you ask us... etc., the line" can be read in both ways, and His saying "You are only among the musaḥḥarin" can mean from nourishment or from deception.]

And others said:

"And we are fed (nusaḥḥar) with food and drink"

[This is the second half of a verse by Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr al-Kindi:
"We find ourselves hastening toward a matter unseen,
and we are fed (nusḥar) with food and drink.
Sparrows, flies and worms,
and bolder than the wolves with their charging."

The author of Lisan al-'Arab, after citing the two lines, said: (s-ḥ-r) means we are nourished or deceived. Ibn Barri said: His words "mūḍi'īn" mean hastening. His words "for a matter unseen" mean death, whose time is hidden from us, while we are distracted from it by food and drink. And saḥr means deception. In Mukhtar al-Shi'r al-Jahili, with the commentary of Mustafa al-Saqqa (Halabi edition, p. 79), on the first line of the two: "mūḍi'īn: hastening. li-amr ghayb: he means death or an unknown future. It is also reported as li-ḥatm ghayb. Nusaḥḥar: we are distracted or nourished. He says: we see ourselves in this world hastening toward death, whose time is hidden from us, or toward an unknown future of which we know nothing, and we are diverted from it by food and drink. He means: how can one who is hastening to drink the cup of death enjoy food and drink? In the commentary on the second line: 'asafir: weak birds; mujallaḥ: bold, the feminine is mujallaḥa. He says: we are most like sparrows, flies and worms in our weakness, but we are bolder in evil and in committing sins than fierce wolves."]

That is, we are nourished by both. So, in his view, the meaning was: "You follow none but a man who has a lung, who eats food and drinks drink, not an angel who has no need of food and drink." And what the one who said this said is not far from the truth.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 48:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Look how they coin for you comparisons, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way.﴾ (17:48)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Look, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart and take heed, how they have coined for you comparisons and likened for you likenesses, by their saying: "He is bewitched," "He is a poet," and "He is possessed." ﴿So they have gone astray﴾ means: they have deviated from the right course by what they have said. ﴿So they cannot find a way﴾ means: they cannot be guided to the path of truth, because of their straying from it and their distance from it, and because God has forsaken them from reaching it. They are therefore unable to find an exit from the disbelief they are in, since they are not granted success in faith in Him.

As related:

◆ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿So they cannot find a way﴾, he said: "An exit." [It refers to] al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and his companions as well.

◆ Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿Look how they coin for you comparisons, so they have gone astray and cannot find a way﴾, "an exit." [It refers to] al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and his companions.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 49:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "When we have become bones and crumbled particles, shall we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾

Exalted is He, mentioning and reporting the saying of those who do not believe in the Hereafter among the polytheists of Quraysh, and they said out of their obstinacy: ﴿When we have become bones﴾, not shattered or broken after our death and our decay, ﴿and crumbled particles﴾, meaning dust in our graves.

As follows:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God ﴿crumbled particles﴾, he said: dust.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muawiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And they say, "When we have become bones and crumbled particles"﴾, he said: dust. The word for crumbled particles (rufat) has no singular, and it is in the position of fine fragments and debris. It is said from it: rufita yarfatu raftan, so he is marfut, when he is made like debris and crushed remains.

* *

And His words ﴿Shall we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?﴾

They said, denying the resurrection after death: "Shall we indeed be resurrected after we have gone into the graves as bones not shattered, and crumbled particles that are shattered, and we have decayed and become dust therein, as a created creation, originated as we were before death, anew? We will be restored as we began." So He, majestic in His majesty, answered them, informing them of His power to resurrect them after their death and to originate them as they were before their decay, a new creation, in whatever state they were in, whether bones or crumbled particles, or stones or iron, or anything else that they consider too great to be recreated like themselves, alive. Say, O Muhammad: "Be stones or iron, or a creation of what is greater in your breasts."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 50–51:

The explanation of the words of His, exalted is He: "Say: Be you stones or iron (50) or a creation of what is greater in your breasts. They will say: 'Who will restore us?' Say: 'He who brought you into being the first time.' Then they will shake their heads at you and say: 'When will it be?' Say: 'It may well be soon.'" (51)

And as the poet said:

"For I, with the praise of God, have not worn the garment of an immoral person, nor have I cloaked myself in treachery."

Meaning: "For I, and praise belongs to God, have not worn the garment of an immoral person."

He says: and you will reckon, upon your arrival at the Resurrection, because of the terror of what you witness there, that you did not remain in the earth except a little, just as He, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿He will say, "How long did you remain on earth, counting years?" They will say, "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count."﴾

Those who said this:

* Ali related to me, he said: Abdullah related to me, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿On the Day when He calls you, and you respond with His praise﴾: he says, "By His command."

* Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, ﴿and you respond with His praise﴾: he said, "By His command."

And others said: The meaning of that is: you will respond with knowledge of Him and obedience to Him.

Those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿On the Day when He calls you, and you respond with His praise﴾: that is, with knowledge of Him and obedience to Him.

The most correct of these sayings, in the view of the truth, is that it should be said: its meaning is: you will respond to God from your graves by His power and His calling you, and praise belongs to God in every state, just as the speaker says: "I did that deed with the praise of God," meaning: praise belongs to God for everything I have done. And as the poet said:

"For I, with the praise of God, have not worn the garment of an immoral person, nor have I cloaked myself in treachery."

Meaning: "For I, and praise belongs to God, have not worn the garment of an immoral person."

* *

And His saying ﴿and you will think that you tarried not but a little﴾.

He says: and you will reckon, upon your arrival at the Resurrection, because of the terror of what you witness there, that you did not remain in the earth except a little, just as He, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿He will say, "How long did you remain on earth, counting years?" They will say, "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who count."﴾

The people of ta'wil said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and you will think that you tarried not but a little﴾: that is, in the world; the world diminished in their own souls and became small when they witnessed the Day of Resurrection.

* *

And His saying ﴿And say to My servants that they should say that which is best﴾.

His exalted remembrance says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ):

"And say, O Muhammad, to My servants: let some of them say to others that which is best in dialogue and address."

As related:

* Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, he said: al-Nadr related to us, he said: al-Mubarak informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding this verse ﴿And say to My servants that they should say that which is best﴾, he said: "That which is best; one should not say to him the like of what he says. He says to him: May God have mercy upon you, may God forgive you."

* *

And His saying ﴿Indeed, Satan incites discord among them﴾.

He says: Indeed, Satan spoils the dialogue of some of them with others; he incites discord among them, meaning: he corrupts them and stirs up evil between them. ﴿Indeed, Satan is ever to mankind an open enemy﴾: he says, Indeed Satan was an enemy to Adam and his offspring, having made clear his enmity toward them by what he showed to Adam of envy and his deception of him until he expelled him from the Garden.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 54:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Your Lord knows best about you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you; or if He wills, He will punish you. And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], as a guardian over them.﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says to these polytheists of Quraysh who said, ﴿"When we are bones and crumbled remains, will we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾: ﴿Your Lord knows best about you, O people.﴾ ﴿If He wills, He will have mercy upon you﴾ by turning to you in His mercy, until you repent of what you are upon of disbelief in Him and in the Last Day. ﴿If He wills, He will punish you﴾ by forsaking you from faith, so that you die upon your polytheism, and He will punish you on the Day of Resurrection for your disbelief in Him.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abd al-Malik ibn Jurayj, regarding His words ﴿Your Lord knows best about you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you﴾, he said: "That you believe. ﴿Or if He wills, He will punish you﴾, that you die upon polytheism as you are."

* *

As for His words ﴿And We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾:

He says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "And We have not sent you, O Muhammad, over those to whom We sent you as a guardian over them, to make them obey Us as a lord or a watcher. We sent you to them only to convey Our messages, and their turning away and their management are in Our hands. If We will, We have mercy on them, and if We will, We punish them."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 55:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth. And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others, and We gave David the Zabur﴾ (55)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet ﷺ: "Your Lord, O Muhammad, knows best who is in the heavens and the earth, and what will set them right, for He is their Creator, their Provider and their Manager. He is also the most knowing of who is deserving of repentance and mercy, and who is deserving of punishment, the one most guided to the truth being the one for whom mercy and happiness have preceded from Me, and the one most astray being the one for whom wretchedness and abandonment have preceded from Me." He means: "So let that not weigh heavily upon you, for that is from My doing with them, and it is part of My preferring some prophets over others, by sending some of them to some of the creation and some of them to all of it, and by raising some of them above others in rank."

As for what has been related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Your Lord knows best who is in the heavens and the earth. And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others﴾: "Allah took Ibrahim as a close friend (khalil), and spoke to Musa directly (taklim). Allah made 'Isa like the likeness of Adam: He created him from dust, then said to him, 'Be,' and he was. He was a servant of Allah and His Messenger, a word from Allah and a spirit from Him. He gave Sulayman a kingdom that would not be fitting for anyone after him, and He gave Dawud the Zabur. We used to narrate that it was a supplication taught to Dawud, containing glorification and praise, with nothing in it of lawful or unlawful, nor of obligations or prescribed limits. And Allah forgave Muhammad what he had done before and after."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others﴾: "Allah spoke to Musa, and He sent Muhammad to the people as a whole."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 56–57:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Him; they have no power to remove the harm from you, nor to transfer it﴾ (17:56).

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people who worship besides God some of His creation: Call upon, O people, those whom you claim to be lords and gods besides Him, at a harm that befalls you, and then look whether they have the power to repel that from you, or to transfer it from you to others, so that you would take them as gods. For they have no power over that and do not possess it; it is He, your Creator and their Creator, who possesses it and has power over it. It was also said: those to whom the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to say this were worshipping the angels, Ezra (ʿUzayr), and the Messiah, and some of them were worshipping a group of the jinn.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Him; they have no power to remove the harm from you, nor to transfer it﴾, he said: The people of polytheism used to say: "We worship the angels and ʿUzayr," and they are the ones who are called upon, meaning the angels, the Messiah, and ʿUzayr.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord, [striving to see] which of them would be nearest, and they hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever feared﴾ (17:57).

He, the Exalted, says: Those whom these polytheists call upon as lords, ﴿seek a means of access to their Lord﴾, meaning: those who are called upon seek nearness and proximity to their Lord, because they are people of faith in Him, while the polytheists worship them besides God. ﴿Which of them would be nearest﴾: which of them, by his righteous deeds and his diligence in worshipping Him, is nearer to Him in rank. ﴿And they hope﴾ by those deeds ﴿for His mercy﴾ and fear His command ﴿His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿is ever feared﴾, meaning: to be guarded against.

The scholars of interpretation said things similar to what we have said, except that they differed regarding those who are called upon. Some of them said: they are a group of the jinn.

Mention of those who said this:

Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Muʿawiya related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from ʿAbdullah, regarding His saying ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord﴾, he said: Some people from mankind used to worship a group of the jinn, then the jinn embraced Islam while mankind remained on their disbelief, so God, the Exalted, revealed ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord﴾, meaning the jinn.

Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu al-Nuʿman al-Hakam ibn ʿAbdullah al-ʿIjli related to us, saying: Shuʿba related to us, from Sulayman, from Ibrahim, from Abu Maʿmar, who said: ʿAbdullah said regarding this verse, ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord, [striving to see] which of them would be nearest﴾, he said: A tribe of the jinn that were worshipped, then they embraced Islam.

ʿAbd al-Warith ibn ʿAbd al-Samad related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: al-Husayn related to me, from Qatada, from Maʿbad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Zimmani, from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUtba ibn Masʿud, from Ibn Masʿud, regarding His saying ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning a group of Arabs who used to worship a group of the jinn, then the jinn embraced Islam, and the humans who were worshipping them did not know of their Islam, so ﴿Those who call upon seek a means of access to their Lord, [striving to see] which of them would be nearest﴾ was revealed.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUtba ibn Masʿud, from the report of his paternal uncle ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, who said: This verse was revealed concerning a group of Arabs who used to worship a group of the jinn, then the jinn embraced Islam while the group of Arabs did not realize that.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Those who call upon seek a means of access to their Lord﴾: a people who worshipped the jinn, then those jinn embraced Islam, so God, the Exalted, said ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord﴾.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from Abu Maʿmar, from ʿAbdullah (﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord﴾), who said: A group of humans used to worship a group of the jinn, then the group of jinn embraced Islam and the humans persisted in worshipping them, so He said ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord﴾.

al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn ʿUyayna informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from Abu Maʿmar, who said: ʿAbdullah said: Some people used to worship a group of the jinn, then those jinn embraced Islam, and humans remained steadfast in their worship, so Allah, blessed and exalted, said ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord﴾.

al-Hasan related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq related to us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord, [striving to see] which of them would be nearest﴾, he said: Some people from the people of ignorance used to worship a group of the jinn; when the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent, they all embraced Islam, and they were seeking which of them would be nearest.

Others said: Rather, they are the angels.

al-Husayn ibn ʿAli al-Sada'i related to me, saying: Yahya ibn al-Sakan related to us, saying: Abu al-ʿAwwam informed us, saying: Qatada informed us, from ʿAbdullah ibn Maʿbad al-Zimmani, from ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, who said: Some tribes of the Arabs used to worship a category of angels called the jinn, and they would say: they are the daughters of God. So God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿Those whom they call upon﴾, O company of Arabs, ﴿seek a means of access to their Lord﴾.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord﴾: those who call upon the angels, the angels seek a means of access to their Lord, ﴿[striving to see] which of them would be nearest, and they hope for His mercy﴾, up to ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever feared﴾. He said: These are the polytheists who worshipped the angels.

Others said: Rather, they are ʿUzayr, Jesus, and his mother.

Mention of those who said this:

Yahya ibn Jaʿfar related to me, saying: Yahya ibn al-Sakan informed us, saying: Shuʿba informed us, from Ismaʿil al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord﴾, he said: Jesus, his mother, and ʿUzayr.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu al-Nuʿman al-Hakam ibn ʿAbdullah al-ʿIjli related to us, saying: Shuʿba related to us, from Ismaʿil al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Jesus son of Mary, his mother, and ʿUzayr are in this verse ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord﴾.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿seek a means of access to their Lord﴾, he said: Jesus son of Mary, ʿUzayr, and the angels.

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas used to say regarding His saying ﴿Those whom they call upon seek a means of access to their Lord﴾: it is ʿUzayr, the Messiah, the sun, and the moon.

The most correct of the sayings regarding the interpretation of this verse is the saying of ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud which we have related from Abu Maʿmar from him. That is because God, the Exalted, informed that those whom the polytheists take as gods seek a means of access to their Lord during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ); and it is well known that ʿUzayr did not exist in the time of our Prophet, peace be upon him, so as to seek a means of access to his Lord, and that Jesus had been raised. Only one who is alive and exists, acting in obedience to God and drawing near to Him through righteous deeds, seeks a means of access to his Lord. As for one who has no way to act, how would he seek a means of access to his Lord? Since this saying has no meaning, there is no saying on this matter except the saying of the one who said what we have chosen as interpretation, or the saying of the one who said they are the angels; these are two sayings which the apparent sense of the revelation allows. As for al-wasilah (the means of access), we have already shown that it is nearness and proximity.

The scholars of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said: al-wasilah: nearness.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada: al-wasilah, he said: nearness and closeness.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 58:

The discussion of the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And there is not a city but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. That is in the Decree inscribed.﴾ (58)

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: There is no city among the cities but that We will destroy its people through annihilation, eradicating them completely before the Day of Resurrection, or We will punish it, whether by affliction through being slain by the sword or by other kinds of punishment, a severe punishment.

As related:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿And there is not a city but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection﴾, [He said: "Annihilating it"] ﴿or punish it﴾ with killing and affliction. He said: Every city on earth will be struck by some of this.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, with similar wording, except that he said: This or some of it will strike it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And there is not a city but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it﴾: It is a decree from Allah, as you hear, from which there is no escape; either He will destroy it by death, or He will destroy it by a eradicating punishment if they abandon His command and deny His messengers.

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And there is not a city but We will destroy it﴾: He said: Annihilating it.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah, who said: When fornication and usury become widespread among the people of a city, Allah permits its destruction.

* *

And His saying ﴿That is in the Decree inscribed﴾

It means: in the Book in which everything that exists is recorded, and that is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

As related:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿That is in the Decree inscribed﴾: "In the Mother of the Book." And he recited ﴿Had it not been for a word from Allah that had preceded﴾. And by His saying ﴿mastur﴾ he means written and clear. From it is the verse of al-Ajjaj:

And know that the Possessor of Majesty has decreed
In the earlier scriptures what was inscribed:
Your affair, so guard it, O Nahr.

[These are three verses of rajaz meter by al-Ajjaj ibn Ru'bah, from a lengthy rajaz poem of 229 verses in which he praises Umar ibn Ubayd Allah ibn Ma'mar (see Diwan al-Ajjaj, ed. Ahlwardt, 1903, pp. 15–21). In it, "al-Suhuf" appears in one place instead of "al-Kutub", and "fa-'lam" appears in one place instead of "wa'lam". See also Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu Ubaydah (1:383), who said: "mastur" means clear and written; in his narration it is "al-Natr" with a fatha on the nun and the ta. He said: al-Natr means deception. In Lisan al-Arab (under n-t-r): "al-natr" with a vowelled nun means corruption and loss. Al-Ajjaj said: "And know... etc." the verses.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 59:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We did not refrain, O Muhammad, from sending the signs that your people asked for, except that those before them, the denying nations, had asked for the same as their request. Then, when the signs came to them that they had asked for, they denied their messengers, and did not believe despite the coming of the signs, so they were hastened (to punishment). Thus We did not send the signs to your people, because if We had sent them and they denied them, We would have followed in hastening the punishment for them the course taken with the nations before them.

We say in this what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd and Ibn WakI' narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ja'far ibn Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The people of Makkah asked the Prophet (ﷺ) to make Safa into gold for them and to remove the mountains from them so that they could farm. It was said to him: If you wish, we will give them respite, perhaps we will gather some of them; and if you wish, we will give them what they asked for, but if they disbelieve they will be destroyed as those before them were destroyed. He said: Rather, give them respite. So Allah revealed: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾.

Ishaq ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Mas'ud ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, from Malik ibn Dinar, from al-Hasan, concerning the saying of God, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾. He said: A mercy for you, O nation; for if We had sent the signs and you denied them, what befell those before you would befall you.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to me, from Ayyub, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The polytheists said to Muhammad (ﷺ): O Muhammad, you claim that there were prophets before you, some of whom the wind was subjected to, and some of whom raised the dead. If it pleases you that we believe in you and affirm you, then ask your Lord to make Safa gold for us. So Allah revealed to him: I have heard what they said. If you wish, We will do what they asked; but if they do not believe, the punishment will descend, for there is no respite after the descent of a sign. And if you wish, you may give your people respite. He said: O Lord, I will give them respite.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾. He said: The people of Makkah said to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ): If what you say is true, and it would delight you that we believe, then turn Safa into gold for us. Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: If you wish, it will be what your people asked of you; but if they do not believe then, they will not be given respite. And if you wish, you may give your people respite. He said: Rather, I will give my people respite. So Allah revealed: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged themselves through it﴾, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿No town that We destroyed believed before them; will they then believe?﴾.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, that they asked that Safa be turned into gold. Allah said: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾. Ibn Juraij said: No town came with a sign and then denied it without being punished; so if Safa were made gold for them and they still did not believe, they would be punished.

The first "an" which is with "manaʻana" (منعنا, "refrained") is in a position of nasb (accusative) by the governing of "manaʻana" upon it, and the second "an" is in rafʻ (nominative), because the meaning of the speech is: And what refrained Us from sending the signs was only the denial of the former peoples; so the verb is for the second "an" (i.e., the second "an" is the subject of the verb).

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged themselves through it, and We do not send the signs except as a warning﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And Thamud had asked for signs, O Muhammad, before your people, so We gave them what they asked, and We made that sign a she-camel that is visible (mubsirah); the seeing is attributed to the she-camel, as you say of a wound: "mudihah" (clear), and this is a "hujjah mubinah" (clear proof). What is meant by "mubsirah" is: the luminous, clear one, which whoever sees it becomes a people of insight regarding it, that it is a proof from God, as it was said: ﴿and the day, giving sight (mubsiran)﴾.

As follows:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign﴾: that is, clear (bayyinah).

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of God, the Mighty, His remembrance: ﴿the she-camel as a visible sign﴾, he said: a sign.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿but they wronged themselves through it﴾

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: Their wrongdoing was through it, and that is because they killed her and hamstrung her; so their wrong was in hamstringing her and killing her. It has been said that the meaning of this is: they disbelieved in it. There is no sense to this except that its sayer intends: they disbelieved in God by killing her, and this would be a valid sense.

As for His saying: ﴿And We do not send the signs except as a warning﴾, He says: We do not send the lessons and the reminders except as a warning to the servants.

As follows:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿And We do not send the signs except as a warning﴾, and that God warns people with whatever sign He wills, so that they may take heed, or be reminded, or return. It was mentioned to us that Kufa quaked in the time of Ibn Mas'ud, and he said: O people, your Lord asks you to make amends, so make amends to Him.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, concerning ﴿And We do not send the signs except as a warning﴾, he said: the devastating death.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 60 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And [remember] when We said to you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people. And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and [also] the cursed tree in the Qur'an. And We threaten them, but it increases them not except in great transgression."﴾

This is an exhortation from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) to convey his message, and an announcement from Him that He has already given him the assurance that He will protect him from anyone who intends him harm or destruction. He, may His praise be exalted, says: Remember, O Muhammad, when We said to you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people" in power, so they are in His grasp and cannot escape His will. And We will protect you from them, so do not be intimidated by any of them, and proceed with what We have commanded you concerning the conveying of Our message.

The scholars of ta'wil (interpretation) have spoken in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', who said: I heard al-Hasan say: "[Allah] has encompassed the people" means: He protected you from the people.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿And when We said to you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people"﴾: He said: It means: "I have encompassed the Arabs for you, so that they will not kill you." So he knew that he would not be killed.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated [to us]; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Waraqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿has encompassed the people﴾: He said: "They are in His grasp."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Mu'ammar, from al-Zuhri, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, regarding his words ﴿has encompassed the people﴾: He said: "He protected you from the people." Mu'ammar said: Qatadah said the same.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatadah, regarding his words ﴿And when We said to you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people"﴾: He said: "He protected you from the people."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And when We said to you, "Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people"﴾: That is, He protected you from the people until you convey the message of your Lord.

* * *

As for His words ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾:

The scholars of ta'wil differed regarding it. Some of them said: It is a sight seen with the eye, which is what the Prophet (ﷺ) saw when he was taken on the Night Journey from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem).

Those who said this:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He said: "It is a sight with the eye which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown on the night he was taken on the Night Journey, and it was not a dream seen in sleep."

- Ibn Wakie narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who was asked about His words ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He said: "It is a sight with the eye which the Prophet (ﷺ) saw on the night he was taken on the Night Journey."

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Amr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, similarly.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: Amr narrated to us, from Furat al-Qazzaz, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He said: "That was on the night he was taken to Bayt al-Maqdis, and he saw what he saw, and the polytheists denied him when he informed them."

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He said: "He was taken by night to Bayt al-Maqdis, prayed there, and Allah showed him what He showed him of the signs. Then he woke up in Mecca, and he informed them that he had been taken to Bayt al-Maqdis. They said to him: 'O Muhammad, what is this matter? You spent the evening there, then you woke up among us, telling us that you went to Bayt al-Maqdis.' They were astonished at that, to the point that some of them apostatized from Islam."

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdhah narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He said: "The disbelievers of Mecca said: 'Is it not the case that whoever lies about the son of Abu Kabshah, he claims that he traveled a two-month journey in a single night?'"

- Abu Husayn narrated to me, saying: Abthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Abu Malik, regarding this verse ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He said: "It is his journey to Bayt al-Maqdis."

- Abu al-Sa'ib and Ya'qub narrated to me, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Abd Allah, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, regarding His words ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He said: "When he was taken by night."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, regarding ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He said: "On the night he was taken by night."

- Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Mu'ammar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He said: "The sight which We showed you in Bayt al-Maqdis on the night you were taken by night; that was the trial of the disbeliever."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He says: "It is what Allah showed him of signs and lessons on his journey to Bayt al-Maqdis." It has been related to us that some people apostatized after their Islam when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told them of his journey; they denied it, disbelieved him, and were astonished by it, and said: "You tell us that you traveled a two-month journey in a single night."

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He said: "It is what was shown to him in Bayt al-Maqdis on the night he was taken by night."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you﴾: He said: "Allah showed him signs on the road to Bayt al-Maqdis on the night he was taken by night. The obligation of prayer was revealed on the night he was taken by night, a year before he migrated, and nine [years] of the ten he spent in Mecca [[Possibly: "and nine years"—i.e., after the passing of nine years... etc.]]. Then he returned that same night. Quraysh said: 'He dined with us and woke up among us, then he claims that he came to Syria in one night and returned. By Allah, the kite would take two months to reach it: one month going and one month returning.'"

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He said: "This is [the sight] at the time he was taken by night to Bayt al-Maqdis, by which some people were tested. They said: 'He goes to Bayt al-Maqdis and returns in one night.'" And he said: "When Gabriel, peace be upon him, brought me the Buraq [the steed of the Night Journey] to carry me upon it, it flicked its ears and drew its parts together. Gabriel looked at it and said: 'By the One who sent me with the truth from Him, no one of the children of Adam has ever ridden a better one than this.' He said: 'So it flicked its ears, and it sweated until what was beneath it flowed, and the extent of its stride was as far as its gaze.'" When he informed them of that, they said: "Muhammad would not stop until he brings a lie that travels from every direction." So they came to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and said: "This companion of yours says such and such." He said: "Did he say that?" They said: "Yes." He said: "If he said that, then he has spoken the truth." They said: "Do you affirm him if he says he went to Bayt al-Maqdis and returned in one night?" Abu Bakr said: "Yes, may Allah strip your minds away! I affirm him regarding the news of the heavens, and the heavens are farther than Bayt al-Maqdis, yet I would not affirm him regarding the news of Bayt al-Maqdis?" They said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "We have come to Bayt al-Maqdis, so describe it to us." When they said that, Allah, blessed and exalted, lifted it up and placed it before his eyes, and he began saying: "It is such and such, and in it is such and such." Some of them said: "By your father, if he has erred in a single letter..." They said: "This man is a sorcerer."

- I was told, on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He means the night he was taken by night to Bayt al-Maqdis, then he returned that same night, and it was a trial for them.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated [to us]; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Waraqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿the sight which We showed you﴾: He said: "At the time Muhammad (ﷺ) was taken by night."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly.

Others said: It is his sight in which he saw that he entered Mecca.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾: He said: It is said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown that he and his companions entered Mecca, while he was at that time in Medina. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) hastened to set out for Mecca before the appointed time, but the polytheists turned him back. Some people said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has been turned back, and he had told us that he would enter it." So his return became a trial for them.

Others said, among those who said it was a dream seen in sleep: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) only saw in his sleep some people climbing his pulpit.

Those who said this:

- I was told, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Zabalah, who said: Abd al-Muhaymin ibn Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from my grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw the Banu Fulan leaping upon his pulpit like monkeys, and that grieved him. So he never again was seen laughing fully until he died. He said: And Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed concerning that: ﴿And We did not make the sight which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾ ... the verse. [[Meaning: the people never saw him laugh a complete laugh after that until he died.]]

The most correct of these sayings in terms of truth is the saying of the one who said: it refers to the sight of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), which he saw of signs and lessons on his route to Bayt al-Maqdis, and Bayt al-Maqdis on the night he was taken by night. We have already mentioned some of that at the beginning of this surah.

We have said that this is more correct because the consensus (ijma') of the authoritative scholars of ta'wil holds that this verse was revealed concerning that, and Allah, mighty and majestic, intended it by it. When that is so, the meaning of the speech is: "And We did not make your sight which We showed you on the night We took you by night from Mecca to Bayt al-Maqdis except as a trial for the people": that is, except as a affliction for the people who apostatized from Islam when they were informed of the sight which he (peace be upon him) had seen, and for the polytheists of Mecca, who by hearing that from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) increased in their wandering astray and in disbelief upon their disbelief.

As:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿except as a trial for the people﴾ [[The text has been abridged, relying on what was previously mentioned shortly before.]].

As for His words ﴿and the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾, the scholars of ta'wil differed regarding it. Some of them said: It is the tree of Zaqqum.

Those who said this:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Abu Ubaydah narrated to us, from Amr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿and the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾: He said: "It is the tree of Zaqqum."

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾: He said: "It is the tree of Zaqqum. Abu Jahl said: 'Does the son of Abu Kabshah threaten me with the tree of Zaqqum?' Then he called for dates and butter, and began saying: 'Zaqqimni' [eat them up for me]." So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed: ﴿Its shoots are like the heads of devils﴾, and He revealed: ﴿And We threaten them, but it increases them not except in great transgression.﴾

- Abu al-Sa'ib and Ya'qub narrated to me, both saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, regarding ﴿and the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾: He said: "It is the tree of Zaqqum."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, similarly.

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿and the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾: "Indeed, the Quraysh used to eat dates and butter, and they would say: 'Eat this Zaqqum.'" Abu Raja' said: Abd al-Quddus narrated to me, from al-Hasan, who said: "Allah described it to them in al-Saffat."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hawdhah narrated to us, saying: Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: Abu Jahl and the disbelievers of Mecca said: "Is it not the case that whoever lies about the son of Abu Kabshah, he promises you a fire in which stones burn, and claims that a tree will grow in it?" ﴿and the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾: He said: "It is the tree of Zaqqum."

- Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: Abthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us, from Abu Malik, regarding this verse ﴿and the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾: He said: "It is the tree of Zaqqum."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, who said regarding His words ﴿and the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾: "It is the tree of Zaqqum."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from a man called Badr, from Ikrimah, who said: "The tree of Zaqqum."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Furat al-Qazzaz, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr was asked about the cursed tree, and he said: "The tree of Zaqqum."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik al-Azrami, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿and the cursed tree﴾: He said: "The tree of Zaqqum."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, similarly.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated [to us]; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Waraqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾: He said: "Zaqqum."

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Abu al-Mahjal, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, that he used to swear without making an exception that the cursed tree is the tree of Zaqqum.

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Furat al-Qazzaz, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about the cursed tree in the Qur'an, and he said: "The tree of Zaqqum."

- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Amr, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "It is the Zaqqum."

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and the cursed tree in the Qur'an, and We threaten them, but it increases them not except in great transgression﴾: "It is the tree of Zaqqum, with which Allah threatened His servants, and they were tested by it, until one of them, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, said: 'Your companion claims that in the Fire there is a tree, and the Fire consumes trees, and by Allah, we know of Zaqqum only as dates and butter, so eat your fill of it.' So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed when they were astonished that there could be a tree in the Fire: ﴿Indeed, it is a tree that springs from the root of Hellfire. Its shoots are like the heads of devils﴾, [and He said:] 'Indeed, I created it from fire, and I torment with it whomever I will of My servants.'"

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 60 (part 2 of 2):

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾, he said: It is the zaqqum. That is because the polytheists said: "This man tells us that there is a tree in the Fire, yet the Fire consumes trees until it leaves nothing of them." And that was a trial (fitnah).

⁕ I was told by al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿And the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾, he said: It is the tree of zaqqum.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾: "The zaqqum is that which they asked God to fill their houses with." He said: "It is ṣarfan with butter, which they gulp down (tatazaqqamuhu). Ṣarfan is a kind of date." He said: Abu Jahl said: "It is ṣarfan with butter," and they were tested by it.

Others said: It is al-kashuth [[al-Kashuth and al-Kashutha: a plant that clings to branches and has no root in the ground. It is a Sawadi (Iraqi) word (see Lisan al-ʿArab and Taj al-ʿArus).]].
Mention of those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from a client of the Banu Hashim who related to him, that ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal sent him to Ibn ʿAbbas, asking him about the cursed tree in the Qur'an. He said: "It is this tree that twines around another tree and is placed in water," meaning the kashuthi.

The more correct of the two opinions in this matter, in our view, is the saying of the one who said that it refers to the tree of zaqqum, due to the consensus of the authoritative scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) upon this. The words "the cursed tree" are in the accusative as a conjunction (ʿatf) with "the vision" (al-ru'ya). The meaning of the sentence therefore is: "And We did not make the vision which We showed you, nor the cursed tree in the Qur'an, except as a trial for people." Their trial in the vision was what you have mentioned of the apostasy of those who apostatized and the persistence of the people of polytheism in their polytheism, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) informed them of what God had shown him in his journey to Bayt al-Maqdis on the night he was taken on the Night Journey. Their trial in the cursed tree was what we have mentioned of the statement of Abu Jahl and the polytheists with him: "Muhammad tells us that there is a tree growing in the Fire, and the Fire consumes trees, so how can it grow in it?"

* *
And His words ﴿And We warn them, but it only increases them in great transgression﴾.
He says: We warn these polytheists with the punishments and chastisements with which We threaten them, yet our warning only increases them in great transgression, meaning in great persistence and wayward excess in their disbelief. That is because when they were warned of the Fire, whose food is the zaqqum, they called for dates and butter and said: "Gulp down (tazaqqamu) this."

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this; some of those who said it have already been mentioned, and we mention some of those who remain.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding ﴿And the cursed tree﴾: "Its spathe (ṭalʿuhā) is like the heads of devils, and devils are cursed." He said, regarding ﴿And the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾: "When He mentioned it, it increased them in trial and transgression." God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And We warn them, but it only increases them in great transgression﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 61–62:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated, except Iblis. He said, "Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?"﴾ (61) ﴿He said, "Have You considered this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize control over his descendants, except for a few."﴾ (62)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And remember, O Muhammad, the persistence of these polytheists in their error and their apostasy, their defiance against their Lord by frightening them with the fulfilment of the words of their enemy and the enemy of their father, when his Lord commanded him to prostrate to him, so he disobeyed and refused to prostrate to him out of envy and arrogance: ﴿If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize control over his descendants, except for a few.﴾ And how they believed his assumption about them, and opposed the command of their Lord and His obedience, and followed the command of their enemy and the enemy of their father."

As for His saying, ﴿And when We said to the angels﴾, He means: "Remember when We said to the angels, ﴿Prostrate to Adam,﴾ so they prostrated, except Iblis, for he was arrogant and said, ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾" That is, "to one whom You created from clay." When "min" (from) was omitted, the verb ﴿created﴾ governed the object and it was put in the accusative. The ignorant one boasts over him that he was created from fire, and Adam was created from clay.

As related:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Lord of Might, blessed and exalted, sent Iblis, and he took from the surface of the earth, from its sweet and its salty parts, and from it He created Adam. So everything created from its sweet part is destined for happiness even if it is the son of two disbelievers, and everything He created from its salty part is destined for wretchedness even if it is the son of two prophets. Therefore Iblis said, ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created from clay?﴾ That is: "I brought this clay." And for this reason Adam was named, because he was created from the surface of the earth.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿Have You considered this one whom You have honored above me?﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "Have You considered this one whom You have honored above me, when You commanded me to prostrate to him?" He means by this Adam. ﴿If You delay me﴾: the enemy of Allah swore and said to his Lord, "If You delay my destruction until the Day of Resurrection, ﴿I will surely seize control over his descendants, except for a few.﴾" He means: "I will surely gain dominion over them, I will uproot them, and I will lead them astray." It is said of this: "Fulan ihtanaka what fulan has of wealth or knowledge or other things," meaning he took it. And from it is the saying of the poet:

We complain to You of a year that has ravaged us, [hardship] upon hardship that has weakened us, and has seized our wealth and stripped it bare. [[These are three verses of mashtur rajaz, from the sixth urjuza in the remainder of the Diwan of al-Zafayan al-Sa'di (Ata' ibn Usayd, the rajaz poet), included with the printed Diwan of al-'Ajjaj in Leipzig in 1903, p. 65, with some variation in the transmission of some of them. The first two verses are: "We complain to You of a year that has stripped our wealth from its root and uprooted it..." As for the third verse, it is not in the urjuza. The meaning of ajhafat: it harmed us and our wealth departed, so we met with hardship upon hardship. And ihtanakat: Abu 'Ubayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an (p. 384): "It is said: fulan ihtanaka what fulan has of wealth, knowledge, speech or other things, all of it: he took all of it and exhausted it." He said: "We complain to You..." etc. The verses. And the meaning of jalafat: it was peeled, or the skin was peeled along with some flesh. The verses are evidence that ihtinak means uprooting.]]

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted, ﴿I will surely seize control over his descendants, except for a few﴾: he said, "I will surely encompass them."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

'Ali narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿I will surely seize control over his descendants, except for a few﴾: he said, "I will surely gain dominion."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿I will surely seize control over his descendants, except for a few﴾: he said, "I will surely lead them astray." These expressions, although they differ, are close in meaning, because gaining control and encompassing have one meaning, and when one gains control over them, one has led them astray.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted, ﴿I will surely seize control over his descendants, except for a few﴾: he said, "I will surely encompass them."
