Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 63:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Go, and whoever follows you among them - indeed, Hell will be your recompense, a sufficient recompense.""﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: God said to Iblis when he said to Him, ﴿"If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize control over his descendants, except for a few."﴾ "Go, for I have delayed you. Whoever among them follows you, meaning among the descendants of Adam (peace be upon him), and obeys you, then indeed Hell is your recompense and their recompense." That is: your reward for calling them to disobey Me, and their reward for following you and opposing My command. ﴿A sufficient recompense﴾: that is, a complete, full reward.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿He said, "Go, and whoever follows you among them - indeed, Hell will be your recompense, a sufficient recompense."﴾ "The punishment of Hell is their recompense, and a vengeance from God upon His enemies, from whose punishment nothing will be diverted."

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿indeed, Hell will be your recompense, a sufficient recompense﴾: he said, "Complete."

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿mawfur﴾, he said, "Complete."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 64:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice, and rally against them your cavalry and your infantry, and share with them in wealth and children, and make promises to them. But Satan promises them nothing except delusion.﴾ (64)

By His saying ﴿And incite﴾ the Exalted means: lead astray and make foolish, from the expression "istafazza fulanan kadha wa kadha, fa-huwa yastafizzuhu" (he incited someone to such-and-such, and he incites him). ﴿Whomever you can among them with your voice﴾.

The exegetes differed concerning the voice that the Exalted meant by His saying ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice﴾. Some of them said: it means the voice of singing and play.

Mention of those who said this:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice﴾, he said: "With frivolity and singing."

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth mention, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice﴾, he said: "Play and frivolity."

Others said: it means ﴿And incite whomever you can among them﴾ by your calling them to obedience to you and disobedience to God.

Mention of those who said this:

ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice﴾, he said: "His voice is every caller who calls to disobedience of God."

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice﴾, he said: "With your calling."

The most correct of these sayings is to say: God, blessed and exalted, said to Iblis: "And incite from the offspring of Adam whomever you can incite with your voice." He did not specify one voice over another. So every voice that was a call to him, to his work and his disobedience, and opposed to the call to obedience to God, is included in the meaning of "his voice" about which God, blessed is His name, said: ﴿And incite whomever you can among them with your voice﴾.

* *

And His saying ﴿And rally against them your cavalry and your infantry﴾

He says: gather against them, from the riders and the walkers of your army, whoever shouts against them by calling to your obedience and turning away from My obedience. It is said of this: "ajlaba fulan ʿala fulan ijlaban" (so-and-so shouted against so-and-so), if he cried out against him. Al-jalaba is the sound, and it is sometimes said "ma hadha al-jalab," just as one says "al-ghalab" and "al-shafaqa" and "al-shafaq."

In accordance with what we have said, the exegetes said likewise.

Mention of those who said this:

Salm ibn Janada narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth mention, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And rally against them your cavalry and your infantry﴾, he said: "Every rider and walker in disobedience to God, the Exalted."

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, ﴿And rally against them your cavalry and your infantry﴾, he said: "Indeed he has cavalry and infantry from the jinn and mankind, and they are those who obey him."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿And rally against them your cavalry and your infantry﴾, he said: "Rijal: the walkers."

ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, his saying ﴿And rally against them your cavalry and your infantry﴾, he said: "His cavalry: every rider in disobedience to God; his infantry: every walker in disobedience to God."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And rally against them your cavalry and your infantry﴾, he said: "Whoever is a rider fighting in disobedience to God is from the cavalry of Iblis, and whoever is a walker in disobedience to God is from the infantry of Iblis." And "rijl" is the plural of "rajil," just as "tijr" is the plural of "tajir" and "sahb" is the plural of "sahib."

As for His saying ﴿And share with them in wealth﴾, in wealth and children, the exegetes differed concerning the sharing that is meant by His saying ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾. Some of them said: it is his commanding them to spend their wealth in other than obedience to God, and their acquiring it from other than its lawful source.

Mention of those who said this:

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth mention, from Mujahid, ﴿And share with them in wealth﴾, that which they obtained from other than its lawful source.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And share with them in wealth﴾, he said: "What is eaten from wealth without obedience to God."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Talha ibn ʿAmr, from ʿAta ibn Abi Rabah, he said: "The sharing in wealth is in the wealth of usury."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, he said: "By God, he has indeed shared with them in their wealth; God gave them wealth, and they spent it in obedience to Satan, in other than the right of God, blessed is His name." This is also the saying of Qatada.

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad narrated to us, from Maʿmar, who said: al-Hasan said, "And share with them in wealth": "Command them to acquire it from what is foul and to spend it on what is forbidden."

ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, he said: "Every wealth in disobedience to God."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾: "His sharing with them in wealth and children is what he adorned for them of the disobediences to God, until they rode it."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, ﴿And share with them in wealth﴾, "all that they spent in other than its right."

Others said: rather, it refers to everything of the prohibitions of the polytheists, what they used to forbid of livestock such as the baha'ir and the sawa'ib and the like.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, he said: "The wealth: what they used to forbid of their livestock."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from ʿImran ibn Sulayman, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, he said: "His sharing in wealth is that they made the baHira, the sa'iba and the wasila for other than God."

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, ﴿And share with them in wealth﴾, "he has indeed done that. As for wealth, he commanded them to make baHira, sa'iba, wasila and ham."

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading is "hamiyan" (protected).

Others said: rather, it refers to what the polytheists used to slaughter for their gods.

Mention of those who said this:

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, meaning what they used to slaughter for their gods.

The most correct of the sayings is the saying of the one who said: it refers to every wealth in which God is disobeyed, by spending it in what is forbidden, or acquiring it from what is forbidden, or slaughtering it for the idols, or leaving it free (as sawa'ib), or dedicating it (as baHira) to Satan, and other things by which one disobeys or in which one disobeys God. For God said ﴿And share with them in wealth﴾, so whatever wealth Satan is obeyed in and God is disobeyed in, the one who does that has shared it with Iblis. There is no basis for restricting it to some of that rather than other.

* *

And His saying ﴿and children﴾

The exegetes differed concerning the nature of Iblis's sharing with the children of Adam in their children. Some of them said: his sharing with them in their children is by their fornication with their mothers.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, his saying ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, he said: "The children of fornication."

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth mention, from Mujahid, ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, he said: "The children of fornication."

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, he said: "The children of fornication."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, he said: "The children of fornication."

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, he said: "The children of fornication, meaning by that the people of polytheism."

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, he said: "The children: the children of fornication."

Others said: it means burying their children alive and killing them.

Mention of those who said this:

ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, he said: "What they killed of their children, and they committed the unlawful regarding them."

Others said: rather, it means their dyeing them in disbelief.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, he said: "By God, he has indeed shared with them in their wealth and their children: they were made Magians, Jews and Christians, dyed with other than the dye of Islam, and they gave a portion of their wealth as a portion to Satan."

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, he said: "He has indeed done that. As for the children, they made them Jews, Christians and Magians."

Others said: rather, it means naming their children ʿAbd al-Harith and ʿAbd Shams.

Mention of those who said this:

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa ibn Yunus narrated to me, from ʿImran ibn Sulayman, from Abu Salih, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾, he said: "His sharing with them in children: they named them ʿAbd al-Harith, ʿAbd Shams and ʿAbd Fulan."

The most correct of the sayings is to say: every child born to a woman whom God disobeyed by naming it with what God dislikes, or by bringing it into a religion other than the one God approved, or by fornicating with its mother, or by killing it and burying it alive, or other matters by which the meaning of sharing is specified in His saying ﴿And share with them in wealth and children﴾ in one sense rather than another. So whatever God is disobeyed in or by, and Satan is obeyed by or in, it is a sharing of the one who disobeys God in it or by it with Iblis in it.

* *

And His saying ﴿And make promises to them. But Satan promises them nothing except delusion﴾

The Exalted says to Iblis: promise your followers from the offspring of Adam victory over whoever intends them harm. God says ﴿But Satan promises them nothing except delusion﴾, because he does not avail them anything of God's punishment when it descends upon them; so they are, in his promises, in falsehood and deception, as the enemy of God said to them when the truth became manifest: ﴿Indeed, God promised you a promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke my promise to you. I had no authority over you except that I invited you, and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieve in your association of me with God before.﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 65–66:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Indeed, My servants – you have no authority over them. And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs.﴾ (65)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to Iblis: Indeed, My servants, who obeyed Me, followed My command and disobeyed you, O Iblis – you have no proof against them.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs﴾:

He, whose praise is exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And sufficient for you, O Muhammad, is your Lord as Guardian and as one who manages your affair. So submit to His command and convey His messages to these polytheists, and do not fear anyone, for He has undertaken to protect and support you.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, My servants – you have no authority over them. And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs﴾: "His servants are the believers." And God said in another verse ﴿His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him﴾.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships through the sea that you may seek of His bounty. Indeed, He is ever Merciful to you.﴾ (66)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the polytheists who associate others with Him: Your Lord, O people, is the One who makes the ships proceed for you upon the sea, carrying you within them, ﴿that you may seek of His bounty﴾, that you may reach by riding in them your places of trade, your needs and your livelihoods, and seek of His provision. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Merciful to you﴾ – that is, indeed Allah has been Merciful to you when He made the ships run for you on the sea, facilitating for you, by that, the movement in seeking His bounty in distant lands, which, were it not for His facilitating that for you, would have been difficult for you to reach.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said regarding His saying ﴿drives for you﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships through the sea﴾: "He makes the ships run."

* Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships through the sea﴾: He said, "He makes them sail upon the sea."

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abbas said regarding ﴿Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships through the sea﴾: "He makes them run."

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Your Lord is He who drives for you the ships through the sea﴾: "He makes them run."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 67–68:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when harm touches you at sea, those whom you invoke vanish, except Him. But when He delivers you to the land, you turn away. And man is ever ungrateful.﴾

His words, mentioned, exalted is He: "And when adversity and hardship reach you at sea, those whom you invoke vanish" means: you lose those you invoke besides God, from among the rivals and gods, and they stray from your path, so they do not help you. You find no helper other than God whom you can call upon. So when you call upon Him, He rescues you and answers your supplication, and delivers you from the terror of what you were in at sea, you turn away from what your Lord calls you to, namely renouncing rivals, disavowing gods, and devoting worship to Him alone, out of disbelief in His favor. ﴿And man is ever ungrateful﴾ means: man is ever one who denies the blessings of his Lord.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Do you feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you, or send against you a violent wind (hasib) and then you will not find for yourselves any protector?﴾

His words, mentioned, exalted is He: "Do you feel secure", O people, from your Lord, when you have disbelieved in His favor by delivering you from the terror you were in at sea and the great destruction you had come close to? When He saved you and you reached the land, you disbelieved and associated others with Him in worship. "That He will cause the side of the land to swallow you" means the side of the land. "Or send against you a violent wind" means: or rain down upon you stones from the sky that destroy you, as He did to the people of Lot. "Then you will not find for yourselves any protector" means: then you will not find anything that can defend you against His punishment or prevent it from you.

Similar to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said so:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, ﴿Do you feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you, or send against you a violent wind (hasib)﴾, he said: "stones from the sky." ﴿Then you will not find for yourselves any protector﴾: meaning, no defender or helper.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words, ﴿Do you feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you, or send against you a violent wind (hasib)﴾, he said: "the rain of stones when you come out of the sea."

Some of the grammarians (ahl al-'Arabiyyah) directed the interpretation of His words ﴿or send against you a violent wind (hasib)﴾ to mean: or send against you a strong wind that pelts (tuhsibu), and they cited for this the verse of the poet:

Facing the north wind of Syria, it strikes us
with a hasib like scattered cotton fluff.
[[The verse is by al-Farazdaq from a qasidah praising Yazid ibn 'Abd al-Malik and satirizing Yazid ibn al-Muhallab (his Diwan, al-Sawi edition, pp. 262–267). The author cited it to show that al-hasib is the wind that carries pebbles, which are small stones, and the verse is evidence that al-hasib is rain of stones, and that the root of al-hasib is a wind that pelts with pebbles; al-hasiba is the land containing sand and small pebbles, as the author clarified.]]

The root of al-hasib is: a wind that pelts with pebbles (al-hasba'); the land containing sand and small pebbles. It is said in speech: "Hasaba fulan fulanan" when he pelted him with pebbles. The wind is described as pelting (tuhsibu) because it pelts people with these, as al-Akhtal said:

Indeed I know when the she-camels in calf went out at dusk,
gliding like young ostriches, the north wind knocking them over...
It pelts the acacias with a hasib of their snow,
until it spends the night upon the acacias, heaped up.
[[The two verses are by al-Akhtal (his Diwan, Beirut edition, 1891) from a qasidah satirizing Jarir and boasting over Qays. Al-'isharr: plural of 'isharda' among camels, meaning one that has passed ten months and is pregnant. Tarawwahat: went out in the evening toward their pens. Al-ra'al: plural of ra'l, the young of the ostrich. Al-hadj: a close trot. Takubbuhunna: knocks them down, meaning the wind knocks them down blowing from the north. Al-hasib: the fine snow that scatters. The pronoun in tarmi refers to the north wind. Al-'idah: every tree with thorns, or every tree with wide shade and many branches, its singular being 'idhah. Al-jifal: what has piled up and layered of snow. This evidence has the same meaning as the previous one.]]

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿Or do you feel secure that He will not return you to it another time and send against you a violent wind [to break you] and drown you for your disbelief? Then you would not find for yourselves against Us any avenger in that matter.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "Or do you feel secure, O people, from your Lord, though you have disbelieved in Him after His bounty upon you, that He will return you into the sea, a bounty you know He has given you, another time?" That is: once more. The "hu" (ه) in His saying "fihi" (in it) refers to the sea.

As related to us:

Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿that He will return you into it another time﴾: meaning, into the sea, once more. ﴿And send against you a violent wind﴾, which is the one that breaks what it passes over and crushes it, from the saying of people: "qasafa fulan zahra fulan" (so-and-so broke so-and-so's back) when he breaks it. ﴿And drown you for your disbelief﴾: he says, God drowns you with this violent wind for your disbelief, that is, for your disbelief in Him. ﴿Then you would not find for yourselves against Us any avenger﴾: he says, you would not find for yourselves against Us a follower who would pursue us for what We did to you, nor an avenger who would seek retribution from us for destroying you. It has also been said that "tabi'an" (avenger) is in the place of "tabi'" (follower), as it is said "alim" in the place of "'alim" (knowing). The Arabs say of every seeker of blood, debt, or otherwise: "tabi'." From it is the poet's saying:

They ran, and their gazelles ran, so it is as if they were
Guarantors of a debt, whose owners seek it (tabi')

[The line is evidence that the meaning of "tabi'" in the verse is: every seeker of blood, debt, or otherwise. Abu 'Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an (1:385): "i.e., one who follows us on your behalf, nor one seeking us for it." In Lisan al-Arab (under t-b-'): "al-tabi' is the follower," and the Qur'anic phrase "then you would not find for yourselves against Us any avenger" — al-Farra' said: that is, an avenger, nor one seeking vengeance, for our drowning you. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: you would not find anyone who follows us in denying what befell you, nor anyone who follows us so as to turn it away from you. It has also been said: "tabi'an" means one who demands. From it is His saying, exalted: "So let there be a following in what is customary and a payment made to him with good conduct" — meaning, upon the one with the blood-claim is pursuit in what is customary, that is, demanding the blood-money, and upon the claimant is payment to him with good conduct.]

In agreement with what we have said regarding "qasif" and "tabi'," the people of interpretation have said:

Those who said that:

Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and send against you a violent wind﴾: he says, a "'asif" (stormy wind).

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "qasif" is that which drowns.

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿then you would not find for yourselves against Us any avenger﴾: he says, a helper.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Muhammad said: "tha'iran" (avenger); al-Harith said: "nasiran tha'iran" (a helper, an avenger).

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿then you would not find for yourselves against Us any avenger﴾: he said: "tha'iran" (avenger).

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿then you would not find for yourselves against Us any avenger﴾: meaning, we do not fear that we would be followed for anything of that.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿then you would not find for yourselves against Us any avenger﴾: he says, no one would follow us for anything of that. And "al-tara" (a time): its plural is "tarat" and "tir," and from it the verb is "atarat" (he did it once more).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 70–71:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.﴾ (70)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: ﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam﴾ by empowering them over others of creation and subjecting all of creation to them. ﴿And We carried them on the land﴾ upon the backs of beasts and vehicles, ﴿and [on] the sea﴾ in the ships which We subjected for them. ﴿And We provided for them of the good things﴾: He says, of the good foods and drinks, meaning their lawful and delicious kinds. ﴿And We preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.﴾ It has been related to us that this refers to their being able to work with their hands, take food and drink with them, and raise them to their mouths, which is not easily available to other creatures.

As narrated:

* Al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words ﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam﴾ ... the verse. He said: ﴿And We preferred them﴾ refers to the hands, with which they eat and work, whereas the rest of creation (other than humans) eats by other means.

* Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, regarding His words ﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam﴾. He said: The angels said: "O our Lord, You have given the children of Adam this world, to eat from and enjoy, and You have not given us that, so give it to us in the Hereafter." He said: "By My might, I will not make the offspring of those whom I created with My hand like those to whom I said 'Be,' and it was."

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader. Then whoever is given his record in his right hand - those will read their records, and they will not be wronged as much as a thread.﴾ (71)

The scholars of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of "the leader" (al-Imam) by which Allah, exalted is His praise, said He would call every people. Some of them said: it is their Prophet, and whoever was followed and taken as a model in the world.

Those who said this:

* Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i related to me, who said: Fudayl related to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader﴾: He said: their prophet.

* Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Hakkam related to us, from Anbasah, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader﴾: He said: their prophet.

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, who said: Abu Asim related to us, who said: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿with their leader﴾: He said: their prophet.

* Al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* Muhammad related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿every people with their leader﴾: He said: their prophet.

* Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, the two said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Others said: rather, the meaning is that He will call them by the records of their deeds which they performed in the world.

Those who said this:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: my father related to me, who said: my uncle related to me, who said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader﴾: He said: The leader is what they did and dictated, so it was recorded against him. Whoever is raised fearing Allah, His record will be placed in his right hand, and he will read it and rejoice, and he will not be wronged as much as a thread. This is like His words ﴿And indeed they are on a clear leader﴾ [Qur'an 15:79]. The leader is what was dictated and done.

* Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader﴾: He said: with their deeds.

* Muhammad related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan said: with their book in which their deeds are.

* I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd related to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader﴾: He says: with their books.

* Al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, who said: with their deeds.

Others said: rather, its meaning is: the Day We will call every people with their book which We sent down to them containing My command and My prohibition.

Those who said this:

* Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: I heard Yahya ibn Zayd regarding the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic, ﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader﴾: He said: with their book, in which the command of Allah, His prohibition, and His obligations were sent down to them, and by which they will be reckoned. He recited ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a method﴾ [Qur'an 5:48] and said: the shir'ah (law) is the religion, and the minhaj (method) is the Sunnah. He recited ﴿He has prescribed for you of the religion what He enjoined upon Noah﴾ [Qur'an 42:13] and said: Noah is the first of them, and you are the last of them.

* Al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿The Day We will call every people with their leader﴾: with their book.

The most correct of these sayings in our view is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of that is: the Day We will call every people with their leader whom they used to follow and take as a model in the world, because the more common usage of the Arabs of "imam" is for what one follows and takes as a model, and directing the meanings of the words of Allah to the most well-known meaning is more appropriate, so long as no proof to the contrary is established that must be accepted.

* *

As for His words ﴿Then whoever is given his record in his right hand﴾:

He says: whoever is given the record of his deeds in his right hand ﴿those will read their record﴾, all of it, until they know everything in it. ﴿And they will not be wronged as much as a thread﴾: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Allah will not wrong them in the recompense of their deeds by as much as a thread, and the thread is the fibre that splits in the cleft of a date stone. The explanation of the thread has already passed, sufficient to not repeat it in this place.

* Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and they will not be wronged as much as a thread﴾: He said: the one in the split of the date stone.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the way﴾ (17:72).

The scholars of exegesis differed regarding the meaning indicated by His words "this" (hadhihi). Some of them said: By that is indicated the blessings which He, mentioned, enumerated in His words: ﴿And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference﴾ [17:70]. So He said: ﴿And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the way.﴾

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, who said: He was asked about this verse, ﴿And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the way﴾, and he said: He said, ﴿And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference﴾. He said: Whoever is blind to thanking these blessings in this world, will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the way.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Whoever was blind in this world to the power of God in it and His proofs, will be blind in the Hereafter.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying, ﴿And whoever is blind in this [world]﴾, he says: whoever is blind to the power of God in this world, ﴿will be blind in the Hereafter﴾.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿in this [world] blind﴾, he said: "this [world]" means the worldly life.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter﴾, he says: whoever was blind in this worldly life to what he witnessed in it of the blessings of God, His creation and His wonders, ﴿will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the way﴾ regarding what is hidden from him of the matter of the Hereafter, and blinder.

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿And whoever is blind in this [world]﴾ in the worldly life, regarding what God showed him of His signs: the creation of the heavens and the earth, the mountains and the stars, ﴿then he is in the Hereafter﴾ which is unseen and which he has not seen, ﴿blind and further astray from the way﴾.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, when he was asked about the saying of God, exalted is He, ﴿And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and further astray from the way﴾, and he recited: ﴿Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers﴾ and ﴿And in yourselves; will you not then see?﴾ and he recited: ﴿And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then suddenly you are human beings dispersing﴾, and he recited until he reached ﴿To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and earth; all are to Him devoutly obedient﴾, and said: All are obedient to Him except the son of Adam. He said: So whoever is blind to these signs, which he knows are from Us, and which he witnesses while seeing Our power and Our blessing, will be blind in the Hereafter, which he has not seen, and further astray from the way.

The most correct of these opinions in my view is the opinion of the one who said: The meaning of that is: Whoever was blind in this world to the proofs of God that He alone created it, arranged it, and directed what is in it, will be blind regarding the matter of the Hereafter, which he has not seen nor witnessed, and regarding what will occur in it, and further astray in the way, meaning: more astray in path than he is regarding the affairs of this world, which he has witnessed and seen.

We only said that this is the most correct interpretation because God, exalted is He, did not specify, in His saying ﴿And whoever is in this [world]﴾ the worldly life, ﴿blind﴾, the blindness of the disbeliever toward some of His proofs in it rather than others, so as to direct that to his blindness to His blessings, by His honoring the children of Adam and carrying them on land and sea, and what He enumerated in the verse in which He mentioned His blessings upon them. Rather, He generalized by the report of their blindness in the worldly life, so they are as God, exalted is He, generalized.

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His saying ﴿will be blind in the Hereafter﴾. All the readers vowed (kasarat) the first letter, meaning His saying ﴿whoever is blind in this [world]﴾. As for His saying ﴿will be blind in the Hereafter﴾, most of the Kufan readers inclined it (amalat) as well. As for some readers of Basra, they pronounced it with a fatha and interpreted it to mean: "he will be more blind in the Hereafter." They cited as evidence for the correctness of their reading His saying ﴿and further astray from the way﴾.

This reading is the more correct of the two readings in this regard, because of the evidence we mentioned from its reciter in this way. Those who disliked reading it thus did so only thinking that it was intended as the blindness of the eyes, to which no one is described as blind relative to another blind person, since blindness of sight does not vary, so that one of them would be more blind than the other, unless by adding "more" or "clearer." The matter in this is not so.

We only said that this is from blindness of the heart, in which variation occurs. What is meant by it is the blindness of the hearts of the disbelievers regarding the proofs of God which their eyes have witnessed; therefore that is permissible and good.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿will be blind in the Hereafter﴾, he said: blind to His proof in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 73:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And indeed they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you, to fabricate other than it against Us; and then they would have taken you as a close friend﴾

The exegetes differed concerning the temptation by which the polytheists almost seduced the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) away from what Allah had revealed to him, toward something else. Some said: it was the touching of the idols, because the polytheists invited him to that, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was inclined toward it.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Ya'qub al-Qummi related to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to touch (istilam) the Black Stone, and Quraysh prevented him, saying: "We will not leave you until you touch our gods." So he spoke to himself and said: "What harm is there in my touching them after they leave me to touch the Stone? Allah knows that I dislike it." But Allah refused, and Allah revealed: ﴿And indeed they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you, to fabricate other than it against Us﴾, the verse.

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined toward them a little﴾. It was mentioned to us that Quraysh secluded themselves with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) one night until morning, speaking to him, exalting him, making him their chief, and drawing near to him. Among what they said was: "You bring something that no one among mankind brings, and you are our lord and the son of our lord." They kept speaking to him until he almost drew near to them (yuqarifahum) [[yuqarifahum: he approached them and came close to them (Lisan al-Arab).]]. Then Allah restrained him and protected him from that, and He said: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined toward them a little﴾.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿to fabricate other than it against Us﴾, who said: They surrounded him one night and said: "You are our lord and the son of our lord," and they wanted him to do some of what they desired. He almost drew near to them (yuqarifahum) [[yuqarifahum: he approached them and came close to them (Lisan al-Arab).]] in some of what they wanted. Then Allah protected him, and that is His saying ﴿You would almost have inclined toward them a little﴾, the thing they wanted, in which he almost drew near to them.

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: They said to him: "Go to our gods and touch them," and that is His saying ﴿a little﴾.

Others said: That occurred only because the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was inclined to give a respite to a people regarding their conversion to Islam, for a term they asked him to grant.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, His words ﴿And indeed they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you, to fabricate other than it against Us; and then they would have taken you as a close friend﴾. That was because the Thaqif had said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, grant us a year's delay until gifts are brought to our gods; then when we collect what is brought to our gods, we will take it, then we will embrace Islam and break the idols." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was inclined to give them what they asked and to grant them the delay, so Allah said: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined toward them a little﴾.

The correct view on this matter is to say: Allah, may He be exalted in remembrance, informed about His Prophet (ﷺ) that the polytheists almost seduced him away from what Allah had revealed to him, so that he would act on something other than it, and that is fabricating against Allah. It is permissible that this was what was mentioned of them, that they asked him to touch their gods and to approach them; and it is permissible that it was what was reported from Ibn Abbas concerning the matter of Thaqif and their request of him, which we have mentioned; and it is permissible that it was other than that. There is no clarification in the Book nor in a report that removes excuse as to which of these it was, and the disagreement regarding it exists as we have mentioned. So nothing is more correct regarding it than believing in its outward meaning, until a report comes whose acceptance is obligatory, clarifying what was intended by it.

* *

As for His words ﴿and then they would have taken you as a close friend﴾:

He, may He be exalted in remembrance, says: Had you done what they invited you to, of the temptation away from what We revealed to you, then they would have taken you, at that time, as a close friend for themselves, and you would have been to them and they would have been allies to you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 74–75:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined toward them a little.﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: And had We not made you firm, O Muhammad, by Our protection of you from the temptation to which these polytheists invited you, ﴿you would almost have inclined toward them a little﴾. That is, you would almost have leaned toward them and been at ease with them a little. This refers to what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had resolved to do, namely to do some of what they had asked him to do. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, as it is related, when this verse was revealed:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined toward them a little﴾: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye."

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] in death; then you would not find for yourself against Us any helper.﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: If you had inclined toward these polytheists, O Muhammad, even a little in what they asked of you, then We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] in death﴾: meaning the double punishment of this world and the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah ﴿double [punishment] in life﴾ he said: its punishment; ﴿and double [punishment] in death﴾ he said: the punishment of the Hereafter.

Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] in death﴾: that is, the punishment of this world and the Hereafter.

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] in death﴾, he said: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying ﴿double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] in death﴾: meaning the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say, concerning His saying ﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life﴾, that it is elliptical, like your saying: "double the punishment of life" (i.e., ﴿double [punishment] in life﴾ with the word "punishment" omitted), ﴿and double [punishment] in death﴾. Thus they are two punishments, the punishment of death being doubled over the punishment of life.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿then you would not find for yourself against Us any helper﴾:

That is: then you would not find, O Muhammad, if We made you taste, because of your inclining toward these polytheists had you inclined toward them, the punishment of life and the punishment of death against Us, a helper who would help you against Us, protect you from Our punishment, and rescue you from the retribution that We had inflicted upon you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 74–75:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined toward them a little.﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: And had We not made you firm, O Muhammad, by Our protection of you from the temptation to which these polytheists invited you, ﴿you would almost have inclined toward them a little﴾. That is, you would almost have leaned toward them and been at ease with them a little. This refers to what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had resolved to do, namely to do some of what they had asked him to do. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, as it is related, when this verse was revealed:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿And had We not made you firm, you would almost have inclined toward them a little﴾: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye."

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] in death; then you would not find for yourself against Us any helper.﴾

His saying, exalted is He, means: If you had inclined toward these polytheists, O Muhammad, even a little in what they asked of you, then We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] in death﴾: meaning the double punishment of this world and the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the saying of Allah ﴿double [punishment] in life﴾ he said: its punishment; ﴿and double [punishment] in death﴾ he said: the punishment of the Hereafter.

Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] in death﴾: that is, the punishment of this world and the Hereafter.

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] in death﴾, he said: the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying ﴿double [punishment] in life and double [punishment] in death﴾: meaning the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter.

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say, concerning His saying ﴿Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life﴾, that it is elliptical, like your saying: "double the punishment of life" (i.e., ﴿double [punishment] in life﴾ with the word "punishment" omitted), ﴿and double [punishment] in death﴾. Thus they are two punishments, the punishment of death being doubled over the punishment of life.

* *

As for His saying, ﴿then you would not find for yourself against Us any helper﴾:

That is: then you would not find, O Muhammad, if We made you taste, because of your inclining toward these polytheists had you inclined toward them, the punishment of life and the punishment of death against Us, a helper who would help you against Us, protect you from Our punishment, and rescue you from the retribution that We had inflicted upon you.

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, they had almost driven you out of the land to expel you from it; but then they would not have remained after you except for a little.﴾

He, may He be exalted and glorified, says: And indeed these people had almost driven you out of the land, meaning: they had almost made you flee from the land in which you are, to expel you from it. ﴿And then they would not remain after you except for a little﴾ means: had they expelled you from it, they would not have remained there after you except for a little, until Allah destroyed them with a swift punishment.

The people of interpretation differed concerning those who almost sought to drive the Messenger of Allah ﷺ out, and concerning the land from which they intended to expel him. Some of them said: those who almost sought to drive the Messenger of Allah ﷺ out were the Jews, and the land from which they intended to expel him was Madinah.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, who said: A man from Hadramawt claimed that it had reached him that some Jews said to the Prophet ﷺ: "The land of the prophets is the land of Syria, and this is not the land of the prophets." So Allah revealed: ﴿And indeed, they had almost driven you out of the land to expel you from it.﴾

Others said: Rather, the people who did this were the Quraysh, and the land was Makkah.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And indeed, they had almost driven you out of the land to expel you from it; but then they would not have remained after you except for a little.﴾ The people of Makkah had resolved to expel the Prophet ﷺ from Makkah. Had they done so, they would not have settled; but Allah restrained them from expelling him until He commanded him (to leave). And they would have remained only briefly after the departure of the Prophet of Allah ﷺ from Makkah, until Allah sent upon them slaughter on the Day of Badr.

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿they would have driven you out of the land﴾: He said: They did it after that, and Allah destroyed them on the Day of Badr; they did not remain after it except for a little, until Allah destroyed them on the Day of Badr. Such has been the way of Allah with the messengers when their peoples do such a thing to them.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿after you except for a little﴾: He said: If Quraysh had expelled Muhammad, they would have been punished for that.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

The more correct of the two opinions in my view is the opinion of Qatadah and Mujahid. This is because His words ﴿And indeed, they had almost driven you out of the land﴾ occur within the context of Allah's report, may He be exalted, concerning the Quraysh and His mention of them, and no mention of the Jews had preceded this, so that His words ﴿And indeed they had almost﴾ would be directed to them as a report about them. Thus it is more fitting that it be a report about those who had already been mentioned than about others. As for the little that Allah, may His mention be exalted, excepted in His words ﴿but then they would not have remained after you except for a little﴾, it is said to be the period between the departure of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from Makkah and the time Allah killed those of their polytheists whom He killed at Badr.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿but then they would not have remained after you except for a little﴾: He meant by "the little" the day He seized them at Badr, and that was the little they remained after.

I was told, from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿but then they would not have remained after you except for a little﴾: The little they remained after the Prophet's departure from among them was until Badr, when He seized them with punishment on the Day of Badr.

By His words "after you" (khilafak) is meant "after you," as the poet said:

"'Aqaba al-radhadh khilafaha fa-ka-annama / basata al-shawatibu baynahunna hasiran"

(The poem is by al-Harith ibn Khalid al-Makhzumi, cited in Lisan al-'Arab under kh-l-f, as evidence that khilafa means "after." The author had cited it earlier in explaining the verse "those who stayed behind rejoiced in their seat, contrary to the Messenger of Allah" [9:81]. The narration here differs from its citation at that verse, where it reads "'aqaba al-rabi' khilafahum...". Abu 'Ubaydah's Majaz al-Quran (1:387) reads: "'afat al-diyar khilafaha fa-ka-annama".)

He means by "khilafaha": after it. It has been related from some of them that they read it as khalfaka (after you), and the meaning of that and the meaning of khilaf in this place are one.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 77–78 (part 1 of 2)**

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿The practice We applied to the messengers We sent before you, and you will not find any change in Our practice.﴾ (17:77)

His words, may His remembrance be exalted: "If they had driven you out, they would not have remained after you except for a little while, and We would have destroyed them with a punishment from Us. This is Our practice concerning those messengers We sent before you, for thus We used to deal with the nations when their messengers were driven out from among them." The word *sunna* (practice) is put in the accusative because it is read as a verbal noun from the meaning of His words ﴿they will not remain after you except for a little while﴾. The meaning is: "We would punish them after a short time, as is Our practice with the nations to whom We sent messengers before you, and you will not find any change in Our practice from what it has followed."

As reported:
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿The practice We applied to the messengers We sent before you, and you will not find any change in Our practice﴾: That is, the practice concerning the nations and messengers before you: when they denied their messengers and drove them out, they did not consider that God would send down His punishment upon them.

* *

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, and the recitation of dawn. Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed.﴾ (17:78)

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, addressed to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Establish the prayer﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿at the decline of the sun﴾.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the time that God meant by "the decline of the sun" (dulūk al-shams). Some of them said: It is the time of its setting, and the prayer He commanded to be established at that time is the Maghrib prayer.

Those who said this:
• Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la al-Asadi told me, saying: Ibn Fudayl told us, from Abu Ishaq, meaning al-Shaybani, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad, from his father, that he was with Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud on a roof when the sun had set. He recited ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾ until he finished the verse. Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, this is the time when the sun declined, the fasting person breaks his fast, and the prayer is due."
• Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi told us, from Sa'id, from Qatada, from Uqba ibn Abd al-Ghafir, that Ubayda ibn Abd Allah wrote to him that Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, when the sun set, would pray the Maghrib prayer and break his fast then if he was fasting. He would swear an oath over it, more than he swore over anything concerning the prayers, "by God, besides whom there is no god, that this hour is the appointed time for this prayer." He would recite in it, as its explanation from the Book of God: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾.
• Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi told us, from Shu'ba, from Asim, from Abu Wa'il, from Abd Allah, who said: "This is the decline of the sun, and this is the darkness of the night," and he gestured towards the east and the west.
• Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The decline of the sun" is its setting; he said: it declined with *barah*.
• al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aswad, from Abd Allah, who said: "When the sun set, it declined," meaning *barah* as a place.
• al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Its decline is its setting."
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, who said: "It has been mentioned to us that Ibn Mas'ud used to pray it when it set, and break his fast at that time if he was fasting. Then he would swear an oath over it, more than he swore over anything concerning the prayers, 'by God, besides whom there is no god, that this hour is the appointed time for this prayer.' Then he would recite and pray it, and its confirmation is from the Book of God: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾."
• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾: "My father used to say: its decline is when the sun is about to set until the night becomes dark. He said: It is the Maghrib, when the night becomes dark, and the sun declines for setting."
• Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' told me, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyayna told us, that he heard Amr ibn Dinar say that Abu Ubayda ibn Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud used to pray the Maghrib when the edge of the sun disappeared, and he would swear that this is the time which God mentioned: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: Abd Allah said when the sun set: "By God, besides whom there is no god, this is the time of this prayer." And he said: "Its decline is its setting."

Others said: "The decline of the sun" is its inclination towards the zenith (zawāl), and the prayer which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was commanded to establish at its decline is the Zuhr prayer.

Those who said this:
• Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from al-A'mash, from Amara ibn Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Abd Allah, who said: "Its decline is its inclination, meaning the sun."
• Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym told us, from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Abbas, who said regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾: "Its decline is its zawal."
• Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman told me, saying: Abu Usama told us, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾: "Its decline is its inclination."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, from Sayyar ibn Salama, from Abu Barza al-Aslami, regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾: "When it has passed the zenith."
• Ibn Humayd told us again, saying: Abu Tumayla told us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, saying: Sayyar ibn Salama al-Riyahi told us, saying: "I came to Abu Barza, and my father asked him about the appointed times of the prayer of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He said: 'The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would pray the Zuhr when the sun passed its zenith.' Then he recited ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾."
• al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada'i told me, saying: My father told us, saying: Mubarak told us, from al-Hasan, who said: God the Mighty and Majestic said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾. He said: "Its decline is the Zuhr, when it has moved away from the middle of the sky, and there is a shadow on the earth for it."
• Ya'qub told us, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Yunus informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾: "Its decline is its zawal."
• Ya'qub told me, saying: Hushaym told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, the like of that.
• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Abu Ja'far, regarding ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾: "For the zawal of the sun."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The decline of the sun is its deviation after midday, meaning the shadow."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: "The decline of the sun: when it deviates from the middle of the sky."
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾: that is, when the sun has passed the middle of the sky, for the Zuhr prayer.
• Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us; all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿at the decline of the sun﴾: "When it deviates."
• al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "The decline of the sun: when it deviates."

The most correct of the two opinions regarding this, in terms of truth, is the view of those who said: By His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾ He meant the Zuhr prayer. This is because "decline" (dulūk) in the speech of the Arabs means inclination. It is said of it: "So-and-so declined toward such-and-such" when he inclined toward it. From this is the report narrated from al-Hasan that a man said to him: "Does a man procrastinate (yudālik) with his wife?" meaning: does he incline her towards delaying her right? From this is the verse of the rajaz poet:

*This is the standing place of my feet, Rabah(?)...*
*At dawn, until the sun declined with barah.*

[[The rajaz verse is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (the University of Jami'a photographic edition, p. 181), and its version in it is "dhabb" in place of "ghadwa," which is the same as the version in Lisan al-Arab (b-r-h). Al-Farra' said: "'Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun': it has come from Ibn Abbas, who said: it is its deviation and its zawal for the Zuhr." Abu Zakariyya (al-Farra') said: "I saw the Arabs take the decline to be the setting of the sun. Some of them recited to me: 'This is my standing place...' the verse, meaning the water-carrier who drives people away with the hand: he says, until he places the palm over the eye and looks to see whether the sun has set." He said: "This is how they explained it to us." Abu Ubayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an (1:387): "The decline of the sun is from its zawal until it sets." And he said: "This is the standing place..." the verse. Do you not see that it is pushed away with the palm, placing the hand over the eyebrows against its rays, to look at what remains of its setting? And "dulūk" is its approach to its setting. Abu Zayd al-Ansari said in al-Nawadir (p. 88): "It is said: dalakat bi-rah and bi-rah (with a fatha on the ba' and a kasra or damma on the ha'), which is a known name for the sun." The rajaz poet said: "This is the standing place of my feet, Rabah..." Abu Hatim said: "barah means barahah (palm)." In Lisan al-Arab (b-r-h): "Barah and Barah (with an open ba' and kasra or damma on the ha'): a definite name for the sun, like Qatam, named so because of its spread and clarity."]]

In the version with a *fatha* on the *ba'* (barah), the sense is the name of the sun, and the *ha'* is made with a *kasra* for it, as in the forms Qatam, Hadham, and Raqash. When the meaning of *dulūk* in the speech of the Arabs is inclination, then there is no doubt that when the sun has moved away from the middle of the sky, it has inclined toward setting, and that is the time of the Zuhr prayer. The report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) confirms this, although there is some weakness in the chain of narration of part of it.

• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Khalid ibn Makhlad told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told me, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id told me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm al-Ansari told me, from Abu Mas'ud Uqba ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me at the decline of the sun, when it had passed the zenith, and he led me in the Zuhr prayer."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Abu Tumayla told us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, saying: Sayyar ibn Salama al-Riyahi told me, saying: Abu Barza said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to pray the Zuhr when the sun passed the zenith." Then he recited ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾.
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir told us, saying: Amr ibn Qays told us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from a man, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: "I invited the Prophet of God (ﷺ) and whoever of his companions wished, and they ate with me. Then they went out when the sun passed the zenith, and the Prophet (ﷺ) went out and said: 'Come out, O Abu Bakr, the sun has declined.'"
• Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Razi told me, saying: Sahl ibn Bakkar told us, saying: Abu Awana told us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Nubayh al-Anazi, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of the report of Ibn Humayd.

So if what we have said is correct, and by what we have cited as evidence, then it is clear that the meaning of His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾ is that the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers, within their limits, are among what God has obligated upon you in them, because they are the two prayers that God made obligatory upon His Prophet from the time of the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night. The darkness of the night (ghasaq al-layl) is its approach and its drawing near with its darkness, as the poet said:

*This night has returned, when it became dark (ghasaq)...*

[[This is the first half of a line by Ubayd Allah ibn Qays al-Ruqayyat, whose second half is: "And I complained of worry and sleeplessness." He cited it as evidence that the meaning of "ghasaq al-layl" is its darkness (Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu Ubayda, 1:388). Abu Ubayda's version is: "Indeed this night has become dark (ghasaq)." The version in Lisan al-Arab also supports it. It says: "Ghasaq al-layl yaghsiq (like yadrib) ghasaqan and ghasaqanan, and aghsaq: according to Tha'lab: it became quiet and dark." From it is the saying of Ibn al-Ruqayyat: "Indeed this night has become dark."]]

In agreement with what we have said regarding this, the interpreters said, though they differed about the prayer which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was commanded to establish at that time. Some of them said: The prayer he was commanded to establish at that time is the Maghrib prayer.

Those who said this:
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾, who said: "The darkness of the night: the appearance of the night."
• Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayya told us, from Abu Raja', who said: "I heard that Ikrima was asked about this verse ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾, and he said: 'The appearance of the night.'"
• Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us; all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The darkness of the night: the setting of the sun."
• al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of that.
• Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding "ghasaq al-layl": the Maghrib prayer. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾: "The appearance of the night for the Maghrib prayer." It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) used to say: "A group of my community will remain upon the fitra as long as they pray the Maghrib before the stars appear."
• It was reported to me (ḥudittu) from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾: "That is, the darkness of the night."
• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "My father used to say: ﴿ghasaq al-layl﴾: the darkness of the night."

Others said: It is the 'Asr prayer.

Those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Abu Ja'far, regarding ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾: "It is the 'Asr prayer."

The most correct of the two opinions regarding this, in terms of truth, is the view of those who said: The prayer which the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to establish at the darkness of the night is the Maghrib prayer and no other, because the darkness of the night is what we have described: the approach of the night and its darkness, and that cannot happen except after the sun has set. As for the 'Asr prayer, it is among those prayers established between the beginning of the decline of the sun and the darkness of the night, not at the darkness of the night. As for His words ﴿and the recitation of dawn﴾, its meaning is: "And establish the recitation of dawn," that is, what is recited of the Qur'an in the Fajr prayer. The phrase "the recitation" is conjoined (ma'tuf) to "the prayer" in His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 77–78 (part 2 of 2):

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The accusative in His words ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾ ("and the recitation of dawn") is by way of incitement (al-ighra', i.e. urging someone to take up an action), as if He had said: "Upon you is the recitation of dawn." ﴿إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾ ("Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed"). He means: what you recite in the dawn prayer of the Qur'an is witnessed, attended by the angels of the night and the angels of the day, as is mentioned.

In accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said, and reports have come from the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said this:

• Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding this verse ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾, he said: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it."

• Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us. And Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Fadala ibn Ubayd, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed God opens the remembrance (al-dhikr) during three hours that remain of the night. In the first of these hours He looks into the Book which no one other than Him looks into, and He erases what He wills and affirms.
