Then in the second hour He descends to the Garden of Eden, which is His abode that no eye has seen and that has not occurred to the heart of any human being, and it is His dwelling, and no one of the children of Adam dwells with Him except three: the Prophets, the truthful ones (al-siddiqun), and the martyrs. Then He says: 'Blessed is whoever has entered you.' Then in the third hour He descends to the lowest heaven with His spirit and His angels, and it shakes, and He says: 'Rise, by My help.' Then He looks down upon His servants and says: 'Whoever seeks forgiveness from Me, I will forgive him; whoever asks Me, I will give to him; whoever calls upon Me, I will respond to him, until the dawn breaks.' That is when He says ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾." Musa said in his narration: "God witnesses it, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day." Ibn Askar said in his narration: "God witnesses it, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada, from Uqba ibn Abd al-Ghafir, who said: Abu Ubayda ibn Abdullah said: Abdullah used to narrate that at the dawn prayer the two guards (al-harasan) of the angels of God assemble, and he would recite this verse ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾: "The recitation of dawn" is the dawn prayer. We used to narrate that at it the two guards of the angels of God assemble, the guard of the night and the guard of the day.

• Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾: the dawn prayer. As for His words ﴿كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾, he means: the angels of the night and the angels of the day witness that prayer.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murra, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, that he said regarding this verse ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾: "The angels of the day descend and the angels of the night ascend."

• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Dirar ibn Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Abu Ubayda, regarding His words ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾, he said: "The guard of the night and the guard of the day among the angels witness it in the dawn prayer."

• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾, he said: "They used to say: the angels of the night and the angels of the day assemble at the dawn prayer, and they all witness it together. Then these ascend and those descend."

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾: "He means the morning prayer."

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾, he said: "The morning prayer."

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾: "The morning prayer," ﴿إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾, he said: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day assemble at the dawn prayer."

• It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾: "He means the morning prayer (salat al-ghadah)."

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾: "The dawn prayer." ﴿إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾: "Witnessed by the angels, as they mention." He said: Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ubayy ibn Ka'b used to say: the middle prayer (al-salat al-wusta) which God urged upon us is the dawn prayer. He said: That is because the noon prayer and the afternoon prayer are the two prayers of the day, and the sunset prayer and the night prayer are the two prayers of the night, and it lies between them; it is a prayer of sleep, and we do not know of a prayer that people neglect more than it.

• Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu al-Ward ibn Thumama, from Abu Muhammad al-Hadrami, who said: Ka'b narrated to us in this mosque, saying: By Him in whose hand is Ka'b's soul, this verse ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾ is indeed the dawn prayer; indeed it is witnessed.

• al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abbas narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, saying: My father informed me, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, that Abu Hurayra said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day assemble at the dawn prayer." Then Abu Hurayra said: Recite, if you wish: ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾, he said: "The dawn prayer, at which the angels of the night and the angels of the day assemble."

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 77–78 (part 1 of 2)**

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿The practice We applied to the messengers We sent before you, and you will not find any change in Our practice.﴾ (17:77)

His words, may His remembrance be exalted: "If they had driven you out, they would not have remained after you except for a little while, and We would have destroyed them with a punishment from Us. This is Our practice concerning those messengers We sent before you, for thus We used to deal with the nations when their messengers were driven out from among them." The word *sunna* (practice) is put in the accusative because it is read as a verbal noun from the meaning of His words ﴿they will not remain after you except for a little while﴾. The meaning is: "We would punish them after a short time, as is Our practice with the nations to whom We sent messengers before you, and you will not find any change in Our practice from what it has followed."

As reported:
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿The practice We applied to the messengers We sent before you, and you will not find any change in Our practice﴾: That is, the practice concerning the nations and messengers before you: when they denied their messengers and drove them out, they did not consider that God would send down His punishment upon them.

* *

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:** ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, and the recitation of dawn. Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed.﴾ (17:78)

His words, may His remembrance be exalted, addressed to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Establish the prayer﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿at the decline of the sun﴾.

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the time that God meant by "the decline of the sun" (dulūk al-shams). Some of them said: It is the time of its setting, and the prayer He commanded to be established at that time is the Maghrib prayer.

Those who said this:
• Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la al-Asadi told me, saying: Ibn Fudayl told us, from Abu Ishaq, meaning al-Shaybani, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad, from his father, that he was with Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud on a roof when the sun had set. He recited ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾ until he finished the verse. Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, this is the time when the sun declined, the fasting person breaks his fast, and the prayer is due."
• Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi told us, from Sa'id, from Qatada, from Uqba ibn Abd al-Ghafir, that Ubayda ibn Abd Allah wrote to him that Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, when the sun set, would pray the Maghrib prayer and break his fast then if he was fasting. He would swear an oath over it, more than he swore over anything concerning the prayers, "by God, besides whom there is no god, that this hour is the appointed time for this prayer." He would recite in it, as its explanation from the Book of God: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾.
• Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi told us, from Shu'ba, from Asim, from Abu Wa'il, from Abd Allah, who said: "This is the decline of the sun, and this is the darkness of the night," and he gestured towards the east and the west.
• Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The decline of the sun" is its setting; he said: it declined with *barah*.
• al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aswad, from Abd Allah, who said: "When the sun set, it declined," meaning *barah* as a place.
• al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Its decline is its setting."
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, who said: "It has been mentioned to us that Ibn Mas'ud used to pray it when it set, and break his fast at that time if he was fasting. Then he would swear an oath over it, more than he swore over anything concerning the prayers, 'by God, besides whom there is no god, that this hour is the appointed time for this prayer.' Then he would recite and pray it, and its confirmation is from the Book of God: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾."
• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾: "My father used to say: its decline is when the sun is about to set until the night becomes dark. He said: It is the Maghrib, when the night becomes dark, and the sun declines for setting."
• Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' told me, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyayna told us, that he heard Amr ibn Dinar say that Abu Ubayda ibn Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: "Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud used to pray the Maghrib when the edge of the sun disappeared, and he would swear that this is the time which God mentioned: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: Abd Allah said when the sun set: "By God, besides whom there is no god, this is the time of this prayer." And he said: "Its decline is its setting."

Others said: "The decline of the sun" is its inclination towards the zenith (zawāl), and the prayer which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was commanded to establish at its decline is the Zuhr prayer.

Those who said this:
• Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from al-A'mash, from Amara ibn Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from Abd Allah, who said: "Its decline is its inclination, meaning the sun."
• Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym told us, from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi, from Ibn Abbas, who said regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾: "Its decline is its zawal."
• Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman told me, saying: Abu Usama told us, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾: "Its decline is its inclination."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, from Sayyar ibn Salama, from Abu Barza al-Aslami, regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾: "When it has passed the zenith."
• Ibn Humayd told us again, saying: Abu Tumayla told us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, saying: Sayyar ibn Salama al-Riyahi told us, saying: "I came to Abu Barza, and my father asked him about the appointed times of the prayer of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He said: 'The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would pray the Zuhr when the sun passed its zenith.' Then he recited ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾."
• al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada'i told me, saying: My father told us, saying: Mubarak told us, from al-Hasan, who said: God the Mighty and Majestic said to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾. He said: "Its decline is the Zuhr, when it has moved away from the middle of the sky, and there is a shadow on the earth for it."
• Ya'qub told us, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Yunus informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾: "Its decline is its zawal."
• Ya'qub told me, saying: Hushaym told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, the like of that.
• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Abu Ja'far, regarding ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾: "For the zawal of the sun."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "The decline of the sun is its deviation after midday, meaning the shadow."
• Ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada: "The decline of the sun: when it deviates from the middle of the sky."
• Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾: that is, when the sun has passed the middle of the sky, for the Zuhr prayer.
• Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us; all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿at the decline of the sun﴾: "When it deviates."
• al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "The decline of the sun: when it deviates."

The most correct of the two opinions regarding this, in terms of truth, is the view of those who said: By His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾ He meant the Zuhr prayer. This is because "decline" (dulūk) in the speech of the Arabs means inclination. It is said of it: "So-and-so declined toward such-and-such" when he inclined toward it. From this is the report narrated from al-Hasan that a man said to him: "Does a man procrastinate (yudālik) with his wife?" meaning: does he incline her towards delaying her right? From this is the verse of the rajaz poet:

*This is the standing place of my feet, Rabah(?)...*
*At dawn, until the sun declined with barah.*

[[The rajaz verse is among the evidences cited by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (the University of Jami'a photographic edition, p. 181), and its version in it is "dhabb" in place of "ghadwa," which is the same as the version in Lisan al-Arab (b-r-h). Al-Farra' said: "'Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun': it has come from Ibn Abbas, who said: it is its deviation and its zawal for the Zuhr." Abu Zakariyya (al-Farra') said: "I saw the Arabs take the decline to be the setting of the sun. Some of them recited to me: 'This is my standing place...' the verse, meaning the water-carrier who drives people away with the hand: he says, until he places the palm over the eye and looks to see whether the sun has set." He said: "This is how they explained it to us." Abu Ubayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an (1:387): "The decline of the sun is from its zawal until it sets." And he said: "This is the standing place..." the verse. Do you not see that it is pushed away with the palm, placing the hand over the eyebrows against its rays, to look at what remains of its setting? And "dulūk" is its approach to its setting. Abu Zayd al-Ansari said in al-Nawadir (p. 88): "It is said: dalakat bi-rah and bi-rah (with a fatha on the ba' and a kasra or damma on the ha'), which is a known name for the sun." The rajaz poet said: "This is the standing place of my feet, Rabah..." Abu Hatim said: "barah means barahah (palm)." In Lisan al-Arab (b-r-h): "Barah and Barah (with an open ba' and kasra or damma on the ha'): a definite name for the sun, like Qatam, named so because of its spread and clarity."]]

In the version with a *fatha* on the *ba'* (barah), the sense is the name of the sun, and the *ha'* is made with a *kasra* for it, as in the forms Qatam, Hadham, and Raqash. When the meaning of *dulūk* in the speech of the Arabs is inclination, then there is no doubt that when the sun has moved away from the middle of the sky, it has inclined toward setting, and that is the time of the Zuhr prayer. The report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) confirms this, although there is some weakness in the chain of narration of part of it.

• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Khalid ibn Makhlad told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told me, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id told me, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Amr ibn Hazm al-Ansari told me, from Abu Mas'ud Uqba ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came to me at the decline of the sun, when it had passed the zenith, and he led me in the Zuhr prayer."
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Abu Tumayla told us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, saying: Sayyar ibn Salama al-Riyahi told me, saying: Abu Barza said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to pray the Zuhr when the sun passed the zenith." Then he recited ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾.
• Ibn Humayd told us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir told us, saying: Amr ibn Qays told us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from a man, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: "I invited the Prophet of God (ﷺ) and whoever of his companions wished, and they ate with me. Then they went out when the sun passed the zenith, and the Prophet (ﷺ) went out and said: 'Come out, O Abu Bakr, the sun has declined.'"
• Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Razi told me, saying: Sahl ibn Bakkar told us, saying: Abu Awana told us, from al-Aswad ibn Qays, from Nubayh al-Anazi, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of the report of Ibn Humayd.

So if what we have said is correct, and by what we have cited as evidence, then it is clear that the meaning of His words, may His praise be exalted, ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾ is that the Zuhr and 'Asr prayers, within their limits, are among what God has obligated upon you in them, because they are the two prayers that God made obligatory upon His Prophet from the time of the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night. The darkness of the night (ghasaq al-layl) is its approach and its drawing near with its darkness, as the poet said:

*This night has returned, when it became dark (ghasaq)...*

[[This is the first half of a line by Ubayd Allah ibn Qays al-Ruqayyat, whose second half is: "And I complained of worry and sleeplessness." He cited it as evidence that the meaning of "ghasaq al-layl" is its darkness (Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu Ubayda, 1:388). Abu Ubayda's version is: "Indeed this night has become dark (ghasaq)." The version in Lisan al-Arab also supports it. It says: "Ghasaq al-layl yaghsiq (like yadrib) ghasaqan and ghasaqanan, and aghsaq: according to Tha'lab: it became quiet and dark." From it is the saying of Ibn al-Ruqayyat: "Indeed this night has become dark."]]

In agreement with what we have said regarding this, the interpreters said, though they differed about the prayer which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was commanded to establish at that time. Some of them said: The prayer he was commanded to establish at that time is the Maghrib prayer.

Those who said this:
• Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾, who said: "The darkness of the night: the appearance of the night."
• Ya'qub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayya told us, from Abu Raja', who said: "I heard that Ikrima was asked about this verse ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night﴾, and he said: 'The appearance of the night.'"
• Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us; all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "The darkness of the night: the setting of the sun."
• al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of that.
• Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding "ghasaq al-layl": the Maghrib prayer. Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾: "The appearance of the night for the Maghrib prayer." It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) used to say: "A group of my community will remain upon the fitra as long as they pray the Maghrib before the stars appear."
• It was reported to me (ḥudittu) from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾: "That is, the darkness of the night."
• Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "My father used to say: ﴿ghasaq al-layl﴾: the darkness of the night."

Others said: It is the 'Asr prayer.

Those who said this:
• Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Abu Ja'far, regarding ﴿until the darkness of the night﴾: "It is the 'Asr prayer."

The most correct of the two opinions regarding this, in terms of truth, is the view of those who said: The prayer which the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to establish at the darkness of the night is the Maghrib prayer and no other, because the darkness of the night is what we have described: the approach of the night and its darkness, and that cannot happen except after the sun has set. As for the 'Asr prayer, it is among those prayers established between the beginning of the decline of the sun and the darkness of the night, not at the darkness of the night. As for His words ﴿and the recitation of dawn﴾, its meaning is: "And establish the recitation of dawn," that is, what is recited of the Qur'an in the Fajr prayer. The phrase "the recitation" is conjoined (ma'tuf) to "the prayer" in His words ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 77–78 (part 2 of 2):

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The accusative in His words ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾ ("and the recitation of dawn") is by way of incitement (al-ighra', i.e. urging someone to take up an action), as if He had said: "Upon you is the recitation of dawn." ﴿إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾ ("Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed"). He means: what you recite in the dawn prayer of the Qur'an is witnessed, attended by the angels of the night and the angels of the day, as is mentioned.

In accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said, and reports have come from the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said this:

• Ubayd ibn Asbat ibn Muhammad al-Qurashi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Ibn Mas'ud, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ), regarding this verse ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾, he said: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness it."

• Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us. And Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Fadala ibn Ubayd, from Abu al-Darda', who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Indeed God opens the remembrance (al-dhikr) during three hours that remain of the night. In the first of these hours He looks into the Book which no one other than Him looks into, and He erases what He wills and affirms. Then in the second hour He descends to the Garden of Eden, which is His abode that no eye has seen and that has not occurred to the heart of any human being, and it is His dwelling, and no one of the children of Adam dwells with Him except three: the Prophets, the truthful ones (al-siddiqun), and the martyrs. Then He says: 'Blessed is whoever has entered you.' Then in the third hour He descends to the lowest heaven with His spirit and His angels, and it shakes, and He says: 'Rise, by My help.' Then He looks down upon His servants and says: 'Whoever seeks forgiveness from Me, I will forgive him; whoever asks Me, I will give to him; whoever calls upon Me, I will respond to him, until the dawn breaks.' That is when He says ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾." Musa said in his narration: "God witnesses it, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day." Ibn Askar said in his narration: "God witnesses it, and the angels of the night and the angels of the day."

• Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatada, from Uqba ibn Abd al-Ghafir, who said: Abu Ubayda ibn Abdullah said: Abdullah used to narrate that at the dawn prayer the two guards (al-harasan) of the angels of God assemble, and he would recite this verse ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾.

• Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾: "The recitation of dawn" is the dawn prayer. We used to narrate that at it the two guards of the angels of God assemble, the guard of the night and the guard of the day.

• Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾: the dawn prayer. As for His words ﴿كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾, he means: the angels of the night and the angels of the day witness that prayer.

• Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Amr ibn Murra, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah, that he said regarding this verse ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾: "The angels of the day descend and the angels of the night ascend."

• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Dirar ibn Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl, from Abu Ubayda, regarding His words ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾, he said: "The guard of the night and the guard of the day among the angels witness it in the dawn prayer."

• Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, regarding His words ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾, he said: "They used to say: the angels of the night and the angels of the day assemble at the dawn prayer, and they all witness it together. Then these ascend and those descend."

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾: "He means the morning prayer."

• Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾, he said: "The morning prayer."

• al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾: "The morning prayer," ﴿إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾, he said: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day assemble at the dawn prayer."

• It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾: "He means the morning prayer (salat al-ghadah)."

• Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ﴾: "The dawn prayer." ﴿إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾: "Witnessed by the angels, as they mention." He said: Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ubayy ibn Ka'b used to say: the middle prayer (al-salat al-wusta) which God urged upon us is the dawn prayer. He said: That is because the noon prayer and the afternoon prayer are the two prayers of the day, and the sunset prayer and the night prayer are the two prayers of the night, and it lies between them; it is a prayer of sleep, and we do not know of a prayer that people neglect more than it.

• Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu al-Ward ibn Thumama, from Abu Muhammad al-Hadrami, who said: Ka'b narrated to us in this mosque, saying: By Him in whose hand is Ka'b's soul, this verse ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾ is indeed the dawn prayer; indeed it is witnessed.

• al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abbas narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn Shu'ayb narrated to us, saying: My father informed me, from al-Zuhri, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salama ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to me, that Abu Hurayra said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "The angels of the night and the angels of the day assemble at the dawn prayer." Then Abu Hurayra said: Recite, if you wish: ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾.

• Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿وَقُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ إِنَّ قُرْآنَ الْفَجْرِ كَانَ مَشْهُودًا﴾, he said: "The dawn prayer, at which the angels of the night and the angels of the day assemble."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 79 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And from the night, perform the tahajjud with it as a supererogatory act for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ (79).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "And from the night, stay awake after sleep, O Muhammad, with the Qur'an, as a supererogatory act specifically for you, apart from your community. Tahajjud (voluntary night vigil) means waking and staying up after sleep during the night. As for hujud itself, it is sleep, as the poet said:

Would that she had visited us while the companions were sleeping, so she spent the night giving the gifts of the beloved (al-'ulat al-nawal tajud)[[The poet is unidentified. Hujud may be the verbal noun of hajada, yahjudu, hujudan, meaning to sleep, and the intended sense would be "and the companions were people in sleep" or "were sleeping", making it equivalent to the participle. Or hujud may be a plural of hajid without any alteration, like 'uqud as a plural of qa'id, and julus as a plural of jalis, and huḍur as a plural of hadir. Al-'ulat is the plural of 'allah, a term for a single instance of "al-'al", which is the second watering after the first. Al-nawal is what the beloved gives the beloved from the fruit of love.]]

And al-Ḥuṭay'ah said:

Would that Hind of the Hunud and my companions had visited, while they were sleeping in Hawran, Hawran of the armies (hujud)[[The verse is by al-Ḥuṭay'ah (his Diwan, Hamidiyya edition, p. 103). Its commentator said: every district of the districts of Syria is a jund. Hujud is the plural of hajid, meaning the sleeper, and like qu'ud, the plural of qa'id. The point of evidence is that hujud in the verse means sleep, as in al-Ḥuṭay'ah's verse. It is the verbal noun of hajada, yahjudu, hujudan, when one sleeps. The verbal noun then carries the sense of the participle, or it means: "and the companions were people of hujud", then the qualifying noun was omitted and the verbal noun was put in its place.]]

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: My father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, from al-Layth, from Mujahid ibn Yazid, from Abu Hilal, from al-A'raj, that he said: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf informed me, from a man of the Ansar, that he was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on a journey, and he said: "I will surely observe how the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prays." He said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ slept, then awoke, raised his head toward the sky, and recited the last four verses of Surah Al 'Imran, ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day﴾, until he finished the four. Then he turned to the waterskin, took a siwak and cleaned his teeth with it, performed ablution, prayed, then slept, then awoke and did as he had done the first time. They claim that this is the tahajjud that Allah commanded.
- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Alqamah and al-Aswad, that they both said: tahajjud is after sleep.
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad, who said: Tahajjud is after sleep.
- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Shu'bah, who said: Abu Ishaq narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, from 'Alqamah and al-Aswad, the same as this.
- al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqamah, who said: Tahajjud is after sleep.
- al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, from Hisham, from al-Hasan, who said: Tahajjud is what occurs after the late night prayer ('isha').
- I was told from 'Abd Allah ibn Salih, from al-Layth, from Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah, from al-A'raj, from Kathir ibn al-'Abbas, from al-Hajjaj ibn 'Amr, who said: Tahajjud is only after a sleep.

As for His saying ﴿as a supererogatory act for you﴾, He means: a supererogation (nafl) for you beyond your obligatory duties which He has imposed upon you.

There has been disagreement about the reason for which this was specific to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, given that each worshipper's prayer after his sleep is a supererogation, since before his sleep he had already fulfilled his obligations, and those prayers were nafl because they were not obligatory on him. Some of them said: the meaning of its being specific to him is that it was an obligation upon him, while for others it is voluntary; and it was said to him: "Establish it as a supererogation for you," meaning, an extra favour for you beyond the obligatory duties which He imposed upon you, over what He imposed upon others.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And from the night, perform the tahajjud with it as a supererogatory act for you﴾: he means by the supererogatory act that it is specific to the Prophet ﷺ; he was commanded to stand in the night and it was prescribed for him.

Others said: rather, this was said to him ﷺ because his doing it did not expiate any of his sins, since Allah had already forgiven him what preceded and what followed of his sins; so for him it was an extra favour, whereas for others it is an expiation, and it is not a supererogation for them.

Mention of those who said that:

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir, from Mujahid, who said: The nafl is specific to the Prophet ﷺ, because his sins, those preceding and those following, have been forgiven. So whatever deed he performs apart from the obligatory prayer is a nafl, because he does not perform it to expiate sins; rather they are supererogations and an increase. People perform what is beyond the obligatory prayer to expiate their sins, so for people there are no supererogations.

The more correct of the two views is the view we have mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas, because Allah, exalted is He, had specifically singled him out with the qiyam al-layl (night standing) which was imposed upon him, apart from the rest of his community. As for what is reported from Mujahid in this regard, it is a view with no meaning, because the Messenger of Allah, as is reported of him, was mostly engaged in seeking forgiveness for his sins after the revelation of the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic, to him: ﴿That Allah may forgive you your earlier and later sins﴾. This surah was revealed to him after his return from al-Hudaybiyah, and there was revealed to him ﴿When the help of Allah and the victory has come﴾ in the year of his death. In it he was told ﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise and seek His forgiveness; indeed He is ever Accepting of repentance﴾. He used to count for the Prophet ﷺ, in a single session, one hundred repetitions of seeking forgiveness; and it is well known that Allah did not command him to seek forgiveness except for what would be forgiven him by that seeking forgiveness. Thus the flaw in what Mujahid said becomes clear.

- Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shamir, from 'Atiyah, from Shahr, from Abu Umamah, who said: The nafl was only for the Prophet ﷺ.
- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿as a supererogatory act for you﴾: he said: a voluntary act and a virtue for you.

* *

As for His saying ﴿perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾:

The "perhaps" (asa) from Allah is binding. The sense of the statement of the scholars that "asa" from Allah is binding is that the people of faith know that Allah does not abandon doing for His servants what He has given them hope in, namely the reward for their deeds and the recompense for their obedience to Him, since it is not part of His attributes to deceive. There is no doubt that whoever is told this and given hope of benefit from it, if he adheres to it and keeps to it, and then it does not benefit him, with no obstacle preventing its benefit to him despite the hope previously given to his companion by adhering to and keeping to it, then he has deceived his companion through the breaking of the promise that had given him hope through the saying spoken to him. Since that is so, and it is impossible that He, mighty is His praise, has the attribute of deceiving His servants, it is established and necessary that everything He gives them hope in, whether a hope for obedience to Him, or for some act, or a command He commands them or prohibition He forbids them, He will fulfil it for them, and that it is for them like a promise which He does not fail to fulfil. They said: "asa" and "la'alla" from Allah are binding.

The meaning of the speech: "Establish the obligatory prayer, O Muhammad, at the times in which I have commanded you to establish it, and from the night perform tahajjud as an obligation I have imposed upon you; perhaps your Lord will raise you on the Day of Resurrection to a praiseworthy station in which you will be praised and envied."

Then the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that praiseworthy station. Most of the scholars said: it is the station which he ﷺ will occupy on the Day of Resurrection to intercede for the people, so that their Lord may relieve them of the great distress of that dreadful day.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah, who said: The people will be gathered in one plain, the caller will make them hear, and the sight will reach them all; barefoot, naked, as they were created, standing, no soul speaking except by His permission. He will call out: "O Muhammad!" and he will say: "At your service, and at your pleasure, and the good is in Your hands, and evil is not attributed to You; the one who is guided is the one You have guided; Your servant is before You, by You and to You; there is no refuge and no escape from You except to You; You are blessed and exalted; glory be to You, Lord of this House." This is the praiseworthy station which Allah, exalted is He, mentioned.
- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah, who said: The people will be gathered in one plain. No soul will speak. The first to be called is Muhammad the Prophet ﷺ, and Muhammad the Prophet ﷺ will stand and say: "At your service," then he mentioned the like.
- Sulayman ibn 'Amr ibn Khalid al-Raqqi narrated to us, saying: 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Rushdin ibn Kurayb, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾: he said: The praiseworthy station is the station of intercession.
- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, who said: Abu al-Za'ra' narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah, in a story he mentioned, who said: Then he will be commanded with the Sirat, and it will be laid over the bridge of Hell, and people will pass according to their deeds; the first of them will pass like lightning, and like the passing of the wind, and like the passing of birds, and like the swiftest beasts; then in this manner until a man passes running, then walking, until the last of them comes dragging himself on his belly, and says: "My Lord, why have You delayed me?" He will say: "I have not delayed you; rather your deeds have delayed you." He said: Then Allah will permit intercession, and the first intercessor on the Day of Resurrection will be Jibril, peace be upon him, the Holy Spirit; then Ibrahim, the Friend of the Most Merciful; then Musa, or 'Isa. Abu al-Za'ra' said: I do not know which of them he said. He said: Then your Prophet ﷺ will stand fourth, and no one will intercede after him in what he intercedes for. This is the praiseworthy station which Allah mentioned: ﴿perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾.
- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, regarding the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And from the night, perform the tahajjud with it as a supererogatory act for you; perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾: he said: The praiseworthy station is the station of intercession on the Day of Resurrection.
- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿a praiseworthy station﴾: he said: The intercession of Muhammad on the Day of Resurrection.
- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu 'Uthman, from Salman, who said: It is the intercession; Allah will grant him intercession for his community, and that is the praiseworthy station.
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾: It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ was given the choice between being a prophet-servant or a king-prophet, and Jibril, peace be upon him, gestured to him: "Be humble," so the Prophet of Allah chose to be a prophet-servant. For this, the Prophet of Allah was given two things: he is the first from whom the earth will be split open, and the first intercessor. The people of knowledge used to hold that it is the praiseworthy station which Allah, blessed and exalted, mentioned: ﴿perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾, the intercession on the Day of Resurrection.
- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿a praiseworthy station﴾: he said: It is the intercession; Allah will grant him intercession for his community.
- al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar and al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar, who said: I heard Hudhayfah say regarding His saying ﴿perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾: Allah will gather the people in one plain where the caller makes them hear and the sight reaches them all, barefoot and naked as they were created, silent, no soul speaking except by His permission. He said: Then Muhammad will be called, and he will say: "At your service and at your pleasure; the good is in Your hands, evil is not from You; the one guided is the one You have guided; Your servant is before You, for You and to You; there is no refuge and no escape from You except to You; You are blessed and exalted; glory be to You, Lord of the House." He said: That is the praiseworthy station which Allah mentioned: ﴿perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾.
- Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar, who said Hudhayfah said: Allah will gather the people in one plain, where the sight reaches them and the caller makes them hear, barefoot and naked as they were created the first time. Then the Prophet ﷺ will stand and say: "At your service and at your pleasure," then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: It is the praiseworthy station.

Others said: rather, that praiseworthy station which Allah promised His Prophet that He would raise him to is that He will seat him with Him on His throne.

Mention of those who said that:

- 'Abbad ibn Ya'qub al-Asadi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾: he said: He will seat him with Him on His throne.

The more correct of the two views on this matter is what has been authentically reported from the Messenger of Allah.

That is what:

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Yazid, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said regarding ﴿perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾, when he was asked about it: "It is the intercession."
- 'Ali ibn Harb narrated to us, saying: Makki ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn Yazid al-Awdi narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying ﴿perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾: he said: "It is the station in which I will intercede for my community."
- Abu 'Utbah al-Himsi Ahmad ibn al-Faraj narrated to us, saying: Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, from al-Zubaydi, from al-Zuhri, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from Ka'b ibn Malik, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and I and my community will be on a hill, and my Lord will clothe me with a green robe; then I will be permitted, and I will say what Allah wills me to say; that is the praiseworthy station."
- Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far, that he said: I heard Hamzah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar say: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The sun will draw near until the sweat reaches halfway to the ears; while they are in that state, they will seek help from Adam, peace be upon him, and he will say, 'I am not the one for this'; then from Musa, peace be upon him, who will say the same; then from Muhammad, who will intercede among the creation until he takes hold of the ring of Paradise; on that day Allah will raise him to a praiseworthy station."
- Abu Zayd 'Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to me, saying: Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Zayd narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn al-Hakam, saying: 'Uthman narrated to me, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad and 'Alqamah, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed I will stand the praiseworthy station." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is that praiseworthy station?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "That is when you are brought barefoot, naked, uncircumcised. The first to be clothed will be Ibrahim, peace be upon him; two white garments will be brought to him, and he will wear them, then he will sit facing the Throne. Then my garment will be brought and I will wear it, and I will stand at his right hand in a station which no one but me will stand, in which the first and the last will envy me. Then a river of al-Kawthar will flow to the Basin."

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAʿlā narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will stretch out the earth like a tanned hide, until there is no room for any human being except the place of his feet. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: I will be the first to be called, and Jibrīl will be at the right hand of the Most Merciful. By God, he had never seen him before. I will say: O Lord, this one informed me that You sent him to me. God, the Mighty and Majestic, will say: He has spoken the truth. Then I will intercede." He said: "That is the praiseworthy station (al-maqām al-maḥmūd)."

⁕ al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, who said: The Prophet said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes..." and he mentioned something similar, adding in it: "Then I will intercede, and I will say: O Lord, Your servants have worshipped You at the far ends of the earth." And that is the praiseworthy station.

⁕ Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿĀmir narrated to us, saying: Ibrāhīm ibn Ṭahmān narrated to us, from Ādam, from ʿAlī, who said: I heard Ibn ʿUmar say: People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and with every prophet will come his community. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) will come, last of the nations, he and his community, and he and his community will ascend a mound above the people. He will say: O so-and-so, intercede; O so-and-so, intercede; O so-and-so, intercede. They will continue returning it from one to another [[Perhaps: until it returns to him.]], and that is the praiseworthy station which God promised him.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAwf narrated to us, saying: Ḥaywa and Rabīʿ narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, from al-Zubaydī, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kaʿb ibn Mālik, from Kaʿb ibn Mālik, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and I and my community will be upon a hill. My Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, will clothe me in a green robe. Then I will be given permission, and I will say what God wills me to say. That is the praiseworthy station."

And this, although it is the correct view regarding the interpretation (ta'wīl, interpretation) of His words ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾, is based on the reports we have cited from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), his Companions, and the Successors. As for what Mujāhid said, that God seats Muhammad (ﷺ) upon His Throne, it is a view whose soundness is not refuted, neither by report nor by reasoning. This is because there is no report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), nor from any of his Companions, nor from the Successors, that rules it out. As for reasoning, all who profess Islam have differed about the meaning of this on three positions:

A group among them said: God, the Mighty and Majestic, is distinct from His creation. He existed before creating things, then He created things without touching them, and He remains as He always was. But since the things He created were not touched by Him, they must be separate from Him, for there is no action of things except that He is either touching bodies or separate from them. They said: If that is so, and God, the Mighty and Majestic, is the Doer of things, and it is not permissible in their view to describe Him as touching things, then by their assumption He must be separate from them. According to the doctrine of these people, it is the same whether Muhammad (ﷺ) is seated on His Throne or on the earth, since by their saying His separation from His Throne and His separation from His earth have the same meaning: He is separate from both of them entirely, not touching either.

Another group said: God, may His mention be exalted, existed before creating things, with nothing touching Him and nothing separate from Him. Then He created things and established them by His power, and He remains as He was before creating things, with nothing touching Him and nothing separate from Him. According to the view of these people too, it is the same whether Muhammad (ﷺ) is seated on His Throne or on His earth, since by their saying His Throne and His earth are equal in that He neither touches nor is separate from either of them, just as He neither touches nor is separate from this.

Another group said: God, the Mighty and Majestic, existed before creating things, with nothing touching Him and nothing separate from Him. Then He brought things into being and created them, and He created for Himself a Throne upon which He sat, and so He came to touch it. Just as He existed before creating things with nothing giving Him provision and nothing denying Him that, then He created things and provided for this one, denied that one, gave to this one and withheld from that one, so, they said, He existed before creating things touching nothing and separate from nothing, and when He created things, He touched the Throne by sitting upon it, in distinction from the rest of His creation. Thus He touches whatever of His creation He wills and is separate from whatever He wills. According to the doctrine of these people too, it is the same whether He seats Muhammad on His Throne or seats him on a pulpit of light, since in their view the Lord's sitting upon His Throne is not a sitting that occupies the whole Throne, and seating Muhammad (ﷺ) does not necessarily confer upon him the attribute of lordship, nor remove him from the attribute of servanthood to his Lord. Just as Muhammad's (ﷺ) separation from things with which he is separate does not necessarily confer upon him the attribute of lordship, nor remove him from the attribute of servanthood to his Lord merely because he is described as separate from them, so God, the Mighty and Majestic, according to the statement of the proponent of this view, is described as separate from them, and they are separate from Him. They said: If the meaning of "separate" and "separate from" does not require that Muhammad (ﷺ) leave the attribute of servanthood and enter the meaning of lordship, then likewise his being seated on the Throne of the Most Merciful does not require that for him. Thus it has become clear from what we have said that it is not impossible, according to any of those who profess Islam, that what Mujāhid said is true: that God, may He be blessed and exalted, seats Muhammad upon His Throne.

If a speaker says: We do not deny that God seats Muhammad upon His Throne; we only deny that He seats him [[The remainder of this sentence appears to have been lost at this point. Its complete counterpart will appear in full in the third line after it.]].

⁕ ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAẓīm narrated to me, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Kathīr narrated to us, from al-Jurayrī, from Sayf al-Sadūsī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, who said: Indeed Muhammad (ﷺ) on the Day of Resurrection will be upon the Kursī of the Lord, before the Lord, may He be blessed and exalted. And they deny only that He seats him together with Him. It was said: Is it permissible in your view that He seats him upon it and not with Him? If he permits that, he moves to affirming either that He seats him with Him, or that He seats him while being separate from the Throne, or while touching nothing and being separate from nothing; and whichever of these he says, he has entered into part of what he denied. If he says that is not permissible, he has departed from the view of all the sects whose views we have related, and that is a separation from the doctrine of all who profess Islam, since there is no position on this except the three positions we have related, and none of them makes what Mujāhid said impossible.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 80:

The explanation of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."﴾

He, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet: "And say, O Muhammad, 'My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance.'"

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of "a sound entrance" (mudkhal sidq), which God commanded His Prophet ﷺ to ask Him to make him enter, and "a sound exit" (makhraj sidq), which He commanded him to ask Him to make him exit by. Some of them said: By "a sound entrance" is meant the entrance of the Messenger of God ﷺ into Medina when he migrated to it, and by "a sound exit" his exit from Mecca when he left it as a emigrant to Medina.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Waki' and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet ﷺ was in Mecca, then he was commanded to emigrate, so God, blessed and exalted is His name, revealed: ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority."﴾.

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Buza' narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, concerning God's saying ﴿cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit﴾, he said: The disbelievers of Mecca, when they conspired against the Messenger of God ﷺ to kill him, or expel him, or imprison him, and God intended to fight the people of Mecca, He commanded him to go out to Medina, and it is this that God referred to in ﴿cause me to enter a sound entrance﴾.

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿a sound entrance﴾ he said: Medina; ﴿a sound exit﴾ he said: Mecca.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit"﴾: God brought him out of Mecca to the emigration to Medina.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit"﴾: Medina when he emigrated to it, and a sound exit: Mecca when he left it as a sound exit; he said this when he left as an emigrant.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "And say, 'My Lord, cause me to die a sound death, and bring me out after death from my grave on the Day of Resurrection as a sound exit.'"

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance"﴾ .... the verse, he said: By the entrance is meant death, and by the exit is meant life after death.

Others said: Rather, He meant by that: "Cause me to enter, in the matter of Your message with which You sent me as a prophet, a sound entrance, and cause me to exit from it a sound exit."

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿cause me to enter a sound entrance﴾ he said: in what You sent me with of Your command; ﴿and cause me to exit a sound exit﴾ he also said likewise.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "Cause me to enter a sound entrance": Paradise; and "a sound exit": from Mecca to Medina.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan said, ﴿cause me to enter a sound entrance﴾ is Paradise, and ﴿a sound exit﴾ is from Mecca to Medina.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "Cause me to enter Islam as a sound entrance."

Mention of those who said that:

Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, concerning His saying ﴿My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance﴾, he said: Cause me to enter Islam as a sound entrance ﴿and cause me to exit﴾ from it ﴿a sound exit﴾.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "Cause me to enter Mecca safe, and cause me to exit from it safe."

Mention of those who said that:

It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying ﴿My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit﴾, meaning Mecca: he entered it safe and exited from it safe.

The most fitting of these sayings to the correct interpretation of this is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: "And cause me to enter Medina as a sound entrance, and cause me to exit from Mecca as a sound exit."

We only said that this is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse because it follows His saying ﴿And indeed, they almost incited you to leave the land to expel you from it; and then they would not remain after you except a little﴾. We have already shown earlier that by this He meant the people of Mecca. Since this follows God's report of what the polytheists intended of provoking the Messenger of God ﷺ to expel him from Mecca, it becomes clear, since God had indeed expelled him from it, that His saying ﴿And say, "My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and cause me to exit a sound exit"﴾ is a command from Him to him to ask Him to bring him out of the town from which the polytheists intended to expel him by a sound exit, and to cause him to enter the town to which God transferred him by a sound entrance.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority﴾.

The people of interpretation differed concerning its explanation. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: "And grant me a supporting kingship that supports me against those who oppose me, and a might by which I establish Your religion and repel from it whoever intends it harm."

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Buza' narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, concerning God's saying, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority﴾, he threatened him: "He will surely strip the kingdom of Persia and the might of Persia and give it to him, and the might of Rome and the kingdom of Rome and give it to him."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority﴾: The Prophet of God knew that he had no power for this matter except with authority, so he asked for a supporting authority for the Book of God, Mighty and Majestic, and for the limits of God, and for the obligations of God, and for establishing the religion of God. Indeed, authority is a mercy from God which He placed among His servants; were it not for it, some of them would raid others, and the strong would devour the weak.

Others said: Rather, by that is meant a clear proof.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's saying, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿a supporting authority﴾, he said: a clear proof.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

The most correct of these sayings in interpretation is the saying of the one who said: This is a command from God Exalted to His Prophet to ask Him to grant him a supporting authority that supports him against whoever seeks him and plots against him and attempts to prevent him from establishing God's obligations in himself and among His servants.

I only said this is more correct because it follows God's report of what the polytheists had resolved to do, namely expelling him from Mecca. God, Mighty and Majestic, informed him that if they did that they would quickly be punished. Then He commanded him to ask Him to bring him out from among them by a sound exit that would prevail over them, and to cause him to enter another town by a sound entrance that would prevail over them and over its people upon his entry into it, and to make for him a supporting authority over the people of the town from which its people expelled him, and over everyone who resembled them. When that is granted to him, then without doubt he has been granted a clear proof.

As for His saying ﴿a supporting authority﴾, Ibn Zayd used to say about it something similar to what we have said.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority﴾: "He will support me." God said to Moses ﴿We will strengthen your arm through your brother and We will grant you both authority, so they will not reach you through Our signs﴾. This is advanced and delayed; it is only: authority through Our signs, so they will not reach you both.

Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿And say, "The truth has come and falsehood has departed; indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart."﴾ ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who almost tried to unsettle you from the land in order to expel you from it: ﴿The truth has come and falsehood has departed.﴾

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of "the truth" that God commanded His Prophet ﷺ to inform the polytheists has come, and "the falsehood" that He commanded him to inform them has departed. Some of them said: The truth here is the Qur'an, and the falsehood is Satan.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿And say, "The truth has come"﴾: He said: The truth is the Qur'an. ﴿And falsehood has departed; indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart.﴾

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And say, "The truth has come"﴾: He said: The Qur'an. ﴿And falsehood has departed﴾: He said: Falsehood has perished, and it is Satan.

Others said: Rather, by "the truth" is meant the jihad against the polytheists, and by "the falsehood" is meant polytheism.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words ﴿And say, "The truth has come"﴾: He said: The fighting has drawn near. ﴿And falsehood has departed﴾: He said: Polytheism and what they were in.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ entered Mecca, and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols, so he began striking them and saying: ﴿The truth has come and falsehood has departed; indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart.﴾

The most correct of these sayings, in our view, is that it should be said: God, blessed and exalted, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to inform the polytheists that the truth has come, which is everything in which there is God's pleasure and obedience, and that falsehood has departed, meaning: everything in which there is no pleasure or obedience of God, and which is disobedience to Him and obedience to Satan, has gone. This is because the truth is everything that opposes the obedience of Iblis, and falsehood is everything that agrees with his obedience. God, may His remembrance be exalted, did not restrict the report to some of His obedience or the departure of some of His disobedience; rather, the report encompassed the coming of all truth and the departure of all falsehood. By this the Qur'an and the revelation came, and upon this the Messenger of God ﷺ fought the people of polytheism against God, meaning: upon establishing all truth and nullifying all falsehood.

As for His words, mighty and majestic, ﴿and falsehood has departed﴾, its meaning is: falsehood went away, from their saying "zahaqat nafsuhu" (his soul departed) when it came out, and "azhaqtuha" (I expelled it); and from their saying "azhaqa al-sahm" (the arrow exceeded the target and continued on its course). It is said from this: zahaqa al-batil, yazhaqu zuhuqan, and God azhaqahu, meaning: removed it.

The interpreters said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

'Ali narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart﴾: he said: going away.

As for His words, mighty and majestic, ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾, God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We send down to you, O Muhammad, of the Qur'an that which is a healing by which one is cured of ignorance and misguidance, and by which one is made to see after blindness, a mercy for the believers, and not for the disbelievers in it. This is because the believers act upon what it contains of God's obligations, they make lawful what He made lawful and forbid what He forbade, and so He admits them to Paradise by this and saves them from His punishment. Thus it is for them a mercy and a blessing from God, which He bestowed upon them. ﴿And it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾: he says: this which We send down to you of the Qur'an does not increase the disbelievers in it except in loss, meaning: destruction. This is because whenever a command from God regarding something or a prohibition against something was revealed, they disbelieved in it, did not comply with His command, and did not desist from what He forbade them; so that increased them in loss, in addition to the loss they were already in before that, and filth added to their previous filth.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾: when the believer hears it, he benefits from it, memorizes it and comprehends it. ﴿And it does not increase the wrongdoers﴾ by it ﴿except in loss﴾: that they do not benefit from it, do not memorize it, and do not comprehend it; and that God made this Qur'an a healing and a mercy for the believers.

Commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿And say, "The truth has come and falsehood has departed; indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart."﴾ ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, and it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who almost tried to unsettle you from the land in order to expel you from it: ﴿The truth has come and falsehood has departed.﴾

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of "the truth" that God commanded His Prophet ﷺ to inform the polytheists has come, and "the falsehood" that He commanded him to inform them has departed. Some of them said: The truth here is the Qur'an, and the falsehood is Satan.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿And say, "The truth has come"﴾: He said: The truth is the Qur'an. ﴿And falsehood has departed; indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart.﴾

Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And say, "The truth has come"﴾: He said: The Qur'an. ﴿And falsehood has departed﴾: He said: Falsehood has perished, and it is Satan.

Others said: Rather, by "the truth" is meant the jihad against the polytheists, and by "the falsehood" is meant polytheism.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning His words ﴿And say, "The truth has come"﴾: He said: The fighting has drawn near. ﴿And falsehood has departed﴾: He said: Polytheism and what they were in.

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ entered Mecca, and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols, so he began striking them and saying: ﴿The truth has come and falsehood has departed; indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart.﴾

The most correct of these sayings, in our view, is that it should be said: God, blessed and exalted, commanded His Prophet ﷺ to inform the polytheists that the truth has come, which is everything in which there is God's pleasure and obedience, and that falsehood has departed, meaning: everything in which there is no pleasure or obedience of God, and which is disobedience to Him and obedience to Satan, has gone. This is because the truth is everything that opposes the obedience of Iblis, and falsehood is everything that agrees with his obedience. God, may His remembrance be exalted, did not restrict the report to some of His obedience or the departure of some of His disobedience; rather, the report encompassed the coming of all truth and the departure of all falsehood. By this the Qur'an and the revelation came, and upon this the Messenger of God ﷺ fought the people of polytheism against God, meaning: upon establishing all truth and nullifying all falsehood.

As for His words, mighty and majestic, ﴿and falsehood has departed﴾, its meaning is: falsehood went away, from their saying "zahaqat nafsuhu" (his soul departed) when it came out, and "azhaqtuha" (I expelled it); and from their saying "azhaqa al-sahm" (the arrow exceeded the target and continued on its course). It is said from this: zahaqa al-batil, yazhaqu zuhuqan, and God azhaqahu, meaning: removed it.

The interpreters said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

'Ali narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿indeed, falsehood is ever bound to depart﴾: he said: going away.

As for His words, mighty and majestic, ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾, God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We send down to you, O Muhammad, of the Qur'an that which is a healing by which one is cured of ignorance and misguidance, and by which one is made to see after blindness, a mercy for the believers, and not for the disbelievers in it. This is because the believers act upon what it contains of God's obligations, they make lawful what He made lawful and forbid what He forbade, and so He admits them to Paradise by this and saves them from His punishment. Thus it is for them a mercy and a blessing from God, which He bestowed upon them. ﴿And it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾: he says: this which We send down to you of the Qur'an does not increase the disbelievers in it except in loss, meaning: destruction. This is because whenever a command from God regarding something or a prohibition against something was revealed, they disbelieved in it, did not comply with His command, and did not desist from what He forbade them; so that increased them in loss, in addition to the loss they were already in before that, and filth added to their previous filth.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾: when the believer hears it, he benefits from it, memorizes it and comprehends it. ﴿And it does not increase the wrongdoers﴾ by it ﴿except in loss﴾: that they do not benefit from it, do not memorize it, and do not comprehend it; and that God made this Qur'an a healing and a mercy for the believers.

The Most High says: "And when We bestow favour upon man, delivering him from the distress he is in at sea, where he had been brought close to destruction by the wind's violent storm upon him, to dry land, and from our other blessings, he turns away from remembering Us, though he had been calling upon Us alone, above anyone else, in the hardship he was in." ﴿And distances himself﴾ means: he moves away from Us with his side, meaning with himself, ﴿as if he had never called on Us for a harm that touched him﴾ before that.

As related:
