⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us. And al-Harith told me, he said: al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa told us, all from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and distances himself﴾. He said: he moved far away from us.

⁕ al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

The recitation (qira'a) with the hamza placed before the alif in naʾa (nā'a, "distanced") is the eloquent dialect, and it is by this that we recite. Some people of Medina recited it as "wanaʾa," placing the hamza after the alif. Although this is a permissible dialect, it came from the Arabs, who in similar cases moved the hamza from a position where it is final to one where it is medial, and vice versa, as the poet said:

A'lam yuqallilu rā'a ru'yā... fahwa yahdhī bimā ra'ā fī al-manām
[[This is how this line appears in the manuscripts, and after investigation we have not been able to identify its speaker. It is from the meter al-Khafif, and its first hemistich contains a distortion. The correct version is likely: "Umm ghulāmun mudallil rā'a ru'yā... fahwa yahdhī bimā ra'ā fī al-manām" (Or a mislead youth who saw a vision... he raves about what he saw in the dream).

As for the point of evidence in the verse, it is sound: in his words "rā'a," it is an inversion (qalb) of ra'ā, with the lam placed before the ayn, and it follows the pattern of "fala'a." The proof is that the verbal noun of both verbs is one and the same, ru'yā. Similarly, in inversion, "nā'a" and its verbal noun is al-nay'.]]

Likewise, it is said "ābār" and "abʾār" (wells), where they moved the hamza. That is not the dialect of al-Judi; rather, the other form is the eloquent one.

As for His words, mighty and majestic, ﴿And when evil touches him, he is despairing﴾, it means: and when evil and hardship touch him, he is despairing of relief and of comfort (rawḥ).

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said the same as what we have said about yā'ūs (despairing).

Those who said that:

⁕ Ali ibn Dawud told us, he said: Abd Allah told us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And when evil touches him, he is despairing﴾, he said: despondent.

⁕ Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And when evil touches him, he is despairing﴾, he said: when evil touches him, he despairs and loses hope.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 84:

The interpretation of His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿Say: Each works according to his own manner, but your Lord knows best who is best guided in the way﴾ (17:84).

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to the people: Each of you works according to his shakila, that is, according to his side and his way. ﴿Your Lord knows best who﴾ is among you ﴿best guided in the way﴾. He says: Your Lord knows best who among you is more rightly guided on the path to the truth than others.

Similar to what we have said on this matter, the people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e., the exegetes) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ali related to us, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿Each works according to his own manner﴾: he said, "On his side."

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿according to his own manner﴾: he said, "According to his side."

* al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, ﴿Say: Each works according to his own manner﴾: he said, "According to his nature, according to his distinct disposition."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿Say: Each works according to his own manner﴾: he said, "According to his side and according to what he intends."

Others said: al-Shakila means the religion.

Mention of those who said that:

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Each works according to his own manner﴾: "According to his religion; al-shakila is the religion."

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 85:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.﴾ (85)

God, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): The disbelievers among the People of the Book ask you about the soul: what is it? Say to them: The soul is by the command of my Lord, and what you and all of mankind have been given of knowledge is only a little. It is mentioned that those who asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the soul, and because of their question this verse was revealed, were a people from among the Jews.

Mention of the narration to this effect: Abu Hisham related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, saying: al-A'mash related to us, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abdullah, who said: I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) in a field in Medina, and he had a palm-stalk on which he leaned. He passed by a group of Jews, and some of them said: Ask him about the soul. And some of them said: Do not ask him. He stood up leaning on his palm-stalk, and I stood behind him, and I thought that he was being revealed to. Then he said: ﴿They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.﴾ Then some of them said to others: Did we not tell you not to ask him?

⁕ Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi related to us, saying: my father related to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abdullah, who said: "While I was walking with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) on a lava field in Medina, we passed by Jews, and some of them said: Ask him about the soul. They said: What makes you want to hear what you dislike? So they stood up to him and asked him. He stood, and I knew that he was being revealed to, so I stayed in my place. Then he recited: ﴿They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.﴾ They said: Did we not forbid you to ask him?"

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Ikrimah, who said: "The People of the Book asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the soul, so God, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.﴾ They said: Do you claim that we have been given only a little knowledge, when we have been given the Torah, which is wisdom? ﴿And whoever is given wisdom has indeed been given much good.﴾ He said: Then it was revealed: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens, and the sea, with seven more seas added to it, were ink, the words of God would not be exhausted.﴾ He said: What you have been given of knowledge, by which God has saved you from the Fire, is abundant and good, and in God's knowledge it is little."

⁕ Ismail ibn Abi al-Mutawakkil related to me, saying: al-Ashja'i Abu Asim al-Himsi related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Isa Abu Ya'qub related to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Ma'n related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abdullah, who said: I was with the Prophet (ﷺ) in a field in Medina when a Jew came to him and said: O Abu al-Qasim, what is the soul? The Prophet (ﷺ) was silent, and God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord.﴾

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: ﴿They ask you about the soul﴾: The Jews met the Prophet of God (ﷺ), surrounded him, and asked him, saying: If he is a prophet, he knows; he will know this. So they asked him about the soul, about the People of the Cave, and about Dhu al-Qarnayn, and God revealed all of that in His Book: ﴿They ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.﴾ He means the Jews.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿They ask you about the soul﴾: The Jews ask about it.

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿They ask you about the soul﴾: The Jews ask him.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to us, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿They ask you about the soul﴾ .... the verse: "That is because the Jews said to the Prophet (ﷺ): Tell us what the soul is, and how the soul that is in the body is punished, for the soul is only from God, Mighty and Majestic. Nothing had been revealed to him about it, so he gave them no answer. Then Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to him and said: ﴿Say: The soul is by the command of my Lord, and you have been given of knowledge only a little.﴾ The Prophet (ﷺ) informed them of that. They said to him: Who brought you this? The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: 'Gabriel brought it to me from God.' They said: By God, nothing said it to you but an enemy of ours. So God, blessed is His name, revealed: ﴿Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel, indeed he has brought it down upon your heart﴾ .... the verse.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, who said: I was walking with the Prophet (ﷺ) one day, and we passed by some Jews, who said: O Abu al-Qasim, what is the Rooh? He was silent, so I saw that he was being revealed to. I moved away from him to a rubbish heap, and then ﴿They ask you about the soul﴾ .... the verse was revealed to him. The Jews said: Thus we find it in our own (scripture).

Scholars of interpretation differed concerning the soul mentioned in this place: what is it? Some of them said: It is Gabriel (peace be upon him).

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿They ask you about the soul﴾: He said: It is Gabriel. Qatadah said: Ibn Abbas used to conceal it.

Others said: It is an angel from among the angels.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿They ask you about the soul﴾: He said: The soul is an angel.

⁕ Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Abu Marwan Yazid ibn Samurah, the companion of Caesarea, related to me, from one who narrated to him from Ali ibn Abi Talib, that he said concerning His saying: ﴿They ask you about the soul﴾: He is an angel from among the angels, who has seventy thousand faces, each face has seventy thousand tongues, each tongue has seventy thousand languages, with which he glorifies God, Mighty and Majestic; God creates from every glorification an angel who flies with the angels until the Day of Resurrection.

We have explained the meaning of the soul (rooh) in another place in this book, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated.

As for His saying: ﴿By the command of my Lord﴾, it means: it is from the matter which God, Mighty and Majestic, knows and which you do not know, so you do not know it, and He knows what it is.

As for His saying: ﴿and you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾, the interpreters differed concerning whom He meant by His saying: ﴿and you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾. Some of them said: He meant by it those who asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the soul, and all of mankind other than them. But when the non-addressed was joined to the addressed, the speech came out in the form of address, because the Arabs do so: when a speech contains a third-person referent and an addressee together, they render the speech as address to all.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to me, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, from some of his companions, from Ata' ibn Yasar, who said: "It was revealed in Mecca: ﴿and you have been given of knowledge only a little.﴾ When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) emigrated to Medina, the rabbis of the Jews came to him and said: O Muhammad, has it not reached us that you say: ﴿and you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾? Do you mean us or your people? He said: 'Both; I mean all of you.' They said: You recite that we were given the Torah, in which is the clarification of everything. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: 'It is little in God's knowledge, and He has given you what, if you act upon it, you will benefit.' So God revealed: ﴿And if whatever trees are on the earth were pens....﴾ to His saying: ﴿Indeed God is Hearing, Seeing.﴾"

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿and you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾: He said: O Muhammad, and all mankind.

Others said: Rather, He meant by it only those who asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about the soul, to the exclusion of others.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿and you have been given of knowledge only a little﴾: He means the Jews.

The most correct of these opinions, in our view, is to say: the speech came out as address to those addressed, and what is meant by it is all creation, because the knowledge of every person other than God, however much it may be, is little in God's knowledge.

The meaning of the speech is: and you, O people, have been given of knowledge only a little, out of much of what God knows.

The explanation of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away that which We have revealed to you; then you would not find for yourself against Us any advocate.﴾ (86)

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "If We willed, We would surely take away the knowledge We have given you, the knowledge We have revealed to you from this Qur'an. We would surely take it away, so you would not know it. Then you would not find for yourself, against what We do to you in that regard, any guardian (wakil) who would stand for you and prevent Us from doing that to you, nor any helper who would support you and stand between Us and what We intend for you." He said: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud used to interpret the meaning of Allah's, the Mighty and Majestic, taking it away as its lifting from the breasts of those who recite it.

Mention of the narration to this effect: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash told us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Rafi', from Bundar, from Ma'qil, who said: I said to Abdullah, and he mentioned that the Qur'an would be removed: "How can that be, when we have fixed it in our breasts and our codices?" He said: "It will be removed by night, so no trace of it will remain in any codex or in the breast of any man." Then Abdullah recited: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away that which We have revealed to you﴾.

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Ishaq ibn Yahya told us, from al-Musayyab ibn Rafi', from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: "A red wind will come upon the people from the direction of Syria, and no verse will remain in the codex of any man or in his heart." A man said: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, I have gathered the Qur'an." He said: "Nothing of it will remain in your breast." Then Ibn Mas'ud recited: ﴿And if We willed, We would surely take away that which We have revealed to you﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 87–88:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Except as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed His bounty towards you has been great.﴾ (17:87)

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And if We willed, We could surely take away﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿that which We have revealed to you﴾, but He does not will that, as a mercy from your Lord and a favour from Him upon you. ﴿Indeed His bounty towards you has been great﴾ by His choosing you for His message, His sending down His Book upon you, and all His other countless blessings upon you.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another helpers.﴾ (17:88)

His saying, may His praise be exalted: Say, O Muhammad, to those who said to you, "We can produce the like of this Qur'an": If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce its like, they would never produce its like, even if some of them were helpers and supporters to others. It is mentioned that this verse was sent down to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning a group of Jews who disputed with him about the Qur'an and asked him to bring them a sign other than it that would testify to his prophethood, since such a Qur'an, they claimed, was within their capability to produce.

The narration with this: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah related to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Mahmud ibn Sayhan and Umar ibn Ada [[Ibn Ishaq clarified the names of the Jewish enemies in the Sirah, and I did not find among them anyone named Umar ibn Asan, as mentioned in the original; perhaps it is Nu'man ibn Ada, from Banu Qaynuqa' (see the Sirah, Halabi edition, 2: 161).]] and Bahri ibn Amr, and Aziz ibn Abi Aziz, and Salam ibn Mishkam came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: "Tell us, O Muhammad, about this which you have brought to us: is it truth from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? For we do not see it as coherent as the Torah is coherent." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "By Allah, you know that it is from Allah; you find it written with you. And if mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of it, they would not produce what it is." Then they all said, at that point: Finhas, Abdullah ibn Suriya, Kinana ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Ushay', Ka'b ibn Asad, Samu'al ibn Zayd, and Jabal ibn Amr: "O Muhammad, neither man nor jinn taught you this." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Allah, you know that it is from Allah; you find it written with you in the Torah and the Gospel." They said: "O Muhammad, Allah makes for His messenger, when He sends him, whatever He wills, and empowers him to do what He desires. So send down to us a book that we can read and recognise, or otherwise we will bring you the like of what you bring." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down concerning them and what they said: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another helpers.﴾

⁕ Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, concerning His saying ﴿If mankind and the jinn gathered together﴾ ... to His saying ﴿even if they were to one another helpers﴾, he said: "Supporters." He said: It means: even if the jinn came forth and mankind assisted them, and they backed one another, they would not produce the like of this Qur'an. As for His saying, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿they would not produce its like﴾, it is in the nominative case and is the answer to the "in" (la'in) clause, because when the Arabs answer la'in with negation, they put the following verb in the nominative; la'in is like an oath, and the answer to an oath with a negation is in the nominative. It may also be in the jussive, since the particle by which it is answered has a lam added to it, as al-A'sha said:

la'in muniyta bina 'an ghibbi ma'raka ... la tulfuna 'an dima'i l-qawmi nantafil [[This verse is by al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays (his Diwan, Cairo edition with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, p. 63), from his qasidah beginning "Wada' Hurayra", which has 66 verses; the verse of evidence is the 63rd, which he said to Yazid ibn Mashar, Abu Thabit al-Shaybani. He says: We do not tire of fighting, and if it were decreed that you be tested by us in the aftermath of a battle we have fought, you would find in us strength for worthy combat, and you would not find us turning away from wading in blood a second time. The point of evidence in it is that Allah's saying (they would not produce its like) is the answer to the preceding oath in His saying (if they gathered together), and the verb of the answer is not emphasised with the nun, because it is preceded by the negation "la". Similarly in al-A'sha's line "la tulfuna", which is not emphasised with the nun although it is the answer to the oath "la'in muniyta", and emphasis was barred because of the presence of negation in the answer.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 87–88:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Except as a mercy from your Lord. Indeed His bounty towards you has been great.﴾ (17:87)

He, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿And if We willed, We could surely take away﴾ O Muhammad, ﴿that which We have revealed to you﴾, but He does not will that, as a mercy from your Lord and a favour from Him upon you. ﴿Indeed His bounty towards you has been great﴾ by His choosing you for His message, His sending down His Book upon you, and all His other countless blessings upon you.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another helpers.﴾ (17:88)

His saying, may His praise be exalted: Say, O Muhammad, to those who said to you, "We can produce the like of this Qur'an": If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce its like, they would never produce its like, even if some of them were helpers and supporters to others. It is mentioned that this verse was sent down to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning a group of Jews who disputed with him about the Qur'an and asked him to bring them a sign other than it that would testify to his prophethood, since such a Qur'an, they claimed, was within their capability to produce.

The narration with this: Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah related to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Mahmud ibn Sayhan and Umar ibn Ada [[Ibn Ishaq clarified the names of the Jewish enemies in the Sirah, and I did not find among them anyone named Umar ibn Asan, as mentioned in the original; perhaps it is Nu'man ibn Ada, from Banu Qaynuqa' (see the Sirah, Halabi edition, 2: 161).]] and Bahri ibn Amr, and Aziz ibn Abi Aziz, and Salam ibn Mishkam came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: "Tell us, O Muhammad, about this which you have brought to us: is it truth from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? For we do not see it as coherent as the Torah is coherent." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to them: "By Allah, you know that it is from Allah; you find it written with you. And if mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of it, they would not produce what it is." Then they all said, at that point: Finhas, Abdullah ibn Suriya, Kinana ibn Abi al-Huqayq, Ushay', Ka'b ibn Asad, Samu'al ibn Zayd, and Jabal ibn Amr: "O Muhammad, neither man nor jinn taught you this." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Allah, you know that it is from Allah; you find it written with you in the Torah and the Gospel." They said: "O Muhammad, Allah makes for His messenger, when He sends him, whatever He wills, and empowers him to do what He desires. So send down to us a book that we can read and recognise, or otherwise we will bring you the like of what you bring." Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sent down concerning them and what they said: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like, even if they were to one another helpers.﴾

⁕ Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, concerning His saying ﴿If mankind and the jinn gathered together﴾ ... to His saying ﴿even if they were to one another helpers﴾, he said: "Supporters." He said: It means: even if the jinn came forth and mankind assisted them, and they backed one another, they would not produce the like of this Qur'an. As for His saying, the Mighty and Majestic, ﴿they would not produce its like﴾, it is in the nominative case and is the answer to the "in" (la'in) clause, because when the Arabs answer la'in with negation, they put the following verb in the nominative; la'in is like an oath, and the answer to an oath with a negation is in the nominative. It may also be in the jussive, since the particle by which it is answered has a lam added to it, as al-A'sha said:

la'in muniyta bina 'an ghibbi ma'raka ... la tulfuna 'an dima'i l-qawmi nantafil [[This verse is by al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays (his Diwan, Cairo edition with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, p. 63), from his qasidah beginning "Wada' Hurayra", which has 66 verses; the verse of evidence is the 63rd, which he said to Yazid ibn Mashar, Abu Thabit al-Shaybani. He says: We do not tire of fighting, and if it were decreed that you be tested by us in the aftermath of a battle we have fought, you would find in us strength for worthy combat, and you would not find us turning away from wading in blood a second time. The point of evidence in it is that Allah's saying (they would not produce its like) is the answer to the preceding oath in His saying (if they gathered together), and the verb of the answer is not emphasised with the nun, because it is preceded by the negation "la". Similarly in al-A'sha's line "la tulfuna", which is not emphasised with the nun although it is the answer to the oath "la'in muniyta", and emphasis was barred because of the presence of negation in the answer.]]

**Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And We have certainly explained to the people in this Qur'an every kind of example, but most of the people refuse except disbelief﴾ (89)**

He says, may He be remembered: And We have certainly made clear to the people in this Qur'an every kind of example, as proof against them all, as a reminder to them, and as an alert to the truth so that they would follow it and act upon it. ﴿But most of the people refuse except disbelief﴾: he says, most of the people refused except to deny the truth and to reject the proofs and evidences of Allah.

* *

**Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush for us from the earth"﴾ (90)**

He, may He be remembered, says: And the polytheists among your people said to you, O Muhammad: "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush for us from this land of ours, a spring that flows for us with water."

* *

As for His words ﴿yanbū'an﴾ (a spring):

It is a pattern (yaf'ūl) derived from the speaker's saying "nabaʿa al-māʾ" (the water sprang up), when it appears and bubbles forth; it is said yanbaʿu and yanbaʾu, and yanbūʿ is that which springs forth.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿until you cause to gush for us from the earth a spring﴾: i.e., until you cause springs to gush for us from the earth, namely in this land of ours.

* Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿until you cause to gush for us from the earth a spring﴾, he said: springs.

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, the like of it.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿yanbū'an﴾, he said: springs.

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

The readers (qurra', the transmitters of the Qur'anic recitations) differed regarding the reading of His words ﴿tafjura﴾ (cause to gush). It is related from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that he read ﴿until you cause (tafjura) to gush for us﴾ with a light (unstressed) pronunciation, and His words ﴿so they cause (fatufajjiru) the rivers to gush forth through it, in abundance﴾ with a stressed (doubled) pronunciation. This was also how the readers of Kufa used to recite them. It seems that by their light pronunciation of the first, they understood the meaning: until you cause water to gush for us from the earth once. And by their stressed pronunciation of the second, they understood that it gushes in various places, one time after another, since that gushing is of rivers, not of a single river. [[There is an apparent omission in the text. The conclusion is that they agreed on the stressed pronunciation of fatufajjiru and differed regarding hatta tafjura; some stressed it and some lightened it, and the author chose the stressed pronunciation for the reason he mentioned.]] The light pronunciation in the first and the stressed pronunciation in the second, as I have mentioned from the reading of the Kufans, is more pleasing to me, because of the difference between their two meanings, although the soundness of the first reading is not rejected.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 91:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Or you have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, and you cause rivers to gush forth within them abundantly﴾ (91)

He, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): The polytheists of your people said to you, O Muhammad: "We will not believe you until you draw forth for us a spring from our land, gushing with water or bubbling forth, or until you have a garden, which is the jannah (garden), of palm trees and grapevines, and you cause rivers to gush forth within it abundantly, in this land of ours where we are." Meaning: within the palm trees and vineyards. And His saying ﴿abundantly gushing forth within them﴾ means: between them, at their roots, gushing forth by means of their channels.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 92:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Or You cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed, or You bring God and the angels before us, face to face.﴾ (17:92)

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying ﴿kisafan﴾. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it with a silent sīn, with the meaning: "Or You cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces (kisafan), as you claimed." This is because al-kisf in the speech of the Arabs is the plural of kisfah (a piece), and it is the plural for a number of the genus, just as sidrah is pluralized as sidr and tamrah as tamr. It is related from the Arabs by hearing: "Give me a kisfah of this cloth," meaning a piece of it. It is said of this: "He brought us thareed kisf," meaning pieces of bread. If it is read thus, "kisfan" with a silent sīn, it may also be intended as a verbal noun from kasafa [[The verbal noun of the verb kasafa, yaksifu (like ḍaraba, yaḍribu), is al-kasf, with a fatḥah on the kāf and a silent sīn (al-Lisan).]]. As for kisaf with a fatḥah on the sīn, it is the plural of what lies between three and ten: one is called kisfah, three are called kisaf, and so up to ten. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Kufans read ﴿kisafan﴾ with a fatḥah on the sīn, meaning the plurals of a single kisfah from three to ten, i.e., pieces (qiṭaʿan): from three to ten.

The more correct of the two readings in my view is the reading of the one who reads it with a silent sīn, because those who asked the Messenger of God ﷺ for this did not intend in their request that it be a known, defined quantity of pieces; they only asked that pieces (qiṭaʿan) be dropped upon them from the sky. The interpretation has also come down in this sense from the people of interpretation.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿kisfan﴾: "The sky, entirely."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Ibn Jurayj said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Kathir said, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿as you claimed against us kisafan﴾: "Once." And the one in Surat al-Rum, ﴿and makes it kisafan﴾: "pieces." Ibn Jurayj said: "Kisafan" (as in) the saying of God: ﴿If We will, We shall cause the earth to swallow them, or drop upon them kisafan from the sky﴾ (34:9).

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Or You cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed﴾: "That is, pieces (qiṭaʿan)."

ʿAli narrated to us, he said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿kisafan﴾: he says, "pieces (qiṭaʿan)."

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿kisafan﴾: "pieces (qiṭaʿan)."

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿Or You cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed﴾: meaning "pieces" (qiṭaʿan).

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Or You bring God and the angels before us, face to face (qabilan).﴾

He, may He be remembered, says, reporting the saying of the polytheists to the Prophet of God ﷺ: "Or You bring God, O Muhammad, and the angels, qabilan."

The people of interpretation differed over the meaning of qabil in this place. Some said: its meaning is: until God and the angels come to every tribe of us, tribe by tribe, and they see them.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, he said: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, he said: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqaʾ narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and the angels, qabilan﴾: "On our side, every tribe."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Or You bring God and the angels, qabilan﴾: "Tribes, each tribe on its own."

Others said: the meaning of that is: "Or You bring God and the angels in plain sight; we confront them face to face and see them directly."

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Or You bring God and the angels, qabilan﴾: "We see them directly."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿Or You bring God and the angels, qabilan﴾: "So we see them."

Some of the grammarians of Arabic took it to mean the guarantor, from their saying: "He is the qabil of so-and-so regarding what is due to so-and-so from him," meaning his surety (zaʿim).

The most likely of the sayings to be correct is the saying of Qatadah, that it means "face to face (muʿayanah)," from their saying: "I faced so-and-so face to face (qabiltu fulanan muqabalah)," and "So-and-so is the qabil of so-and-so," meaning in front of him, as the poet said:

We would make peace with you until you return with the like of it,
Like the cry of a pregnant woman whom her qabil has helped (yassarat-hā qabīluhā).

[The verse is by al-Aʿsha Maymun ibn Qays (his Diwan, Cairo edition with the commentary of Dr. Muhammad Husayn, p. 177), from an ode of eighteen verses. The witness is the 17th verse. Before it: "By the Lord of the prostrators at evening, and by the bells of the Christians being struck by their monks..." In one version of the witness, "uṣāliḥukum" is with a hamzah instead of nūn. He says: I will not make peace with you until you return with the like of your offence and transgression, and cry out the cry of a pregnant woman when the midwife helps her in labour. "Qabūluhā" appears in place of "qabīluhā." Al-abīl is the monk. Tabūʾū: return. Yassarat-hā: made her delivery easy and assisted her in it. Al-qabūl: the woman who receives the child at birth.

In Majaz al-Quran of Abu ʿUbayda (1:390), at His saying (wal-malāʾikati qabīlan), its majaz is muqābalah, i.e., muʿāyanah (direct sight). He said: "We would make peace with you until you return with the like of it... like the cry of a pregnant woman whom her qabīl has helped," meaning: she faced her. When they describe with the pattern faʿīl derived from their saying "qābalat" and similar, they make the word for the description of the dual, plural, masculine and feminine, one form, as in your saying: "She is my qabīl, they two are my qabīl, and so they (f.) are my qabīl." End of quotation. In Lisan al-ʿArab (qabal): "al-qabīl and al-qabūl: the midwife. Al-Muhkam: the midwife received the child (qabalat al-qābilah al-walada qibālan): she took it from the mother; she is the woman's qābilah, qabūlahā and qabīlahā." Al-Aʿsha said: "We would make peace with you until you return with the like of it... like the cry of a pregnant woman whom her qabīl has delivered." It is also narrated as "qabalūhā," meaning they despaired of her.]

meaning: her midwife (qābilatuhā). Some scholars of Arabic speech from Basra used to say: when they describe with the pattern faʿīl derived from their saying "qābalta" and similar, they make the word for the description of the dual, plural, and masculine and feminine one form, as in their saying: "This is my qabīl, they two are my qabīl, they (m.) are my qabīl, and they (f.) are my qabīl."

**Commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Or you have a house of gold (zukhruf), or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book that we can read. Say: "Glory be to my Lord! Am I anything but a human messenger?"﴾ (17:93)**

Allah, may He be remembered, says, reporting about the polytheists whose affair He mentioned in these verses: "Or you have, O Muhammad, a house of gold, which is *zukhruf*."

As follows:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿or you have a house of zukhruf﴾: he said, "A house of gold."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿of zukhruf﴾, he said: "Of gold."

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿or you have a house of zukhruf﴾: "The zukhruf here is gold."

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿or you have a house of zukhruf﴾, he said: "Of gold."

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from a man, from al-Hakam, who said: Mujahid said: "We did not know what zukhruf was until we saw it in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: 'Or you have a house of gold (dhahab).'"

⁕ Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, who said: "I did not know what zukhruf was until we heard it in the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: 'a house of gold.'"

* *

And His words ﴿or you ascend into the sky﴾

That is: "or you climb up a ladder into the sky." It is said "in the sky," though one ascends *to* it and not *in* it, because the people said: "or you ascend a ladder to the sky," so the preposition *fi* (in) was introduced into the sentence to indicate the meaning of the speech. It is said: "I ascended (raqiytu) in the ladder (fi al-sullam), so I ascend (arqa) ascent (ruqiyan), ascent (riqiyan), ascent (ruqiyan)," as the poet said:

You are the one who burdened me with climbing the stairs
Despite exhaustion, gray hair, and lameness.[[The verse is cited in Lisan al-Arab (root r-q-y): "wa-raqiytu fi al-sullam raqiyan..." and Ibn Barri recited it without attributing it to its speaker.]]

* *

And His words ﴿and we will not believe in your ascension﴾

That is: "and we will not believe you because of your ascent to the sky," ﴿until you bring down to us a book﴾ written, ﴿that we can read﴾ in which is our command to follow you and to believe in you.

As follows:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying, and Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿a book that we can read﴾, he said: "From the Lord of the worlds to so-and-so. Every man has a scroll that is placed by his head, which he reads."

⁕ al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "a book that we can read from the Lord of the worlds," and he also said: "it is placed by his head, and he reads it."

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿until you bring down to us a book that we can read﴾: that is, "a special book in which we are commanded to follow you."

* *

And His words ﴿Say: "Glory be to my Lord!"﴾

Allah, may He be remembered, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists of your people, who say these things to you, exalting Allah above what they attribute to Him, and magnifying Him from that He should be accompanied by His angels, or that I should have any means to what you ask of me: ﴿Am I anything but a human messenger?﴾" That is: "Am I anything but a servant of His servants, from the children of Adam? How could I be able to do what you ask of me in these matters? Only my Creator and your Creator is able to do them. I am only a messenger who conveys to you what I have been sent with. What you ask me to do is in the hand of Allah, whose servant I am and you are, and no one other than Him is able to do that."

This speech, which Allah informed us that He addressed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was, as it is reported, from a group of Quraysh who gathered to debate and argue with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so they spoke to him with what Allah reported about them in these verses.

*Mention of the names of those who debated the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) among them, and the reason for which they debated him* [[See this report in Ibn Hisham's Sira (al-Halabi edition, 1:315), with slight variation in some wording, and in al-Qurtubi's tafsir (10:328–330).]]

Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: A shaykh from the people of Egypt related to me, who had arrived some forty-odd years earlier, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, that Utba and Shayba, the two sons of Rabi'a, and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and a man from Banu Abd al-Dar, and Abu al-Bakhtari, brother of Banu Asad, and al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, and Zam'a ibn al-Aswad, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya, and Umayya ibn Khalaf, and al-As ibn Wa'il, and Nubayh and Munabbih, the two sons of al-Hajjaj al-Sahmiyyun, gathered, or some of them gathered, after sunset near the back of the Ka'ba. Some of them said to others: "Send to Muhammad, speak with him and dispute with him until you have an excuse regarding him." So they sent to him: "The nobles of your people have gathered to you so that they may speak with you." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to them quickly, thinking that some change of mind had come upon them regarding his affair, and he was eager for them, loving their guidance, and it grieved him that they should suffer harm. He sat down with them, and they said: "O Muhammad, we have sent for you so that we may have an excuse concerning you. By Allah, we know of no man among the Arabs who has brought upon his people what you have brought upon yours. You have insulted the forefathers, denounced the religion, declared foolish the wise, cursed the gods, and split the community. Nothing ugly has been left undone that you have not come with between us and you. If you have come with this message seeking wealth, we will gather for you some of our wealth so that you may be the richest of us; if you seek honor among us, we will make you our lord; if you want kingship, we will make you king over us; and if what comes to you is a *rī* (jinn companion) that has overpowered you, for they called the companion from the jinn *al-ri*, then perhaps that is so, and we will spend our wealth in seeking medicine for you until we cure you of it, or until we have an excuse concerning you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What is wrong with me is not what you say. I have not come to you with what I have come with seeking your wealth, nor honor among you, nor kingship over you. But Allah has sent me to you as a messenger, and has revealed to me a book, and has commanded me to be a bringer of good tidings and a warner to you. I have conveyed to you the message of my Lord, and I have given you sincere counsel. So if you accept from me what I have brought you, it is your share in this world and the Hereafter; and if you reject it from me, I shall be patient with the command of Allah until Allah judges between me and you," or as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said. They said: "O Muhammad, if you are not going to accept what we have offered you, you know that no one among people has narrower lands, less wealth, or harder living than we do. So ask your Lord who sent you with what He sent you with to remove these mountains from us that have constricted us, to spread out our lands for us, and to make rivers gush forth in them for us [[In some copies of the Sira and in al-Qurtubi: "and to split (yakhriq)."]] like the rivers of Syria and Iraq. Let Him also raise up for us those of our forefathers who have passed away, and let Qusayy ibn Kilab be among those He raises for us, for he was an honest old man, and we will ask them about what you say: is it true or false? If you do what we ask, and they confirm you, we will confirm you, and we will know your standing with Allah, and that He sent you with the truth as a messenger, as you say." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I was not sent with this. I have only come to you from Allah with what He sent me with. I have conveyed to you what I was sent with to you. If you accept it, it is your share in this world and the Hereafter; and if you reject it from me, I shall be patient with the command of Allah until Allah judges between me and you." They said: "If you will not do this for us, then ask for yourself. Ask your Lord to send an angel who will confirm what you say and answer us on your behalf, and ask Him to make for you gardens, treasures, and palaces of gold and silver, and to enrich you with them so that you do not need what we see you seeking. For you walk in the markets and seek livelihood as we do, so that we may know the excellence of your standing with your Lord, if you are a messenger as you claim." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: "I will not do it. I am not one who asks his Lord for this, and I was not sent to you with this. But Allah has sent me as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. So if you accept what I have brought you, it is your share in this world and the Hereafter; and if you reject it from me, I shall be patient with the command of Allah until Allah judges between me and you." They said: "Then make the sky fall upon us in pieces, as you claimed your Lord would do if He wished, for we will not believe you unless you do it." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "That is up to Allah. If He wills, He will do that to you." They said: "O Muhammad, does your Lord not know that we will sit with you and ask you what we asked you, and demand from you what we demanded, so that He may come to you and teach you what you should answer us with, and inform you what He will do with us since we did not accept from you what you brought us? We have heard that it is only a man in al-Yamama called al-Rahman who teaches you this. By Allah, we will never believe in al-Rahman! O Muhammad, we have given you an excuse. By Allah, we will not leave you and what you have achieved against us until we destroy you or you destroy us." One of them said: "We worship the angels, and they are the daughters of Allah." Another said: "We will not believe you until you bring Allah and the angels before us as a group." When they said this, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up from them, and Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya ibn al-Mughira ibn Abdullah ibn Amr ibn Makhzum got up with him—he was the son of his paternal aunt, Atika bint Abd al-Muttalib—and said to him: "O Muhammad, your people offered you what they offered, and you did not accept it from them. Then they asked you for things for themselves, so that they might know your standing with Allah, and you did not do that. Then they asked you to hasten the punishment with which you threatened them. By Allah, I will never believe in you until you take a ladder to the sky and ascend upon it while I look on, until you reach it and bring with you a written scroll with four angels accompanying you who testify that you are as you say. By Allah, even if you did that, I would think I should not believe you." Then he turned away from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned to his family, grieved and sorrowful over what he had missed of what he had hoped for from his people when they called him, and because of their estrangement from him. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) left them, Abu Jahl said: "O assembly of Quraysh, Muhammad has refused anything but what you see: he reviles our religion, insults our forefathers, makes our wisdom foolish, and curses our gods. I swear by Allah that tomorrow I will sit for him with a rock as heavy as I can lift, and when he prostrates in his prayer I will smash his head with it."

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, related to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrima, client of Ibn Abbas, from Ibn Abbas, similarly, except that he said: "and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, the sons of Banu Abd al-Dar, and Abu al-Bakhtari ibn Hisham."

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id, who said: I asked him about Allah's words ﴿We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth﴾ [17:90], and he said: "It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya." He said: "They claim so."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 94–96:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And nothing prevented the people from believing when guidance came to them, except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ (94)

His saying, exalted is He, means: Nothing prevented the polytheists of your people, O Muhammad, from believing in Allah and in what you brought them of the truth, ﴿when guidance came to them﴾, that is, when clear proof came to them from Allah of the reality of what you call them to and the truth of what you brought them, except their saying out of ignorance, ﴿"Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾. The first (the particle of interrogation with the verb) is in a position of accusative (naṣb) by the governing of the verb "prevented" upon it, and the second (the word "a human") is in a position of nominative (rafʿ), because the verb belongs to it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Say, "If there had been upon the earth angels walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."﴾ (95)

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to those who refused to believe in you and to affirm what I have sent you with, denouncing the idea that Allah should send a messenger from among humans: If there were, O people, angels upon the earth walking securely, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger, because angels are only seen by their own kind, and by those among the children of Adam whom Allah has singled out to see them. As for others, they are not able to see them. So how would angels be sent to them as messengers, when they cannot see them in the forms in which Allah created them? Rather, a messenger is sent to humans from among them, just as, if there were angels upon the earth walking securely, then We sent to them a messenger whom We had sent from among them, an angel like them.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Say, "Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you. Indeed, He is ever, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing."﴾ (96)

His saying, exalted is He, to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say to you, ﴿"Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾, ﴿"Sufficient is Allah as Witness between me and you"﴾, for He is the best sufficer and judge. ﴿"Indeed, He is ever, of His servants, Acquainted"﴾, meaning: indeed Allah has knowledge and awareness of His servants' affairs and deeds, both the righteous among them and the falsifiers, the guided and the astray. ﴿"Seeing"﴾ of their management, their governance, and His disposing of them as He wills, however He wills and loves. Nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him, and He will recompense all of them for what they have put forward when they come before Him.
