Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 97:

The interpretation of the words of God, exalted is He: ﴿Whomever God guides, he is the one guided; and whomever He leaves astray, you will not find for them protectors besides Him. And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf. Their refuge is Hell; whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze.﴾ (97)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Whomever God guides, O Muhammad, to faith in Him and to affirming you and what you have brought from your Lord, He grants them success in that. So he is the one who is guided, the rightly guided, who hits the truth, not the one whom anyone else guides, for guidance is in His hand. ﴿And whomever He leaves astray﴾ means: whomever God leads astray from the truth, forsaking him from attaining it, and does not grant him success in faith in God and in affirming His Messenger. So you will not find for them, O Muhammad, any protectors who will help them besides God, when God wills to punish them and to rescue them from Him.

﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces﴾ means: We will assemble them at the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, after their dispersal in the graves at the establishment of the Hour. ﴿Upon their faces, blind, and mute﴾ — it is the plural of abkam (mute), and by "mute" is meant: those who are dumb.

As:

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq told us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿and mute﴾, he said: the dumb. ﴿And deaf﴾, which is the plural of aṣamm.

If someone says: How does God describe these people as being gathered blind, mute, and deaf, when He has said ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are about to fall into it﴾, thereby informing that they see, and said ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they hear its raging and roaring. And when they are thrown into a narrow place therein, bound together, they will call out there for destruction﴾, thereby informing that they hear and speak?

It is said: It is permissible that what God described them with—blindness, muteness, and deafness—is their state at the time of their gathering to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, and then He will give them hearing, sight, and speech in other states besides the state of gathering. It may also be as was related from Ibn ʿAbbas in the report which ʿAli ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Muʿawiyah related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection upon their faces, blind, mute, and deaf﴾, then He said ﴿And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain﴾, and He said ﴿they hear its raging and roaring﴾, and He said ﴿they will call out there for destruction﴾. As for His words ﴿blind﴾, they will not see anything that would please them.

* *

And His words ﴿mute﴾: they will not speak with any proof. His words ﴿deaf﴾: they will not hear anything that would please them. His words ﴿Their refuge is Hell﴾ — May His praise be exalted — mean: their destination is Hell, and in it are their dwellings, and they are its fuel.

As:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿Their refuge is Hell﴾: meaning, they are its fuel.

* *

And His words ﴿Whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze﴾

By His words "subsides" is meant: it becomes soft and calms, as ʿAdi ibn Zayd al-ʿAbbadi said describing a cloud:

In its middle, like fireflies or lamps of the high castle... at times it dims and at times it shines [[This is a verse by ʿAdi ibn Zayd al-ʿAbbadi (Poets of Christianity, p. 455), from what he wrote to al-Nuʿman, and it is among the gems of his odes. Al-yarāʿ is a moth which, when it flies at night, anyone who knows it does not doubt that it is a flying spark from a fire. Al-Jahiz said: the fire of al-yarāʿa is said to be the fire of ḥabāḥib, and it resembles lightning. He said: al-yarāʿa is a small bird which, if it flies at night, looks like a falling meteor or a flying lamp. Al-majdal, with a kasra on the mim: the raised palace, for the soundness of its construction, and its plural is majādil. "Khabat" — the fire, the war, and the heat "yakhbū" — "khabwan" (on the pattern fa'ala) and "khubuwwan" (on the pattern fu'ul): subsided and was extinguished, and its flame died down. And His words, exalted is He: (whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze): it is said its meaning is: its flame calmed; and it is said its meaning is: whenever they wish that it would subside, and they desire that it subside. (See Lisan al-ʿArab: y-r-ʿ, j-d-l, kh-b-a.)]]

He means by His words "the lamp subsides": it becomes soft and weakens at times, and grows strong and shines at other times. From this is the saying of al-Qatami: "Then it subsides for a while and then blows, flaring up." [[This is the second half of a verse by al-Qatami, whose first half is: * And we were like a conflagration that struck a thicket *

(See his Diwan, Leiden edition of 1902, p. 39.) He said: yakhbū: it calms down. Yahubb: it is agitated. Sāʿ: the plural of sāʿa. In (Lisan: s-r-ʿ), the sāʿa is a portion of the night and the day, and its plural is sāʿāt and sāʿ. Al-Qatami said: * And we were like a conflagration for one who fights face to face * ... the verse. Ibn Burri said: the well-known version of the first half of this verse is: * kunnā ka-l-ḥarīq aṣāba ghāban *

In Abu ʿUbaydah's Majaz al-Qur'an (1:391), "whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze": meaning, a kindling. "Khabat" means "calmed." He recited the second half of the verse, then said: he did not mention here "their skins," so that subsiding would apply to them.]]

Those who interpreted the Qur'an said things similar to what we have said on this matter, though they differed in how they expressed its interpretation.

Those who said so:

⁕ ʿAli ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah told us, saying: Muʿawiyah related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿whenever it subsides﴾, he said: it calmed.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, ﴿whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze﴾, meaning: whenever it has burned them, the fire is kindled anew with them as fuel; when it has burned them and left nothing of them, it becomes glowing embers, and that is its subsiding; then when they are replaced with a new creation, it returns to them.

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqaʾ told us, all from Mujahid: Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said, ﴿whenever it subsides﴾, he said: its subsiding is that it is kindled anew with them as fuel; when it has burned them and nothing of them remains, it becomes glowing embers, and when they are replaced with a new creation, it returns to them.

⁕ Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze﴾, he said: whenever their skins are burned, they are replaced with other skins, so that they may taste the punishment.

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿whenever it subsides, We increase for them the blaze﴾, he said: whenever something of it softens.

⁕ I was told from Marwan, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, ﴿whenever it subsides﴾, he said: it calmed.

* *

And His words ﴿We increase for them the blaze﴾

He says: We increase these disbelievers in blaze, and that is the kindling of the fire upon them and its blazing among them and its flaring up after its subsiding, within their bodies.

**Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿That is their recompense, because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, "When we have become bones and crumbled particles, will we truly be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾ (98)**

Exalted is He, says: This is what We have described of Our doing on the Day of Resurrection to these polytheists, what We mentioned that We would do to them by gathering them upon their faces, blind, mute and deaf, and by burning them in the Fire, according to the condition We have explained of them there. It is their recompense for their disbelief in the Dunya in Our signs, meaning Our proofs and arguments, and they are His messengers who called them to worship Him and to single Him out as God, to the exclusion of idols and images, and for their saying, when they were commanded to believe in the promise and in Allah's reward and punishment in the Hereafter, ﴿When we have become bones﴾ decayed, ﴿and crumbled particles﴾ we have become dust, ﴿will we truly be resurrected in a new creation?﴾ They say: will we be raised after that as a new creation, just as He began us the first time in the world, in denial of that and in amazement and astonishment that such a thing should be.

* *

**Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them? And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt. But the wrongdoers refuse except disbelief.﴾ (99)**

Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do these polytheists who say ﴿When we have become bones and crumbled particles, will we truly be resurrected in a new creation?﴾ not look with the eyes of their hearts, so that they would know that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, originating them from nothing and establishing them by His power, is able by that power to create their likenesses, and likenesses of them of creation after their annihilation and before that, and that whoever is able to do that, it is not impossible for Him to restore them as a new creation after they have become bones and crumbled particles. His words ﴿And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt﴾ mean: Allah, exalted is He, has appointed for these polytheists a term for their destruction and a time for their punishment about which there is no doubt, that is to say, there is no doubt that that term will come upon them. ﴿But the wrongdoers refuse except disbelief﴾ means: the disbelievers refuse except to deny the reality of His threat which He threatened them with, and to call it a lie.

**Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿That is their recompense, because they disbelieved in Our signs and said, "When we have become bones and crumbled particles, will we truly be resurrected in a new creation?"﴾ (98)**

Exalted is He, says: This is what We have described of Our doing on the Day of Resurrection to these polytheists, what We mentioned that We would do to them by gathering them upon their faces, blind, mute and deaf, and by burning them in the Fire, according to the condition We have explained of them there. It is their recompense for their disbelief in the Dunya in Our signs, meaning Our proofs and arguments, and they are His messengers who called them to worship Him and to single Him out as God, to the exclusion of idols and images, and for their saying, when they were commanded to believe in the promise and in Allah's reward and punishment in the Hereafter, ﴿When we have become bones﴾ decayed, ﴿and crumbled particles﴾ we have become dust, ﴿will we truly be resurrected in a new creation?﴾ They say: will we be raised after that as a new creation, just as He began us the first time in the world, in denial of that and in amazement and astonishment that such a thing should be.

* *

**Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, is able to create the likes of them? And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt. But the wrongdoers refuse except disbelief.﴾ (99)**

Exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do these polytheists who say ﴿When we have become bones and crumbled particles, will we truly be resurrected in a new creation?﴾ not look with the eyes of their hearts, so that they would know that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth, originating them from nothing and establishing them by His power, is able by that power to create their likenesses, and likenesses of them of creation after their annihilation and before that, and that whoever is able to do that, it is not impossible for Him to restore them as a new creation after they have become bones and crumbled particles. His words ﴿And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt﴾ mean: Allah, exalted is He, has appointed for these polytheists a term for their destruction and a time for their punishment about which there is no doubt, that is to say, there is no doubt that that term will come upon them. ﴿But the wrongdoers refuse except disbelief﴾ means: the disbelievers refuse except to deny the reality of His threat which He threatened them with, and to call it a lie.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 100:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "If you possessed the treasures of the mercy of my Lord, then you would withhold them for fear of spending; and man is ever stingy."﴾

He, exalted is He, says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: "If you, O people, possessed the treasuries of the possessions of my Lord, of wealth," and by "mercy" in this place He means wealth. ﴿Then you would withhold them for fear of spending﴾ means: then you would be stingy with it, and would not be generous with it toward others, out of fear of spending and of poverty.

As related:

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said regarding ﴿then you would withhold them for fear of spending﴾: "Poverty."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿for fear of spending﴾: that is, for fear of destitution (faqah).

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, the same.

* * *

As for His saying ﴿and man is ever stingy﴾:

He says: and man has always been stingy and tight-fisted.

As related:

* ʿAli narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya told me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿and man is ever stingy﴾: he says: "Stingy."

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas said, regarding His saying ﴿and man is ever stingy﴾: "Stingy."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿and man is ever stingy﴾: he said: "Stingy and tight-fisted."

Regarding the word qatur (stingy) in the speech of the Arabs there are four forms. It is said: qatara fulan yaqtur and yaqtir, qattara yuqattir, and aqtara yuqtir, as Abu Dawud said:

"I do not count straitened circumstances as ruin, but the loss of the one whom I have lost is the ruin."

[[The verse is by Abu Dawud (spelled with unhamzated waw after the dal, as in al-Taj), whose name is Jariya ibn al-Hajjaj, or it is Hanzala ibn al-Shartha al-Iyadi. The verse appears in (al-Shi'r wa'l-Shu'ara' by Ibn Qutayba, Leiden edition 1902, p. 122). In al-Lisan: qatara yaqtur and yaqtir qatran and qutura, so he is qatir and qatur; and aqtara, i.e. became poor. And qatara ʿala ʿiyalihi, aqtara and qattara: he restricted them in spending. It is said: "He is indeed qatur," i.e. muqtir. Thus it is concluded that the forms in this are four: qatara yaqtur and yaqtir (from the patterns naṣara and ḍaraba), qattara (with shadda), and aqtara (with hamza), as the author said.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 101:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs. So ask the Children of Israel, when he came to them, and Pharaoh said to him, "Indeed, I think you, O Moses, are bewitched."﴾

Says God, mentioning Himself: And We certainly gave Moses, son of Imran, nine clear signs, which make clear to whoever sees them that they are proofs for Moses, testifying to his truthfulness and the reality of his prophethood.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have differed concerning them and what they are.

Some of them said concerning that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs﴾: "The nine clear signs: his hand, his staff, his tongue, the sea, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood, as distinct signs."

I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs﴾: the throwing of the staff twice before Pharaoh, the drawing out of his hand, the knot that was in his tongue, and five signs in al-A'raf: the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood.

Others said something similar to this, except that they made two of them: one is the effacement (al-tamsah), and the other is the stone (al-hajar).

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Burayda ibn Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz asked me about His saying ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs﴾. I said to him: They are the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the sea, his staff, the effacement, and the stone. He said: "And what is the effacement?" I said: Moses supplicated and Aaron said "Amen," and [God] said: "Your supplication has been answered." 'Umar said: "How could understanding (al-fiqh) be other than this?" Then 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz called for a bag that had belonged to 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Marwan, which had been struck in Egypt, and in it were a walnut, an egg, and a lentil, unrecognizable, having been turned into stones, which were from the wealth of Pharaoh that had been struck in Egypt.

Others said something similar to that, except that they made two of them: one is the years (al-sinin), and the other is the loss of fruits.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from 'Ikrimah and Mutar al-Warraq, regarding His saying ﴿nine signs﴾, they both said: the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the staff, the hand, the years, and the loss of fruits.

Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, regarding His saying ﴿nine clear signs﴾, he said: the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the years, the loss of fruits, his staff, and his hand.

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah was asked about His saying ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs﴾, what are they? He said: the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the staff of Moses, and his hand.

He said: Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said the same as 'Ata', and added ﴿We seized the people of Pharaoh with years and loss of fruits﴾. He said: These two are the ninth ones, and they say: the ninth ones are the years and the removal of the impediment from Moses' tongue.

al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿nine clear signs﴾, and they are consecutive, and in surah al-A'raf: ﴿And We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years and loss of fruits﴾. He said: The years were for the people of the desert, and the loss of fruits for the people of the towns; so these are two signs. And the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood: these are five. And the hand of Moses when he brought it out white for the onlookers without harm: the leprosy; and his staff when he threw it, and it became a manifest serpent.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs﴾, he said: the hand of Moses, his staff, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the years, and the loss of fruits.

Others said something similar to that, except that they made the years and the loss of fruits one sign, and made the ninth: the staff swallowing what they fabricate.

Mention of those who said that:

al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: al-Hasan said, regarding His saying ﴿nine clear signs﴾, and ﴿We certainly seized the people of Pharaoh with years and loss of fruits﴾: this is one sign; and the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the hand of Moses, and his staff when he threw it and it became a manifest serpent, and when he threw it and it swallowed what they fabricate.

Others said regarding that:

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Salamah narrate from Safwan ibn 'Assal, who said: A Jew said to his companion: "Come, let us go to the Prophet so that we may ask him about this verse ﴿And We certainly gave Moses nine clear signs﴾." His companion said: "Do not call him a prophet, for if he hears you, he will have four eyes." He said: So they asked, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Do not associate anything with God, do not steal, do not commit adultery, do not kill the soul which God has forbidden except by right, do not practise sorcery, do not consume usury, do not walk with an innocent person to an authority to have him killed, do not slander a chaste woman" — or he said: "do not flee from the battle line" — Shu'bah being in doubt — "and for you, O Jews, especially: do not transgress on the Sabbath." They kissed his hands and feet, and said: "We testify that you are a prophet." He said: "What prevents you from following me?" They said: "Indeed Dawud (David) supplicated that there should never cease to be a prophet among his descendants, and we fear that if we follow you, the Jews will kill us."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Sahl ibn Yusuf, Abu Dawud and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from 'Amr, who said: I heard 'Abd Allah ibn Salamah narrate from Safwan ibn 'Assal al-Muradi, from the Prophet ﷺ, with something similar, except that Ibn Mahdi said: "Do not walk to an authority," and Ibn Mahdi said: I think he said: "with an innocent person."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Idris and Abu Usamah narrated to us, similarly, from Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Salamah, from Safwan ibn 'Assal, who said: A Jew said to his companion: "Come, let us go to this Prophet." His companion said: "Do not call him a prophet, for if he heard you, he would have four eyes." So they came to the Messenger of God ﷺ, asking him about the nine clear signs, and he said: "They are: Do not associate anything with God, do not steal, do not commit adultery, do not kill the soul which God has forbidden except by right, do not walk with an innocent person to an authority to have him killed, do not practise sorcery, do not consume usury, do not slander a chaste woman, do not turn back on the day of battle, and for you, O Jews, especially: that you do not transgress on the Sabbath." They kissed his hands and feet, and said: "We testify that you are a prophet." He said: "What prevents you from following me?" They said: "Indeed Dawud supplicated that there should never cease to be a prophet among his descendants, and we fear that if we follow you, the Jews will kill us."

Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Salamah, from Safwan ibn 'Assal, from the Prophet ﷺ, with something similar.

As for His saying ﴿So ask the Children of Israel, when he came to them﴾, the majority of the readers of the Muslims recite it in the imperative form, meaning: "So ask, O Muhammad, the Children of Israel, when Moses came to them."

It is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri in its interpretation:

al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, from Isma'il, from al-Hasan: ﴿So ask the Children of Israel﴾, he said: "Your asking them is your looking into the Qur'an."

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to read it: "fasa'ala" (he asked), meaning: Moses asked Pharaoh to release the Children of Israel to go with him, in the form of a report.

Mention of those who said that:

Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, from Hanzalah al-Sadusi, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he read: "fasa'ala Bani Isra'il idh ja'ahum," meaning that Moses asked Pharaoh to release the Children of Israel with him.

The reading which I do not permit to be recited otherwise is the reading upon which the readers of the major cities agree, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers on its correctness and their rejection of what opposes it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Then Pharaoh said to him, "Indeed, I think you, O Moses, are bewitched."﴾

He means: Pharaoh said to Moses: "Indeed, I think you, O Moses, are pursuing the knowledge of sorcery, and these wonders you perform are from your sorcery." It is also permissible that it be intended as: "Indeed, I think you, O Moses, are a sorcerer," so the passive participle is placed in the place of the active, as it is said: "Indeed you are ill-omened (mash'um) for us, and auspicious (maymun)," when the actual words are "shā'im" and "yāmin." Some have also interpreted "ḥijāban mastūran" (a veil concealed) as meaning "ḥijāban sātiran" (a veil screening), and the Arabs often use an active form in the wording of a passive.

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿He said, "You have certainly known that none has sent down these [signs] except the Lord of the heavens and the earth as evidence, and indeed I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed."﴾

The reciters differed over the reading of His saying ﴿لَقَدْ عَلِمْتَ (laqad 'alimta, "you have certainly known")﴾. The majority of the reciters of the principal cities read it ﴿laqad 'alimta﴾ with a fatha on the ta', as direct address from Musa to Pharaoh. It is related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he read "laqad 'alimtu" with a damma on the ta', as a statement from Musa about himself. Whoever reads it in this reading should, according to his view, interpret His saying ﴿إِنِّي لأَظُنُّكَ يَا مُوسَى مَسْحُورًا (inni la-azunnuka ya Musa maskhuran, "indeed I think you, O Musa, are bewitched")﴾ as meaning: "Indeed I think you have been bewitched, so that you see yourself speaking correctly when you are not." This is one aspect of interpretation, but the reading upon which the reciters of the principal cities agree is other than it, and it is not permissible in our view to oppose the proof contained in the reading on which there is consensus.

Furthermore, Allah, may He be remembered, has informed us about Pharaoh and his people that they denied the signs which Musa brought, the nine signs, while they knew that they were from Allah, by His saying: ﴿And insert your hand into your pocket; it will come out white without harm, among nine signs to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they were a defiantly disobedient people. And when Our signs came to them as clear evidence, they said, "This is obvious magic." And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and haughtiness﴾. So He, exalted is His praise, informed that they said, "They are sorcery," while knowing and being certain in their souls that they were from Allah. Likewise His saying ﴿laqad 'alimta﴾ is only a statement from Musa to Pharaoh that he knows that they are signs from Allah. It has been mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas that he argued in this matter with the same kind of proof that we have mentioned.

⁕ He said: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to read ﴿laqad 'alimta﴾ "O Pharaoh" with a fatha, ﴿مَا أَنزلَ هَؤُلاءِ إِلا رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ (ma anzala ha'ula'i illa Rabbu l-samawati wa l-ard, "none has sent down these except the Lord of the heavens and the earth")﴾, then he recited ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and haughtiness﴾.

If that is the case, then the meaning of the speech is: Musa said to Pharaoh, "You have certainly known, O Pharaoh, that none has sent down these nine clear signs which I showed you as proof for the truth of what I call you to, and as a witness for me to the veracity and soundness of my words, that I am a messenger of Allah, and that the Lord of the heavens and the earth alone did not send me to you, because no one other than Him is able to do such a thing, nor anyone like it." ﴿Baṣā'ir (clear evidences)﴾: by the baṣā'ir he means the signs, that they are insights for whoever gains insight through them, and guidance for whoever is guided through them; by them whoever sees them recognizes that the one who brought them is truthful, and that they are from Allah and not from anyone else, since they are miracles which none can produce, nor any part of them, except the Lord of the heavens and the earth. It is the plural of baṣīrah.

* *

And His saying ﴿وَإِنِّي لأَظُنُّكَ يَا فِرْعَوْنُ مَثْبُورًا (wa inni la-azunnuka ya Fir'awnu mathburan, "and indeed I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed")﴾

He says: "Indeed I think you, O Pharaoh, are cursed, prevented from good." The Arabs say: "ma thabaraka 'an hadha al-amr," meaning, what prevented you from this matter and turned you away from it? "Thabarahu Allah, fa-huwa yuthbiruhu wa yathburuhu" are two dialects, and a man who is "mathbur" is one restrained from good things and destroyed. From this is the saying of the poet:

"When I contend with Satan in the paths of error... and whoever inclines to its inclination is mathbur"

[The verse belongs to 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ara, from a poem of four verses, which he composed when he came to the Prophet as a Muslim apologizing for what he had done of satire, under incitement from the Quraysh (see the Sirah of Ibn Hisham, edition of Mustafa al-Halabi and sons, edited by Mustafa al-Saqqa, al-Abyari and Shalabi, second edition, part two, p. 419). The first two verses of it are: "O Messenger of the King, indeed my tongue... is a mender of what I tore when I was ruined (bur)," "When I contend with Satan in the paths of error... and whoever inclines to its inclination is mathbur." Al-Raziq is one who closes a tear, you say: "irtaqtu al-shay'" when you repair and close it. "Fataqtu" means, in religion, every sin is a tearing and rending, and every repentance is a mending. For this reason repentance is called "nasuh," from "nasahtu al-thawb," when you sew it, and "al-nisah" is the thread. "Bur" means destroyed; one says "rajul bur" and "ba'ir," and "qawm bur." "Ubari" means "ujari" and "u'ariḍ," and this is a variant in the verse. "Al-sanan" with a vowel is the middle of the road. "Mathbur" is destroyed. Here is the point of evidence for the author. He said: "Thabarahu Allah yathburuhu wa yuthbiruhu" (like nasara and daraba) are two dialects, and a man who is mathbur is restrained from good and destroyed.]

Similar to what we have said in its interpretation, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Abd Allah ibn Abd Allah al-Kilabi narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿wa inni la-azunnuka ya Fir'awnu mathburan﴾, he said: "cursed."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Abd Allah al-Thaqafi informed us, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

⁕ 'Ali narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to us, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying ﴿wa inni la-azunnuka ya Fir'awnu mathburan﴾, he says: "cursed."

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "Indeed I think you, O Pharaoh, are overcome."

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His saying ﴿wa inni la-azunnuka ya Fir'awnu mathburan﴾, meaning: overcome.

⁕ It was narrated to me from al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿wa inni la-azunnuka ya Fir'awnu mathburan﴾: "overcome."

Others said: The meaning of that is: "Indeed I think you, O Pharaoh, are destroyed."

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "mathburan" means: destroyed.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿wa inni la-azunnuka ya Fir'awnu mathburan﴾: that is, destroyed.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, something similar.

Others said: its meaning is: "Indeed I think you are one who alters and changes."

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Musa, from 'Atiyya, regarding ﴿wa inni la-azunnuka ya Fir'awnu mathburan﴾, he said: "one who alters."

Others said: its meaning is: "one who is bewildered and has no intellect."

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿wa inni la-azunnuka ya Fir'awnu mathburan﴾: "If a person has no intellect, what good is he? That is, if he has no intellect by which he benefits in his religion and his livelihood, the Arabs call him mathbur." He said: "I think you have no intellect, O Pharaoh." He said: "While he feared him, his tongue would not utter that he say this to Pharaoh; but when Allah expanded his breast, he became bold to say to him beyond what Allah had commanded him."

We have already explained which of these is most correct regarding this.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 103–104:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So he wished to scare them from the land, but We drowned him and those with him, all together. And We said after him to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you together in a mixed throng."﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Pharaoh wished to expel Moses and the Children of Israel from the land, ﴿so We drowned him﴾ in the sea, ﴿and those with him﴾ of his soldiers, ﴿all together﴾. We saved Moses and the Children of Israel, and We said to them, ﴿after﴾ the destruction of Pharaoh, ﴿"Dwell in the land"﴾, meaning the land of Syria, ﴿and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you together in a mixed throng﴾. He says: when the Hour comes, which is the promise of the Hereafter, We will bring you from your graves to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection in a mixed throng (lafif), meaning: mingled, with some of you pressed against others, not recognising one another, and none of you withdrawing to his tribe and his clan. From your saying: "I mixed the armies (laffat al-juyush)," when you strike some of them against others, so that all of them are mixed together; and likewise, everything mixed with something else is said to be "lufa" with it.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the explanation of this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibn Abi Razin, regarding ﴿We will bring you together in a mixed throng﴾, he said: "From every people."

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: "We will bring you all together."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 103–104:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿So he wished to scare them from the land, but We drowned him and those with him, all together. And We said after him to the Children of Israel: "Dwell in the land, and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you together in a mixed throng."﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Pharaoh wished to expel Moses and the Children of Israel from the land, ﴿so We drowned him﴾ in the sea, ﴿and those with him﴾ of his soldiers, ﴿all together﴾. We saved Moses and the Children of Israel, and We said to them, ﴿after﴾ the destruction of Pharaoh, ﴿"Dwell in the land"﴾, meaning the land of Syria, ﴿and when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you together in a mixed throng﴾. He says: when the Hour comes, which is the promise of the Hereafter, We will bring you from your graves to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection in a mixed throng (lafif), meaning: mingled, with some of you pressed against others, not recognising one another, and none of you withdrawing to his tribe and his clan. From your saying: "I mixed the armies (laffat al-juyush)," when you strike some of them against others, so that all of them are mixed together; and likewise, everything mixed with something else is said to be "lufa" with it.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the explanation of this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And with truth We have sent it down, and with truth it has descended. And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And a Qur'an We have separated [into parts], that you might recite it to the people over a period. And We have sent it down in stages.﴾ (17:105–106)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And with truth We have sent down this Qur'an." That is: We have sent it down, commanding in it justice, fairness, good character, and praiseworthy and commendable matters, and forbidding in it injustice, reprehensible matters, base character, and blameworthy deeds. ﴿And with truth it has descended﴾: that is, with this it descended from God upon His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

* *

As for His saying, ﴿And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "And We have not sent you, O Muhammad, to those among Our servants to whom We sent you, except as one bringing good tidings of Paradise to those who obey Us and submit to Our command and prohibition, and as a warner to those who disobey Us and oppose Our command and prohibition." ﴿And a Qur'an We have separated [into parts], that you might recite it﴾: The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of the great cities read ﴿farqnāhu﴾ with a light (unstressed) *rāʾ*, meaning: We made it firm, distinguished it, and clarified it. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read it with a stressed *rāʾ*, "farraqnāhu," meaning: We sent it down piece by piece, verse after verse, and story after story.

The more correct of the two readings in our view is the first reading, because it is the reading upon which the proof is agreed, and it is not permissible to oppose it in what is agreed upon in matters of religion and the Qur'an. Since this is the more correct of the two readings, the meaning of the speech is: "And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and We have made it a Qur'an distinguished (into its parts), and clarified and made it firm, that you might recite it to the people over a period."

Similar to what we have said in this interpretation, a group of the people of interpretation (*ahl al-taʾwīl*) have said.

Those who said that:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿And a Qur'an We have separated﴾: he said: "We have explained it (faṣṣalnāhu)."

- Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Jaʿfar, from Abu al-Rabiʿ, from Abu al-ʿĀliya, from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb that he read ﴿And a Qur'an We have separated﴾ with a light (unstressed) *rāʾ*: meaning, "We have clarified it."

- Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās said, ﴿And a Qur'an We have separated﴾: "We have explained it."

- Ibn al-Muthannā related to us, saying: Badal ibn al-Muhabbar related to us, saying: ʿAbbād, meaning Ibn Rashid, related to us, from Dawud, from al-Hasan, that he read it with a light (unstressed) *rāʾ*: "God separated between truth and falsehood."

As for those who read the other reading, they interpreted it in the way I have mentioned.

Those who said what I have related of the interpretation from the one who reads it that way: Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ, from Abu al-ʿĀliya, who said: Ibn ʿAbbās used to read it: "wa-qurʾānan farraqnāhu" with a stressed *rāʾ*, saying: "He sent down verse by verse."

- Ibn al-Muthannā related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, saying: Dawud informed us, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The Qur'an was sent down all at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of Power (laylat al-qadr), then it was sent down after that over twenty years." He said: ﴿And they do not bring you any example except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation﴾ (25:33), and "And a Qur'an We have separated, that you might recite it to the people over a period, and We have sent it down in stages."

- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "And a Qur'an We have separated, that you might recite it to the people": "It was not sent down all together, and between its beginning and its end was about twenty years."

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And a Qur'an We have separated﴾: "He separated it: He did not send down all of it together." And he recited ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?"﴾ (25:32) ... until he reached ﴿and the best explanation﴾, [meaning] that He refutes by it what they bring.

Some of the Arabic grammarians of Kufa used to say: the accusative of His saying ﴿And a Qur'an﴾ is in the sense of "and as a mercy," and they interpret it as ﴿And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ "and as a mercy," and he said: "This is permissible, because the Qur'an is a mercy." But its accusative in the manner we have stated is more correct, and it is like His, may His praise be exalted, saying ﴿And the moon—We have determined for it stations﴾ (36:39). As for His saying ﴿that you might recite it to the people over a period﴾, it means: that you might recite it to the people slowly and deliberately, so that you chant it and make it clear, and do not hasten in its recitation, lest it not be understood from you.

Similar to what we have said in this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from ʿUbayd al-Mukattib [[al-Mukattib: an active participle from *akttaba* or from *kataba* with the stress, meaning the teacher, who teaches children to write the Qur'an on their boards.]], who said: I said to Mujahid: "A man recited al-Baqara and Al ʿImran, and another recited al-Baqara, and their bowing and prostrations are the same: which of them is better?" He said: "The one who recited al-Baqara, and recited ﴿And a Qur'an We have separated, that you might recite it to the people over a period﴾."

- Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah related to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His saying ﴿that you might recite it to the people over a period﴾: he said: "with support (taʾyīd)."

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿĀsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqaʾ related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿over a period﴾: he said: "with measured recitation (tartīl)."

- Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying ﴿that you might recite it to the people over a period﴾: he said: "in measured recitation."

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿that you might recite it to the people over a period﴾: "The explanation is what God said: ﴿And recite the Qur'an in measured recitation﴾ (73:4); its explanation."

- Al-Hasan related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from ʿUbayd, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿that you might recite it to the people over a period﴾: "with deliberation (taʾadda)." And regarding *al-mukth* the Arabs have several dialects: *mukth*, *makth*, *mikth*, *mikkīthā* (with a short vowel), and *mukthānā*; and the reading is with a *ḍamma* on the *mīm*.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And We have sent it down in stages﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "We have divided its sending down and sent it down piece by piece."

As:

- Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya related to us, saying: He related to us, from Abu Rajaʾ, who said: al-Hasan recited: "And a Qur'an We have separated, that you might recite it to the people over a period, and We have sent it down in stages." He said: "God, blessed and exalted, used to send down this Qur'an, some of it before some, because He knew what would occur and happen among the people." And it has been reported to us that between its beginning and its end there were eighteen years. He said: "I asked him one day in a state of displeasure, and I said: 'O Abu Saʿid, [what about] "wa-qurʾānan farraqnāhu" (with a stressed *rāʾ*)?'" Abu Rajaʾ made it heavy, and al-Hasan said: "It is not *farraqnāhu*, but *faraqnāhu*," and al-Hasan read it with a light (unstressed) *rāʾ*. I said: "From whom do you narrate this, O Abu Saʿid? The Companions of Muhammad?" He said: "Who else would narrate it to me?" He said: "It was sent down to him in Mecca eight years before he migrated to Medina, and in Medina ten years."

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿And a Qur'an We have separated, that you might recite it to the people over a period, and We have sent it down in stages﴾: "It was not sent down in a night or two nights, nor a month or two months, nor a year or two years, but between its beginning and its end there were twenty years, and whatever else God willed of that."

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, who said: He used to say: "The Qur'an was sent down upon the Prophet of God for eight years, and ten years after he migrated." And Qatada used to say: "ten years in Mecca, and ten years in Medina."

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verses 107–108:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Whether you believe in it or do not believe, indeed those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down on their faces in prostration (ﷺ)..." ﴾ (17:107)

Here He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to these who say to you, ﴿"We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth"﴾ (17:90): Believe in this Qur'an, which, even if all of mankind and the jinn gathered to produce its like, they would not produce it, even if they were helpers to one another. Or do not believe in it. Your belief in it will not increase anything in the treasuries of Allah's mercy, nor will your abandonment of belief in it diminish that. And if you disbelieve in it, then indeed those who were given knowledge of Allah and His signs before its revelation, from among the believers of the two scriptures (the People of the Book), when this Qur'an is recited to them, they fall down upon their faces, prostrating to the earth, out of exaltation and honour for it, and out of their knowledge that it is from Allah.

The people of interpretation differed concerning what is meant by His saying ﴿fall down upon their faces﴾ (li-l-adhqan). Some of them said: it means the faces.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, he said: Abdullah narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿fall down upon their faces in prostration﴾, he said: it means the faces.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿fall down upon their faces in prostration﴾, he said: for the faces.

- Al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Others said: rather, it means the beards.

Mention of those who said that:

- Al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, he said: al-Hasan said, concerning His saying ﴿fall down upon their faces﴾, he said: the beards.

* *

And His saying ﴿"Glory be to our Lord! Indeed the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled"﴾ (17:108).

His majesty, exalted is His praise, says: And those who were given knowledge before the revelation of this Qur'an, when they fell down in prostration upon their faces upon hearing the Qur'an recited to them, will say, glorifying our Lord and declaring Him free of what the polytheists attribute to Him: the promise of our Lord, of reward and punishment, has certainly been a thing fulfilled, a true and certain matter, [and this is] belief in the Qur'an and affirmation of it. In the speech of the Arabs, al-adhqan is the plural of dhaqan, which is the meeting-place of the two jaws (lihyayn). Given that this is so, what al-Hasan said concerning it is closer to the apparent meaning of the revelation.

And in the manner of what we have said on this, the people of interpretation said, though they differed about those meant by His saying ﴿those who were given knowledge﴾ and concerning ﴿when it is recited to them﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: Mujahid said, concerning ﴿those who were given knowledge before it﴾ ... to His saying ﴿in humility﴾, he said: they are people from the People of the Book who, when they heard what Allah revealed to Muhammad, said ﴿"Glory be to our Lord! Indeed the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled"﴾.

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿Say: "Whether you believe in it or do not believe, indeed those who were given knowledge before it"﴾, from before the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿when it is recited to them﴾ what was revealed to them from Allah, ﴿they fall down upon their faces in prostration, and say: "Glory be to our Lord! Indeed the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled"﴾.

Others said: what is meant by His saying ﴿those who were given knowledge before it﴾ is the Qur'an revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, concerning ﴿when it is recited to them﴾, [it means] their scripture.

- Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning ﴿when it is recited to them﴾, what Allah revealed to them from Allah.

We only said that what is meant by ﴿when it is recited to them﴾ is the Qur'an, because within the context of the mention of the Qur'an no mention of other books has preceded, so the speech is directed to it. Likewise, the pronoun in His saying ﴿before it﴾ refers to the mention of the Qur'an, because the speech concerning it came before, and that is His saying ﴿and a Qur'an which We have divided﴾ and what follows it is within the context of the report about it. Therefore the correctness of what we have said is established, since no contrary view has come with a proof that must be accepted.

Or do not believe in it. Your belief in it will not increase anything in the treasuries of Allah's mercy, nor will your abandonment of belief in it diminish that. And if you disbelieve in it, then indeed those who were given knowledge of Allah and His signs before its revelation, from among the believers of the two scriptures (the People of the Book), when this Qur'an is recited to them, they fall down upon their faces, prostrating to the earth, out of exaltation and honour for it, and out of their knowledge that it is from Allah.
