Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 109:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they fall down upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility (khushu')﴾

Allah, the One mentioned, says: And those among the people of the two scriptures who were given knowledge from before the revelation of the Furqan (the Criterion, i.e., the Qur'an), who are believers, fall down upon their chins weeping when the Qur'an is recited to them, and what is in the Qur'an of admonitions and lessons increases them in khushu', meaning submission (khudu') to the command of Allah and obedience to Him, and humbling themselves (istikanah) before Him.

* Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, he said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, he said: Mis'ar informed us, from Abd al-A'la al-Taymi, that whoever is given knowledge and does not weep is likely not to have been given knowledge that benefits him, because Allah described the scholars, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it, when it is recited to them, fall down upon their chins﴾ ... the two verses.

* Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, he said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Mis'ar ibn Kidam, from Abd al-A'la al-Taymi, with a similar report, except that he said: ﴿When it is recited to them, they fall down upon their chins﴾, then he said: ﴿And they fall down upon their chins weeping﴾ ... the verse.

* Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿And they fall down upon their chins weeping, and it increases them in humility﴾: This is a response and explanation of the verse in Maryam (Surah Kaf Ha Ya 'Ayn Sad): ﴿When the signs of the Most Merciful are recited to them, they fall down prostrating and weeping.﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 110 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Gracious; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names. And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein, but seek between that a way.﴾

He, may He be exalted, says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people who deny the calling upon the Most Gracious: ﴿Call upon Allah﴾, O people, ﴿or call upon the Most Gracious; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾, that is, by whichever of His names, may His majesty be great, you call upon your Lord, for you are calling upon One, and to Him belong the most beautiful names. This was said to him, peace and blessings be upon him, because the polytheists, as it is reported, heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, calling upon his Lord: "O our Lord, Allah," and "O our Lord, the Most Gracious," so they thought that he was calling upon two gods. So Allah sent down this verse to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, as an argument for His Prophet against them.

The narration with what we have mentioned: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to me, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Waqid, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, was prostrating and calling: "O Most Gracious, O Most Merciful." So the polytheists said: "This one claims that he calls upon One, yet he calls upon two, two by two." So Allah, exalted, sent down: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Gracious; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾ .... the verse.

⁕ Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to me, from al-Awza'i, from Makhul, that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, "was performing the night prayer in Mecca one night, saying in his prostration: 'O Most Gracious, O Most Merciful.' A man from the polytheists heard him, and when morning came he said to his companions: 'See what Ibn Abi Kabsha said. Tonight he calls upon the Most Gracious of Yamama, and there was a man in Yamama called al-Rahman.' So it was revealed: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Gracious; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿Say: Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Gracious; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾. [[Thus it is in the originals; the text was not mentioned, relying on what preceded, and this has recurred from him.]]

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿whichever you call upon﴾: by any of His names.

⁕ Musa ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakkar al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn ʿIsa narrated to me, from ʿUbayd ibn al-Tufayl al-Juhani, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, from Makhul, from ʿArrak ibn Malik, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: "Indeed Allah has ninety-nine names, all of them in the Qur'an; whoever counts them enters Paradise."

Abu Ja'far said: The particle "ma" in His words ﴿whichever you call upon﴾ has two possible functions: one is that it is an extra element (ṣila), as in the saying ﴿in a little while they will surely become regretful﴾; the other is that it has the meaning of "in" (in), repeated because the two words differ, as it is said: "ma in ra'aytu ka-l-laylati laylatan" (I have not seen a night like tonight).

* *

As for His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein, but seek between that a way﴾:

The people of interpretation differed concerning "prayer" (ṣalāt). Some of them said: By this is meant: "And do not be loud in your supplication, nor be silent therein, but between that"; and they said: By "prayer" in this place is meant supplication.

Those who said this:

⁕ Yahya ibn ʿIsa al-Damaghani narrated to me, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿA'isha, regarding His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, she said: "It is about supplication."

⁕ Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn ʿUrwa narrated to us, from his father, from ʿA'isha, who said: "It was revealed concerning supplication."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿA'isha, the like of it.

⁕ al-Hasan ibn ʿArafa narrated to us, saying: ʿAbbad ibn al-ʿAwwam narrated to us, from Ashʿath ibn Sawwar, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding the words of God, exalted, ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "They used to be loud in supplication, so when this verse was revealed they were commanded not to be loud, nor to be silent."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Malik al-Bakri, from Abu al-Jawza', from ʿA'isha, who said: "It was revealed concerning supplication."

⁕ Matar ibn Muhammad al-Dabbi narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Fayyad, from Abu ʿIyad, regarding His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "Supplication."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibrahim al-Hajari, from Abu ʿIyad: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "It was revealed concerning supplication."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Fayyad, from Abu ʿIyad, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from one he mentioned, from ʿAta': ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "It was revealed concerning supplication."

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid regarding the verse ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "It is about supplication."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, who said: "It was revealed concerning supplication."

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾: "in supplication and in request."

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "It was revealed concerning supplication and request."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to me, saying: Qays ibn Muslim narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "It is about supplication."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn ʿAyyash al-ʿAmiri, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Shaddad, who said: "Bedouins, when the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, finished the prayer, would say: 'O Allah, grant us camels and children.' So this verse was revealed: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾."

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, regarding His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "It is about supplication."

⁕ Ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer﴾ .... the verse, he said: "It is about supplication and request."

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to me, from al-Awza'i, from Makhul: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "That is about supplication."

And others said: By this is meant the prayer (ṣalāt).

Those who held this view differed concerning the meaning of the prohibition against being loud in it. Some of them said: What he was prohibited from being loud in is the recitation.

Those who said this:

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "This verse was revealed while the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was hidden: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾. He used to recite the Qur'an aloud when he prayed with his companions, and when the polytheists heard that, they reviled the Qur'an, him who revealed it, and him who brought it. So Allah said to His Prophet: (And do not be loud in your prayer), so that the polytheists hear, ﴿nor be silent therein﴾ before your companions, so that you do not make them hear the Qur'an until they take it from you."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿUthman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn ʿUmara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was loud in leading the Muslims in prayer with the recitation, it grieved the polytheists when they heard it, and they would harm the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, with insults and disparagement of him, and that was in Mecca. So Allah revealed: O Muhammad, ﴿do not be loud in your prayer﴾, meaning: do not announce the recitation of the Qur'an with a strong announcement that the polytheists hear, so that they harm you; and ﴿do not be silent therein﴾, meaning: do not lower your voice so that you do not make your own ears hear it; ﴿but seek between that a way﴾, meaning: seek between announcing and loudness, and between silence and lowering, a path: neither a strong loudness nor a lowering that does not make your ears hear. That is the measure. When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, emigrated to Medina, all of this was dropped, and he now does whichever of these he wishes."

⁕ I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾ .... the verse: "This was when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, was in Mecca. When he prayed with his companions and raised his voice with the recitation, he made the polytheists hear, and they harmed him. So Allah commanded him not to raise his voice, so that his enemy would hear it, nor to be silent, so that those behind him among the Muslims would not hear it, and Allah commanded him to seek a way between that."

⁕ Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Jaʿfar ibn Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to raise his voice with the Qur'an, and when the polytheists heard his voice they reviled the Qur'an and him who brought it. So the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, would lower the Qur'an so that his companions could not hear it. Then Allah revealed ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein, but seek between that a way﴾."

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: Abu Hamza informed us, from al-Aʿmash, from Jaʿfar ibn Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, raised his voice and the polytheists heard, they reviled the Qur'an and him who brought it; and when he lowered it, his companions did not hear. Allah said: ﴿but seek between that a way﴾."

⁕ Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, recited the Qur'an aloud while praying, they scattered and refused to listen to him. A man who wanted to hear some of what he recited while he prayed would eavesdrop out of their sight, out of fear of them; and if he saw that they had realized he was listening, he would leave, fearing their harm, and would not listen. If the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, lowered his voice, those who listened to his recitation would hear nothing of it. So Allah revealed to him: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer﴾, so that they scatter away from you, ﴿nor be silent therein﴾, so that you do not make audible to whoever wants to hear it, from among those eavesdropping out of their sight, so that perhaps he may be moved by some of what he hears and benefit from it, ﴿but seek between that a way﴾."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: "The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to recite the Qur'an aloud in the Sacred Mosque, and the Quraysh said: 'Do not recite aloud, lest you harm our gods, and so revile your Lord.' So Allah revealed ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾ .... the verse."

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "It was revealed to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, while he was hiding in Mecca. When he prayed with his companions he raised his voice with the Qur'an, and when the polytheists heard it they reviled the Qur'an and him who revealed it and him who brought it. So Allah said to His Prophet: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer﴾, that is, with your recitation, so that the polytheists hear and revile the Qur'an. ﴿Nor be silent therein﴾, before your companions, so that you do not make them hear it, ﴿but seek between that a way﴾."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from Jaʿfar ibn Iyas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "It is about the recitation."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding this verse ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "When the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, raised his voice, his companions were pleased with it, and when the polytheists heard that, they reviled him, so this verse was revealed."

⁕ Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Salama, from ʿAlqama, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "I was told that Abu Bakr, when he prayed and recited, lowered his voice, and that ʿUmar raised his voice. It was said to Abu Bakr: 'Why do you do this?' He said: 'I am conversing with my Lord, and He knows my need.' It was said: 'You have done well.' And it was said to ʿUmar: 'Why do you do this?' He said: 'I drive away the devil and wake the drowsy.' It was said: 'You have done well.' So when ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein, but seek between that a way﴾ was revealed, it was said to Abu Bakr: 'Raise your voice somewhat,' and it was said to ʿUmar: 'Lower your voice somewhat.'"

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Hassan ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Ibrahim al-Sa'igh, from ʿAta', regarding His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "Some people say it is about the prayer, and others say it is about supplication."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein, but seek between that a way﴾: "The Prophet of Allah, while in Mecca, when the polytheists heard his voice, pelted him with every foulness. So Allah commanded him to lower his voice and to make his prayer between himself and his Lord. It used to be said: What your ear hears is not silence."

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾, he said: "The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, used to raise his voice in prayer, and he was pelted with foulness. So He said: Do not raise your voice so that you are harmed, nor be silent therein, and seek between that a way."

And others said: It was only meant: "Do not be loud in the tashahhud in your prayer, nor be silent therein."

Those who said this:

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿA'isha, who said: "This verse was revealed concerning the tashahhud: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾."

⁕ Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from Ashʿath, from Ibn Sirin, the like of it, and he added: "A Bedouin used to be loud and say: 'At-tahiyyatu lillah, wa-l-salawatu lillah,' raising his voice in it, so ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer﴾ was revealed."

And others said: Rather, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, used to pray openly in Mecca, so he was commanded to conceal it.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrima and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said: "It was said concerning the Children of Israel: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein, but seek between that a way﴾. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, when he prayed, would pray aloud, and that harmed the polytheists in Mecca, until he and his companions concealed their prayer. Therefore He said: ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein, but seek between that a way﴾." And in al-A'raf He said: ﴿And remember your Lord within yourself, humbly and in fear, and without loudness in speech, in the mornings and evenings, and do not be among the heedless﴾.

And others said: The meaning is: "Do not be loud in your prayer" by making it good through performing it openly, "and do not be silent therein" by making it bad in secret.

Those who said this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, that al-Hasan used to say regarding ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾: "That is, do not show off by it openly, and do not make it light in secret, ﴿but seek between that a way﴾."

⁕ al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: al-Hasan used to say regarding His words ﴿And do not be loud in your prayer, nor be silent therein﴾: "Do not make its openness good, and make its secrecy bad."

Yaqub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Awf, from al-Hasan, regarding His words ﴿Neither speak your prayer aloud, nor be silent in it﴾. He said: "Do not show off in it openly, and do not conceal it in your inner heart."

Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azraqi narrated to me, saying: al-Ashja'i narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from al-Hasan, regarding ﴿Neither speak your prayer aloud, nor be silent in it﴾. He said: "He makes its outward appearance good and its inner intention bad."

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Neither speak your prayer aloud, nor be silent in it﴾. He said: "Do not pray out of showing off to people, and do not abandon it out of fear."

Others said something else on this matter:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Neither speak your prayer aloud, nor be silent in it, but seek between that a way﴾: "The way between them is that which Jibril (Gabriel) prescribed for the prayer, on which the Muslims are. He said: The People of the Book used to be silent, and then one of them would raise his voice with a word, and he would cry out with it, and they would cry out behind him. So He forbade him to cry out as these people cry out, and to be silent as those people are silent. Then the way between that was what Jibril prescribed for the prayer."

The most correct of these opinions is what we have mentioned from Ibn Abbas in the report narrated by Abu Ja'far, from Sa'id, from Ibn Abbas, because that is the most sound chain of narration (isnad) that has come from a Companion (sahabi) with a transmitted opinion on it, and the most similar of the opinions to what the apparent meaning of the revelation (tanzil) indicates. This is because His words ﴿Neither speak your prayer aloud, nor be silent in it﴾ come after His words ﴿Say: Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call, to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾, and after the rebuke of the disbelievers for their disbelief in the Qur'an, which is their distance from it and from faith. Since this is so, the more fitting and more similar meaning to His words ﴿Neither speak your prayer aloud, nor be silent in it﴾ is that it should be taken from the context of what precedes it, unless there comes a meaning that requires diverting it from that, or there is evidence for diverting it from the context by which the diversion is known.

Since this is so, the interpretation (ta'wil) of the speech is: "Say: Call upon Allah, or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call, to Him belong the most beautiful names. And do not raise your voice, O Muhammad, in your recitation in your prayer, nor in your supplication in it, in which you call upon your Lord, ask Him, and mention Him, so that the polytheists harm you by your raising your voice with that; and do not be silent in it so that your companions do not hear it. ﴿But seek between that a way﴾: rather, seek a path between raising the voice and being silent, so that your companions hear you and the polytheists do not hear, and so they do not harm you."

Were it not that the sayings of the people of interpretation have gone with what I have mentioned from them as interpretation, and we do not seek to oppose them regarding what has come from them, there would be a possible reading that the interpretation could bear: that it be said, "Do not raise your voice in your prayer about which We have commanded you to be silent, which is the daytime prayer, since it is silent and is not vocalized, and do not be silent in your prayer about which We have commanded you to raise your voice, which is the night prayer, since it is vocalized. ﴿But seek between that a way﴾: by raising your voice in what We commanded you to raise it in, and being silent in what We commanded you to be silent in; do not raise your voice in all of it, nor be silent in all of it." This would have been a reading not far from correctness. But we do not consider this sound, because the consensus (ijma', scholarly agreement) of the authoritative scholars among the people of interpretation is against it.

If someone says: "What is this reading that lies between raising the voice and being silent?"

It is said: Matar ibn Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Qutayba and Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, both saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Ash'ath ibn Sulaym, from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, who said: Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) said: "The one who makes his own ears hear is not silent."

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from al-Ash'ath, from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, from Abd Allah, the like of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 17, verse 111:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And say, "All praise is due to Allah, who has not taken a son, and does not have a partner in dominion, and does not have any ally out of weakness. And glorify Him with [great] glorification."﴾ (17:111)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And say﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿"All praise is due to Allah, who has not taken a son"﴾, for then He would be one who is nurtured, not the Lord, since the Lord of lords should not have a son. ﴿"And does not have a partner in dominion"﴾, for then He would be incapable, in need of the help of another, weak, and one who needs an assistant in what he attempts is not a god; and He is not alone in sovereignty and authority. ﴿"And does not have any ally out of weakness"﴾ means: He does not have an ally who allies with Him out of the weakness that would afflict Him, because whoever needs the help of another is humbled and debased, and one who is humbled and debased and needs a helper is not a god to be obeyed. ﴿"And glorify Him with [great] glorification"﴾ means: Magnify your Lord, O Muhammad, with what We have commanded you to magnify Him with, in word and deed, and obey Him in what He has commanded and forbidden you.

Similar to what we have said regarding His saying ﴿"And does not have any ally out of weakness"﴾ is what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿"And does not have any ally out of weakness"﴾, he said: He has not allied with anyone, nor does He seek the help of anyone.

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to teach his family this verse: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has not taken a son, and does not have a partner in dominion, and does not have any ally out of weakness. And glorify Him with [great] glorification.﴾ The young among his family and the old."

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Junayd narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Indeed, the whole Torah is in fifteen verses from the Children of Israel. Then he recited ﴿"Do not set up with Allah another god"﴾.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr informed me, from al-Qurazi, that he used to say regarding this verse ﴿"All praise is due to Allah, who has not taken a son"﴾ ... the verse. He said: The Jews and Christians said: Allah has taken a son. The Arabs said: "Here I am, here I am, You have no partner, except a partner who is Yours, You own him." The Sabians and Magians said: "Were it not for the allies of Allah, Allah would be humiliated." So Allah revealed ﴿"And say, 'All praise is due to Allah, who has not taken a son, and does not have a partner in dominion, and does not have any ally out of weakness. And glorify Him'"﴾, you, O Muhammad, [say it] regarding what they say ﴿"with [great] glorification"﴾.

End of the commentary on Surah Bani Isra'il, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
